title: Dolt 2.0.6 breaks migration 0041 (FK on base col of stored generated col) — all CI red
description:
## Symptom
Every PR's CI went red on 2026-05-22/23 on jobs: "Test (storage domain + uow)", "Test (ubuntu-latest)", "Test (macos-latest)", and repro-dolt. Not caused by any application change.

## Root cause
CI installs dolt via `install.sh latest`. Dolt 2.0.6 (shipped 2026-05-22) rejects `ADD FOREIGN KEY` on the base column of a stored generated column (errno 1105 "Cannot add foreign key on the base column of a stored generated column"). Migration internal/storage/schema/migrations/0041_split_dependencies_target.up.sql adds the STORED generated `depends_on_id = COALESCE(depends_on_issue_id,depends_on_wisp_id,depends_on_external)` and THEN adds `fk_dep_issue_target FOREIGN KEY (depends_on_issue_id)` — depends_on_issue_id is a base column of that generated column. Aborts mid-migration on 2.0.6. Parent main (cfcc95799) passed on 2.0.5.

The UOW provider failures surface as "pending schema migrations alter pre-existing dirty tables: dependencies" — secondary effect of 0041 aborting and leaving `dependencies` dirty (non-retryable in initSchema, doltserver_provider.go:192).

## Proof
Minimal DDL repro: 2.0.5 ADD FK -> OK; 2.0.6 -> errno 1105. All three failing tests reproduced under dolt 2.0.6 locally and pass with the fix; no 2.0.5 regression. SHOW CREATE TABLE identical after reorder.

## Fix
PR #4120 (quad341:fix/dolt206-fk-on-generated-col): reorder the FK add to before the generated-column add in 0041.up.sql. Identical final schema.

## Optional stopgap
Pin CI dolt to 2.0.5 in .github/workflows/ci.yml (install.sh) if a green CI is needed before #4120 merges — but #4120 is the real fix and lets CI keep tracking latest dolt.

## Follow-up worth considering
The Dolt 2.0.6 restriction (FK on base column of a stored generated column) may be an upstream regression worth reporting to dolthub/dolt.
notes: Investigated + fix pushed as PR #4120 (verified on dolt 2.0.6 + 2.0.5). Humans merge the PR. Discovered while verifying be-kjp7x / PR #4118 (whose red CI was this same Dolt break, not the be-kjp7x change).

title: fix(schema): runMigrations passes wrong source, ignored migrations never apply
description:
PR #3914 introduced a regression: extracted runMigrations() hardcodes mainSource instead of using receiver m. This causes ignoredSource.migrate() to re-iterate main migrations and leave ignored_schema_migrations table empty. Result: wisp tables (created by ignored migrations) never exist after bd open.

Repro: BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -run TestSchemaAfterInit ./internal/storage/embeddeddolt/...
Fails with: 'reading max ignored_schema_migrations version: sql: no rows in result set'

Fix: pass migrationSource as parameter to runMigrations.
close_reason: Closed

title: Review: be-ucslk4 P0 label-filter regression fix (Dolt + PG backends)
description:
## Branch

`fix/be-ucslk4` off `local-integ` (a67427829), worktree at /var/tmp/be-ucslk4-fix, three commits:

1. **f3a38aa8e** — `fix(list): suppress truncation hint in --json mode + lock-in label filter tests (be-acnquj)` — cherry-pick of 9885fc20c. AC#7 fix (truncation hint suppression) plus TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj harness (skipped locally without Dolt server, runs in CI).

2. **67925ad54** — `fix(filters): wire LabelPattern/LabelRegex through SQL builder (be-ucslk4)` — adds the missing WHERE clauses in internal/storage/issueops/filters.go BuildIssueFilterClauses for LabelPattern (glob -> LIKE ESCAPE '|') and LabelRegex (REGEXP). Includes globToLikePattern helper, four new unit tests (filters_test.go), and a strengthened negative-case assertion on the existing TestEmbeddedList/label_pattern.

3. **1f12523af** — `fix(postgres): wire label + title-contains filters in SearchIssues (be-ucslk4)` — the actual live regression. PostgresStore.SearchIssues was scoped to a 'smoke path' and silently dropped Labels, LabelsAny, ExcludeLabels, LabelPattern, LabelRegex, TitleContains. Adds EXISTS / NOT EXISTS subqueries against the labels table (mirroring the GetReadyWork pattern) plus an ILIKE clause for TitleContains. New pgGlobToLikePattern helper + table test.

## Why three commits not one

f3a38aa8e is a clean cherry-pick of the existing approved commit (preserves authorship + SHA). 67925ad54 and 1f12523af are scoped per-backend so the diff is reviewable backend-by-backend. The first two cover the Dolt path; the third covers the PG path which is what unblocks the live city.

## Verified

- `make build`: clean, ldflags=-X main.Build=1f12523af
- `golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/postgres/ ./internal/storage/issueops/ ./cmd/bd/`: 0 issues
- Unit tests pass without Docker / PG: filters_test.go, issues_test.go (postgres pgGlobToLikePattern)
- Embedded integration test pass: `BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -run TestEmbeddedList/label_pattern`
- End-to-end against the live gc-management PG city: every filter named in be-ucslk4 AC returns the correct row count; `gc hook beads/pm` injection returns 1 bead (be-rhtega) instead of 50 unfiltered.
- Installed bd at /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd reports version 1f12523af.

## Acceptance criteria from be-ucslk4

| AC | Status |
|----|--------|
| #1 — every label/title filter returns correct count | PASS (live verification) |
| #2 — TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj exists on the branch | PASS (cherry-picked) |
| #3 — `bd list --json` does not emit truncation hint | PASS (manual verify) |
| #4 — `gc hook beads/pm` returns only labeled beads | PASS (1 needs-pm bead returned) |
| #5 — installed bd reports merge SHA | PASS (1f12523af) |

## Follow-ups filed

- **be-8skfsh** (needs-tests, postgres) — integration_pg coverage for the new SearchIssues filter clauses on the PG path, routed to validator. Linked discovered-from be-ucslk4. The unit-level pgGlobToLikePattern test pins the conversion; the SQL emission has not been pinned in CI yet.

## Caveats / context

- My prior close of be-acnquj was wrong. I claimed PM's repro was a stale-binary artifact based on a build that walked up to a Dolt-embedded .beads directory; I missed that the live city had migrated to PG and that LabelPattern/LabelRegex were never SQL-wired in either backend. The regression-guard test in 9885fc20c was correct in spirit, but it ran against a path the live system does not use. Hence the re-open and the broader fix.

- Per project memory, PG backend follow-ups are gated on mayor greenlight (be-ekw, 2026-05-04 'several days' rule). This fix is on local-integ (the integration branch, where the PG backend already lives), not on main, so it follows the existing local-only PG deployment posture. Mailed mayor at gm-tmjenf and gm-kgejbx as the scope expanded; no objection received.
notes:
## Review verdict: PASS

Reviewed by **beads/reviewer** (claude-opus-4-7) at 2026-05-07T17:38Z.
Branch `fix/be-ucslk4` @ 1f12523af off local-integ a67427829.

### Triage

| Category | Outcome |
|----------|---------|
| Style / lint | PASS — `golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/issueops/ ./internal/storage/postgres/ ./cmd/bd/` 0 issues |
| Security (OWASP) | PASS — see notes below |
| Spec compliance (be-ucslk4 AC#1–5) | PASS — independently verified live against gc-management PG city |
| Coverage | PASS — option (a) for Dolt path, option (b) for PG path (be-8skfsh filed) |
| Architecture | PASS — Dolt fix mirrors existing single-label clause; PG fix mirrors GetReadyWork's EXISTS pattern |

### Per-commit findings

**f3a38aa8e — cherry-pick of 9885fc20c (truncation hint + lock-in tests)**
- `cmd/bd/list_output.go:20` — `|| jsonOutput` gate is the minimal correct change for AC#7. Comment updated to reference be-acnquj.
- `cmd/bd/list_test.go:528-705` — `TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj` exercises AC#1–5 (single label, AND, OR, glob, case-insensitive title, nonexistent). `TestPrintTruncationHintJSONSuppression` covers six cases for AC#7 with proper `t.Cleanup` of `os.Stderr` and `jsonOutput`. Tests are tagged `cgo && dolt_only` so they run in the Dolt CI leg.

**67925ad54 — Dolt: wire LabelPattern/LabelRegex (be-ucslk4)**
- `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go:26-46` — `globToLikePattern` correctly escapes `%`/`_`/`|` (verified by `TestGlobToLikePattern` 8 cases including the escape-char itself).
- `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go:201-208` — new clauses use the same shape as the existing single-label clause (line 178). User input bound via `?`; identifier `tables.Labels` is a package-level constant.
- `cmd/bd/list_embedded_test.go:270-278` — negative-case assertions added (feature/chore must NOT match `back*`). Without these, the prior test would have passed when the filter was a no-op — that's a real regression-guard improvement.
- Unit tests: `TestBuildIssueFilterClauses_LabelPattern`, `_LabelPatternWispsTable`, `_LabelRegex`, `TestGlobToLikePattern` — all PASS with `source .buildflags && go test ./internal/storage/issueops/`.

**1f12523af — Postgres: SearchIssues filters (be-ucslk4) ← the live regression**
- `internal/storage/postgres/issues.go:325-347` — `pgGlobToLikePattern` is a deliberate mirror of `issueops.globToLikePattern` to keep the postgres package free of an issueops import. Drift risk mitigated by identical table tests on both sides (8 cases each, same fixture set).
- `internal/storage/postgres/issues.go:411-435` — six new clauses (TitleContains, Labels, LabelsAny, ExcludeLabels, LabelPattern, LabelRegex). Pattern mirrors `queries.go:40-53` (GetReadyWork) — same EXISTS / NOT EXISTS shape against the labels table, qualified to `issues.id` since SearchIssues queries the issues table directly.
- Placeholder counter (`next`) advances correctly: `add()` increments by `len(vals)`; `joinPlaceholders(next, len(LabelsAny))` is called before `add()` so it captures the current value, and `add()` then bumps `next` by the slice length.
- `TestPgGlobToLikePattern` PASSes (8 cases mirroring the dolt-side test).

### Security walk

- **SQL injection** (OWASP A03): All user-controlled values (label text, glob pattern, regex pattern, title substring) flow through positional parameters (`?` for Dolt, `$N` for Postgres). Identifiers (`tables.Labels`, the literal `labels`) are static. No string concatenation of user input into SQL. ✓
- **LIKE injection**: `globToLikePattern` / `pgGlobToLikePattern` escape literal `%`/`_`/`|` with `|` and emit `ESCAPE '|'`. Verified by table test cases (`literal_percent`, `literal_underscore`, `literal_pipe`). ✓
- **REGEXP DoS**: User-supplied regex is passed verbatim. Dolt under `gms_pure_go` uses Go stdlib RE2 (linear-time guarantees). Postgres regex (`~`) is NFA and theoretically vulnerable to ReDoS, but `bd` is a local CLI where the operator IS the user — not in scope as a security concern, and consistent with how the existing GetReadyWork path handles labels. ✓
- **Sensitive data exposure**: No PII added to logs or error paths.
- **Misconfiguration**: `//nolint:gosec` annotation on the SearchIssues query is justified — clauses contain only placeholders and static identifiers (issues.go:445).

### AC verification (live, installed bd `1f12523af`)

```
open total                              : 105
--label=needs-pm                        :   1   (was 105)
--label=ZZZZZZZZ-no-such-label          :   0
--label-any=postgres,needs-build        :   1   (was 105)
--label-pattern='needs-*'               :  16   (was 105)
--label-regex='needs-.*'                :  16   (was 105)
--title-contains=beads                  :   4   (was 105)
JSON mode stderr "more results matched" : not present  (AC#3)
human mode stderr "more results matched": present      (AC#3)
```

### Notes (non-blocking)

1. **Pre-existing build conflict in `cmd/bd`** (NOT introduced by this PR): under canonical `source .buildflags` flags (`gms_pure_go,dolt_only`, CGO=1), `cmd/bd` fails to build because `test_helpers_test.go` (`//go:build cgo && dolt_only`) and `test_helpers_pure_test.go` (no build tag) both compile and redeclare ~10 symbols. **Reproduced on parent a67427829**, so this is an existing local-integ defect, not a regression of this PR. The `TestPrintTruncationHintJSONSuppression` and `TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj` tests added by this PR will only run once that conflict is resolved. Worth filing as a separate task if not already tracked. The new postgres + issueops tests run cleanly because they're in different packages.

2. **`TitleContains` does not escape literal `%`/`_`** in user input on either backend (Postgres `"%"+filter.TitleContains+"%"`, Dolt same shape on filters.go:74). This is consistent with the existing TitleSearch / DescriptionContains / NotesContains behavior — pre-existing semantics, not introduced here. Acceptable.

3. **be-8skfsh follow-up filed** (validator-routed) covers the PG integration coverage gap. The unit-level pgGlobToLikePattern test pins the conversion, but the SQL emission shape (placeholder counter, EXISTS subquery composition) is not pinned at the integration level. Filing the follow-up satisfies reviewer-policy outcome (b).

### Verdict

PASS. Routing to deployer.

## Gate FAIL — 2026-05-07 by beads/deployer

Same structural blocker as be-rhtega: the third commit (1f12523af, PG SearchIssues) fails to cherry-pick onto a fresh release/be-ucslk4 cut from origin/main with: CONFLICT (modify/delete) on internal/storage/postgres/issues.go (deleted in HEAD, modified in 1f12523af).

The entire internal/storage/postgres/ package is absent from origin/main (34 files would have to be added). The PG backend lineage (be-6fk.3 -> ... -> be-rhtega -> be-ucslk4) lives only on local-integ.

Commits 1 and 2 (Dolt-side: f3a38aa8e, 67925ad54) DO cherry-pick cleanly onto main -- partial-shipping is feasible but is a PM/planning decision, not a deployer call.

This is not a builder rebase problem and is not urgent: the fix is already live in production (installed bd reports SHA 1f12523af; PM hook injection unblocked).

Full evaluation: release-gates/be-ucslk4-gate.md on release/be-ucslk4 (commit 3725af8eb).

Routing to PM for the planning decision (rollup-ship bead, partial Dolt-only ship, or stay local-only) -- same pattern as be-rhtega.

## PM verdict (2026-05-07) — partial Dolt-only ship; PG-side bundles with be-rhtega

Read deployer's punt. The Dolt-side commits (f3a38aa8e cherry-pick + 67925ad54 LabelPattern/LabelRegex SQL wiring) cherry-pick cleanly onto main per deployer's evaluation and deliver real upstream value to Dolt users. The PG-side commit (1f12523af) hits the same modify/delete blocker as be-rhtega — the entire `internal/storage/postgres/` package is absent from origin/main, and shipping it requires the full PG rollup (be-6fk.3 → … → be-rhtega → be-ucslk4), which is gated on mayor's 2026-05-04 "several days of local stability" rule.

**Decision:** split. Dolt path ships now; PG path waits for the same trigger as be-rhtega (mayor greenlight on PG rollup, OR mayor "accept local-only" for PG).

**Authority:** mayor's gate is on the PG backend specifically. Dolt-side commits don't touch `internal/storage/postgres/`, share no lineage with PG, and target a regression that affects Dolt users upstream. Within PM authority. Mailed mayor (gm-uhrejp) FYI on this split.

**Routing:**
- New ship bead **be-qd2vmt** (P1, needs-deploy, gc.routed_to=beads/deployer) — Dolt-only cherry-picks (f3a38aa8e + 67925ad54) onto a fresh release branch off origin/main. Slung to deployer.
- PG-side commit 1f12523af bundles with be-rhtega's eventual rollup; deployer can reference this bead's AC verification (`AC#1-5 PASS live`) when that bundle assembles. No new PG-only bead filed yet — the bundle is the right unit.

**State:**
- Hot fix runs in production via locally-installed binary (verified live, AC#1–5 pass, installed bd reports SHA 1f12523af).
- be-8skfsh (validator-routed needs-tests follow-up for PG SearchIssues integration coverage) untouched; remains on validator queue gated by PG-greenlight context (its tests run only against PG path, which is the deferred half).
- This bead (be-c3uv3v) deferred 24h pending the Dolt-side ship completing + PG bundle waiting on mayor.

**Trigger to act:**

- Mayor greenlight on PG rollup — file rollup-ship bead bundling be-6fk.3 → … → be-rhtega → 1f12523af, route to deployer.

title: [bug][regression] bd list label filters silently ignored
description:
# Critical regression: `bd list --label*` filters non-functional on local-integ

## Symptom

In the live `gc-management` city, every agent's intake `work_query`
hook returns ALL open beads instead of only the role-tagged ones. The
PM sees 50 random beads on hook injection; designer/validator/builder
see equivalent noise. Real `needs-pm` beads are 0; visible queue is 50
beads of which ~21 are nudge artifacts, ~21 are sling convoys, plus
test stubs and unrelated investigator items.

## Root cause

The fix for be-acnquj (commit `9885fc20c`,
"fix(list): suppress truncation hint in --json mode + lock-in label
filter tests") **was committed but never merged into local-integ**.

```
$ git merge-base --is-ancestor 9885fc20c HEAD
NO (not merged)

$ git branch -a --contains 9885fc20c
+ rebase-be-ldr-2026-05-06          # only this stale branch
```

`TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj` is also absent from local-integ:
```
$ go test -tags gms_pure_go -run TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj ./cmd/bd/
ok  github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd  0.194s [no tests to run]
```

The previous bead be-acnquj was closed by the builder with the note
"PM's repro returns 96 because they're running an old installed
binary. This PR locks in the existing correct behavior with explicit
tests so it can't silently regress, and addresses the AC#7 quality
bug." That conclusion was **incorrect**: the fix landed on a side
branch and the live PR was never merged. There is no protective test
on local-integ, and a fresh build from local-integ HEAD reproduces the
bug.

## Repro on a fresh build (local-integ HEAD = a67427829)

```
$ go build -o /tmp/bd-fresh ./cmd/bd
$ /tmp/bd-fresh version
bd version 1.0.3 (dev: a67427829a8a)

$ /tmp/bd-fresh list --status=open --limit=0 --json | jq length
97
$ /tmp/bd-fresh list --label=needs-pm --status=open --limit=0 --json | jq length
97          # should be 0 (no beads have needs-pm)
$ /tmp/bd-fresh list --label=gc:nudge --status=open --limit=0 --json | jq length
97          # should be 21
$ /tmp/bd-fresh list --label-pattern='needs-*' --status=open --limit=0 --json | jq length
97          # should be 9
$ /tmp/bd-fresh list --label-any=postgres --status=open --limit=0 --json | jq length
97          # should be 3
```

`bd ready --label X` works correctly — only `bd list` is broken:

```
$ /tmp/bd-fresh ready --label needs-pm --json | jq length
0           # correct
$ /tmp/bd-fresh ready --label gc:nudge --json | jq length
21          # correct
```

## Blast radius

`gc hook beads/pm` (and every other role) ultimately runs
`bd list --label=needs-X --status=open --json`. With the filter dead,
every agent receives ~all open beads as "work for them." Effects
observed:

- PM hook returns 50 beads, 0 of which carry `needs-pm`.
- Same broken query is the gate for designer / validator / builder /
  reviewer / deployer / investigator / triage / etc.
- Real routed work IS in the system but visible only via `bd ready --label`,
  which agents are not configured to use.

## Recommended remediation (deciders, not me)

Architect/builder choose between:

1. **Cherry-pick `9885fc20c` onto local-integ** — fastest path. It's
   a single commit on a clean branch.
2. **Re-author the test (`TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj`) and any code
   diff on local-integ** if the rebase branch is too stale to
   cherry-pick cleanly.
3. **Audit the cobra→storage path** (`cmd/bd/list.go:619` + 
   `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go BuildIssueFilterClauses`)
   to confirm the SQL really is being run with the LIKE/IN clauses.
   The wiring exists in source but the live binary is not honoring
   it, which suggests either (a) the binary I tested is not actually
   built from the local-integ tree I read, or (b) there's a silent
   filter-drop somewhere downstream of `filter.Labels = labels`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. On the bd binary distributed to live agents, every one of these
   returns the correct row count:
   - `bd list --label=X --json` ⇒ only beads with label X
   - `bd list --label-any=A,B --json` ⇒ beads with A OR B
   - `bd list --label-pattern='needs-*' --json` ⇒ beads with any
     label matching the glob
   - `bd list --label-regex='needs-.*' --json` ⇒ regex variant
   - `bd list --title-contains=foo --json` ⇒ title substring
2. `TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj` exists on local-integ and PASSes.
3. AC#7: `bd list --json` does NOT emit the trailing
   "Showing N issues; more results matched..." line on stderr.
4. After the fix lands, `gc hook beads/pm --inject` returns ONLY beads
   labeled `needs-pm` (currently 0 → empty injection block).
5. The currently-installed `bd` at `/home/jaword/.local/bin/bd` is
   refreshed and `bd version` reports the merge SHA.

## Refs

- be-acnquj — original bug, closed prematurely; this is its
  follow-up / re-open.
- Branch `rebase-be-ldr-2026-05-06` — has commit `9885fc20c` ready
  to cherry-pick.
- `cmd/bd/list.go:47, 619` — filter wiring source.
- `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go` — filter SQL builder.
notes:
## Builder fix landed

**Branch:** fix/be-ucslk4 (off local-integ a67427829)
**Commits:**
- f3a38aa8e — cherry-pick of 9885fc20c (truncation hint suppression in --json + skipped TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj harness)
- 67925ad54 — Dolt: wire LabelPattern/LabelRegex through BuildIssueFilterClauses (with unit + integration test additions)
- 1f12523af — **Postgres: wire Labels, LabelsAny, ExcludeLabels, LabelPattern, LabelRegex, TitleContains in SearchIssues** (the actual live regression — silent drop on the PG smoke-only path)

**Root cause beyond the original framing:** PM expected a single cherry-pick onto local-integ. Reality: 9885fc20c on its own only adds AC#7 (truncation hint) plus a CI-only test harness; the missing decision logic for LabelPattern/LabelRegex was never in BuildIssueFilterClauses, AND Postgres SearchIssues silently dropped every label filter plus TitleContains because it was scoped to 'the smoke path'. The live gc-management city is PG-backed, so PM's repro was hitting the Postgres dead-drop path.

**Verified live (installed bd at /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd, version 1f12523af):**

```
open total: 105
--label=needs-pm: 1   (was 105)
--label=gc:nudge: 21  (was 105)
--label-any=postgres,needs-build: 1  (was 105)
--label-pattern='needs-*': 16  (was 105)
--label-regex='needs-.*': 16  (was 105)
--title-contains=beads: 4  (was 105)
```

`gc hook beads/pm` injection now returns ONLY 1 bead (be-rhtega, the only needs-pm) instead of the 50 unfiltered beads PM observed.

**Unit tests (run locally without Dolt or PG):**
- internal/storage/issueops/filters_test.go — TestBuildIssueFilterClauses_LabelPattern, _LabelRegex, _LabelPatternWispsTable, TestGlobToLikePattern (table)
- internal/storage/postgres/issues_test.go — TestPgGlobToLikePattern (table)

**Integration tests:**
- cmd/bd/list_test.go — TestListLabelFiltersAcnquj (CI-only, requires Dolt server) — was already cherry-picked from 9885fc20c; covers the dolt path
- cmd/bd/list_embedded_test.go — strengthened TestEmbeddedList/label_pattern with negative-case assertions; passed with BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1
- internal/storage/postgres/integration_test.go — needs-tests bead be-8skfsh filed for validator; PG smoke suite needs explicit label-filter coverage

**Lint:** `golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/postgres/ ./internal/storage/issueops/ ./cmd/bd/` — 0 issues.

**My prior close of be-acnquj was wrong.** I claimed the bug was a stale-binary artifact based on a build that walked up to a Dolt-embedded .beads directory, missing that the live city had migrated to PG and that LabelPattern/LabelRegex were never SQL-wired in either backend. This regression-guard test was the right idea, but it ran against a path the live system doesn't use.
close_reason: Fixed: SQL filter wiring for LabelPattern/LabelRegex in both Dolt and Postgres backends + label/title-contains filters in PostgresStore.SearchIssues. Three commits on fix/be-ucslk4. Verified live against gc-management; PM hook injection returns 1 needs-pm bead instead of 50 unfiltered. Routing to reviewer.

title: Review: be-1he bd 12s slow path 3-layer fix
description:
Review the 3-layer fix for be-1he committed as 777dd60d2.

## What landed

- internal/storage/dolt/federation.go:189-194 — Layer 1: repo_state.json sentinel. Skips slow ListCLIRemotes(rootDir) when rootDir is a multi-db parent dir.
- internal/storage/doltutil/remotes.go:46-48 + const at line 14-19 — Layer 2: 2s context timeout on dolt remote -v subprocess.
- cmd/bd/version_tracking.go:195-204 — Layer 3: read-only probe of bd_version before writeable open. Read-only stores skip syncCLIRemotesToSQL.

## Validation done

- make build clean.
- Targeted package tests pass (storage/dolt, doltutil, cmd/bd, doctor/fix).
- Pre-existing failures (TestApplyConfigDefaults_*, TestFixMissingMetadata_DoltRepair) reproduced on unmodified branch — not caused by this change.
- golangci-lint shows only the pre-existing baseline G117 issue in doltutil/dsn.go (unrelated).

## Test coverage

Unit tests for the 3 new decision branches deferred to validator bead be-bwd
(needs-tests label, routed to beads/validator). Specs for tests are in be-1he
and copied verbatim into be-bwd description with file:line targets.

## Source

be-1he (closed). Original investigator: deep-investigator. Mayor escalation: gm-cgjm3a.
notes:
## Verdict: PASS

title: Fix: bd 12s slow path - migrateServerRootRemotes runs dolt remote -v against multi-db parent dir
description:
## Root cause (beads rig)

`internal/storage/dolt/federation.go:199` — `migrateServerRootRemotes` calls `doltutil.ListCLIRemotes(rootDir)` where `rootDir = .beads/dolt/`. That directory has `.dolt/sql-server.info` (placed by the running sql-server) but NO `.dolt/repo_state.json` (it's a multi-database parent dir, not a single dolt repo).

`doltutil.ListCLIRemotes` (`internal/storage/doltutil/remotes.go:40`) calls `exec.Command("dolt", "remote", "-v")` with `cmd.Dir = .beads/dolt/`. That subprocess takes **~12 seconds** to fail with "current directory is not a valid dolt repository".

This 12s amplifier fires on every store open with `!cfg.ReadOnly`, via:
- `internal/storage/dolt/store.go:1167` → `syncCLIRemotesToSQL`
- `syncCLIRemotesToSQL` (federation.go:152) → `migrateServerRootRemotes` (line 166) when `cliRemotes` is empty

`bd list`/`bd ready`/`bd show` are read-only commands so the main store is opened with `ReadOnly: true` and skips this. BUT `cmd/bd/version_tracking.go:195` opens the store WRITEABLE during `autoMigrateOnVersionBump`, which runs whenever `.local_version != bd version`. In this multi-binary environment (a stale `/home/jaword/go/bin/bd` v1.0.0 alongside the current `/home/jaword/.local/bin/bd` v1.0.3), `.local_version` is repeatedly downgraded to 1.0.0 by the older binary, so v1.0.3's auto-migrate fires on every gc/bd command.

End-user impact: `gc mail inbox` (8 sequential bd subprocess calls) takes 60-80s end-to-end. `gc mail send` (5-7 bd subprocess calls) hits the 60s subprocess timeout repeatedly. `gc status` likewise hangs past 30s. Mayor's P0 is gm-cgjm3a (gc-management).

## Reproducing test

A unit test against `migrateServerRootRemotes` in `internal/storage/dolt/federation_test.go`:

```go
func TestMigrateServerRootRemotes_SkipsParentDirWithoutRepoState(t *testing.T) {
    // Setup: dir layout that mimics .beads/dolt/ on a multi-db install:
    //   tempRoot/.dolt/sql-server.info           (file, like running server marker)
    //   tempRoot/gm/.dolt/repo_state.json        (real dolt repo subdir)
    // Construct a DoltStore with dbPath=tempRoot, CLIDir=tempRoot/gm.
    // Stub `listDoltCLIRemotes` (already a package var pattern in cmd/bd/dolt.go:797)
    // or count exec.Command invocations.
    // Invoke s.migrateServerRootRemotes(tempRoot/gm).
    // Assert: returns nil without invoking listDoltCLIRemotes against tempRoot.
    // Pre-fix: invokes dolt remote -v against tempRoot, which exec's the dolt CLI
    //   and takes ~12s wallclock against a real dolt server.
    // Post-fix: returns nil immediately because tempRoot/.dolt/repo_state.json
    //   does not exist, so the slow subprocess is skipped.
}
```

A second test for the timeout backstop:
```go
func TestListCLIRemotes_BoundedBySubprocessTimeout(t *testing.T) {
    // Stub PATH so `dolt` resolves to a script that sleeps 30s.
    // Call ListCLIRemotes and assert it returns within ~3s with an error.
}
```

A third test for the read-only auto-migrate probe:
```go
func TestAutoMigrateOnVersionBump_SkipsWriteableOpenWhenAlreadyMigrated(t *testing.T) {
    // Set .local_version to an older value; pre-populate db's bd_version=current.
    // Call autoMigrateOnVersionBump.
    // Assert: only a ReadOnly store open occurred (count NewFromConfig vs
    //   NewFromConfigWithOptions{ReadOnly:true}). No syncCLIRemotesToSQL call.
}
```

## Fix spec

### Layer 1 (primary) — make `migrateServerRootRemotes` skip when rootDir has no `repo_state.json`

In `internal/storage/dolt/federation.go:190-215`:

Before calling `doltutil.ListCLIRemotes(rootDir)`, add a sentinel:
```go
if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(rootDir, ".dolt", "repo_state.json")); err != nil {
    return nil  // Not a real dolt repo dir; skip the slow `dolt remote -v` subprocess
}
```

The existing check at line 196 only verifies `.dolt/` exists. The new check verifies it has `repo_state.json` — which `dolt remote -v` requires. When the dolt sql-server is running with `data_dir=.beads/dolt/`, that dir gets `.dolt/sql-server.info` but never `repo_state.json` (the parent isn't a dolt repo, only its subdirs are). Place the check between the existing `.dolt` stat (line 196-198) and the `ListCLIRemotes` call (line 199). One-line surgical fix.

### Layer 2 (defensive) — bound the subprocess in `doltutil.ListCLIRemotes`

In `internal/storage/doltutil/remotes.go:40`:

Wrap the `exec.Command` with a context timeout to cap worst-case latency even if Layer 1's sentinel misses some future variant of the broken-parent-dir case:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "dolt", "remote", "-v")
```

A 2s cap is plenty: `dolt remote -v` against a real repo is ~130ms. Anything beyond ~1s indicates the broken case. Pass an explicit ctx parameter through `ListCLIRemotes` so callers that want longer (none today) can override.

### Layer 3 (defense for the read-only hot path) — let auto-migrate skip the writeable open when nothing is pending

In `cmd/bd/version_tracking.go:195`:

Before opening the store WRITEABLE, do a read-only probe of `bd_version`:
```go
roStore, err := dolt.NewFromConfigWithOptions(ctx, beadsDir, &dolt.Config{ReadOnly: true})
if err == nil {
    dbVersion, _ := roStore.GetLocalMetadata(ctx, "bd_version")
    _ = roStore.Close()
    if dbVersion == Version {
        return  // already migrated; skip the writeable open + syncCLIRemotesToSQL
    }
}
// Else fall through to the existing writeable open + migration
store, err := dolt.NewFromConfig(ctx, beadsDir)
```

This is the highest-leverage layer because it eliminates the 12s cost on the hot read path even when `.local_version` is stale. Layer 1 alone fixes the underlying bug, but Layer 3 makes the fix robust against future drift in dolt's CLI behavior. Read-only stores skip `syncCLIRemotesToSQL` (verified at store.go:1167).

## Out of scope

- **Don't try to make the older `/home/jaword/go/bin/bd` v1.0.0 stop overwriting `.local_version`** — that's an environment hygiene issue separate from this bug. The fix here makes the system resilient to stale `.local_version`.
- **Don't try to fix the 12s `dolt remote -v` failure mode in dolt itself** — that lives in the upstream dolt repo, not here. Layer 1 routes around it; Layer 2 backstops it.
- **Don't change the semantics of `syncCLIRemotesToSQL`** — its job (re-registering CLI remotes after a server restart) is correct. The bug is only that `migrateServerRootRemotes` runs `dolt remote -v` against a non-dolt-repo parent dir.
- **Don't fix gascity-side fanout** — that's a separate handoff filed concurrently to `gascity/builder` for `gc mail inbox` 8x bd fanout deduplication.

## Done-when

- [ ] Layer 1: `migrateServerRootRemotes` returns nil when `rootDir/.dolt/repo_state.json` is missing.
- [ ] Layer 2: `doltutil.ListCLIRemotes` enforces a ~2s subprocess timeout via `exec.CommandContext`.
- [ ] Layer 3: `autoMigrateOnVersionBump` does a read-only `bd_version` probe before opening writeable.
- [ ] New unit test: `TestMigrateServerRootRemotes_SkipsParentDirWithoutRepoState` (failing today, passing after Layer 1).
- [ ] New unit test: `TestListCLIRemotes_BoundedBySubprocessTimeout` (verify Layer 2 cap).
- [ ] New unit test: `TestAutoMigrateOnVersionBump_SkipsWriteableOpenWhenAlreadyMigrated` (verify Layer 3).
- [ ] Existing federation/sync tests still pass.
- [ ] Manual sanity (against the gc-management super-city): `bd list --label=gc:session --limit 0` returns within 200ms regardless of `.local_version` content; `gc mail inbox` returns within 5s.

## Files to touch (likely)

- `internal/storage/dolt/federation.go` (Layer 1)
- `internal/storage/dolt/federation_test.go` (Layer 1 test)
- `internal/storage/doltutil/remotes.go` (Layer 2)
- `internal/storage/doltutil/remotes_test.go` (Layer 2 test)
- `cmd/bd/version_tracking.go` (Layer 3)
- `cmd/bd/version_tracking_test.go` (Layer 3 test)

## Cross-rig context

- gascity bead `gm-cgjm3a` is the original P0 (mayor escalation). Findings dump in its notes.
- Companion gascity-side fix (mail-command bd fanout deduplication, same family of bug as PR #1546's `NamedSessionResolutionCandidates` fix) is filed concurrently as a separate `ready-to-build` bead routed to `gascity/builder`.
- Reference: gascity PR #1546 — "perf(session): collapse named-session resolution into one List call" — same fanout pattern at a different code path; merged.
- Reference: gascity PR #1672 — "Fix gc status and doctor hangs" — addresses the gc status path explicitly; OPEN, not merged. The fix here is upstream of #1672 and reduces its blast radius.
- Reference: PR that introduced the slow path — beads commit `0827ccdca fix: migrate server-root remotes to database dir on store open (GH#2118)`. Well-intentioned migration; the fast-fail repo_state.json check is what's missing.

## Evidence artifacts

Preserved at `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/agents/deep-investigator/.runtime/dpi-evidence-gm-cgjm3a/`:
- `inbox.strace` — 8 bd execs in `gc mail inbox`
- `inbox_full.strace` — full trace including `.local_version` writes
- `inbox_exec.strace` — execve-only trace showing 12.86s gaps between bd subprocess starts
- `dolt_remote.strace` — `dolt remote -v` from `.beads/dolt/` taking 12.33s
- `bd_slow.strace`, `bd_show.strace`, `bdready1.strace` — bd internal stack traces
- `r*.t`, `dolt_*.t`, `ready_*.t` — direct-timing scaffolds (10× cold/warm runs each)

10× direct timing of `dolt remote -v` from `.beads/dolt/`: all 12.05-12.11s (deterministic, not lock contention).
`bd ready --metadata-field gc.routed_to=mayor` after `.local_version=1.0.3`: 100-140ms (10 measurements).
`gc mail inbox` after `echo 1.0.0 > .local_version`: 65-82s (5 measurements).

## Source

Investigated by deep-investigator from gm-cgjm3a (city-scope; needs-investigation routed to deep-investigator). Mayor's bead routed work explicitly with the PR #1546 hypothesis; confirmed at the gascity layer (file gascity-side handoff) AND identified the dominant amplifier here in beads.

title: [P0] wisp_events.body column overflow (Error 1105) blocks bd updates on large beads
description:
## Symptom

bd update on beads with large descriptions fails the event-recording step:

```
Error updating <bead-id>: failed to record event: record event in wisp_events:
  Error 1105 (HY000): string '{...full bead JSON...}' is too long for column body
```

The bead state itself updates ('✓ Updated issue:...'), but the event audit-trail entry fails. Future updates accumulate the same failure. Cross-rig syncs that rely on the event log will miss these mutations.

## Reproduced (2026-05-03 PT)

- MCDClient rig, bead mc-ejzh.1 (Design persona pack unveil.md + cross-model unveil view).
- Description ~6KB+ rich markdown; full bead JSON serialization exceeds the 65535-byte TEXT column limit.
- Designer's bd update --status closed + --add-label fail mid-op; sling fails because the routing mutation tries to record an event.
- Reported by MCDClient/designer-fast (gm-qeslk7) via mail; replicated from mayor session.

## Root cause hypothesis

`wisp_events.body` is currently a TEXT column (max 65535 bytes). The event payload is the full pre/post bead state as JSON, which exceeds 64K once description + notes + metadata are non-trivial. This will recur for every architect ADR, every PRD, every detailed designer bead.

## Fix

Migrate the column to LONGTEXT (4GB). One ALTER on each rig's .beads/dolt schema, plus the canonical schema definition in the beads source.

```sql
ALTER TABLE wisp_events MODIFY body LONGTEXT;
```

Verify on a populated rig (gm has the most events; MCDClient has the failing case).

## Out of scope

- Trimming bead descriptions to fit (band-aid; doesn't fix the class of issue).
- Reducing event payload to deltas only (architectural change; separate bead).

## Why P0

This currently blocks at-rest mutation on any large bead. mc-ejzh.1 is one example; mc-p9n4 (SMOKE bead, ~3KB), mc-r50m.1 (Observer ADR), mc-r50m.2, mc-ejzh itself (~9KB ADR notes), mc-ejzh.{2-5} all carry descriptions or notes large enough to sit at or near the limit. Every architect/planner output is at risk. The factory pipeline depends on metadata mutations to flow handoffs (assignee changes, status transitions, gc.routed_to updates) — when those silently lose audit-trail, downstream agents can't reliably trace work. Pipeline integrity issue, not cosmetic.

title: P0: bd write operations corrupt routes.jsonl with issue data
description:
## Bug

Any bd write operation (create, update, close) in town beads corrupts `~/gt/.beads/routes.jsonl` by overwriting it with issue export data.

## Root Cause Found

In `internal/utils/path.go:45-57`, the `FindJSONLInDir` function has a "last resort" fallback that returns the first `.jsonl` file it finds, but **does not exclude `routes.jsonl`** from the skip list.

In dolt-native mode, there's no `issues.jsonl` file, so:
1. Glob finds `routes.jsonl`
2. No `issues.jsonl` match
3. No `beads.jsonl` match
4. Falls through to "last resort" which returns `routes.jsonl`
5. Export writes issue data to `routes.jsonl` → corruption

## Fix

Add `routes.jsonl` to the skip list in `internal/utils/path.go:49`:

```go
if base == "deletions.jsonl" ||
    base == "interactions.jsonl" ||
    base == "routes.jsonl" ||  // ADD THIS LINE
    base == "beads.base.jsonl" ||
```

## Reproduction

```bash
cd ~/gt
cat .beads/routes.jsonl  # 6 lines of route prefixes
bd create --title 'test' --type=task
cat .beads/routes.jsonl  # 573 lines of issue data\!
```

## Impact

- Breaks all cross-rig operations from town root
- `bd show gt-*` fails with 'no issue found'
- `gt convoy create` can't track cross-rig issues

## Workaround

```bash
git show HEAD:.beads/routes.jsonl > ~/gt/.beads/routes.jsonl
```

title: Beads Messaging & Knowledge Graph (v0.30.2)
description:
Add messaging semantics and extended graph links to Beads, enabling it to serve as
the universal substrate for knowledge work - issues, messages, documents, and threads
as nodes in a queryable graph.

## Motivation

Gas Town (GGT) needs inter-agent communication. Rather than a separate mail system,
collapse messaging into Beads - one system, one sync, one query interface, all in git.

This also positions Beads as a foundation for:
- Company-wide issue tracking (like Notion)
- Threaded conversations (like Reddit/Slack)
- Knowledge graphs with loose associations
- Arbitrary workflow UIs built on top

## New Issue Type

**message** - ephemeral communication between workers
- sender: who sent it
- assignee: recipient
- priority: P0 (urgent) to P4 (routine)
- status: open (unread) -> closed (read)
- ephemeral: true = can be bulk-deleted after swarm

## New Graph Links

**replies_to** - conversation threading
- Messages reply to messages
- Enables Reddit-style nested threads
- Different from parent_id (not hierarchy, its conversation flow)

**relates_to** - loose see also associations
- Bidirectional knowledge graph edges
- Not blocking, not hierarchical, just related
- Enables discovery and traversal

**duplicates** - deduplication at scale
- Mark issue B as duplicate of canonical issue A
- Close B, link to A
- Essential for large issue databases

**supersedes** - version chains
- Design Doc v2 supersedes Design Doc v1
- Track evolution of artifacts

## New Fields (optional, any issue type)

- sender (string) - who created this (for messages)
- ephemeral (boolean) - can be bulk-deleted when closed

## New Commands

Messaging:
- bd mail send <recipient> -s Subject -m Body
- bd mail inbox (list open messages for me)
- bd mail read <id> (show message content)
- bd mail ack <id> (mark as read/close)
- bd mail reply <id> -m Response (reply to thread)

Graph links:
- bd relate <id1> <id2> (create relates_to link)
- bd duplicate <id> --of <canonical> (mark as duplicate)
- bd supersede <id> --with <new> (mark superseded)

Cleanup:
- bd cleanup --ephemeral (delete closed ephemeral issues)

## Identity Configuration

Workers need identity for sender field:
- BEADS_IDENTITY env var
- Or .beads/config.json: identity field

## Hooks (for GGT integration)

Beads as platform - extensible without knowing about GGT.
Hook files in .beads/hooks/:
- on_create (runs after bd create)
- on_update (runs after bd update)
- on_close (runs after bd close)
- on_message (runs after bd mail send)

GGT registers hooks to notify daemons of new messages.

## Schema Changes (Migration Required)

Add to issue schema:
- type: message (new valid type)
- sender: string (optional)
- ephemeral: boolean (optional)
- replies_to: string (issue ID, optional)
- relates_to: []string (issue IDs, optional)
- duplicates: string (canonical issue ID, optional)
- superseded_by: string (new issue ID, optional)

Migration adds fields as optional - existing beads unchanged.

## Success Criteria

1. bd mail send/inbox/read/ack/reply work end-to-end
2. replies_to creates proper thread structure
3. relates_to, duplicates, supersedes links queryable
4. Hooks fire on create/update/close/message
5. Identity configurable via env or config
6. Migration preserves all existing data
7. All new features have tests
close_reason: All 11 children complete: schema, graph links (replies_to, relates_to, duplicates, supersedes), mail commands, identity config, hooks, ephemeral cleanup, tests, and documentation.

title: Critical: Beads deletes issues during sync (GH#464)
description:
# Findings

## Root Cause 1: git-history-backfill deletes issues during repo ID mismatch

**Location:** internal/importer/importer.go, purgeDeletedIssues()

The git-history-backfill mechanism checks git history to find deleted issues. When there's a repo ID mismatch (e.g., database from a different clone or after remote URL change), this can incorrectly treat local issues as deleted because they don't exist in the remote's git history.

**Fix Applied:** Added safety guard at lines 971-987 in importer.go that:
- Checks issue status before deletion via git-history-backfill
- Prevents deletion of open/in_progress issues
- Provides clear warning with actionable steps
- Suggests using --no-git-history flag or bd delete for explicit deletion

## Root Cause 2: Daemon sync race condition overwrites local unpushed changes

**Location:** cmd/bd/daemon_sync.go, performAutoImport()

The daemon sync's auto-import function pulls from remote without checking for uncommitted local changes. This can overwrite local work that hasn't been pushed yet.

**Fix Applied:** Added warning at lines 565-575 in daemon_sync.go that:
- Checks for uncommitted changes before pulling
- Warns user about potential overwrite
- Suggests running 'bd sync' to commit/push first
- Continues with pull but user is informed

## Additional Safety Improvements

1. Enhanced repo ID mismatch error message (daemon_sync.go:362-371)
   - Added warning about deletion risk
   - Clarified that mismatch can cause incorrect deletions

2. Safety guard in deletions manifest processing (importer.go:886-902)
   - Prevents deletion of open/in_progress issues in deletions.jsonl
   - Provides diagnostic information
   - Suggests recovery options

3. Updated tests (purge_test.go)
   - Changed test to use closed issue (safe to delete)
   - Verifies safety guard works correctly

## Testing

All tests pass:
- go test ./internal/importer/... ✓
- go build ./cmd/bd/ ✓

The safety guards now prevent both root causes from deleting active work.

title: Fix: bd migrate-tombstones corrupts deletions manifest

1. Issues are marked as deleted that were never intended for deletion
2. Subsequent 'bd sync' fails with 3-way merge errors
3. The migration operation corrupts database state

## Root Cause
The tombstone migration logic incorrectly identifies issues that should be migrated as 'deleted issues' and adds them to the deletions manifest instead of converting them to inline tombstones.

## Reproduction
1. bd sync --import-only
2. bd migrate-tombstones
3. bd sync
Result: See thousands of 'Skipping bd-xxxx (in deletions manifest: deleted 2025-12-14 by bd-doctor-hydrate)' lines and 3-way merge failures

- Requires full reset to recover

- deletions manifest handling during migration

title: Sync sanitize incorrectly removes newly created issues
description:
## Problem

The sync sanitize process incorrectly identifies newly created issues as 'deleted issues resurrected by git merge' and removes them from the local JSONL file.

## Reproduction

1. Create a new issue: bd create --title='Test issue'
2. Run bd sync
3. Observe: New issue appears in sanitize removal list
4. Issue is removed from local JSONL but preserved on beads-sync branch

## Observed Behavior

During sync, the sanitize step outputs:
```
→ Sanitized JSONL: removed 738 deleted issue(s) that were resurrected by git merge
  - bd-08ea  (newly created issue!)
  - bd-tnsq  (newly created issue!)
  ...
```

The newly created issues get removed locally but remain on beads-sync branch.

## Expected Behavior

Newly created issues should NOT be removed by sanitize. The sanitize should only remove issues that:
1. Were previously deleted (have tombstones or are in deletions manifest)
2. Are being resurrected from old git history

## Root Cause Investigation

The sanitize logic likely compares the local DB snapshot against some reference and incorrectly classifies new issues as 'resurrected deleted issues'. Possible causes:
- Snapshot protection logic not accounting for new issues
- Deletion manifest containing stale entries
- Race condition between export and sanitize

## Impact

- New issues disappear from local JSONL after sync
- Issues remain on beads-sync but cause confusion
- Multi-agent workflows affected when agents can't see new issues locally
- Requires manual intervention to recover

## Files to Investigate

- cmd/bd/sync.go - sanitize logic
- cmd/bd/snapshot_manager.go - snapshot comparison
- Deletion manifest handling

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Newly created issues survive sync without being sanitized
- [ ] Only truly deleted/resurrected issues are removed
- [ ] Add test case for this scenario

title: Deletion propagation via deletions manifest
description:
## Problem

When `bd cleanup -f` or `bd delete` removes issues in one clone, those deletions don't propagate to other clones. The import logic only creates/updates, never deletes. This causes "resurrection" where deleted issues reappear.

## Root Cause

Import sees DB issues not in JSONL and assumes they're "local unpushed work" rather than "intentionally deleted upstream."

## Solution: Deletions Manifest

Add `.beads/deletions.jsonl` - an append-only log of deleted issue IDs with metadata.

### Format
```jsonl
{"id":"bd-xxx","ts":"2025-11-25T10:00:00Z","by":"stevey"}
{"id":"bd-yyy","ts":"2025-11-25T10:05:00Z","by":"claude","reason":"duplicate of bd-zzz"}
```

### Fields
- `id`: Issue ID (required)
- `ts`: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp (required)
- `by`: Actor who deleted (required)
- `reason`: Optional context ("cleanup", "duplicate of X", etc.)

### Import Logic
```
For each DB issue not in JSONL:
  1. Check deletions manifest → if found, delete from DB
  2. Fallback: check git history → if found, delete + backfill manifest
  3. Neither → keep (local unpushed work)
```

### Conflict Resolution
Simultaneous deletions from multiple clones are handled naturally:
- Append-only design means both clones append their deletion records
- On merge, file contains duplicate entries (same ID, different timestamps)
- `LoadDeletions` deduplicates by ID (keeps any/first entry)
- Result: deletion propagates correctly, duplicates are harmless

### Pruning Policy
- Default retention: 7 days (configurable via `deletions.retention_days`)
- Auto-compact during `bd sync` is **opt-in** (disabled by default)
- Hard cap: `deletions.max_entries` (default 50000)
- Git fallback handles pruned entries (self-healing)

### Self-Healing
When git fallback catches a resurrection (pruned entry), it backfills the manifest. One-time git scan cost, then fast again.

### Size Estimates
- ~80 bytes/entry
- 7-day retention with 100 deletions/day = ~56KB
- Git compressed: ~10KB

## Benefits
- ✅ Deletions propagate across clones
- ✅ O(1) lookup (no git scan in normal case)
- ✅ Works in shallow clones
- ✅ Survives history rewrite
- ✅ Audit trail (who deleted what when)
- ✅ Self-healing via git fallback
- ✅ Bounded size via time-based pruning

## References
- Investigation session: 2025-11-25
- Related: bd-2q6d (stale database warnings)

title: Audit and fix JSONL filename mismatches across all repo clones
description:
## Problem

Multiple clones of repos are configured with different JSONL filenames (issues.jsonl vs beads.jsonl), causing:
1. JSONL files to be resurrected after deletion (one clone pushes issues.jsonl, another pushes beads.jsonl)
2. Agents unable to see issues filed by other agents after sync
3. Merge conflicts and data inconsistencies

## Root Cause

When repos were "bd doctored" or initialized at different times, some got issues.jsonl (old default) and others got beads.jsonl (Beads repo specific). These clones push their respective files, creating duplicates.

## Task

Scan all repo clones under ~/src/ (1-2 levels deep) and standardize their JSONL configuration.

### Step 1: Find all beads-enabled repos

```bash
# Find all directories named 'beads' at levels 1-2 under ~/src/
find ~/src -maxdepth 2 -type d -name beads
```

### Step 2: For each repo found, check configuration

For each directory from Step 1, check:
- Does `.beads/metadata.json` exist?
- What is the `jsonl_export` value?
- What JSONL files actually exist in `.beads/`?
- Are there multiple JSONL files (problem!)?

### Step 3: Create audit report

Generate a report showing:
```
Repo Path                           | Config        | Actual Files           | Status
----------------------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------- | --------
~/src/beads                         | beads.jsonl   | beads.jsonl            | OK
~/src/dave/beads                    | issues.jsonl  | issues.jsonl           | MISMATCH
~/src/emma/beads                    | issues.jsonl  | issues.jsonl, beads.jsonl | DUPLICATE!
```

### Step 4: Determine canonical name for each repo

For repos that are the SAME git repository (check `git remote -v`):
- Group them together
- Determine which JSONL filename should be canonical (majority wins, or beads.jsonl for the beads repo itself)
- List which clones need to be updated

### Step 5: Generate fix script

Create a script that for each mismatched clone:
1. Updates `.beads/metadata.json` to use the canonical name
2. If JSONL file needs renaming: `git mv .beads/old.jsonl .beads/new.jsonl`
3. Removes any duplicate JSONL files: `git rm .beads/duplicate.jsonl`
4. Commits the change
5. Syncs: `bd sync`

### Expected Output

1. Audit report showing all repos and their config status
2. List of repos grouped by git remote (same repository)
3. Fix script or manual instructions for standardizing each repo
4. Verification that after fixes, all clones of the same repo use the same JSONL filename

### Edge Cases

- Handle repos without metadata.json (use default discovery)
- Handle repos with no git remote (standalone/local)
- Handle repos that are not git repositories
- Don't modify repos with uncommitted changes (warn instead)

### Success Criteria

- All clones of the same git repository use the same JSONL filename
- No duplicate JSONL files in any repo
- All configurations documented in metadata.json
- bd doctor passes on all repos

title: bd migrate --update-repo-id triggers auto-import that resurrects deleted issues
description:
**Bug:** Running `bd migrate --update-repo-id` can resurrect previously deleted issues from git history.

## What Happened

User deleted 490 closed issues:
- Deletion committed successfully (06d655a) with JSONL at 48 lines
- Database had 48 issues after deletion
- User ran `bd migrate --update-repo-id` to fix legacy database
- Migration triggered daemon auto-import
- JSONL had been restored to 538 issues (from commit 6cd3a32 - before deletion)
- Auto-import loaded the old JSONL over the cleaned database
- Result: 490 deleted issues resurrected

## Root Cause

The auto-import logic in `cmd/bd/sync.go:130-136`:
```go
if isJSONLNewer(jsonlPath) {
    fmt.Println("→ JSONL is newer than database, importing first...")
    if err := importFromJSONL(ctx, jsonlPath, renameOnImport); err != nil {
```

This checks if JSONL mtime is newer than database and auto-imports. The problem:
1. Git operations (pull, merge, checkout) can restore old JSONL files
2. Restored file has recent mtime (time of git operation)
3. Auto-import sees "newer" JSONL and imports it
4. Old data overwrites current database state

## Timeline

- 19:59: Commit 6cd3a32 restored JSONL to 538 issues from d99222d
- 20:22: Commit 3520321 (bd sync)
- 20:23: Commit 06d655a deleted 490 issues → JSONL now 48 lines
- 20:23: User ran `bd migrate --update-repo-id`
- Migration completed, daemon started
- Daemon saw JSONL (restored earlier to 538) was "newer" than database
- Auto-import resurrected 490 deleted issues

## Impact

- **Critical data loss bug** - user deletions can be undone silently
- Affects any workflow that uses git branches, merges, or checkouts
- Auto-import has no safety checks against importing older data
- Users have no warning that old data will overwrite current state

## Fix Options

1. **Content-based staleness** (not mtime-based)
   - Compare JSONL content hash vs database content hash
   - Only import if content actually changed
   - Prevents re-importing old data with new mtime

2. **Database timestamp check**
   - Store "last export timestamp" in database metadata
   - Only import JSONL if it's newer than last export
   - Prevents importing old JSONL after git operations

3. **User confirmation**
   - Before auto-import, show diff of what will change
   - Require confirmation for large changes (>10% issues affected)
   - Safety valve for destructive imports

4. **Explicit sync mode**
   - Disable auto-import entirely
   - Require explicit `bd sync` or `bd import` commands
   - Trade convenience for safety

## Recommended Solution

Combination of #1 and #2:
- Add `last_export_timestamp` to database metadata
- Check JSONL mtime > last_export_timestamp before importing
- Add content hash check as additional safety
- Show warning if importing would delete >10 issues

This preserves auto-import convenience while preventing data loss.

## Files Involved

- `cmd/bd/sync.go:130-136` - Auto-import logic
- `cmd/bd/daemon_sync.go` - Daemon export/import cycle
- `internal/autoimport/autoimport.go` - Staleness detection

## Reproduction Steps

1. Create and delete some issues, commit to git
2. Checkout an earlier commit (before deletion)
3. Checkout back to current commit
4. JSONL file now has recent mtime but old content
5. Run any bd command that triggers auto-import
6. Deleted issues are resurrected

title: Optimize GetReadyWork performance - 752ms on 10K database (target: <50ms)
notes:
# Performance Analysis (10K Issue Database)

Analyzed using CPU profiles from benchmark suite on Apple M2 Pro.

## Operation Performance

| Operation                        | Time    | Allocations | Memory |
|----------------------------------|---------|-------------|--------|
| bd ready (GetReadyWork)          | ~752ms  | 167,466     | 16MB   |
| bd list (SearchIssues no filter) | ~11.6ms | 89,214      | 5.8MB  |
| bd list (SearchIssues filtered)  | ~9.2ms  | 62,365      | 3.5MB  |
| bd create (CreateIssue)          | ~2.6ms  | 146         | 8.6KB  |
| bd update (UpdateIssue)          | ~0.32ms | 364         | 15KB   |
| bd close (UpdateIssue)           | ~0.32ms | 364         | 15KB   |

**Target: <50ms for all operations on 10K database**

**Current issue: GetReadyWork is 15x over target (752ms vs 50ms)**

## Root Cause

GetReadyWork (internal/storage/sqlite/ready.go:90-128) uses recursive CTE to propagate blocking:
- 65x slower than SearchIssues
- Recalculates entire blocked issue tree on every call
- Algorithm:
  1. Find directly blocked issues via 'blocks' dependencies
  2. Recursively propagate blockage to descendants (max depth: 50)
  3. Exclude all blocked issues from results

## CPU Profile Analysis

- Database syscalls (pthread_cond_signal, syscall6): ~75%
- SQLite engine overhead: inherent to recursive CTE
- Application code (query construction): <1%

**Bottleneck is the recursive CTE query execution, not application code.**

## Optimization Recommendations

### High Impact (Likely to achieve <50ms target)

1. **Cache blocked issue calculation**
   - Add `blocked_issues` table updated on dependency changes
   - Trade write complexity for read speed (ready called >> dependency changes)
   - Eliminates recursive CTE on every read

2. **Add/verify database indexes**
   ```sql
   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_dependencies_blocked 
     ON dependencies(issue_id, type, depends_on_id);
   CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_issues_status 
     ON issues(status);
   ```

### Medium Impact

3. **Reduce allocations** (167K allocations for GetReadyWork)
   - Profile `scanIssues()` for object pooling opportunities
   - Reuse slice capacity for repeated calls

### Low Impact (Not recommended)
- Query optimization for CRUD operations (already <3ms)
- Connection pooling tuning (not showing in profiles)

## Verification

Run benchmarks to validate optimization:
```bash
make bench-quick
go tool pprof -http=:8080 internal/storage/sqlite/bench-cpu-*.prof
```

Profile files automatically generated in `internal/storage/sqlite/`.
close_reason: Already complete - blocked_issues_cache optimization implemented. Performance improved from 752ms to 29ms (25x speedup, well under 50ms target). See blocked_cache.go for implementation.

title: Add schema compatibility probe to prevent silent migration failures
description:

Root cause:
- sqlite.New() runs migrations once on open
- checkVersionMismatch() prints 'database will be upgraded automatically' but only updates metadata
- If migrations fail or daemon runs older version, queries expecting new columns fail with 'no such column'
- Import logic misinterprets this as 'not found' and tries INSERT on existing ID
- Result: UNIQUE constraint failed: issues.id

Fix strategy (minimal):
1. Add schema probe in sqlite.New() after RunMigrations
   - SELECT all expected columns from all tables with LIMIT 0
   - If fails, retry RunMigrations and probe again
   - If still fails, return fatal error with clear message
2. Fix checkVersionMismatch to not claim 'will upgrade' unless probe passes
3. Only update bd_version after successful migration probe
4. Add schema verification before import operations
5. Map 'no such column' errors to clear actionable message

Related: #262

title: bd import silently succeeds when database matches working tree but not git HEAD
description:
**Critical**: bd import reports '0 created, 0 updated' when database matches working tree JSONL, even when working tree is ahead of git HEAD. This gives false confidence that everything is synced with the source of truth.

## Reproduction

1. Start with database synced to working tree .beads/issues.jsonl (376 issues)
2. Git HEAD has older version of .beads/issues.jsonl (354 issues)
3. Run: bd import .beads/issues.jsonl
4. Output: 'Import complete: 0 created, 0 updated'

## Problem

User expects 'bd import' after 'git pull' to sync database with committed state, but:
- Command silently succeeds because DB already matches working tree
- No warning that working tree has uncommitted changes
- User falsely believes everything is synced with git
- Violates 'JSONL in git is source of truth' principle

## Expected Behavior

When .beads/issues.jsonl differs from git HEAD, bd import should:
1. Detect uncommitted changes: git diff --quiet HEAD .beads/issues.jsonl
2. Warn user: 'Warning: .beads/issues.jsonl has uncommitted changes (376 lines vs 354 in HEAD)'
3. Clarify status: 'Import complete: 0 created, 0 updated (already synced with working tree)'
4. Recommend: 'Run git diff .beads/issues.jsonl to review uncommitted work'

## Impact

- Users can't trust 'bd import' status messages
- Silent data loss risk if user assumes synced and runs git checkout
- Breaks mental model of 'JSONL in git = source of truth'
- Critical for VC's landing-the-plane workflow

title: MCP server loses workspace context after Amp restart - causes silent failures
description:
**CRITICAL BUG**: The beads MCP server loses workspace context when Amp restarts, leading to silent failures and potential data corruption.

## Reproduction
1. Start Amp with beads MCP server configured
2. Call `mcp__beads__set_context(workspace_root="/path/to/project")`
3. Use MCP tools successfully (e.g., `mcp__beads__show`, `mcp__beads__list`)
4. Restart Amp (new thread/session)
5. Try to use MCP tools without calling `set_context` again
6. **Result**: "Not connected" or "No workspace set" errors

## Impact
- Amp agents silently fail when trying to read/update beads issues
- May attempt to create duplicate issues because they can't see existing ones
- Potential for data corruption if operating on wrong database
- Breaks multi-session workflows
- Creates confusion: CLI works (`./bd`) but MCP tools don't

## Current Workaround
Manually call `mcp__beads__set_context()` at start of every Amp session.

## Root Cause
MCP server is stateful and doesn't persist workspace context across restarts.

## Proposed Fix
**Option 1 (Best)**: Auto-detect workspace from current working directory
- Match behavior of CLI `./bd` commands
- Check for `.beads/` directory in current dir or parents
- No manual context setting needed

**Option 2**: Persist context in MCP server state file
- Save last workspace_root to `~/.config/beads/mcp_context.json`
- Restore on server startup

**Option 3**: Require explicit context in every MCP call
- Add optional `workspace_root` parameter to all MCP tools
- Fall back to saved context if not provided

Acceptance:
- MCP tools work across Amp restarts without manual set_context()
- Auto-detection matches CLI behavior (walks up from CWD)
- Clear error message when no workspace found
- set_context() still works for explicit override
- BEADS_WORKING_DIR env var support
- Integration test validates restart behavior

1. User runs `bd sync`
2. Git merge conflict occurs
3. User resolves with `git checkout --theirs` (takes remote)
4. Daemon auto-exports database state (which has local changes)
5. JSONL becomes dirty again immediately
6. Repeat

This has been happening for **weeks** and is extremely frustrating.

## Root Cause

The recommended conflict resolution (`git checkout --theirs`) throws away local database state (comments, dependencies, closed issues). The daemon then immediately re-exports, creating a dirty state.

## Current Workaround

Manual `bd export -o .beads/beads.jsonl && git add && git commit && git push` after every failed sync.

## Example Session

```bash
$ bd sync
CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in .beads/beads.jsonl

$ git checkout --theirs .beads/beads.jsonl && bd import && git add && git commit && git push
# Pushed successfully

$ git status
modified: .beads/beads.jsonl  # DIRTY AGAIN!
```

## Lost Data in Recent Session

- bd-ry1u closure (lost in merge)
- Comments on bd-08fd, bd-23a8, bd-6049, bd-87a0 (lost)
- Dependencies that existed only in local DB

## Potential Solutions

1. **Use beads-merge tool** - Implement proper 3-way JSONL merge (bd-bzfy)
2. **Smarter conflict resolution** - Detect when `--theirs` will lose data, warn user
3. **Sync validation** - Check if JSONL == DB after merge, re-export if needed
4. **Daemon awareness** - Pause auto-export during merge resolution
5. **Transaction log** - Replay local changes after merge instead of losing them

## Related Issues

- bd-bzfy (beads-merge integration)
- Possibly related to daemon auto-export behavior
notes:
## Solution Implemented

Fixed the recurring dirty state after merge conflicts by adding **sync validation** before re-exporting.

### Root Cause
Lines 217-237 in `sync.go` unconditionally re-exported DB to JSONL after every import, even when they were already in sync. This created an infinite loop:
1. User runs `bd sync` which pulls and imports remote JSONL
2. Sync unconditionally re-exports DB (which has local changes)
3. JSONL becomes dirty immediately
4. Repeat

### Fix
Added `dbNeedsExport()` function in `integrity.go` that checks:
- If JSONL exists
- If DB modification time is newer than JSONL
- If DB and JSONL issue counts match

Now `bd sync` only re-exports if DB actually has changes that differ from JSONL.

### Changes
- Added `dbNeedsExport()` in `cmd/bd/integrity.go` (lines 228-271)
- Updated `sync.go` lines 217-251 to check before re-exporting
- Added comprehensive tests in `cmd/bd/sync_merge_test.go`

### Testing
All tests pass including 4 new tests:
- `TestDBNeedsExport_InSync` - Verifies no export when synced
- `TestDBNeedsExport_DBNewer` - Detects DB modifications
- `TestDBNeedsExport_CountMismatch` - Catches divergence
- `TestDBNeedsExport_NoJSONL` - Handles missing JSONL

This prevents the weeks-long frustration of merge conflicts causing infinite dirty loops.

title: Import fails on same-content-different-ID instead of treating as update
description:
## Problem

The importer still has rename detection (importer.go:482-500) that triggers when same content hash has different IDs. With hash IDs, this shouldn't happen, but when it does (test data, bugs, legacy data), the import fails:

```
failed to handle rename bd-ce75 -> bd-5a90: rename collision handling removed - should not occur with hash IDs
```

## Current Behavior

1. Importer finds same content hash with different IDs
2. Calls handleRename() (line 490)
3. handleRename() errors out (line 294): "rename collision handling removed"
4. Import fails

## Expected Behavior

Same content hash + different IDs should be treated as an **update**, not a rename:
- Keep existing ID (already in database)
- Update fields if incoming has newer timestamp
- Discard incoming ID (it's wrong - hash should have generated same ID)

## Impact

- Import fails on legitimate edge cases (test data, data corruption)
- Cryptic error message
- Blocks sync operations

## Fix

In handleRename() or import loop, instead of erroring:
```go
// Same content, different ID - treat as update
if incoming.UpdatedAt.After(existing.UpdatedAt) {
    existing.Status = incoming.Status
    // ... copy other fields
    s.UpdateIssue(ctx, existing)
}
result.Updated++
```

## Files
- internal/importer/importer.go:271-294 (handleRename)
- internal/importer/importer.go:482-500 (rename detection)

## Repro
Import JSONL with bd-ce75 and bd-5a90 (both "Test parent issue" but different content hashes).

title: Fix transaction conflict in TryResurrectParent
description:
Integration test TestImportWithDeletedParent fails with 'database is locked' error when resurrection happens inside CreateIssue.

Root cause: TryResurrectParent calls conn.Get() and insertIssue() which conflicts with existing transaction in CreateIssue.

Error: failed to create tombstone for parent bd-parent: failed to insert issue: sqlite3: database is locked

Solution: Refactor resurrection to accept optional transaction parameter, use existing transaction when available instead of creating new connection.

Impact: Blocks resurrection from working in CreateIssue flow, only works in EnsureIDs (which may not have active transaction).

title: Modify CreateIssue to support parent resurrection
description: Update internal/storage/sqlite/sqlite.go:182-196 to call TryResurrectParent before failing on missing parent. Coordinate with EnsureIDs changes for consistent behavior. Handle edge case where parent never existed in JSONL (fail gracefully).

title: Implement TryResurrectParent function
description: Create internal/storage/sqlite/resurrection.go with TryResurrectParent(ctx, parentID) function. Parse JSONL history to find deleted parent, create tombstone with status=deleted and is_tombstone=true flag. Handle recursive resurrection for multi-level missing parents (bd-abc.1.2 with missing bd-abc and bd-abc.1).

title: Modify EnsureIDs to support parent resurrection
description: Update internal/storage/sqlite/ids.go:189-202 to call TryResurrectParent before failing on missing parent. Add resurrection mode flag, log resurrected parents for transparency. Maintain backwards compatibility with strict validation mode.

title: Implement topological sort for import ordering
description: Refactor upsertIssues() to sort issues by hierarchy depth before batch creation. Ensures parents are created before children, fixing latent bug where parent-child pairs in same batch can fail if ordered wrong. Sort by dot count, create in depth-order batches (0→1→2→3).

title: Add depth-based batch creation in upsertIssues
description: Replace single batch creation with depth-level batching (max depth 3). Create issues at depth 0, then 1, then 2, then 3. Prevents parent validation errors when importing hierarchical issues in same batch. File: internal/importer/importer.go:534-546

title: Fix import failure on missing parent issues
description: Import process fails atomically when JSONL references deleted parent issues. Implement hybrid solution: topological sorting + parent resurrection to handle deleted parents gracefully while maintaining referential integrity. See docs/import-bug-analysis-bd-3xq.md for full analysis.

title: Fix :memory: database connection pool issue causing "no such table" errors
description:
Critical bug in v0.21.6 where :memory: databases with cache=shared create multiple connections in the pool, causing intermittent "no such table" errors. SQLite's shared cache for in-memory databases only works reliably with a single connection.

Root cause: Missing db.SetMaxOpenConns(1) after sql.Open() for :memory: databases.

Impact: 37 test failures in VC project, affects all consumers using :memory: for testing.

title: Widespread double JSON encoding bug in daemon mode RPC calls
description:
Multiple CLI commands had the same double JSON encoding bug found in bd-1048. All commands that called ResolveID via RPC used string(resp.Data) instead of properly unmarshaling the JSON response. This caused IDs to retain JSON quotes ("bd-1048" instead of bd-1048), which then got double-encoded when passed to subsequent RPC calls.

Affected commands:
- bd show (3 instances)
- bd dep add/remove/tree (5 instances)
- bd label add/remove/list (3 instances)
- bd reopen (1 instance)

Root cause: resp.Data is json.RawMessage (already JSON-encoded), so string() conversion preserves quotes.

Fix: Replace all string(resp.Data) with json.Unmarshal(resp.Data, &id) for proper deserialization.

All commands now tested and working correctly with daemon mode.

title: Daemon gets stuck when auto-import blocked by git conflicts
description:
CRITICAL: The daemon enters a corrupt state that breaks RPC commands when auto-import is triggered but git pull fails due to uncommitted changes.

Impact: This is a data integrity and usability issue that could cause users to lose trust in Beads. The daemon silently fails for certain commands while appearing healthy.

Reproduction:
1. Make local changes to issues (creates uncommitted .beads/beads.jsonl)
2. Remote has updates (JSONL newer, triggers auto-import)
3. Daemon tries to pull but fails: 'cannot pull with rebase: You have unstaged changes'
4. Daemon enters bad state - 'bd show' and other commands return EOF
5. 'bd list' still works, daemon process is running, no errors logged

Technical details:
- Auto-import check runs in handleRequest() before processing RPC commands
- When import is blocked, it appears to corrupt daemon state
- Likely: deadlock, unclosed transaction, or storage handle corruption
- Panic recovery (server_lifecycle_conn.go:183) didn't catch anything - not a panic

Required fix:
- Auto-import must not block RPC command execution
- Handle git pull failures gracefully without corrupting state
- Consider: skip auto-import if git is dirty, queue import for later, or use separate goroutine
- Add timeout/circuit breaker for import operations
- Log clear warnings when auto-import is skipped

Without this fix, users in collaborative environments will frequently encounter mysterious EOF errors that require daemon restarts.

title: Daemon crashes silently on RPC query after startup
description:
The daemon fails to handle 'show' RPC commands when:
1) JSONL is newer than database (needs import)
2) git pull fails due to uncommitted changes

Symptoms:
- Daemon appears to run (ps shows process)
- 'bd list' and other commands work fine  
- 'bd show <id>' returns "failed to read response: EOF"
- No panic or error logged in daemon.log

Root cause likely: auto-import deadlock or state corruption when import is blocked by git conflicts.

Workaround: 
- Restart daemon after syncing git state (commit/push changes)
- OR use --no-daemon flag for all commands

The panic recovery added in server_lifecycle_conn.go:183 didn't catch any panics, confirming this isn't a panic-based crash.
notes: Root cause found and fixed: Two bugs - (1) nil pointer check missing in handleShow causing panic, (2) double JSON encoding in show.go ID resolution. Both fixed. bd show now works with daemon.
