title: bd ready broken: 'depends_on_id' column not found in schema (database 0.48.0 vs CLI 1.0.4)
description:
## Symptom

`bd ready` fails in this worktree with:

  Error: get ready work: filter blocked candidates: compute blocked IDs: deps from dependencies: Error 1105 (HY000): column "depends_on_id" could not be found in any table in scope

`bd stats` works fine (does not check dependencies). Only dependency-aware queries fail.

## Context

`bd doctor` reports:
- Database schema version: 0.48.0
- CLI version: 1.0.4
- Repo fingerprint mismatch (stored: e59d38f2, current: b6599b84)

The 1.0.4 CLI may reference a renamed column post-migration-0041 (split_dependencies_target), while the local database schema predates that migration rename, or vice versa.

## Impact

PM and other agents cannot use `bd ready` to find work. Workaround: use `bd list` with filters.

## Fix direction

Check which column name the 1.0.4 `bd ready` query uses vs the column name in this DB's dependencies table. Running pending schema migrations may resolve. See `bd doctor` output for migration gaps.
notes:
=== 2026-05-22 investigator root-cause (be-zbxe) — RESOLVED: stale binary, not stale DB ===

PROVEN ROOT CAUSE: the operator's bd binary was built BEFORE commit d15c7572f
("/{cmd,internal}: remove depends_on_id", 2026-05-19) and run against a DB whose
`dependencies` table has had the generated `depends_on_id` column dropped
(migration 0043_drop_dependencies_generated_column). Old binaries SELECT a
physical `depends_on_id`; current main resolves it as
`COALESCE(depends_on_issue_id, depends_on_wisp_id, depends_on_external) AS depends_on_id`
via issueops.DepTargetExpr (internal/storage/issueops/blocked.go:24,
dependencies.go:36). Querying the dropped column => errno 1105 "column
depends_on_id could not be found in any table in scope".

DISPROVES the bead's own hypothesis ("DB schema predates the migration ... running
pending migrations may resolve"): the live DB is POST-split, not pre-split.
`SHOW COLUMNS FROM dependencies` on the live Dolt server (127.0.0.1:28231/beads)
returns depends_on_issue_id/depends_on_wisp_id/depends_on_external and NO
depends_on_id. A pre-split DB would still HAVE depends_on_id and would NOT error.
The error only occurs when the DB is AHEAD of the binary; running migrations
forward does nothing.

ARTIFACT: /tmp/be-zbxe-artifact.txt — same live DB, same connection:
  OLD form  SELECT issue_id, depends_on_id, type FROM dependencies WHERE ...
            => ERROR 1105 column "depends_on_id" could not be found  (the symptom)
  NEW form  SELECT issue_id, COALESCE(...) AS depends_on_id, ... => clean
  bd ready  with current binary a19e1c5c7 => returns rows, no 1105.

WHY THE REPORTER WAS MISLED: bd doctor showed "CLI version: 1.0.4". The current
WORKING binary is ALSO "1.0.4 (dev: a19e1c5c7312)" — the headline version is
identical; only the build commit differs (a19e1c5c7 includes the refactor; the
reporter's 1.0.4 did not). Trust the build/commit, not the headline.

REMEDY (operational, no main code change for this path):
  rebuild bd from current main — CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd
  (or `make install`). Then `bd version` build/commit must be >= d15c7572f.
  NOTE: a stale second binary exists at ~/go/bin/bd (devel, unstamped); the active
  ~/.local/bin/bd is current and `bd ready` works. Recommend removing the stale dup.

SYSTEMIC UX FIX (separate, already in flight): be-wwbsv (impl) + be-cdhvj (tests)
add a SchemaSkewError / CheckForwardDrift guard that turns this cryptic 1105 into
a clear "binary is N versions behind the DB; rebuild" message + BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW
escape hatch. That is the durable fix for the confusing-error UX; this bead's
immediate symptom is already resolved by a current binary.

Closing as resolved. See also: discovered a SEPARATE live bug in merged PR #4010
(bd show --include-dependents silently returns no dependents on Dolt server) —
filing its own bead.
close_reason: Resolved: stale bd binary (built pre-d15c7572f) run against post-split DB — NOT a DB-too-old issue. Artifact /tmp/be-zbxe-artifact.txt: old query form 1105s / new form works on same live DB; bd ready works with current binary a19e1c5c7. Remedy: rebuild bd. Systemic schema-skew UX guard tracked by be-wwbsv/be-cdhvj. See full notes.

title: Move city beads storage back to Dolt server via bd export — try first, fix what blocks
description:
Operator decision 2026-05-17: move the city's beads storage from
PG-embedded back to a Dolt server. The act of attempting the move IS
the diagnostic — we don't know what will break, so we try first and
fix only what blocks us.

> "see if we can do a bd export and move back to a dolt server. if we
> can, awesome, go back to main. if not, fix it then do it and go back
> to main. at this point we have no context on what would need to be
> fixed; we need to move back to that infrastructure and document."
>   — operator, 2026-05-17

Sibling context: the PG-driver ship epic gm-mdoi6b was closed today as
superseded by the parking commit (316e5f0b on beads main,
parking/pg-driver-shelved-2026-05-17 branch). The bd codebase is back
on main (Dolt-only); only the city's storage backend is still PG.

## Plan

1. **Try the export.** `bd export` from the current PG-embedded state
   to JSONL (or whatever format `bd export` produces today).
2. **Stand up a Dolt server** for the city if one isn't already running
   (server mode, shared per the city's previous topology).
3. **Import / restore** into the Dolt server. Verify counts match
   (issue count, comment count, label count, dep edges).
4. **Switch the city** to read from the Dolt server. Run normal bd
   commands across rigs (`bd ready`, `bd show <id>`, `bd create`,
   `bd update --claim`, sling, etc.). Watch for breakage.
5. **Fix only what blocks.** If something is broken, file a bead for
   it and patch in place. Don't generalize, don't anticipate; fix the
   specific failure encountered.
6. **Document everything** that surprised us in gm-4lxazp (the pain
   log). Even successful moves with caveats deserve an entry — that's
   the evidence we need for any future PG case.

## Done-when

1. City's beads storage is on a Dolt server (server mode).
2. Standard cross-rig bd commands work without regressions.
3. Any incidents encountered have an entry in gm-4lxazp.
4. Anything that had to be fixed has a bead (closed if landed on main,
   open if upstream-pending).

## Routing

- Sling to beads/builder. The work is "execute the move, fix what

RELATED

  - gm-mdoi6b — closed today, superseded

title: Fix: PR #4015 CI failures — nocgo test signature + upgrade-smoke migrate step (be-1ix9zn)
description:
PR: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4015
Branch: feat/be-o7fh35-be-gudo26-schema-guards
Parent investigation: be-1ix9zn

## Root cause

Two distinct CI failures introduced by PR #4015 (schema-stale guard + `bd migrate schema`):

1. **`cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go:17` doesn't compile under `CGO_ENABLED=0`.** The PR widened `newDoltStore`'s signature from `(ctx, cfg)` to `(ctx, cfg, autoMigrate bool)`. All four callers were updated (`cmd/bd/store_factory.go`, `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo.go`, `cmd/bd/init.go`, `cmd/bd/main.go`) — EXCEPT this test file, which is gated by `//go:build !cgo` and so isn't compiled by the author's local `make test` (which uses CGO). The error escaped to the "Check cmd/bd pure-Go tests compile (CGO_ENABLED=0)" CI step.

   CI artifact: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/25984931582/job/76380387745 — exact error:
   ```
   cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go:17:38: not enough arguments in call to newDoltStore
       have (context.Context, *"github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/dolt".Config)
       want (context.Context, *"github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/dolt".Config, bool)
   ```

2. **5× "Upgrade smoke (v1.0.x → candidate)" failures.** Pre-PR, `EmbeddedDoltStore.initSchema` unconditionally called `schema.MigrateUp` on every store Open. The smoke test exercises the cross-version flow by:
   1. `prev init` (v1.0.x) → DB at schema 32 (v1.0.4 has 0001–0032 migrations on disk)
   2. `prev create` "Pre-upgrade issue"
   3. `cand_init` — exits with "This workspace is already initialized" (`cmd/bd/init.go:1631-1646`, via `checkExistingBeadsData → FatalError`); error masked by `2>/dev/null || true`, **no migration runs**.
   4. `cand list --json` (or `cand update`) — PersistentPreRun calls `newDoltStore(rootCtx, doltCfg, autoMigrateForCmd)` at `cmd/bd/main.go:1012`. `autoMigrateForCmd` is `false` for any cmd other than `bd migrate schema`. The new guard at `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go:179-194` calls `PendingMigrationCount` (returns 10: migrations 33-42 are unapplied) and returns `fmt.Errorf("beads schema is at version %d, binary requires %d — run: bd migrate schema", ...)`. PersistentPreRun's `FatalError` exits non-zero. Output is empty, assertion fails.

   Pre-PR main (SHA def4242, 2026-05-13) had Cross-Version Smoke passing — confirmed via `gh api repos/gastownhall/beads/actions/workflows/cross-version-smoke.yml/runs?branch=main`. Regression introduced solely by this PR.

   Note: `autoMigrateOnVersionBump` (PersistentPreRun's pre-step) does NOT save us — it gates on `versionUpgradeDetected`, which compares `.beads/.local_version` to the `Version` constant in `cmd/bd/version.go`. Both `prev` and `cand` ship with `Version = "1.0.4"` (the constant hasn't been bumped on this branch), so no upgrade is detected and `autoMigrateOnVersionBump` returns immediately.

   The PR's design — per its own description and test plan — is that "any other bd command against a stale store exits non-zero with the redirect message". So the explicit-migration UX is intentional; the smoke test simply needs to learn the new contract.

## Reproducing artifacts

- Compile error (failure 1): `gh run view 25984931582 --repo gastownhall/beads --job 76380387742 --log-failed`
- Upgrade smoke failure (failure 2, v1.0.4 example): `gh run view 25984931581 --repo gastownhall/beads --job 76380405224 --log-failed` — shows the `✗ Pre-upgrade issues NOT visible after upgrade` and `✗ Updated notes NOT visible after bd update` assertions

No local repro built — the branch is checked out in `beads/builder`'s worktree (do not disturb). The CI artifacts are the failing tests themselves; the root cause is provable from the diff alone.

## Fix spec

### Change 1: `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go`

Line 17 — replace exact text:

```go
	_, err := newDoltStore(t.Context(), cfg)
```

with:

```go
	_, err := newDoltStore(t.Context(), cfg, false)
```

`autoMigrate=false` is correct here. The test asserts the error message returned for `ServerMode: false`, which is produced at `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo.go:30-32` BEFORE `autoMigrate` is read; the value is irrelevant to the assertion. Using `false` is consistent with the runtime (non-bootstrap) callers.

Do NOT change the other two tests in that file — they call `newDoltStoreFromConfig` / `newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig`, which already pass `false` internally and don't need updating.

### Change 2: `scripts/upgrade-smoke-test.sh`

The candidate binary now refuses to open a stale-schema DB unless it's `bd init` (which already errors with "already initialized") or `bd migrate schema`. Add the explicit migration step to both data-touching scenarios.

**Scenario 1 (around line 253)** — after `cand_init`, before `cand list`:

Find the block:
```bash
# Upgrade: run candidate init (simulates upgrade)
cand_init 2>/dev/null || true

# Verify
```

Replace with:
```bash
# Upgrade: run candidate init (simulates upgrade)
cand_init 2>/dev/null || true

# PR #4015 (be-o7fh35): schema-stale guard refuses to open stale schemas;
# explicit migration is now required after a binary upgrade. Tolerate
# failure on candidates that don't yet have "bd migrate schema" — this
# script is bidirectional across versions.
cand migrate schema >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

# Verify
```

**Scenario 5 (around line 404)** — after `cand_init`, before `cand update`:

Find the block:
```bash
    # Upgrade: run candidate init
    cand_init 2>/dev/null || true

    # Mutate using the candidate binary
    cand update "$MUT_ID" --notes "smoke test mutation" 2>/dev/null || true
```

Replace with:
```bash
    # Upgrade: run candidate init
    cand_init 2>/dev/null || true

    # PR #4015 (be-o7fh35): schema-stale guard requires explicit migration.
    cand migrate schema >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

    # Mutate using the candidate binary
    cand update "$MUT_ID" --notes "smoke test mutation" 2>/dev/null || true
```

Scenarios 2, 3, 4 do NOT need changes — they only check `beads.role` git config and embedded-DB directory presence, neither of which opens the store.

### Build & commit

Then:
```bash
git -C /home/jaword/projects/beads add cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go scripts/upgrade-smoke-test.sh
git -C /home/jaword/projects/beads commit -m "fix(ci): pure-go test signature + upgrade-smoke migrate step (be-1ix9zn)

cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go:17 was missed when newDoltStore
widened to take an autoMigrate bool (be-o7fh35). The file is //go:build
!cgo only so make test never compiled it.

scripts/upgrade-smoke-test.sh's scenarios 1 and 5 relied on the
pre-PR implicit auto-migrate that initSchema did on every Open. With
the schema-stale guard active (be-o7fh35), upgraders must run
'bd migrate schema' explicitly — add it to the smoke test to match
the new contract."
git -C /home/jaword/projects/beads push origin feat/be-o7fh35-be-gudo26-schema-guards
```

### Verify

```bash
# Compile check should now pass:
cd /home/jaword/projects/beads && CGO_ENABLED=0 GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go go test -c -o /tmp/bd-cmd-puregeo-test ./cmd/bd

# Smoke test if you can spare a few minutes (downloads v1.0.4 binary; cached after first run):
cd /home/jaword/projects/beads && CANDIDATE_BIN="" ./scripts/upgrade-smoke-test.sh v1.0.4
# Expected: all 5 scenarios pass.

# Then wait for CI:
gh pr checks 4015 --repo gastownhall/beads
```

## Out of scope (do NOT touch)

- The schema-stale guard logic in `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/store.go`, `internal/storage/dolt/store.go`, or `internal/storage/uow/doltserver_provider.go`. The design is intentional per PR description.
- The error message format ("beads schema is at version N, binary requires M — run: bd migrate schema"). Users will see this; don't reword it.
- The `Version` constant in `cmd/bd/version.go`. Bumping it would make `autoMigrateOnVersionBump` fire and paper over the design — that's a release-engineering decision, not part of this fix.
- `cmd/bd/init.go`'s "already initialized" early exit. The PR's contract is that init refuses to touch an existing DB; users are explicitly redirected to `bd migrate schema`.
- Any data migration logic, the `MigrateSchemaUp` interface, or the schema package itself.

## Done-when

- [ ] `cmd/bd/store_factory_nocgo_test.go` compiles cleanly under `CGO_ENABLED=0 GOFLAGS=-tags=gms_pure_go go test -c -o /tmp/x ./cmd/bd`.
- [ ] `scripts/upgrade-smoke-test.sh v1.0.4` passes all 5 scenarios with `CANDIDATE_BIN` built from `feat/be-o7fh35-be-gudo26-schema-guards` HEAD.
- [ ] Commit pushed to `feat/be-o7fh35-be-gudo26-schema-guards`. Do NOT amend the PR author's existing commits — push a new commit on top.
- [ ] After push, CI shows the "Check cmd/bd pure-Go tests compile (CGO_ENABLED=0)" check green and all 5 "Upgrade smoke (v1.0.x → candidate)" checks green. `gh pr checks 4015 --repo gastownhall/beads` exits 0.
- [ ] Comment on PR #4015 noting the fix commit, e.g. `gh pr comment 4015 --repo gastownhall/beads --body "..."` — keep it short, credit the original author, and explain WHY (the PR's explicit-migration UX is the design; the smoke test was lagging the design).

title: Architect: explicit schema migration design — open questions from be-3z3fmi
description:
# Schema Migration Design: Explicit `bd migrate schema` + Schema-Stale Guard

**Bead:** be-sa4ls9
**Architect:** beads/architect
**Date:** 2026-05-17
**Refs:** be-3z3fmi, be-lw5fak (closed), be-o7fh35 (closed), be-gudo26 (closed), be-l4z4xw (closed), be-t4n07l

---

## Context

PR #3462 surfaced that `MigrateUp` running silently on every `Store.Open` creates an operational hazard: any `bd` command invocation after a binary upgrade can trigger migrations, causing orchestrators to SIGKILL a "hung" process. be-3z3fmi proposed an explicit migration step — `Store.Open` refuses stale schema; new `bd migrate schema` applies them.

**The builder implemented all five components before this document was written** (be-lw5fak, be-o7fh35, be-gudo26, be-l4z4xw — all closed). This document records the architectural decisions as implemented, addresses the upstream rejection (be-t4n07l), and specifies the Postgres extension expectation.

---

## Decisions

### Q1 — Which commands are blocked vs. allowed with stale schema?

**Decision: ALL commands are blocked except `bd init`, `bd migrate schema`, and `bd migrate schema --dry-run`.**

The guard must be total. A partial guard (allowing reads, blocking writes) creates a false sense of safety — read commands can trigger auto-commits or state transitions that fail on stale schema. The implementation uses `noDbCommands` in `cmd/bd/main.go` to exclude the `migrate` subtree from `PersistentPreRun`'s store open. `bd init` opens the store with `autoMigrate=true`, bypassing the guard entirely.

`bd doctor` and `bd migrate --inspect` are also excluded because they use diagnostic-only store paths. The authoritative exception list is `noDbCommands` in main.go.

### Q2 — Exact error format, exit code, and --json output

**Human error (stderr, exit 1):**
```
beads schema is at version N, binary requires M — run: bd migrate schema
```

**Machine-readable JSON** (when the failing command was invoked with `--json`):
```json
{
  "error": "schema_stale",
  "current_version": N,
  "required_version": M,
  "hint": "run: bd migrate schema"
}
```

The `"error": "schema_stale"` key lets orchestrators branch without parsing message strings.

### Q3 — Subcommand placement

**Decision: `bd migrate schema`.**

`bd migrate` is the existing home for migration-related operations (`bd migrate sync`, `bd migrate hooks`). Adding schema migration here is consistent. A new top-level `bd schema migrate` would create surface area with no benefit.

### Q4 — Does `bd init` continue to auto-migrate?

**Decision: Yes. `bd init` always auto-migrates.**

First-run bootstrap must work without a manual `bd migrate schema` step afterward. The implementation passes `autoMigrate=true` to the store open path used by `bd init`. No exceptions.

### Q5 — Does the Postgres backend need the same treatment?

**Decision: Yes, with identical semantics, when the PG driver ships.**

`schema.PendingMigrationCount(ctx, db)` accepts any `DBConn`. When the PG driver implements `Store.Open` (see be-aa1cqy), it MUST call `PendingMigrationCount` and return an error if > 0, using the same error string format. `bd migrate schema` dispatches to the appropriate backend via the `SchemaMigrator` interface introduced in PR #4015. The PG migration files and tooling are specified in be-33hwkn.

---

## Upstream Status: be-t4n07l — Fork vs. Pivot vs. Upstream Issue

**Situation:** PR #4015 was rejected by coffeegoddd (gastownhall maintainer): _"we are not going to merge this, it doesnt make any sense. the application code and the database schema need to match. the migrate schema command is on our roadmap."_

**Decision: Fork-local patch + upstream issue.**

Reasoning:
- The feature is fully implemented and CI-green. Reverting it removes observable, controllable upgrade UX for the gc-rig's CI/orchestration flows.
- The upstream maintainer's philosophy is correct for standard deployments where binary and schema arrive together. It doesn't account for orchestration contexts where the binary upgrade and schema migration are separate atomic steps.
- The upstream plans to implement `bd migrate schema` themselves. When they do, our patch may merge cleanly or require adaptation.

**Actions:**

1. **File a GitHub issue with gastownhall/beads** documenting the use case — CI/orchestrator upgrade visibility — and linking to our implementation. This puts the use case on record for their roadmap work. (Child bead to be filed.)

2. **Maintain `feat/be-o7fh35-be-gudo26-schema-guards` as a gc-rig-local branch.** When pulling upstream, rebase this branch on top. The changeset is small and localized to:
   - `internal/storage/schema/schema.go` — `PendingMigrationCount`
   - `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/open.go` — `OpenForMigration`, guard in `initSchema`
   - `internal/storage/dolt/store.go` — guard in `initSchemaOnDB`
   - `internal/storage/uow/doltserver_provider.go` — guard in provider
   - `cmd/bd/migrate_schema.go` — the new subcommand

3. **Do not** re-open PR #4015. The upstream decision is final.

4. **be-1vz5e8 (stale-guard tests) proceeds on the local branch.** The tests validate locally-maintained behavior and make future rebases easier to verify.

---

## Non-Functional Notes

- `SchemaMigrator` interface + `UnwrapStore(getStore())` — the right abstraction. Handles the decorator chain (e.g., `HookFiringStore`).
- `embeddeddolt.OpenForMigration` is the only call site that bypasses schema-init. No other callers should bypass the guard.
- `schema.PendingMigrationCount` MUST remain idempotent and read-only — it MUST NOT apply migrations.

description:
## Root cause

A Go race-detector failure fires non-deterministically on macOS CI runs for
the beads cmd/bd test suite. Two parallel tests both invoke methods on the
**shared global root cobra.Command** that lazily merge persistent parent
flags into a single pflag cache:

- TestStaleCommandInit (cmd/bd/stale_test.go:282) — calls `staleCmd.InheritedFlags()`
- TestNotionCommandsRegistered (cmd/bd/notion_test.go:26) — calls `notionCmd.Find(...)`

Both paths reach `updateParentsPflags → FlagSet.AddFlagSet → FlagSet.AddFlag`,
which mutate the shared parent's pflag map. The race manifests as:

```
WARNING: DATA RACE
Write at 0x... by goroutine N: pflag.(*FlagSet).AddFlag()
Previous read at 0x... by goroutine M: cobra.(*Command).updateParentsPflags.func1.(*FlagSet).AddFlagSet.1()
```

A third test (TestWhereNoWorkspace) is also reported as FAIL even when all
its subtests pass — this is the race-detector's parent-level FAIL signal.

## Reproducing test

The race fires on macOS-latest under `-race` whenever the two test functions
land on parallel workers in the right order. Most recent observation:

  PR #4009 — https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/25979506814/job/76365515114
  (PR #4009's diff is a pure refactor of internal/ui markdown extraction —
   completely unrelated to the racing tests.)

## Fix spec — already written, just needs to land

The fix already exists as commit `d8a97c6bb` ("test: prevent Cobra command
flag cache races") by Julian Knutsen, 2026-05-16. It lives on three feature
branches but has **not** been merged to main and has **no standalone PR**:

- origin/fix/ready-wisp-filter-parity
- origin/runtime/perf-integrated-plus-local-perf-20260516
- origin/runtime/perf-integrated-ready-filter-20260517

The commit changes 4 files (+24 -22):

1. cmd/bd/notion_test.go — remove `t.Parallel()` from TestNotionCommandsRegistered
2. cmd/bd/stale_test.go — remove `t.Parallel()` from TestStaleCommandInit
3. cmd/bd/stdio_race_guard_test.go — extend `cobraParallelUnsafeMethods` to
   include `.Find(` and `.InheritedFlags(`, update guard comments
4. cmd/bd/test_helpers_pure_test.go — update stdioMutex doc comment

**Builder steps:**

```bash
git fetch origin
git checkout main && git pull --ff-only origin main
git checkout -b fix/cobra-pflag-race-d8a97c6bb
git cherry-pick d8a97c6bbca347c01de64138115b6da79246962c
# Resolve any conflicts (unlikely — changes are isolated to test files).
git push -u origin fix/cobra-pflag-race-d8a97c6bb
gh pr create --repo gastownhall/beads --base main \
  --title "test: prevent Cobra command flag cache races" \
  --body "<see template below>"
```

Suggested PR body:

> Cherry-picks d8a97c6bb (originally authored by Julian Knutsen) as a
> standalone PR on main. The fix removes t.Parallel() from
> TestStaleCommandInit and TestNotionCommandsRegistered, and extends
> the cobra parallel-policy guard to flag .Find( and .InheritedFlags(.
>
> Root cause: both methods lazily merge persistent parent flags into a
> shared pflag cache, racing under -race when the two tests run in
> parallel workers. Race trace example (PR #4009 macOS-latest job):
> pflag.(*FlagSet).AddFlag write vs. updateParentsPflags read on the
> same FlagSet.
>
> Currently sitting on fix/ready-wisp-filter-parity and runtime/perf-*
> branches without its own PR — landing this on main fixes the flake
> for every open PR.

## Out of scope

- Do **not** bundle other changes from the source branches — only
  cherry-pick d8a97c6bb itself.
- Do **not** rewrite the commit message or change the author attribution
  beyond what `git cherry-pick` does automatically (Julian Knutsen
  remains the author; cherry-pick is fine).
- Do **not** attempt to fix the underlying cobra/pflag library bug —
  that's an upstream issue; this PR only adjusts beads' tests.

## Done-when

- [ ] Cherry-pick succeeds cleanly on main with no conflicts.
- [ ] PR opened against main, all CI checks pass — explicitly verify
      Test (macos-latest) is green.
- [ ] PR merged.

## Reference

- Original commit: d8a97c6bbca347c01de64138115b6da79246962c
- Trail: discovered while investigating PR #4009 (bead be-vmvqmq).
close_reason: Cherry-picked d8a97c6bb onto fix/cobra-pflag-race-d8a97c6bb (from fork quad341/beads), opened PR #4011 against gastownhall/beads:main. Push to origin failed (quad341 lacks write access to gastownhall org).

title: bd CLI process repeatedly grows to ~1.7GB RSS — investigate memory leak
description:
On 2026-05-16 (mayor host, gc-management) the kernel OOM-killed two bd processes within 2 hours, both at ~1.7GB RSS. bd should be short-lived and lightweight; this is anomalous.

## OOM evidence (journalctl -b -2)

```
May 16 03:43:03 — Out of memory: Killed process 1748595 (bd)
  total-vm:5310568kB, anon-rss:1721828kB, file-rss:912kB
  (oom-killer invoked by: claude, oom_score_adj=200)
  cgroup: tmux-spawn-da8e0a20-6db0-461c-82c3-ab8aa3acdbf1.scope

May 16 05:45:21 — Out of memory: Killed process 2767275 (bd)
  total-vm:5455376kB, anon-rss:1729368kB, file-rss:1932kB
  (oom-killer invoked by: notify-rs inoti, oom_score_adj=200)
  cgroup: tmux-spawn-836a3e17-8808-41b2-8719-567b9f5596d2.scope
```

Both were in tmux-spawn scopes (agent-spawned subprocesses). Same RSS shape (~1.7GB) and same VSZ shape (~5.3GB) — looks like the same code path bloating consistently.

## Context

- bd 1.0.4 (commit 4c065c05b on tests/be-2bvr4u-pg-promote-savepoint-poison)
- Postgres backend; bd reads/writes pg directly (Dolt is dead)
- ~105,438 issues across pg DBs total
- Several rig agents had hook reconciliation churning during this window

## Hypotheses to investigate

1. A query loading full issue rows without LIMIT (e.g. `SELECT * FROM issues` somewhere in the hot path)
2. JSON marshal/unmarshal of large result sets into oversized Go slices
3. pg driver result buffer leak (pgx/sql.Rows not closed)
4. Reconciler cache growth in a long-lived bd subprocess (though bd is supposed to be one-shot)
5. JSONL export rebuild on every invocation when run inside an agent's loop

## Available forensics

A 5-min memory snapshot watchdog was installed today on the mayor host: `~/.local/bin/memwatch.sh` + systemd user timer `memwatch.timer`. Logs at `~/.local/share/memwatch/YYYY-MM-DD.log`. Next time bd bloats we'll have the rising curve and surrounding processes captured.
notes:
2026-05-16 follow-up: deep-investigator's be-aw0afh report (closed 14:42, mail gm-00bgaq) is likely the same class as this bead.

## Evidence

Per gc event emit (shell hook fork-exec of gc binary):
- 670ms wall
- 50MB RSS per process
- 800ms CPU

City idle baseline: ~38 emits/min × 50MB = transient 1.9GB+ across short-lived gc processes per minute. The two bd 1.7GB OOM kills observed on this rig (May 16 03:43, 05:45) almost certainly involve the gc-fork-exec spew piggy-backing on the bd subprocess — not bd itself leaking, but a bd write triggering a hook that spawns gc, with the OOM happening while many of these are concurrent and the rest of the system is under memory pressure.

deep-investigator filed ga-813ouh (gascity, needs-architecture) with 4 mitigation options:
- A: daemon socket (gc-supervisor listens, hook sends line) — RECOMMENDED
- B: slim gc-event-emit-only binary (~5MB vs 105MB, ~50ms vs 670ms)
- C: in-process emit in bd (zero fork-exec; requires beads-side Runner.RunInProcess change)
- D: batched periodic emit (bounded latency)

## Implication for this bead

This bead may collapse into ga-813ouh's mitigation work. Recommended path for the investigator on this bead:
1. Confirm via memwatch logs (~/.local/share/memwatch/) that bd OOMs correlated with gc-fork-exec storms
2. If yes, close be-bx0tm7 as duplicate-of ga-813ouh and let the gascity architecture work resolve it
3. If no, narrow to a different mechanism with the data in hand

## Cross-refs

- be-aw0afh (beads rig, closed 2026-05-16 — origin investigation, Exit C)
- ga-813ouh (gascity rig, architect-routed — the mitigation work)
- be-b0t (beads rig, related — separate bd-cold-start cost; may or may not converge with this)
## 2026-05-16 investigator (beads/investigator) — narrowed but not concluded

Hypotheses TESTED and DISPROVEN:
- (5) Auto-export JSONL: `export.auto: false` on every PG-backed city — gated off. Independent of leak.
- (own hyp) `maybeAutoImportJSONL` on every bd write: PG path returns in main.go:953 before line 1075 invokes it. Not reached on PG.
- (1) `bd list` unbounded: `bd list --status=open` on 105k-issue gc-management = 79MB.
- `bd export -o`, `bd lint`, `bd stale`, `bd orphans`, `bd doctor --quiet`, `bd duplicates`: all <100MB peak RSS on gc-management PG.

Hypotheses NARROWED but UNFINISHED:
- Cross-rig routing IS the trigger. Captured live bd argvs at 1.5-1.8GB RSS (50+ samples over 20 min):
  - `bd show --json <gm-XXX session bead>`  → 1.6-1.8GB
  - `bd show --json <Rig/Agent>` (cross-rig agent IDs)  → 1.6-1.8GB
  - `bd list --json --include-infra --include-gates --limit 0 --metadata-field session_name=gm-XXX`  → 1.7-1.8GB
  - `bd list --json --include-infra --include-gates --limit 0 --metadata-field alias=gm-XXX`  → 1.7-1.8GB
  - `bd list --json --label=gc:session --include-infra --include-gates --limit 0`  → 1.7GB
  - Stays SMALL (83MB): `bd ready`, `bd show <local bead>`, `bd show beads/reviewer` (where this rig's IDs hit local DB fast)

Repro: when run from my shell with the same argv, same cwd, same BEADS_DIR=/home/jaword/projects/beads/.beads, bd terminates in 80ms / 83MB returning "no issue found". So the leak fires only under the agent's full env (not BEADS_DIR alone, not BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD alone). Environ-capture monitor armed (>400MB threshold) at /tmp/be-bx0tm7-bdmon2.sh; will dump environ of next big bd to /tmp/be-bx0tm7-env-<pid>.

Capture artifacts:
- /tmp/be-bx0tm7-big-bd.log — 50+ bd argv/cwd/RSS samples
- /home/jaword/.local/share/memwatch/2026-05-16.log — 5-min global snapshots showing clusters of 3 bds at 1.7-1.8GB

Code reading: cmd/bd/routed.go:55 resolveAndGetIssueWithRouting fans out across local → prefix-route → contributor auto-route paths. cmd/bd/show.go:160 + internal/storage/postgres/dependencies.go:150 still fetch full Issue records per dependent (be-4d36f2 only made the JSON OUTPUT shallow, not the FETCH) — but observed hub IDs have 0 dependents so this is not the trigger here; it remains a latent issue for hub beads with thousands of deps.

Earlier note attributing the 1.7GB to gc-fork-exec storm (be-aw0afh) is incomplete: the OOM-killer's anon-rss accounts for the killed bd's own private memory only. Memwatch + ps prove individual bd processes do grow to 1.7GB. The gc-storm explains additional cgroup pressure but not the bd allocation.

NEXT: capture environ of a live big bd; reproduce; localize.
## 2026-05-16 investigator — ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED

**Root cause: stale bd 1.0.3 binary at /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd (commit 8f5622b91, May 4 2026) is invoked by agents whose HOME=/home/jaword/jim-claude. That binary does NOT have the Postgres backend compiled in. When pointed at a PG-backed BEADS_DIR (every modern .beads/metadata.json with backend=postgres), it enters a non-functional fallback path that allocates 0.8–1.8 GB RSS per invocation and returns 'no issue found' after 30–60 s.**

### Reproducer (artifact)

Stale binary (1.0.3) — leaks:
```
$ /usr/bin/time -v env -i HOME=/home/jaword/jim-claude PATH=/home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin BEADS_DIR=/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd show --json gm-m80sdq
Elapsed (wall clock) time:        0:47.39
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 1805820
Error fetching gm-m80sdq: no issue found matching "gm-m80sdq"
Exit status: 1
```

Current binary (1.0.4) — same env, same query, same BEADS_DIR:
```
$ /usr/bin/time -v env -i HOME=/home/jaword/jim-claude PATH=/home/jaword/.local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin BEADS_DIR=/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd show --json gm-m80sdq
Elapsed (wall clock) time:        0:00.03
Maximum resident set size (kbytes): 84692
Exit status: 0
```

### Why this matches the original OOM events

The two May 16 OOM kills (03:43, 05:45) were in tmux-spawn-* cgroups (per-agent scopes) where claude triggered the OOM-killer and bd was the victim. The killed bd processes show total-vm:5.3GB / anon-rss:1.7GB — exactly the leak shape this stale binary produces (Go runtime mmap reservations + ~1.5 GB allocator working set during a flailing fallback path). The patterns I captured live (50+ samples, /tmp/be-bx0tm7-big-bd.log) — bd show gm-XXX, bd list --metadata-field session_name=gm-XXX, bd list --label=gc:session — all originate from session-start hook fan-out in jim-claude agents, and they all use the stale binary.

### How the binaries diverge in PATH

agent env (e.g. beads/pm): PATH=/home/jaword/jim-claude/go/bin:/home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin:/home/jaword/.local/bin:/home/jaword/bin:...
   → `bd` resolves to /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd (1.0.3, 8f5622b91, May 4 2026, pre-PG)

investigator env (this session): /home/jaword/.local/bin first
   → `bd` resolves to /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd (1.0.4, 4c065c05b, May 11 2026, includes PG support)

Stale binary is missing all 176 commits between 8f5622b91 and 4c065c05b — notably including the Postgres backend itself (`d7d81eab3 feat(storage): be-6fk.3 PostgresBackend core (pgx/v5)`) and the filter coverage fixes (`ba52ae708`, `e2b90142e`). The remembered memory about "PG/Dolt SearchIssues query-clause asymmetry" is the same class of issue — earlier PG was a smoke-path-only implementation that silently dropped most filters.

### IMMEDIATE FIX (user environment, no beads-code change required)

```
cp /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd
# OR
rm /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd   # falls through to /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd via PATH
```

### Latent beads-code follow-up (lower priority)

bd 1.0.3 should fail-fast when it encounters metadata.json with `backend: postgres` it cannot open, instead of silently entering a 1.7 GB fallback. The current 1.0.4 has PG support so this only matters for users with stale binaries — but those users get a confusing memory leak + wrong-answer combo. File a separate bead if you want a defense-in-depth guard.

### Disposes of prior framing

- be-aw0afh / ga-813ouh (gc fork-exec storm) is a real and independent phenomenon affecting per-emit CPU/RSS rate, but it does NOT explain individual bd processes at 1.7 GB anon-rss. The leak documented here is fully explained by the stale binary, not by piggy-backed gc subprocesses.

### Captured artifacts

- /tmp/be-bx0tm7-big-bd.log — 50+ live bd argv/RSS samples (1.5–1.8 GB)
- /tmp/be-bx0tm7-env-NNN — environ dumps for each leaking bd (proves jim-claude HOME + stale PATH)
- /home/jaword/.local/share/memwatch/2026-05-16.log — system-wide 5-min snapshots showing clusters of 3 bds at 1.7–1.8 GB
- Reproducer commands above (deterministic, ~50 s to demonstrate)
Filed follow-up be-y0sm9s for defense-in-depth fail-fast guard in current bd. Notified mayor (gm-kfrgre) and beads/builder (gm-rlg1gt). Immediate fix is on-host (cp current bd over the stale one or rm the stale copy); not a beads-code change.
close_reason: Root cause: stale bd 1.0.3 binary at /home/jaword/jim-claude/.local/bin/bd predates PG backend support. Agent PATH puts it first → non-functional 1.8GB fallback. Fix: replace that binary with /home/jaword/.local/bin/bd. Defense-in-depth follow-up at be-y0sm9s.

title: Review: be-nzo2iu bd doctor Postgres health + legacy detection + JSON backend block
notes:
## Review verdict: request-changes

**Reviewer:** beads/reviewer
**Commit:** a570a0da5
**Date:** 2026-05-16

---

### FINDING 1 — CRITICAL BUG (blocker)
**File:** cmd/bd/doctor/legacy_dolt_artifacts.go:22-29
**Category:** Correctness / Spec compliance
**Severity:** HIGH — blocks pass

CheckLegacyDoltArtifacts performs its own un-gated os.Stat() on `filepath.Join(beadsDir, "dolt")` rather than reading bi.LegacyDoltDir from ResolveBackendInfo. On any embedded-Dolt workspace .beads/dolt always exists; this produces a false-positive INFO check:

    ℹ  legacy   .beads/dolt present (inactive — backend is postgres)

...on EVERY existing Dolt user, despite backend being dolt.

The infrastructure already exists: DetectLegacyDoltState (configfile/legacy.go) gates on BackendPostgres and populates bi.LegacyDoltDir — but the function ignores it. Fix is minimal:

    // Replace the os.Stat block (lines 22-29) with:
    doltDir := bi.LegacyDoltDir   // already backend-gated; empty on Dolt workspaces

title: Build: store_factory env-override wiring (dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides at runtime) (be-zdhe4l §FR-6/§7)
description:
## What to build

Wire `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` into the runtime connection path so that BEADS_POSTGRES_* env vars take effect on every `bd` invocation (not just at init time).

### Files to update

**`store_factory.go`** and **`store_factory_nocgo.go`**

Current code pattern (approximately):
```go
connCfg.DSN = dsn.Compose(cfg.PostgresDSN, os.Getenv("BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD"))
```

New code pattern:
```go
overriddenDSN, overrideFields := dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides(cfg.PostgresDSN)
connCfg.DSN = dsn.Compose(overriddenDSN, os.Getenv("BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD"))
// Store overrideFields in connCfg or context for error messages
```

On connection error, the error message must include the redacted target AND the override list:
```
postgres unreachable: staging.db:5433/mybd (overrides applied: host) — err=<wrapped, no DSN>
```

The override list should be stored so `bd context` / `bd backend status` (be-pbnoaa work) can
report `overrides_applied: ["host", "port"]`. Pass it through to wherever the BackendInfo
resolver reads (internal/configfile or the resolved view).

### Downstream: be-pbnoaa.1 reporting integration

The be-0w5z7u bead (BackendInfo resolver) should also call `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` so that
`bd context` and `bd backend status` reflect the *runtime* target, not the persisted DSN.
Note this as a dependency comment in store_factory.go near the override call.

### Integration test (be-zdhe4l §15 item 10)

```
  Then run: BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST=staging.db bd ready
  → connection error against staging.db (expected; PG not there)
  → error message includes "overrides_applied: [host]"
```

## Acceptance criteria
- BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST/PORT/USER/DATABASE/SSLMODE take effect at runtime without re-init (NFR-3)
- Connection error message renders only redacted target + override field names (NFR-4)

title: Build: bd init --pg-* flags + runPostgresInit discovery flow (be-zdhe4l §FR-1-13)
description:
## What to build

Update `cmd/bd/init.go` and `cmd/bd/init_postgres.go` to support the new flag surface and discovery flow.

### New flags on `bd init` (be-zdhe4l §5 flag matrix)

| Flag              | Type   | Default          | Notes                                                       |
|-------------------|--------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--pg-host`       | string | (discovery)      | Postgres host                                               |
| `--pg-port`       | int    | (discovery)      | Postgres port                                               |
| `--pg-user`       | string | `beads`          | Postgres user                                               |
| `--pg-database`   | string | sanitized prefix | Database name (per-rig)                                     |
| `--pg-sslmode`    | string | `disable`        | sslmode for loopback; `require` default for non-loopback    |
| `--pg-cluster-dir`| string | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data` | Override discovery dir    |

**Mutex constraint:** `--dsn` and any `--pg-*` flag are mutually exclusive — fatal error on conflict (FR-5, §14 criterion 3).

### Updated `runPostgresInit` flow

**Priority chain:**
1. `--dsn` given → use verbatim, strip, persist (existing behavior — no change)
2. Any `--pg-*` flags given → compose DSN via `dsn.BuildFromFields` (new §14 criterion 4)
3. Neither → run `discoverLocalPostgres(pgClusterDir)`:
   - Success: compose DSN with discovered host/port + defaults
   - Failure: fatal with remediation ("no local Postgres cluster found at $XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data; either start it, pass `--pg-host=<remote>`, or pass `--dsn=<full>`")

**Partial flags:** when only some `--pg-*` flags are given, fill unspecified fields:
- host: required if discovery fails (fatal error)
- port: from discovery if available, else error
- user: `beads` (static default)
- sslmode: `disable` for loopback host, `require` for non-loopback
- database: sanitized prefix (same as today's `resolveInitPrefix`)

**Validation:**
- `--pg-database=postgres` (or `template0`/`template1`) → fatal error with remediation (§14 criterion 12)
- `--pg-host=<non-loopback> --pg-sslmode=disable` → print WARNING before persisting (§14 criterion 11, §12)
- Remove unconditional `errMissingDSN` fatal from flag-validation block (~line 117 init.go) (§14 criterion 9)

**After DSN composition:**
- Write `.beads/.discovery_log`: one-line append-only record of the discovery decision, no credentials
- Add `.beads/.discovery_log` to `.gitignore` (matches `.beads/.pid` pattern)
- Success banner: print resolved target (host:port/db) — example: "✓ bd initialized; backend: postgres; target: 127.0.0.1:5433/mybd"

## Integration tests required (be-zdhe4l §15 items 7-14)

```
TestInit_PostgresLocalDiscovery: spin up local PG; bd init --backend=postgres --prefix=mybd (no flags)
  → metadata.json postgres_dsn matches discovered target, rig queryable

TestInit_PostgresPartialFlags: --pg-host=127.0.0.1 --pg-database=mybd (no user/port/sslmode)
  → composed DSN uses discovery for port, static defaults for rest

TestInit_PostgresRemoteFlags: --pg-host=remote.example.com --pg-database=mybd
  → no discovery, sslmode defaults to require, warning printed

TestInit_NonLoopbackDisableWarns: --pg-host=remote.example.com --pg-sslmode=disable
  → init succeeds, stderr has WARNING: sslmode=disable on non-loopback host

TestInit_SystemDbRejected: --pg-database=postgres → fatal exit 1

Backward-compat smoke: replay existing init_postgres_test.go invocations unchanged → all pass

No-leak smoke: for each new test file, capture stdout+stderr, assert fixture password not present
```

## Acceptance criteria
- New --pg-* flags present on bd init --help
- --dsn and --pg-* are mutually exclusive (fatal error if mixed)
- bd init --backend=postgres with no flags succeeds when local PG discoverable
- bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=<full> still works (backward compat)
- System database names rejected (postgres/template0/template1)
- sslmode=disable warning on non-loopback host
- .beads/.discovery_log written and gitignored
- Success banner shows resolved host:port/db
- All integration tests pass
- No fixture passwords appear in test output
- go test ./cmd/bd/... passes, golangci-lint clean

- be-5w6nt9 (dsn.BuildFromFields + dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides)
- be-jnxg8d (discoverLocalPostgres)

title: Build: local PG cluster discovery (postmaster.pid + postgresql.conf fallback) (be-zdhe4l §6)
description:
## What to build

New file: `cmd/bd/init_postgres_discovery.go`

```go
// discoverLocalPostgres reads the cluster dir to find the running PG host and port.
// Preferred: postmaster.pid (line 4 = port, line 6 = listen host).
// Fallback: postgresql.conf (port directive, listen_addresses).
// Returns found=false cleanly when both are missing — never panics.
func discoverLocalPostgres(clusterDir string) (host string, port int, found bool)
```

### Discovery algorithm (be-zdhe4l §6)
1. Stat `clusterDir`. If missing → return found=false.
2. Try reading `clusterDir/postmaster.pid`:
   - Line 4 = port (integer), Line 6 = listen host
   - If truncated (< 6 lines) → log warning, fall through to postgresql.conf
3. Fallback: read `clusterDir/postgresql.conf`:
   - Parse `port = <number>` line
   - Parse `listen_addresses = '<addr>'` line
   - If file missing or fields not found → return found=false
4. Never modifies disk state (NFR-2)
5. Must complete in <50ms in the happy path (NFR-1)

### Default cluster dir
`$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data` (Linux/macOS both use XDG — `~/.local/share/beads/postgres`). The caller passes this; `--pg-cluster-dir` flag overrides it.

## Unit tests required (be-zdhe4l §15 items 3-6)

```
TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_PostmasterPidPresent:
  fixture postmaster.pid with realistic 5-line content
  → returns ("127.0.0.1", 5433, true)

TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_PostgresConfFallback:
  cluster dir without postmaster.pid but with postgresql.conf
  containing port=5433 and listen_addresses='127.0.0.1'
  → returns ("127.0.0.1", 5433, true)

TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_NoCluster:
  empty dir / no dir → returns ("", 0, false), no panic

TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_MalformedPid:
  postmaster.pid with only 2 lines (truncated)
  → returns ("", 0, false) with warning, no panic
```

## Acceptance criteria
- discoverLocalPostgres reads postmaster.pid preferred, postgresql.conf fallback
- found=false on missing dir, missing files, or truncated files (no panic)
- Read-only — never writes to cluster dir
- All 4 unit tests pass
- go test ./cmd/bd/... passes
- golangci-lint run ./... clean

## Dependencies

as the discovery result feeds directly into dsn.BuildFromFields.

```go
// BuildFromFields composes a stripped (no-password) DSN from individual fields.
func BuildFromFields(host string, port int, user, db, sslmode string) string
```
- Produces: `postgres://user@host:port/db?sslmode=sslmode`
- Password never included (stripped DSN only)


title: Fix bddgen: GetLabelsReply.strings unexported field loses data over gob/RPC
description:
bddgen generates GetLabelsReply with an unexported field:

  type GetLabelsReply struct {
      strings  []string  // lowercase — gob skips this
      RPCError *RPCError
  }

gob (used by net/rpc) only encodes exported fields. The result is that GetLabels silently returns nil to RPC clients even when the server has labels. server.go sets reply.strings = r0, client.go reads reply.strings — both compile fine within-package but the data never crosses the wire.

Fix: in the bddgen template, capitalize the field name to Strings. Then regenerate client.go, server.go, and types.go.

Surfaced during review of be-e2pufb (commit 869b6664b, types.go is Code generated by bddgen).

## Summary

## Findings

### [MEDIUM] driver.go — Driver.Open / DriverOpener contract is ambiguous
File: internal/storage/driver.go, lines 26-29 and 58-60 and 78-93

The two comments contradict each other:
- DriverOpener doc (line 59): 'It must return a fully constructed Driver that is ready to Open' — implying Open has NOT been called yet.
- OpenDriver doc (lines 79-80): 'The opener is responsible for constructing and opening the driver. The returned Driver is ready to use.' — implying Open HAS already been called.

OpenDriver never calls d.Open() after the opener returns. So the actual behavior is: DriverOpener must call Open internally (otherwise the returned driver is in a half-open state). But if DriverOpener always calls Open, why is Open a public method on the Driver interface?

Recommended fix: have OpenDriver call d.Open(ctx, cfg) after the opener returns and update DriverOpener's doc to say it only constructs (does not open). This matches the database/sql pattern and makes Open's purpose unambiguous to every future backend implementor.

### [MEDIUM] driver.go — No tests for RegisterDriver / OpenDriver
File: internal/storage/driver.go, lines 67-93

RegisterDriver/OpenDriver have non-trivial logic: panic on duplicate name, error on unregistered name, RWMutex concurrency. None of it is exercised. Either add a driver_test.go with registry round-trip, dup-panic, and unknown-name tests, or file a needs-tests follow-up bead.

### [LOW] capability_test.go:106-116 — contains() reimplements strings.Contains
File: internal/storage/capability_test.go, lines 106-116

The contains() helper is a manual reimplementation of strings.Contains. Replace with strings.Contains from the standard library.

## What passes
- Capability type, CapabilitySet, Has, Require, ErrCapabilityNotSupported: clean design, immutable value semantics, correct errors.Is chaining.
- DoltCapabilities / PostgresCapabilities constants: exhaustive and independently verified by tests.
- RWMutex usage in registry: correctly scoped (lock released before opener call, avoiding deadlock).
- No security issues. No injection vectors. DriverConfig.Options (DSN/password storage) is not logged.

title: PG driver Phase-1 acceptance: CreateIssue must honor custom types (carries forward from be-rhtega)
description:
Carries forward the be-rhtega fix content as an explicit acceptance requirement
for the Phase-1 PG driver implementation, so the bug is not re-introduced
when PG support is rebuilt behind the Driver interface (per pg-driver-ship-plan.md).

## What must be preserved from be-rhtega

PG's CreateIssue must call `ValidateWithCustom(customStatuses, customTypes)`,
NOT `Validate()` (which defaults to nil/nil). Without this, any `bd create
--type <custom-type>` (session, molecule, etc.) is rejected with
"validation failed for issue : invalid issue type: <name>" — blocking all
new session/molecule creation on PG-backed rigs.

a67427829.
Existing test branch: tests/be-mrhgpt-create-custom-types @ 3239a59c6

interface's PG implementation when it lands).

- CreateIssue with a custom issue_type registered via SetCustomTypes
- CreateIssue with a custom status registered via SetCustomStatuses
- CreateIssue rejection of an unregistered custom type (negative-path)

All three must pass against the new Driver-abstraction PG implementation
under `integration_pg` build tag, before Phase 1 closes.

## Why this is a separate bead, not just a note

Closing be-rhtega without a tracking artifact risks losing the fix during
the Driver refactor (drivers/postgres/idgen.go or equivalent rewrite).

title: bdd daemon iter transport: extend bddgen to emit iter_types.go, iter_server.go, iter_client.go
description: Extend cmd/bddgen/main.go to detect Iter* method names on storage.Storage and DependencyQueryStore and emit three additional generated files for the iterator transport layer (be-60kmhm §8). The generator already walks interface methods for the slice path; the iter path is a conditional branch on the 'Iter' name prefix. Running go generate produces all four generated files in one pass.
notes:
## What to build

### cmd/bddgen/main.go
Add an iterator-detection branch: for any method whose name starts with "Iter", bddgen emits additional iter-specific stubs beyond the standard slice-path Args/Reply/server/client stubs.

For each of the 10 Iter* methods (IterIssues, IterEvents, IterAllEventsSince, IterDependentsWithMetadata, IterDependenciesWithMetadata, IterIssueComments, IterReadyWork, IterBlockedIssues, IterWisps, IterAllDependencyRecords):

1. **IterXxxStartArgs** — method's non-ctx params + BatchSize int
2. **IterXxxNextReply** — []*T, Done bool, RPCError *RPCError
3. **daemonServer.IterXxxStart** — generates UUIDv4 sessionID, opens underlying storage.Iter, calls iterMgr.openSession; returns ErrTooManyIterators as RPCError if cap hit
4. **daemonServer.IterXxxNext** — type-asserts session, serializes Next calls, batch-fetches with value copy, sets Done=true on exhaustion and auto-closes session
5. **rpcXxxIter struct** — implements storage.Iter[T] with Next(ctx)/Value()/Err()/Close() + optional prefetch pipeline (see §4.1)
6. **daemonClient.IterXxx** — calls IterXxxStart, handles ErrTooManyIterators fallback to slice path
7. **xxxIterSession concrete struct** — implements serverIterSession (TypeName, LastUsedAt, Touch, Close)

Output files:
- internal/storage/rpc/iter_types.go (GENERATED) — per-type StartArgs + NextReply
- internal/storage/rpc/iter_server.go (GENERATED) — IterXxxStart + IterXxxNext + xxxIterSession
- internal/storage/rpc/iter_client.go (GENERATED) — rpcXxxIter + daemonClient.IterXxx

Generator invocation: go generate ./internal/storage/rpc/... (add gen.go with //go:generate directive)

## Open questions for builder (§14)
1. **Prefetch**: Design recommends prefetch=true by default (fire next IterXxxNext RPC at batch boundary to hide latency). Builder may omit in first pass if rpc.Client.Go complexity outweighs gain — document the tradeoff in a bead note and create follow-up bead if deferred.
2. **Session ID**: UUIDv4 via crypto/rand is the default. Base58-encoded 8 bytes is fine if shorter IDs preferred — just needs to be unique per daemon lifetime.

## Key implementation notes
- Value copy on server (§5): v := *issueSess.iter.Value(); batch = append(batch, &v) — Iter[T].Value() may reuse the pointer across Next() calls
- Context cancellation on client (§4.1): use rpc.Client.Go() + select { case <-ctx.Done(): ... case <-call.Done: ... }
- ErrTooManyIterators fallback: daemonClient.IterXxx checks reply.RPCError; on ErrTooManyIterators, logs warning and calls SearchIssues -> storage.NewSliceIter

## Acceptance criteria
- bddgen emits all 10 Iter* method sets (all 10 methods listed above)
- Generated files have // Code generated by bddgen. DO NOT EDIT. headers
- rpcXxxIter satisfies storage.Iter[T] (compile check)
- rpcXxxIter.Next(ctx) respects context cancellation
- daemonClient.IterXxx falls back to slice path on ErrTooManyIterators
- go vet passes on all generated files
- go build ./... clean after go generate

title: bdd daemon iter transport: iter_shared.go — session manager, shared types, server wiring
description: Handwrite the shared RPC infrastructure for the iterator transport layer (be-60kmhm §2.2, §3, §5 IterClose). This includes the shared wire types (IterStartReply, IterNextArgs, IterClose args/reply), the serverIterSession interface, the iterSessionManager with its thread-safe session map + cap enforcement + idle reaper goroutine + drainAll shutdown path, and the IterClose server method. Also wires iterSessionManager into the daemonServer struct and extends both RPC error tables with the two new sentinels.
notes:
## What to build

### internal/storage/rpc/iter_shared.go (NEW — handwritten)
Shared wire types (§2.2):
- IterStartReply{SessionID string; RPCError *RPCError}
- IterNextArgs{SessionID string; BatchSize int}
- IterCloseArgs{SessionID string}
- IterCloseReply{RPCError *RPCError}

serverIterSession interface (§3.1):
- TypeName() string; LastUsedAt() time.Time; Touch(); Close() error

Concrete per-type session example (§3.1) — one per Iter* method (generator emits all but this pattern is established here).

iterSessionManager (§3.2–3.4):
- thread-safe map[string]serverIterSession + sync.RWMutex
- maxCap from GetDaemonIterMax(); idleReap from GetDaemonIterIdleSeconds()*time.Second
- openSession(id, sess): enforces cap, returns ErrTooManyIterators when full
- closeSession(id): idempotent, calls sess.Close()
- reapLoop(): ticker at idleReap/2, calls reapStale(); exits on stopCh close
- reapStale(): removes sessions idle longer than idleReap
- drainAll(): closes all sessions (called from reapLoop on stopCh)
- stats counters: sessionsActive (atomic gauge), sessionStartsTotal, sessionReapedTotal, rowsStreamedTotal

IterClose server method — shared (§5):
```go
func (s *daemonServer) IterClose(args *IterCloseArgs, reply *IterCloseReply) error {
    s.iterMgr.closeSession(args.SessionID)
    return nil  // idempotent — not an error if session missing
}
```

### internal/storage/rpc/server.go
- Wire iterMgr *iterSessionManager field into daemonServer struct
- Add ErrTooManyIterators → "ErrTooManyIterators" and ErrIterSessionNotFound → "ErrIterSessionNotFound" to encodeRPCError table
- Initialize iterMgr in daemonServer constructor with config values
- Stop iterMgr (close stopCh) in daemon shutdown path — AFTER acceptLoop exits

### internal/storage/rpc/client.go
- Add ErrTooManyIterators and ErrIterSessionNotFound cases to decodeRPCError table

## Key implementation notes
- Shutdown ordering (§14 open question 3): iterMgr.stop() must run AFTER acceptLoop exits, so no new IterStart calls arrive after drainAll
- lastUsed field: atomic int64 (unix nano) for lock-free Touch() and LastUsedAt()
- per-type session mu serializes concurrent Next calls for the same session (see §3.1)

## Acceptance criteria
- iterSessionManager: race detector passes (`go test -race ./internal/storage/rpc/...`)
- openSession returns ErrTooManyIterators when len(sessions) >= maxCap
- reapStale removes sessions idle > idleReap duration
- drainAll closes all sessions synchronously
- IterClose is idempotent (safe to call twice or with unknown sessionID)
- `go build ./...` clean

### FINDING 1 — LOW — internal/storage/dbproxy/pidfile/pidfile.go:17

**Category:** Correctness / Data integrity

`StartedAt time.Time `json:"started_at,omitempty"`` — the `omitempty` tag is a no-op for struct types in encoding/json. Go's `isEmptyValue` only omits nil pointers, nil interfaces, and zero-length arrays/maps/strings. A zero `time.Time` serializes as `"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, not as absent.

When daemon code writes a pidfile that does not set `StartedAt`, readers will see a non-null zero timestamp rather than absence, breaking any `!pf.StartedAt.IsZero()` guard.

**Fix:** Change to `*time.Time`. Pointer is nil when unset → omitempty works; IsZero-style checks become nil checks.

---

### FINDING 2 — INFO — internal/configfile/configfile.go:494-502

**Category:** Code quality / Inconsistency

`GetDaemonMode()` dereferences `c.DaemonMode` without a nil guard on `c`, while `GetDaemonIdleSeconds()` and `GetDaemonMaxLifetimeSeconds()` both check `c != nil`. The existing codebase (e.g., `GetDoltMode`) also lacks nil guards, so either remove the checks from the two idle getters (follow existing pattern) or add one to `GetDaemonMode` (follow the idle getter pattern).

Not a blocker — nil configs are not passed in practice — but inconsistency is confusing.

---

### FINDING 3 — INFO — internal/configfile/configfile.go

**Category:** Test coverage

No new tests for `GetDaemonMode`/`GetDaemonIdleSeconds`/`GetDaemonMaxLifetimeSeconds`. These default-value paths are exactly what silently breaks when someone changes a default constant. A 10-line table test would pin the defaults. File a follow-up bead or add inline tests.

After loading cfg from configfile.Load(beadsDir), add daemon probe before existing in-process path:

func openConfiguredStore(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string, readOnly bool) (storage.Storage, error) {
    cfg, err := configfile.Load(beadsDir)
    // ...

    // Daemon-mode probe (new code)
    if cfg != nil && cfg.GetDaemonMode() != configfile.DaemonModeOff {
        if store, ok := tryDaemonClient(beadsDir, cfg); ok {

        }
        // daemon_mode=auto: fall through to in-process
    }

    // In-process path (existing, unchanged)
    // ...
}

tryDaemonClient(beadsDir string, cfg *configfile.Config) (*daemonClient, bool):
1. Read bdd.pid — if absent, use GetCreateDaemonEndpoint to spawn daemon child.
2. Dial bdd.sock with 500ms timeout.
3. Return *daemonClient on success; return nil, false on any failure (log to bdd.log).

title: bdd daemon: daemon child process + lifecycle endpoint
notes:
## Context

Design: be-oyer9z §5 (A4). Part of bdd daemon implementation series.
Depends on: bead be-A (foundation), bead be-C (RPC package), bead be-D (kill module).

## What to build

Two new files:

### 1. cmd/bd/daemon_child.go

Build tag: //go:build !no_dolt (mirroring db_proxy_child.go).

Hidden cobra subcommand: bd daemon-child

Skip root PersistentPreRun/PostRun (no issue-store init, no telemetry spans).
Exit code 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL) when bdd.lock is already held (lost spawn race).

daemonChildRun steps (in order):
1. Acquire bdd.lock via util.TryLock. On lockfile.IsLocked: exit code 75. On other error: return error.
2. Open storage via openConfiguredStore(ctx, beadsDir, false) — must bypass daemon probe to avoid recursion.
   Use a build-tag-gated flag or context value to signal "I am the daemon; skip probe."
3. Readiness probe: call store.GetStatistics(ctx). If error: return it.
4. Listen on Unix socket: net.Listen("unix", sockPath(beadsDir)). Set socket permissions to 0600.
5. Write bdd.pid atomically via internal/atomicfile as JSON:
   {"pid": 12345, "socket": "/path/to/bdd.sock", "version": "v0.14.2", "started_at": "..."}
6. Install signal handlers (SIGTERM, SIGINT) → cancel root context → graceful shutdown.
7. Run errgroup: idleWatcher + acceptLoop + context-cancel-on-signal goroutine.
8. On shutdown: remove bdd.sock and bdd.pid; close store; exit 0.

Flags on daemon-child:
  --root <beadsDir>     (required) beads directory
  --idle-timeout <dur>  default: 5m (from configfile GetDaemonIdleSeconds)
  --max-lifetime <dur>  default: 1h (from configfile GetDaemonMaxLifetimeSeconds)
  --log <path>          default: <beadsDir>/bdd.log

bdd.log rotation: truncate on startup (O_TRUNC) per design §15 Q4.

### 2. cmd/bd/daemon_endpoint.go

GetCreateDaemonEndpoint(beadsDir string, cfg *configfile.Config) (string, error):
- Analogous to GetCreateDatabaseProxyServerEndpoint in endpoint.go.
- Returns socket path (not a TCP endpoint).
- Read bdd.pid → if exists and socket is dialable, return socket path.
- Otherwise acquire bdd.lock, spawn daemon-child via fork-exec, poll for bdd.pid with
  exponential backoff (100ms → 1s, hard timeout 2 min), return socket path.
- Lock hand-off follows same pattern as forkExecChild in endpoint.go.

## Acceptance Criteria

- bd daemon-child is Hidden from help output
- Acquiring bdd.lock while another daemon holds it → exits code 75 (EX_TEMPFAIL)
- bdd.pid written atomically with correct JSON shape (pid, socket, version, started_at)
- Socket file has mode 0600
- Daemon exits cleanly on SIGTERM/SIGINT
- bdd.sock and bdd.pid removed on shutdown; bdd.log left intact
- bdd.log is truncated (O_TRUNC) on startup
- GetCreateDaemonEndpoint returns socket path when daemon is running
- GetCreateDaemonEndpoint spawns daemon when not running
- go build ./... clean (both cgo and no_dolt build tags)

title: bdd daemon: RPC package — types, server, client, error round-trip
notes:
## Context

Design: be-oyer9z §2-3 (A1b + A2). Part of bdd daemon implementation series.
Depends on: bead be-B (bddgen must exist and run first).

## What to build

Package internal/storage/rpc/ — the generated RPC surface for the bdd daemon.

File layout:
  internal/storage/rpc/
  ├── gen.go          // //go:generate directive + package doc
  ├── types.go        // Args/Reply structs + handwritten RPCError (GENERATED)
  ├── server.go       // daemonServer + registered methods (GENERATED)
  └── client.go       // daemonClient satisfying storage.Storage (GENERATED)

Run go generate ./internal/storage/rpc/... to produce types.go, server.go, client.go.
Commit all generated files (not .gitignore'd).

### net/rpc method shape (design §2)

Server methods:
  func (s *DaemonServer) MethodName(args *MethodNameArgs, reply *MethodNameReply) error

### Error round-trip (design §3 — A2)

Each Reply struct embeds RPCError. Server returns nil as RPC method error; client checks reply.RPCError.

encodeRPCError maps 5 sentinels to Kind strings:
  ErrAlreadyClaimed, ErrNotClaimable, ErrNotFound, ErrNotInitialized, ErrPrefixMismatch

decodeRPCError reconstructs sentinels so errors.Is works across the wire.
Parity test to verify this is in bead be-H.

### daemonClient (client.go)

Must satisfy storage.Storage fully.
Must also satisfy storage.StoreLocator via lightweight Locator.Path and Locator.CLIDir RPC pair.
Must NOT satisfy storage.RawDBAccessor (no raw SQL over RPC — security boundary).

### Iter* batch limit

Per design §2 open question Q3: use server-side hard cap + truncation error.
BatchLimit default = 10000. If result count > BatchLimit, set Truncated=true in reply.
Client returns truncation error (not a sentinel) when Truncated=true.

### Concurrency (design §2 / NFR-08)

acceptLoop: go s.rpcServer.ServeConn(conn) per accepted connection.
Each connection served sequentially; connections concurrent.
50 simultaneous connections = NFR-08 satisfied (no additional locking needed at RPC layer).

## Acceptance Criteria

- daemonClient satisfies storage.Storage: all methods implemented
- daemonClient satisfies storage.StoreLocator: Locator.Path and Locator.CLIDir work
- daemonClient does NOT satisfy storage.RawDBAccessor (type assertion returns nil, false)
- errors.Is(err, storage.ErrXxx) works for all 5 sentinels after RPC round-trip
- RPCError is a plain struct with string fields (gob-safe, no explicit gob.Register needed)
- go build ./... clean after generation
- golangci-lint clean or matches baseline

title: bdd daemon: kill module — internal/daemon/kill.go
notes:
## Context

Design: be-oyer9z §7 (A6). Part of bdd daemon implementation series.
Depends on: bead be-A (foundation — for extended pidfile.PidFile struct with SocketPath).

## What to build

New file: internal/daemon/kill.go

Package: daemon

func Kill(beadsDir string) error

Steps (in order):
1. Read bdd.pid — absent → return nil (clean no-op)
2. Parse JSON into pidfile.PidFile. Validate pid is alive via os.FindProcess(pid) + Signal(0).
   If dead but pid file exists (stale): remove bdd.pid and bdd.sock, return nil.
3. Send SIGTERM to the pid.
4. Poll for exit up to 10s (check Signal(0) returns an error indicating process gone).
5. If still alive after 10s: send SIGKILL + wait 2s.
6. Remove bdd.pid and bdd.sock. Leave bdd.log intact.

Kill is used by:
- bd init --reinit (bead be-G)
- Any other reinit/migration flows listed in design §7 table

## Acceptance Criteria

- Kill on non-existent beadsDir returns nil
- Kill on beadsDir with no bdd.pid returns nil
- Kill is idempotent (calling twice is safe)
- Stale pid file (process dead) is cleaned up without error
- bdd.log is NOT removed by Kill
- go build ./... clean

description:
# Reporting surfaces: bd context, bd info, bd where (resolver-driven)

Derived from be-pbnoaa architecture. Wires the existing reporting surfaces to the new `BackendInfo` resolver and renders the result truthfully for both Dolt and Postgres backends.

**Depends on:** the foundation child (resolver + DSN helpers must exist).

## Scope

Three surfaces, one resolver call each, no surface re-implements backend selection.

### `bd context` — `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go`

Bug today (line 49): `Backend: configfile.BackendDolt` is hardcoded. Output reads `type: dolt` even when `metadata.json` says `backend: "postgres"`.

Fix:
1. Replace hardcoded `Backend` with `cfg.GetBackend()` (or directly: call `ResolveBackendInfo`).
2. Add a `BackendInfo` substruct to `ContextInfo`. Existing fields stay populated for Dolt (NFR-1 superset rule).
3. Render text: `Backend:` block with `type`, `mode`, `host`, `port`, `database`, `user`, `sslmode` (PG) or `data dir` (Dolt embedded).
4. Render `Legacy:` block when `BackendInfo.LegacyDoltDir` or `LegacyDoltFields` non-empty: e.g. `Legacy: dolt directory present at .beads/dolt (inactive — backend is postgres)`.
5. JSON output: same fields as text, plus the full `BackendInfo` struct under `backend` key.

### `bd info` — `cmd/bd/info.go`

Bug today (lines 56-57): `database_path` always emitted; `mode` hardcoded to `"direct"`.

Fix:
1. Resolve via `BackendInfo`.
2. For Postgres: emit `mode: "postgres"` and `connection_target: "host:port/database"` (or split fields). **Omit `database_path`** — it has no meaning for PG.
3. For Dolt server: `mode: "server"`, host/port; keep `database_path` as `<beadsDir>/dolt` for back-compat (the path *exists*, even if not actively used).
4. For Dolt embedded: `mode: "embedded"`, retain `database_path`.
5. Drop the literal `"direct"` token everywhere.

### `bd where` — `cmd/bd/where.go`

Bug today: shows the filesystem DB path only. For Postgres-backed rigs the data lives on a TCP server.

Fix:
1. Add a `data lives in:` line that renders:
   - Postgres: `host:port/database`
   - Dolt server: `host:port/database`
   - Dolt embedded: `<beadsDir>/dolt`
2. Keep existing path output for back-compat; `data lives in:` is *additional*, not a replacement, when the filesystem path exists.

## Tests (per §13/§14)

- `TestContextBackendField_BackendMatrix` — verifies top-level `backend` is no longer always `"dolt"` across the 9 matrix cases.
- `TestInfoMode_BackendMatrix` — Dolt embedded → `"embedded"`, Dolt server → `"server"`, Postgres → `"postgres"`. The literal `"direct"` MUST NOT appear in any case.
- `TestWhere_DataLivesIn` — for each backend matrix, the rendered `data lives in:` value matches expectations.
- `TestBdContextJSON_Compatibility` — golden fixture from current `bd context --json` for a Dolt embedded workspace. After the change, the new output must contain every key from the golden file with the same value (NFR-1 superset).
- **Defence-in-depth password leak test** for each surface: capture combined stdout/stderr; assert fixture password (e.g. `s3cretP@ss`) does not appear in any output, ever.

## Acceptance criteria (from §13)

- `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go:49` no longer hardcodes the backend.
- `cmd/bd/info.go:57` no longer hardcodes `"mode": "direct"`. PG → `"mode": "postgres"`, `connection_target` set, no `database_path`.
- `cmd/bd/where.go` includes a `data lives in:` line that renders correctly for each backend.
- Stale-state detection: workspace with `.beads/dolt` present and `backend=postgres` shows `Legacy:` block, not active Dolt.
- All three surfaces work in `--json` form.
- Existing JSON keys preserved (NFR-1 superset).
- No password ever appears in any test fixture's captured output.
- Reporting commands run in <100 ms (no DB open).
- `golangci-lint run ./...` and `go test ./...` pass.

## Out of scope

- Health/reachability checks (those are `bd doctor`'s job, separate child).
- New `bd backend status` command (separate child).

## References

- Architecture: be-pbnoaa §5 (table of surfaces), §7 (sequence diagram for `bd context`), §13 (acceptance items 3-5, 9-11), §14 (test plan items 1-9).

title: be-pbnoaa(3/5): new bd backend status command
description:
# New command: `bd backend status` (generic backend surface)

Derived from be-pbnoaa architecture. Adds the generic surface that subsumes `bd dolt status` over time.

**Depends on:** the foundation child (resolver must exist).

## Scope

Create a new top-level subcommand `bd backend status` that returns truthful backend identity in both text and `--json` form. This is the answer to "what backend am I actually on?" without making the operator guess from `bd context` quirks.

### New code

**`cmd/bd/backend.go`** (new file)

- Cobra command `bd backend` with subcommand `status`. Room to grow (`bd backend ping`, `bd backend version`, etc.) without crowding the top-level namespace.
- Calls `configfile.ResolveBackendInfo(beadsDir)`.
- Output:
  - **Text:** human-friendly block — `backend: postgres`, `mode: postgres`, `host: 127.0.0.1`, `port: 5433`, `database: gm_beads`, `user: beads`, `sslmode: disable`, `healthy: yes/no/skipped`, optional `legacy:` lines.
  - **JSON:** the `BackendInfo` struct verbatim plus a `healthy` boolean from a lightweight probe (see below).

### Lightweight health probe

`bd backend status` should be cheap to run. The probe is a trimmed version of what `bd doctor` will eventually do:

- **Postgres:** `pgxpool.New` with 1 s timeout, `SELECT 1`. No version check, no project_id drift check (those live in `bd doctor`).
- **Dolt server:** existing `runServerHealth`-style ping via `cfg.GetDoltServer*`.
- **Dolt embedded:** report `healthy: skipped` (no live server to probe).

Probe result lands in JSON as `healthy: true/false/null` and in text as `healthy: yes/no/skipped`. Failure → exit 0 with `healthy: false` plus a one-line redacted error; do NOT exit non-zero (this command is diagnostic).

A `--no-probe` flag suppresses the probe entirely (for use in tight loops or CI).

## Tests

- `TestBackendStatus_Text_BackendMatrix` — verify text output for each backend (incl. unconfigured/unknown).
- `TestBackendStatus_JSON_BackendMatrix` — verify JSON shape.
- `TestBackendStatus_PasswordRedacted` — defence-in-depth.
- `TestBackendStatus_NoProbe` — `--no-probe` produces zero connect attempts.
- `TestBackendStatus_HealthyOnReachable` (integration, gated by env or testcontainer) — Postgres reachable → `healthy: true`. Bad host → `healthy: false`, no panic.

## Acceptance criteria (from §13 item 7)

- `cmd/bd/backend.go` defines `bd backend status` and `bd backend status --json`.
- Output equals `BackendInfo` plus a live `healthy` boolean.
- `--no-probe` suppresses the network call.
- Exit code is 0 even when probe fails (diagnostic semantics).
- No password leaks (test enforced).
- `golangci-lint` and `go test` pass.

## Out of scope

- Replacing `bd dolt status`. The redirect is in a separate child.
- Full doctor checks (version, project_id drift) — those stay in `bd doctor`.

## References

- Architecture: be-pbnoaa §5 (NEW row), §13 item 7.
