title: architect: Postgres DSN/defaults and arbitrary host/db configuration
description:
# Architecture — Postgres DSN / defaults / arbitrary host configuration (be-zdhe4l)

**Bead:** be-zdhe4l
**Parent epic:** be-k4ur5v
**Author:** beads/architect (Actual Software Factory)
**Date:** 2026-05-09
**Sibling:** be-pbnoaa (truthful backend reporting). This bead writes the persistence model that be-pbnoaa.1's resolver reads. The two compose; neither blocks the other for design, but be-pbnoaa.1's foundation must land before this bead's runtime-override surfaces depend on `dsn.ParseConnectionTarget`.

---

## 1. Problem

`bd init --backend=postgres` requires a hand-written `--dsn` even when there is a known-good local Postgres cluster running on `127.0.0.1:5433`. Operators are expected to type:

```
postgres://beads@127.0.0.1:5433/<derived-db-name>?sslmode=disable
```

…on every fresh rig — even though the host, port, user, and SSL mode are identical for every rig pointed at the local cluster, and the per-rig database name is the only thing that varies. There is no environment-variable override path for any field other than the password (`BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`); to point a rig at a different Postgres host you must rewrite the DSN by hand or hand-edit `metadata.json`.

This contrasts sharply with the Dolt backend, which carries 13 `BEADS_DOLT_*` env vars covering every connection parameter and supports both embedded and server modes by inference.

The other risk — verified empirically on 2026-05-08 — is environment contamination: if an unrelated `DATABASE_URL` env var is set (e.g. from a Rails project sharing the shell), the operator may *expect* `bd` to honor it. The Explore agent confirmed `bd` does not read `DATABASE_URL` today. We must keep it that way.

**The fix is not adding a new feature — it is two things:**

1. Make the local case **default to working** by discovering the local Postgres cluster (`$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data` → `postmaster.pid` → port). No DSN required.
2. Define a **complete override surface** (CLI flags + env vars + persisted DSN) with crisp precedence rules that `bd context` / `bd doctor` can render verbatim, so operators always know which value won.

---

## 2. Requirements

### Functional (FR-nn)

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                 |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FR-1  | `bd init --backend=postgres` (no `--dsn`, no `--pg-*` flags) succeeds when a local PG cluster is discoverable; persists a complete stripped DSN. |
| FR-2  | Discovery reads `$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data/postmaster.pid` (line 4 = port, line 6 = listen host) when present; falls back to reading `postgresql.conf` `port` and `listen_addresses`. |
| FR-3  | Discovery default user: `beads`. Default sslmode: `disable` (loopback). Default database name: sanitized `--prefix` (or cwd basename) — same rules `resolveInitPrefix` applies today. |
| FR-4  | `bd init --backend=postgres --pg-host=h --pg-port=p --pg-user=u --pg-database=d --pg-sslmode=m` composes a full DSN from the per-field flags + discovery defaults; persists the stripped form. |
| FR-5  | `bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=<full DSN>` keeps current behavior — `--dsn` overrides everything else. Mixing `--dsn` and `--pg-*` is a fatal error. |
| FR-6  | At runtime, `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST`, `BEADS_POSTGRES_PORT`, `BEADS_POSTGRES_USER`, `BEADS_POSTGRES_DATABASE`, `BEADS_POSTGRES_SSLMODE` env vars override the corresponding fields in the persisted DSN before pgx connects. |
| FR-7  | `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` continues to be the only credential channel, runtime-only, never persisted, never logged. Empty falls through to `.pgpass` / peer auth. |
| FR-8  | `bd` does **not** read `DATABASE_URL`, `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`, `PGDATABASE`, or `PGSSLMODE`. (libpq-style env vars contaminate too easily; the `BEADS_POSTGRES_*` prefix is non-negotiable.) |
| FR-9  | The persisted DSN in `metadata.json` is the **single source of truth** for connection identity; per-field metadata fields (`postgres_host`, `postgres_port`, etc.) are NOT introduced. (See §12 Alt B for why.) |
| FR-10 | `bd init --backend=postgres --pg-host=remote.example.com --pg-database=mybd` composes a remote DSN without local discovery. Discovery is short-circuited as soon as any explicit `--pg-*` flag is given. |
| FR-11 | `bd init --backend=postgres --pg-database=existing_db` against a database with an existing `_project_id` row adopts that project ID rather than minting a new one (matches today's `runPostgresInit` path). |
| FR-12 | Re-init guard: a Dolt-backed `metadata.json` requires `--reinit-local` to switch to Postgres (matches today's `guardPostgresInit`). The architecture does not relax this guard. |
| FR-13 | `bd init` writes a `.beads/.discovery_log` (one line, gitignored) recording the discovery result so `bd doctor` can render `discovered local PG at 127.0.0.1:5433 (postmaster.pid)` in the future. |
| FR-14 | A new helper `dsn.BuildFromFields(host string, port int, user, db, sslmode string) string` produces a stripped DSN (zero password) suitable for persistence. Lives in the existing `internal/storage/postgres/dsn` package. |
| FR-15 | A new helper `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides(strippedDSN string) (string, []string)` returns the DSN after applying any `BEADS_POSTGRES_*` env-var overrides plus a list of override field names (for `bd context` to surface which fields were overridden). |

### Non-functional (NFR-nn)

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                |
|-------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NFR-1 | Discovery completes in <50 ms in the happy path (read two short text files; no syscalls beyond stat + read). |
| NFR-2 | Discovery never modifies state on disk. It is pure read. |
| NFR-3 | Runtime env-var overrides do not require re-init; they are applied on every `Open` via `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides`. |
| NFR-4 | No password ever appears in: `metadata.json`, `bd context`, `bd info`, `bd where`, `bd doctor`, `bd backend status`, log files, error messages, or test fixtures. (Same standard as today's `dsn.Strip`.) |
| NFR-5 | When discovery and explicit flags both run, the result is deterministic across machines (same flags + same `metadata.json` ⇒ same composed DSN). |
| NFR-6 | A failed discovery (no local PG cluster) does NOT cause `bd init --backend=postgres --pg-host=...` to fail — discovery only kicks in for the no-flags case. |
| NFR-7 | Backward compat: every existing `bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=...` invocation in tests / docs / scripts continues to work unchanged. |
| NFR-8 | New env vars work even when `bd` is invoked from `gc bd` or any other shell wrapper — they are read at `Open` time, not at process start. |
| NFR-9 | DSN composition from fields produces a string that round-trips through `pgconn.ParseConfig` + `dsn.ConfigToConnString` cleanly (existing strip invariant). |

---

## 3. Constraints

| Type        | Constraint                                                                                                                                                  |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Technical   | `metadata.json` schema is shared with installed `bd` binaries in the wild; **must not** add per-field PG fields (FR-9) — only changes are reads, not writes. |
| Technical   | The `internal/storage/postgres/dsn` package is the canonical home for DSN parse/strip/compose; new helpers (`BuildFromFields`, `ApplyEnvOverrides`) belong here. |
| Technical   | `pgconn.ParseConfig` is the existing parser; reuse it. Round-trip via `dsn.ConfigToConnString` is already tested by `dsn.Strip`. |
| Technical   | Discovery must work on Linux (XDG paths) and macOS (`~/Library/Application Support` is **not** what we use; we follow XDG on macOS too because that is where the existing local cluster lives — `~/.local/share/beads/postgres`). |
| Technical   | The `actual` skill / city-level config (`city.toml [beads] backend = postgres`) is not a source of truth for `bd init` either — it is gc's view, not bd's. (Same boundary be-pbnoaa drew.) |
| Business    | Operators dogfooding the migration must not be required to learn DSN syntax to start a new rig. Today's friction blocks per-rig adoption. |
| Business    | Five rigs already on Postgres (`gm_beads`, `gascity_ga`, `projectwrenunity`, `mcdclient_mc`, `beads_be`). Their persisted DSNs must continue to work without change. |
| Regulatory  | No password in any output, log, support bundle, error string. Same standard as `dsn.Strip` already enforces. |
| Operational | The local PG cluster lifecycle (start/stop/upgrade) is **not** owned by `bd`. We discover, we do not manage. Daemon ownership is out of scope (see §16). |

## 4. Source-of-truth precedence

The single rule: **at runtime, the connection target is the persisted DSN with `BEADS_POSTGRES_*` env-var overrides applied. The persisted DSN is whatever `bd init` composed.**

### Precedence — at `bd init` time (composing the persisted DSN)

1. `--dsn=<full>` if given → use verbatim, strip password, persist.
2. else `--pg-host` / `--pg-port` / `--pg-user` / `--pg-database` / `--pg-sslmode` flags (any subset given) → compose with discovery defaults filling the gaps.
3. else discovery: read local PG cluster's `postmaster.pid` → port + listen host. Defaults: user=`beads`, sslmode=`disable`, database=sanitized prefix.
4. If discovery fails AND no flags given → fatal error with remediation: "no local Postgres cluster found at $XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data; either start it, pass `--pg-host=<remote>`, or pass `--dsn=<full>`."

### Precedence — at runtime (every `bd` invocation)

1. `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST/PORT/USER/DATABASE/SSLMODE` env vars override individual fields of the persisted DSN.
2. `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is composed in last (matches today).
3. pgx defaults / `.pgpass` for anything still empty.

### What is NOT a source of truth

- `DATABASE_URL`, `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`, `PGDATABASE`, `PGSSLMODE` — bd does not read libpq-style env vars (FR-8). They are too easily set by unrelated tools.
- Per-field metadata.json fields (`postgres_host`, `postgres_port`, `postgres_user`, `postgres_database`) — not introduced (§12 Alt B).
- `city.toml [beads] backend` — gc's view, not bd's.
- File existence (e.g. `.beads/dolt`) — that is be-pbnoaa.1's *legacy detector*, not a backend identity signal.
- Live process state (is `postgres` running? is port 5433 listening?) — those are *health* checks (be-pbnoaa.4 doctor), not configuration.

## 5. Configuration UX surfaces

### `bd init --backend=postgres` flag matrix

| Flag                    | Type   | Default        | Notes                                                            |
|-------------------------|--------|----------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `--dsn`                 | string | (none)         | Full DSN; strips password before persistence. Mutex with `--pg-*`. |
| `--pg-host`             | string | (discovery)    | Postgres host. `127.0.0.1` if discovery succeeds.                |
| `--pg-port`             | int    | (discovery)    | Postgres port. From `postmaster.pid` line 4 if discovery succeeds. |
| `--pg-user`             | string | `beads`        | Postgres user. Default matches existing local convention.        |
| `--pg-database`         | string | sanitized prefix | Database name. Per-rig.                                          |
| `--pg-sslmode`          | string | `disable`      | sslmode. `disable` for loopback; explicit `require`/`verify-full` for remote. |
| `--pg-cluster-dir`      | string | `$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data` | Override the discovery directory. Useful for non-default local clusters. |

### Env vars (read at `Open` time, not at process start)

| Name                        | Type   | Effect                                              |
|-----------------------------|--------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST`       | string | Override host in persisted DSN.                     |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_PORT`       | int    | Override port. Invalid → ignore + warn.             |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_USER`       | string | Override user.                                      |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_DATABASE`   | string | Override database.                                  |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_SSLMODE`    | string | Override sslmode. Validated against pgx-allowed set. |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`   | string | Composed in (existing). Never persisted.            |

### What removed / never added

- No `--postgres-database` (long-name) — `--pg-database` is canonical.
- No per-field metadata.json (FR-9).
- No `DATABASE_URL` reading.
- No "auto-discover remote PG" — discovery is local only. Remote requires explicit `--pg-host`.

## 6. Discovery flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start([bd init --backend=postgres]) --> ParseFlags{Parse flags}
  ParseFlags -->|--dsn given| StripDSN[dsn.Strip persist]
  ParseFlags -->|--pg-* flags any| ComposeFlags[Compose from flags + defaults]
  ParseFlags -->|no flags| Discover{Read postmaster.pid}

  Discover -->|file missing| ConfFallback{Read postgresql.conf}
  Discover -->|file present| ParsePidFile[port = line 4, host = line 6]

  ConfFallback -->|file missing| FailDiscovery[fatal: no local PG; suggest --pg-host or start cluster]
  ConfFallback -->|file present| ParseConf[port = port directive, host = listen_addresses]

  ParsePidFile --> DefaultsApplied[user=beads, sslmode=disable, db=sanitized-prefix]
  ParseConf --> DefaultsApplied
  ComposeFlags --> StripDSN
  DefaultsApplied --> StripDSN
  StripDSN --> WriteMeta[Persist stripped DSN to metadata.json]
  WriteMeta --> WriteLog[Append discovery decision to .beads/.discovery_log]
  WriteLog --> Open[storage.Open with composed DSN + BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD]
  Open --> ProjectID[Adopt or mint _project_id]
  ProjectID --> Done([bd init succeeds])
  FailDiscovery --> Exit([exit 1 with remediation])
```

## 7. Runtime flow (every `bd` invocation)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start([bd <subcommand>]) --> LoadMeta[configfile.Load metadata.json]
  LoadMeta --> Backend{cfg.GetBackend}
  Backend -->|dolt| DoltPath[existing path, unchanged]
  Backend -->|postgres| ReadStrippedDSN[strippedDSN = cfg.PostgresDSN]
  ReadStrippedDSN --> ApplyEnv[dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides strippedDSN]
  ApplyEnv --> ComposePassword[dsn.Compose with BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD]
  ComposePassword --> OpenStore[storage.Open with full DSN + 3s timeout]
```

## 8. End-to-end action — `bd init --backend=postgres` (no flags, local discovery)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Op as Operator
  participant CLI as bd init
  participant FS as XDG path
  participant PID as postmaster.pid
  participant CONF as postgresql.conf
  participant DSN as dsn.BuildFromFields
  participant STRIP as dsn.Strip
  participant ST as storage.Open
  participant META as metadata.json
  participant LOG as .beads/.discovery_log

  Op->>CLI: bd init --backend=postgres --prefix=mybd
  CLI->>CLI: validate flags (no --dsn, no --pg-*)
  CLI->>FS: stat $XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data
  alt directory missing
    FS-->>CLI: ENOENT
    CLI->>CONF: stat / read postgresql.conf
    CONF-->>CLI: ENOENT
    CLI-->>Op: FATAL "no local PG cluster; pass --pg-host=<remote> or --dsn=<full>"
  else directory present
    FS-->>CLI: ok
    CLI->>PID: read postmaster.pid (4 lines)
    alt postmaster.pid missing
      PID-->>CLI: ENOENT
      CLI->>CONF: read postgresql.conf
      CONF-->>CLI: port=5433, listen_addresses="127.0.0.1"
    else postmaster.pid present
      PID-->>CLI: pid, datadir, starttime, port=5433, sock, host=127.0.0.1
    end
    CLI->>CLI: derive dbname = sanitize(prefix or cwd-basename)
    CLI->>DSN: BuildFromFields("127.0.0.1", 5433, "beads", "mybd", "disable")
    DSN-->>CLI: postgres://beads@127.0.0.1:5433/mybd?sslmode=disable
    CLI->>STRIP: Strip(...)  (defence-in-depth, even though no pwd in input)
    STRIP-->>CLI: stripped DSN (idempotent)
    CLI->>ST: storage.Open(BackendPostgres, DSN=stripped + BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD)
    alt open fails (e.g. PG not running, missing user)
      ST-->>CLI: error
      CLI-->>Op: FATAL with redacted target + remediation
    else open ok
      ST-->>CLI: store
      CLI->>ST: GetMetadata("_project_id")
      alt _project_id exists in DB
        ST-->>CLI: existing UUID
        CLI->>CLI: cfg.ProjectID = existing
      else
        CLI->>CLI: cfg.ProjectID = configfile.GenerateProjectID()
        CLI->>ST: SetMetadata("_project_id", new UUID)
      end
    end
    CLI->>META: cfg.PostgresDSN = stripped; cfg.Save
    CLI->>LOG: write one-line "discovered local PG at 127.0.0.1:5433 (postmaster.pid)"
    CLI-->>Op: "✓ bd initialized; backend: postgres; target: 127.0.0.1:5433/mybd"
  end
```

1. Operator runs `bd init --backend=postgres --prefix=mybd`.
2. `bd` validates flag mutex: `--dsn` not given, no `--pg-*` flags — discovery path.
3. Stat the XDG cluster dir. If missing, try `postgresql.conf` fallback. If both missing, fatal with remediation.
4. Read `postmaster.pid` (4-line read). Line 4 = port, line 6 = listen host.
5. If `postmaster.pid` missing but the dir exists, fall back to parsing `postgresql.conf` for `port` and `listen_addresses`.
6. Derive database name from `--prefix` (or cwd basename) using the same sanitization `resolveInitPrefix` already applies.
7. Compose DSN via `dsn.BuildFromFields(host, port, user, db, sslmode)`.
8. Idempotently `Strip` the composed DSN (defence in depth — `BuildFromFields` produces no password but Strip is the persistence gate).
9. `storage.Open` against the composed DSN + `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. Failure → fatal with redacted target + remediation hint.
10. On success, adopt or mint `_project_id` (matches today's `runPostgresInit`).
11. Persist stripped DSN to `metadata.json`. Append a single line to `.beads/.discovery_log` documenting the decision.
12. Print a confirmation that names the *resolved target* (host:port/db).

## 9. End-to-end action — runtime env override

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Op as Operator
  participant SH as Shell
  participant CLI as bd <subcommand>
  participant CFG as configfile.Load
  participant ENV as os.Environ
  participant APP as dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides
  participant CMP as dsn.Compose
  participant ST as pgxpool

  Op->>SH: BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST=staging.db ./bd ready
  SH->>CLI: exec
  CLI->>CFG: Load metadata.json
  CFG-->>CLI: cfg{Backend=postgres, PostgresDSN="postgres://beads@127.0.0.1:5433/mybd?sslmode=disable"}
  CLI->>ENV: read BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST/PORT/USER/DATABASE/SSLMODE
  ENV-->>CLI: HOST=staging.db, others empty
  CLI->>APP: ApplyEnvOverrides(persisted DSN, env)
  APP-->>CLI: ("postgres://beads@staging.db:5433/mybd?sslmode=disable", ["host"])
  CLI->>CMP: Compose(overridden DSN, BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD)
  CMP-->>CLI: full DSN (in-process only)
  CLI->>ST: pgxpool.New(ctx, full DSN, 3s timeout)
  alt connect fails
    ST-->>CLI: error
    CLI-->>Op: FATAL "postgres unreachable: staging.db:5433/mybd (overrides applied: host) — err=<wrapped, no DSN>"
  else connect ok
    ST-->>CLI: pool
    CLI->>CLI: run subcommand
  end
```

1. Operator sets `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST=staging.db` in their shell.
2. `bd <subcommand>` loads `metadata.json` as usual.
3. `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` parses the persisted DSN with `pgconn.ParseConfig`, overrides the host field with the env value, returns the recomposed stripped DSN plus `["host"]` indicating which fields were overridden.
4. `dsn.Compose` adds the password from `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`.
5. `pgxpool.New` opens with a 3 s timeout.
6. On error, the wrapped message renders only the redacted target plus the *list of override field names* — operators immediately know which env var influenced the connection.
7. On success, the subcommand runs; subsequent `bd context` will report the override list under `backend.overrides_applied: ["host"]` (a new sub-field — additive, see §12 Alt B compromise).

## 10. Security controls

| Concern                     | Control                                                                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Password in metadata.json   | `dsn.BuildFromFields` produces a passwordless DSN; `dsn.Strip` is idempotent on it. (Existing invariant.) |
| Password in env-override path | `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` operates on the stripped DSN; password is never in scope. Compose happens after. |
| Password in error / log     | Connection errors render `host:port/database (overrides_applied: [...])` only. Wrap pgx errors at the `Open` boundary; drop the upstream pgconn message verbatim (existing pattern in `dsn.Strip`). |
| Cross-project leak          | `_project_id` drift check (be-pbnoaa.4 doctor) catches two rigs that point at the same database with mismatched metadata. |
| Env-var contamination       | We do **not** read libpq-style `PGHOST`/`PGUSER`/`DATABASE_URL`. Operators in mixed-tooling shells will not silently get their Rails URL applied to bd. |
| Discovery filesystem read   | `postmaster.pid` and `postgresql.conf` are read-only. `bd init` does not chmod, chown, write, or delete in the cluster dir. |
| `.discovery_log`            | Line-oriented, no credentials. Path: `.beads/.discovery_log`. Excluded from `git add` via `.gitignore` rule appended at `bd init` time (matches existing `.beads/.pid` pattern). |
| Override visibility         | `bd context`, `bd backend status`, and `bd doctor` all surface `overrides_applied: [host, port]` so operators can see which env vars influenced the connection. (Crucial when reading prod incident output.) |

## 12. Risks

| Risk                                                                                          | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                                                                                              |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Discovery picks up a *stopped* local PG cluster (postmaster.pid stale)                        | M          | M      | `bd init` runs `storage.Open` on the discovered DSN — failure surfaces immediately as a bootstrap error, not a silent misconfig. |
| Operator sets `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST` in their shell rc and forgets, breaking every rig         | M          | M      | `bd context` and `bd backend status` always render `overrides_applied: [...]` so the operator can see the override. (Worth printing prominently — proposed: yellow text in CLI.) |
| Remote DSN with `sslmode=disable` accidentally persisted                                      | M          | M      | `bd init` warns when `--pg-host` is non-loopback and `--pg-sslmode=disable`. Default sslmode for non-loopback host is `require`. |
| `BEADS_POSTGRES_PORT=abc` (non-numeric) silently ignored                                      | L          | L      | `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` validates port as integer, logs a warning, falls through to persisted value.                    |
| Two rigs initialized with the same prefix collide on the same PG database                     | M          | H      | `_project_id` drift check (be-pbnoaa.4 doctor) FAILs immediately. Init prints DB name in the success banner so operator can rename via `--pg-database` on retry. |
| Discovery log fills up disk                                                                   | L          | L      | `.beads/.discovery_log` is one line per init (rare event). Capped at 100 lines via rotation only if needed; not initial scope. |
| pgx version mismatch parses sslmode differently after `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides`                 | L          | M      | `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` round-trips through `pgconn.ParseConfig` + `ConfigToConnString` — the same path `dsn.Strip` uses. Existing strip tests cover the round-trip. |
| Operator runs `bd init --backend=postgres --pg-database=postgres` (the system db)            | M          | H      | `bd init` refuses to use `postgres` as the database name (matches what `runPostgresInit` already does — schema migration would target the system db). Fatal with hint. |
| User has both `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST` and `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` for staging, but accidentally runs against prod metadata.json | M | H | The `overrides_applied` list in `bd context` makes this visible. Doctor prints it in PASS line. We rely on operator awareness; do not auto-block. |

## 13. Trade-offs and alternatives considered

### Alt A: Auto-start the local PG cluster from `bd init`

**Considered.** "Just spin up Postgres for the operator" — no discovery needed, full control.

**Rejected.** The local PG cluster is shared across rigs (and possibly across non-bd uses on the same machine). `bd` is not a daemon manager; that responsibility belongs to a separate process supervisor (systemd user unit, `actual` skill, or operator's manual script). Auto-starting from a bd subcommand creates ambiguous lifetime: who stops it? Reaping orphans is hard. The operational complexity outweighs the convenience. Discovery is sufficient.

### Alt B: Add per-field PG metadata.json entries (`postgres_host`, `postgres_port`, `postgres_user`, `postgres_database`, `postgres_sslmode`)

**Considered.** "Mirror the Dolt pattern: split fields in metadata.json, easy partial overrides."

**Rejected for the persistence layer.** Two sources of truth (DSN + split fields) is an open invitation to drift bugs. The DSN parses cleanly via `pgconn.ParseConfig`; split fields can always be derived. Single-source via `postgres_dsn` keeps the credential-strip invariant air-tight: one field, one `dsn.Strip`, one rule.

**Compromise adopted:** for the *runtime* surface (`bd context --json`, `bd backend status --json`, `bd doctor --json`), expose split fields *derived from the parsed DSN plus env overrides*, alongside `overrides_applied: ["host", ...]`. Reporting consumers get split-field convenience without persistence ambiguity.

### Alt C: Read `DATABASE_URL` / libpq env vars (`PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, …)

**Considered.** "Free compatibility with every other Postgres tool the operator already uses."

**Rejected.** The user explicitly called this out: unrelated `DATABASE_URL` from a Rails project must not drive bd. libpq-style env vars are too noisy in mixed-tooling shells. Operators who *want* their `DATABASE_URL` to drive bd can write a one-line shell wrapper:

```sh
BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST=$(extract host from $DATABASE_URL) bd ready
```

The `BEADS_POSTGRES_*` prefix is non-negotiable.

### Alt D: Discovery via "try-connect" to common ports (5432, 5433, 5434)

**Considered.** "If we don't find a local cluster dir, try connecting."

**Rejected.** Slow (network timeouts), brittle (firewalls), and produces wrong defaults (pointing at a system Postgres unrelated to bd). Filesystem discovery is fast, deterministic, and points at the *bd-managed* cluster only.

### Alt E: Make `--dsn` accept partial DSNs (e.g. `--dsn=host=staging.db`)

**Considered.** "Use the keyword form for partial overrides."

**Rejected.** The `--pg-*` per-field flags are clearer; mixing `--dsn` semantics overloaded for "full or partial" is confusing. Mutex stays.

### Alt F: Make `bd backend set` (or `bd config set postgres.host=...`) the override path instead of env vars

**Considered.** "Persistent overrides without re-init."

**Deferred.** The env-var path covers ad-hoc per-invocation overrides cleanly. A `bd backend set` command can layer on later if persistent overrides become a real need; today every persistent change can be done by re-init or hand-editing the DSN. Not in scope for this bead.

### Alt G: Default sslmode = `require` even for loopback

**Considered.** "Secure by default."

**Rejected.** Loopback PG with `sslmode=require` requires either a valid cert or pgx-side cert relaxation. The local cluster is loopback-only (`listen_addresses = '127.0.0.1'`). `disable` is the pragmatic default. We DO default to `require` for any non-loopback host (FR-12 mitigation).

## 14. Acceptance criteria (for the builder)

A builder follow-up has shipped this work when:

1. `dsn.BuildFromFields(host, port, user, db, sslmode)` exists in `internal/storage/postgres/dsn`. Round-trips through `pgconn.ParseConfig` + `dsn.ConfigToConnString`. Unit tests cover: loopback, remote, user without password, empty sslmode (defaults to disable), explicit sslmode=require.
2. `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides(strippedDSN string) (string, []string)` exists. Reads `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST/PORT/USER/DATABASE/SSLMODE` from `os.Environ()`. Returns the rewritten DSN plus a sorted list of overridden field names. Invalid `BEADS_POSTGRES_PORT` (non-numeric) → ignored + warning logged once. Validated `BEADS_POSTGRES_SSLMODE` against the allowed set (`disable`, `allow`, `prefer`, `require`, `verify-ca`, `verify-full`); invalid → ignored + warning.
3. `cmd/bd/init.go` flag set gains `--pg-host`, `--pg-port`, `--pg-user`, `--pg-database`, `--pg-sslmode`, `--pg-cluster-dir`. `--dsn` and any `--pg-*` flag are mutually exclusive (fatal error on conflict).
4. `cmd/bd/init_postgres.go` `runPostgresInit` accepts the new fields and composes a DSN via `dsn.BuildFromFields` when `--dsn` is empty.
5. New `cmd/bd/init_postgres_discovery.go` with `discoverLocalPostgres(clusterDir string) (host string, port int, found bool)` that reads `postmaster.pid` (preferred) or `postgresql.conf` (fallback). Returns `found=false` cleanly when both are missing — never panics.
6. `runPostgresInit` flow: if neither `--dsn` nor any `--pg-*` flag is given, run discovery. Discovery success → compose DSN with discovered host/port + defaults (user=`beads`, sslmode=`disable`, db=sanitized prefix). Discovery failure → fatal with remediation hint listing the three options (start cluster / use `--pg-host=<remote>` / use `--dsn=<full>`).
7. `runPostgresInit` flow: if only some `--pg-*` flags are given, fill the unspecified fields with discovery defaults *if discovery succeeds*, else with the static defaults (user=`beads`, sslmode for loopback=`disable`, sslmode for non-loopback=`require`, db=sanitized prefix). ## 15. Suggested test plan (regression prevention)

1. **Unit, `dsn.BuildFromFields`** — `TestBuildFromFields_Matrix`: 8 input combinations (loopback / remote × user-only / user+sslmode × empty / explicit db). Each output round-trips cleanly through `pgconn.ParseConfig`.
2. **Unit, `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides`** — `TestApplyEnvOverrides_Matrix`: each of HOST/PORT/USER/DATABASE/SSLMODE individually; all five together; invalid PORT (alpha → ignored); invalid SSLMODE (`bogus` → ignored); empty env → no-op identity. Verify the returned override-name list is alphabetically sorted.
3. **Unit, discovery happy path** — `TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_PostmasterPidPresent`: fixture `postmaster.pid` with realistic 5-line content → returns `(127.0.0.1, 5433, true)`.
4. **Unit, discovery fallback** — `TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_PostgresConfFallback`: fixture cluster dir without `postmaster.pid` but with `postgresql.conf` containing `port = 5433` and `listen_addresses = '127.0.0.1'` → returns `(127.0.0.1, 5433, true)`.
5. **Unit, discovery failure** — `TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_NoCluster`: empty dir → returns `("", 0, false)`. No panic, no error.
6. **Unit, discovery malformed** — `TestDiscoverLocalPostgres_MalformedPid`: `postmaster.pid` with 2 lines (truncated) → returns `("", 0, false)` and a warning. `bd init` falls through to conf or fails with remediation.
7. **Integration, no-flag init** — `TestInit_PostgresLocalDiscovery`: spin up a local PG via existing test harness; run `bd init --backend=postgres --prefix=mybd` with no other flags; assert `metadata.json` `postgres_dsn` matches the discovered target and the rig is queryable.
8. **Integration, partial-flag init** — `TestInit_PostgresPartialFlags`: `--pg-host=127.0.0.1 --pg-database=mybd` (no user, no port, no sslmode) → composed DSN uses discovery for port + static defaults for the rest.
9. **Integration, remote init** — `TestInit_PostgresRemoteFlags`: `--pg-host=remote.example.com --pg-database=mybd` → no discovery, sslmode defaults to `require` (non-loopback host), warning printed.
10. **Integration, env override** — `TestRuntime_HostEnvOverride`: bd init against local PG; then `BEADS_POSTGRES_HOST=staging.db bd ready` → connection error against staging.db (expected; PG not there); error message includes `overrides_applied: [host]`.
11. **Integration, sslmode warning** — `TestInit_NonLoopbackDisableWarns`: `--pg-host=remote.example.com --pg-sslmode=disable` → init succeeds but stderr has `WARNING: sslmode=disable on non-loopback host`.
12. **Integration, system-db rejected** — `TestInit_SystemDbRejected`: `--pg-database=postgres` → fatal exit 1.
13. **Backward-compat smoke** — replay existing `init_postgres_test.go` invocations unchanged; assert all pass.
14. **No-leak smoke** — for every new test file, capture stdout+stderr; assert fixture password not present.
15. **Dogfood smoke** — manually run `bd init --backend=postgres --prefix=test-zdhe4l` against the local 5433 cluster with no other flags; verify rig works end-to-end and `bd context` / `bd backend status` (be-pbnoaa.3) report the discovered target.

---

## 16. Out of scope (for explicit hand-off)

- **Local PG cluster lifecycle** (start/stop/upgrade) — `bd` discovers, does not manage. Daemon ownership belongs to a separate process supervisor.
- **`bd backend set` persistent override command** — env vars cover ad-hoc; persistent changes go through re-init or hand-editing. (See §13 Alt F.)
- **IAM / cloud-managed PG auth** (RDS IAM, Cloud SQL OAuth) — out of scope; covered by `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<token>` plus `.pgpass` rewrites if needed.
- **Connection pooling tuning** (max conns, idle timeout) — sticks with pgx defaults; tunable via separate future bead if needed.
- **Postgres TLS cert paths** (`sslrootcert`, `sslcert`, `sslkey`) — pgx reads them from libpq-style env vars (`PGSSLROOTCERT` etc.) which we DO NOT shadow with `BEADS_POSTGRES_*`. If a builder needs these, extend `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` in a follow-up — not this bead.
- **`gc bd` wrapper UX** — inherits truthful behavior automatically; no separate work.
- **Migration tooling from Dolt to Postgres** — already covered by export → init → import in `cmd/bd/init.go` (existing `--from-jsonl` flag).

---

## 17. Guardrails (downstream agents)

- **Designer:** persistence stays single-source (`postgres_dsn` only). No new metadata.json fields for split host/port/user/db/sslmode (FR-9, §12 Alt B). Reporting surfaces *expose* split fields by parsing the DSN at read time.
- **Designer:** the new flags go on `bd init`, not on a new top-level command. `bd init` is the canonical configuration entry point for a backend.
- **Designer:** `--dsn` and `--pg-*` are mutually exclusive at the flag level. Operators who want both must pass a full `--dsn`.
- **Builder:** never read `DATABASE_URL`, `PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`, `PGDATABASE`, `PGSSLMODE`. Only `BEADS_POSTGRES_*`.
- **Builder:** `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` returns a stripped DSN — `Compose` happens after, in the same place it does today (`store_factory.go`).
- **Builder:** discovery is read-only. `bd init` never writes inside `$XDG_DATA_HOME/beads/postgres/data` — that is the cluster's territory.
- **Builder:** the warning for `--pg-sslmode=disable` on non-loopback is a *warning*, not a failure. Operators with internal-network PG behind a VPN may legitimately use disable.
- **Reviewer:** the password-leak defence-in-depth tests apply to every test file added by this bead. Same gate as be-pbnoaa.

---

## 18. Hand-off checklist

| Item                                                                       | Owner              | Bead label            |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------|-----------------------|
| `dsn.BuildFromFields` + `dsn.ApplyEnvOverrides` helpers                    | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| Local PG discovery (`postmaster.pid` + `postgresql.conf` fallback)         | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| `bd init` flag set (`--pg-host`, `--pg-port`, `--pg-user`, `--pg-database`, `--pg-sslmode`, `--pg-cluster-dir`) | designer → builder | needs-design |
| `runPostgresInit` discovery + composition flow                             | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| `store_factory.go` + `store_factory_nocgo.go` env-override wiring          | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| `--pg-sslmode=disable` non-loopback warning + system-db reject             | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| `.beads/.discovery_log` + `.gitignore` integration                         | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| Reporting integration (be-pbnoaa.1 resolver consumes `ApplyEnvOverrides`)  | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| Defence-in-depth password leak tests (every new test file)                 | designer → builder | needs-design          |
| Smoke: 5 PG rigs + 1 Dolt rig before close                                 | builder            | needs-design          |
acceptance_criteria: Architecture defines intelligent local defaults plus explicit override behavior for arbitrary Postgres hosts/databases/users, including config keys/env vars/CLI flags, credential handling, validation, migration behavior, and tests.
close_reason: Decomposed into 4 builder beads: be-5w6nt9 (DSN helpers, ready now), be-jnxg8d (discovery, blocks be-5w6nt9), be-fsobdu (bd init flow, blocks both), be-s67c8m (runtime wiring, blocks be-5w6nt9). Plan: docs/plans/be-zdhe4l-pg-dsn-defaults.md

title: architect: make bd/gc status report Postgres backend truthfully
description:
# Architecture — Truthful Postgres backend reporting (be-pbnoaa)

**Bead:** be-pbnoaa
**Parent epic:** be-fkq1em
**Author:** beads/architect (Actual Software Factory)
**Date:** 2026-05-08
**Backend snapshot:** Postgres 14+ (default) at `127.0.0.1:5433` from
`/home/jaword/.local/share/beads/postgres/data`; per-rig DBs (e.g.
`gm_beads`, `gascity_ga`, `projectwrenunity`, `mcdclient_mc`, `beads_be`).

---

## 1. Problem

`bd` and `gc` cannot truthfully report the active backend during/after a
Dolt → Postgres migration. The only way Mayor verification could prove
the production city was on Postgres on 2026-05-08 was `strace` of `bd
list` showing TCP connects to `127.0.0.1:5433` plus direct `psql`
queries. Every user-facing reporting surface either lies, omits the
backend, or surfaces stale Dolt metadata as if Dolt were live.

Concretely:

- `bd context` hardcodes `Backend: configfile.BackendDolt` at
  `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go:49`. Output always reads `type: dolt` even when
  `metadata.json` says `backend: "postgres"`.
- `bd info` hardcodes `"mode": "direct"` at `cmd/bd/info.go:57`. Wrong
  for Dolt-server mode and meaningless for Postgres.
- `bd where` shows the *filesystem* DB path (`.beads/dolt` etc.). For
  Postgres-backed rigs the data lives on a TCP server, not on disk —
  the shown path is irrelevant or actively misleading.
- `bd dolt show` and `bd dolt status` error or short-circuit when
  `cfg.GetBackend() != "dolt"`. There is no Postgres equivalent.
- `bd doctor` runs Dolt health checks (`runServerHealth`,
  `CheckDoltStatus`) regardless of backend. There is no Postgres
  reachability/version check. Stale `.beads/dolt` directories are
  reported as if Dolt were active.
- The on-disk `.beads/dolt`, `.beads/.pid`, `.beads/dolt_debug.log`,
  and any `dolt_*` keys still in `metadata.json` are kept verbatim
  through migration. Operators cannot distinguish "dolt currently
  in use" from "dolt left behind, backend is now postgres".
- The `bd dolt status probes SQL when local server is
  externally-managed` fix landed in commit `2a5a9802b` for the Dolt
  case; the same class of bug for Postgres is unaddressed.

The fix is not adding a new feature — it is enforcing a single
*source-of-truth precedence* across every status surface, and teaching
each surface to render whichever backend that resolver says is active.

---

## 2. Requirements

### Functional (FR-nn)

| ID    | Requirement                                                                                                                                       |
|-------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| FR-1  | A single backend resolver returns the active backend (`dolt`/`postgres`), connection target, and configuration source for any `.beads/` workspace |
| FR-2  | `bd context` reports the resolved backend, host/port/database/user, and project ID for both Dolt and Postgres                                     |
| FR-3  | `bd info` reports the resolved backend mode (e.g. `embedded`/`server`/`postgres`), drops the hardcoded `direct`, and shows connection target      |
| FR-4  | `bd where` reports a `data lives in:` line that is correct for both filesystem-backed (Dolt embedded) and network-backed (Postgres, Dolt server)  |
| FR-5  | `bd doctor` runs backend-appropriate health checks: PG reachability + version for Postgres; existing PID/SQL probe for Dolt                       |
| FR-6  | `bd dolt status` and `bd dolt show` exit cleanly with a clear "not applicable; backend is postgres" message when run against a Postgres workspace |
| FR-7  | Stale `.beads/dolt` directories are detected and rendered as `(inactive — backend is postgres)` rather than mistaken for live Dolt state          |
| FR-8  | Stale `dolt_*` fields in `metadata.json` are tolerated but reported as `inactive: backend is postgres` rather than as live config                 |
| FR-9  | A new generic command `bd backend status` (or alias) returns truthful backend identity in both text and `--json` form                             |
| FR-10 | All connection rendering paths strip Postgres passwords as a defence-in-depth check, even though `postgres_dsn` in `metadata.json` is stripped at write time |
| FR-11 | The resolver does not require the database to be open. Failure to connect must not change which backend is reported as configured                 |
| FR-12 | `gc bd` wrapper inherits truthful behavior automatically (it just shells `bd`); the city-level `[beads] backend = postgres` config is not a separate truth source for `bd` itself |

### Non-functional (NFR-nn)

| ID     | Requirement                                                                                                                                   |
|--------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| NFR-1  | No regression in existing Dolt status output. JSON shapes for `bd context --json`, `bd info --json`, `bd dolt status --json` remain compatible — new fields are added, never renamed |
| NFR-2  | Reporting commands run in <100 ms for the read-only `metadata.json` resolution path (no DB open) and <500 ms for paths that ping Postgres     |
| NFR-3  | Postgres password never appears in any output or log line, even if the user has manually edited `metadata.json` to embed credentials         |
| NFR-4  | The resolver fail-open: if `metadata.json` is malformed, surfaces report `backend: unknown` with the parse error rather than defaulting silently to dolt |
| NFR-5  | All new code paths covered by unit tests with the full backend matrix (dolt-embedded, dolt-server, postgres). One regression test per surface |
| NFR-6  | `bd doctor --json` must include a top-level `backend` block listing resolved backend + connection state, suitable for CI/observability scrapers |

---

## 3. Constraints

| Type        | Constraint                                                                                                                                                         |
|-------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Technical   | `metadata.json` schema is shared with installed `bd` binaries in the wild. New fields fine; existing field semantics must not change                              |
| Technical   | `bd context` must keep working without DB open (it is the diagnostic-of-last-resort when the DB cannot be reached)                                                |
| Technical   | `internal/configfile.Config` is the canonical source for backend identity. The Postgres DSN parser lives at `internal/storage/postgres/dsn`                        |
| Technical   | `internal/storage/postgres/open.go` already enforces PG ≥ 14 (`minServerVersionNum = 140000`). Reporting must surface that                                        |
| Technical   | `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` is the only Postgres credential channel. There is no Postgres credentials file (unlike Dolt's `BEADS_CREDENTIALS_FILE`)                  |
| Business    | The Dolt → Postgres migration is in progress across multiple rigs. Some rigs still on Dolt, some on Postgres, some mid-migration. Reporting must work for all three |
| Business    | Operators must not need `strace`/`psql` to verify the active backend. That was the trigger for this work                                                           |
| Regulatory  | No password in any output, log, support bundle, or error string. Same standard as `dsn.Strip` already enforces                                                     |
| Operational | This rig (`beads`) is its own dogfood. Every change here is exercised on `gm_beads` (16920 issues / 120316 events) within hours of merge                          |

---

## 4. Source-of-truth precedence (the resolver contract)

The single rule: **`backend` is whatever `metadata.json` says, full
stop.** Env vars and city config can flip *modes within a backend*
(e.g. Dolt server-vs-embedded) but cannot silently override which
backend is active.

### Precedence — backend identity

1. `metadata.json` `backend` field — case-insensitive, defaults to `dolt`
   when empty (legacy)
2. Nothing else. No env var, no `city.toml`, no DSN sniff.

If `metadata.json` is missing → `backend: unconfigured` (workspace not
initialized). If unparseable → `backend: unknown` plus the parse error.

### Precedence — Dolt connection details

1. `BEADS_DOLT_SERVER_MODE`, `BEADS_DOLT_SHARED_SERVER` — flip
   embedded/server mode
2. `BEADS_DOLT_SERVER_HOST/PORT/USER/SOCKET/TLS/DATABASE/DATA_DIR` —
   override individual fields
3. `metadata.json` `dolt_*` fields
4. `config.yaml` `dolt.host`, `dolt.port` (rig-shared overrides, GH#2073)
5. Hard defaults: `127.0.0.1:3307`, user `root`, db `beads`

Already implemented in `internal/configfile.Config`. The gap is
*reporting* this resolved view, not changing the resolution.

### Precedence — Postgres connection details

1. `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` env var — runtime password injection only.
   Never persisted, never reported.
2. `metadata.json` `postgres_dsn` (credential-stripped) — host, port,
   user, database, sslmode, all parsed via `pgconn.ParseConfig`
3. pgx defaults for anything not in the DSN (peer auth, `.pgpass`,
   port `5432`)

There is no precedent for Postgres host/port env-var overrides at the
moment. We **explicitly defer** that decision to be-zdhe4l (the sibling
configuration bead) — this bead's resolver only needs to *read* what
`metadata.json` already persists.

### What is NOT a source of truth

- Process state (is dolt sql-server running?) — that is a *health*
  check, not an identity check
- File existence (`.beads/dolt` directory, `.beads/.pid` file) — those
  are stale-state detectors, not backend identity
- TCP reachability of `127.0.0.1:5433` — same
- Unrelated `DATABASE_URL` env var — `bd` does not read it (verified
  by the Explore agent: zero references in the codebase). Continue not
  to read it
- `city.toml [beads] backend` — that is **gc's** view, not `bd`'s. The
  city config's job is to know what backend each rig *should* use,
  but `bd` itself is run inside the rig and reads only `metadata.json`.
  If they disagree, the truth-as-installed is `metadata.json`; `gc bd
  doctor` (a separate skin, out of scope here) can detect drift.

---

## 5. Reporting surfaces — concrete file targets

Every surface gets the same treatment: replace ad-hoc backend reads
with the centralized resolver, render whichever backend it returns.

| Surface              | File                         | Current bug                                                                | Fix                                                                                    |
|----------------------|------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `bd context`         | `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go:49`   | Hardcoded `Backend: configfile.BackendDolt`                                | Read `cfg.GetBackend()`. Render Postgres `host:port/database` when backend is postgres |
| `bd context` JSON    | `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go:13`   | `ContextInfo` has only Dolt fields                                          | Add `BackendInfo` substruct that holds resolved backend identity                       |
| `bd info`            | `cmd/bd/info.go:57`          | Hardcoded `"mode": "direct"`                                                | Replace with resolved mode: `embedded` / `server` / `postgres`                         |
| `bd info` (Postgres) | `cmd/bd/info.go:48-58`       | `database_path` makes no sense for Postgres                                 | When backend=postgres, emit `connection_target` instead, omit `database_path`          |
| `bd where`           | `cmd/bd/where.go`            | Reports filesystem DB path only                                             | Add a `data lives in:` line that renders Postgres host:port/db when applicable         |
| `bd dolt show`       | `cmd/bd/dolt.go:1247-1382`   | Errors with cryptic message when backend != dolt                            | Detect early; print friendly redirect: `backend is postgres — try 'bd backend status'` |
| `bd dolt status`     | `cmd/bd/dolt.go:425-484`     | Same                                                                        | Same                                                                                   |
| `bd doctor`          | `cmd/bd/doctor.go:67-325`    | Runs Dolt-only checks; no Postgres reachability                             | Branch on resolved backend; run `pgPing()` for Postgres                                |
| `bd doctor` JSON     | `cmd/bd/doctor.go`           | No top-level backend block                                                  | Add `backend: { type, mode, host, port, database, healthy, error }` for both backends   |
| **NEW** `bd backend status` | `cmd/bd/backend.go` (new) | Does not exist                                                              | Generic surface; works for dolt + postgres; subsumes `bd dolt status` over time        |
| Stale-dolt detector  | shared helper                | No detection                                                                | Returns `(stale: true, reason: "backend is postgres")` for context/where/doctor to render |

### `BackendInfo` resolver — the new abstraction

```go
// internal/configfile/backend_info.go (new file)
type BackendInfo struct {
    Backend          string `json:"backend"`            // "dolt" | "postgres" | "unconfigured" | "unknown"
    Mode             string `json:"mode"`               // "embedded" | "server" | "postgres" | ""
    Host             string `json:"host,omitempty"`     // PG: from DSN; Dolt server: from cfg
    Port             int    `json:"port,omitempty"`     // PG: from DSN; Dolt server: from doltserver.DefaultConfig
    Database         string `json:"database"`           // PG: from DSN dbname; Dolt: cfg.DoltDatabase
    User             string `json:"user,omitempty"`     // PG: from DSN; Dolt: cfg.DoltServerUser
    SSLMode          string `json:"sslmode,omitempty"`  // PG only
    DataDir          string `json:"data_dir,omitempty"` // Dolt embedded only
    ProjectID        string `json:"project_id,omitempty"`
    Source           string `json:"source"`             // always "metadata.json" for now
    LegacyDoltDir    string `json:"legacy_dolt_dir,omitempty"` // path to stale .beads/dolt when backend=postgres
    LegacyDoltFields []string `json:"legacy_dolt_fields,omitempty"` // names of dolt_* fields populated when backend=postgres
    ParseError       string `json:"parse_error,omitempty"`        // when metadata.json is unparseable
}

// Resolve reads metadata.json + env vars and returns the resolved view.
// Does not open the database. Does not ping anything. Pure resolution.
func ResolveBackendInfo(beadsDir string) BackendInfo
```

Every reporting surface calls `ResolveBackendInfo` exactly once and
renders. No surface re-implements backend selection.

### Postgres rendering — defence-in-depth password strip

```go
// internal/storage/postgres/dsn (extend existing package)
func RenderRedacted(dsn string) string  // user@host:port/database?sslmode=...
func ParseConnectionTarget(dsn string) (host string, port int, db, user, sslmode string, err error)
```

`postgres_dsn` in `metadata.json` is already stripped at write time
(`runPostgresInit` calls `dsn.Strip` at `cmd/bd/init_postgres.go:43`).
Reporting code calls `dsn.RenderRedacted` — even if the file was hand-
edited to embed `:password@`, the renderer parses → drops password →
re-marshals. The same path used today in `dsn.Strip` is reused. JSON
output emits `host`/`port`/`database`/`user`/`sslmode` as separate
fields (per `BackendInfo`), never the raw DSN, so even a regex-broken
strip can't leak.

### Stale Dolt artifact detection

```go
// internal/configfile/legacy.go (new file)
func DetectLegacyDoltState(beadsDir string, cfg *Config) (
    legacyDir string,        // .beads/dolt path if it exists and backend!=dolt
    legacyFields []string,   // names of dolt_* fields populated in metadata.json when backend=postgres
)
```

Detection rule: if `cfg.GetBackend() == BackendPostgres` AND
`.beads/dolt` exists, that directory is *legacy*. Same for any
populated `dolt_mode`, `dolt_server_*`, `dolt_database`,
`dolt_data_dir`, `global_dolt_database` field while backend=postgres.

### `bd doctor` — Postgres health check

Add a check function:

```go
// internal/doctor/postgres.go (new file)
func CheckPostgresHealth(ctx context.Context, info BackendInfo) DoctorResult
```

Steps:
1. If `info.Backend != "postgres"` → not applicable, skip.
2. Parse the persisted DSN; report parse failure as a doctor failure.
3. Compose with `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`; report missing password as a
   warning (peer auth / `.pgpass` may still work).
4. Open a `pgxpool` with a 3 s timeout. Run `SELECT
   server_version_num`. Report version, `host:port/database`, and
   reachability. Failure = doctor error.
5. Cross-check `_project_id` row in DB matches `metadata.json`
   `project_id` (the same drift check `bd init --backend=postgres`
   does today, lifted into doctor — defends against a rig pointing at
   the wrong PG database).

`bd doctor --json` gains:

```json
{
  "backend": {
    "type": "postgres",
    "mode": "postgres",
    "host": "127.0.0.1",
    "port": 5433,
    "database": "beads_be",
    "user": "beads",
    "sslmode": "disable",
    "version": "140012",
    "healthy": true,
    "project_id_match": true,
    "legacy_dolt_dir": "/home/jaword/projects/beads/.beads/dolt",
    "legacy_dolt_fields": ["dolt_mode", "dolt_server_host"]
  }
}
```

---

## 6. Resolver decision flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Start([Reporting surface invoked]) --> ReadMeta{Read .beads/metadata.json}
  ReadMeta -->|missing| Unconfigured[Backend: unconfigured]
  ReadMeta -->|parse error| Unknown[Backend: unknown + parse_error]
  ReadMeta -->|ok| GetBackend{cfg.GetBackend}

  GetBackend -->|dolt| DoltMode{cfg.IsDoltServerMode}
  DoltMode -->|true| DoltServer[Mode: server, Host/Port from cfg + env, Database from cfg]
  DoltMode -->|false| DoltEmbedded[Mode: embedded, DataDir from cfg.GetDoltDataDir]

  GetBackend -->|postgres| PGParse{dsn.ParseConnectionTarget cfg.PostgresDSN}
  PGParse -->|error| PGBadDSN[Backend: postgres, parse_error: ...]
  PGParse -->|ok| PGFields[Mode: postgres, Host/Port/Database/User/SSLMode from DSN]

  DoltServer --> CheckLegacy{Detect legacy state}
  DoltEmbedded --> CheckLegacy
  PGFields --> CheckLegacy
  PGBadDSN --> CheckLegacy

  CheckLegacy -->|backend=postgres + .beads/dolt exists| LegacyDir[LegacyDoltDir = path]
  CheckLegacy -->|backend=postgres + dolt_* fields set| LegacyFields[LegacyDoltFields = names]
  CheckLegacy -->|else| Done([Return BackendInfo])
  LegacyDir --> Done
  LegacyFields --> Done
  Unconfigured --> Done
  Unknown --> Done
```

---

## 7. End-to-end action — `bd context`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Op as Operator
  participant CLI as bd context
  participant FS as Filesystem
  participant CFG as configfile.Load
  participant RES as ResolveBackendInfo
  participant DSN as dsn.ParseConnectionTarget
  participant LEG as DetectLegacyDoltState
  participant OUT as Renderer

  Op->>CLI: bd context [--json]
  CLI->>FS: Resolve .beads dir (BEADS_DIR env -> walk-up)
  CLI->>CFG: Load metadata.json
  alt missing
    CFG-->>CLI: nil cfg
    CLI->>RES: Resolve(beadsDir, nil)
    RES-->>CLI: BackendInfo{Backend: unconfigured}
  else parse error
    CFG-->>CLI: error
    CLI->>RES: Resolve(beadsDir, nil-with-error)
    RES-->>CLI: BackendInfo{Backend: unknown, ParseError: ...}
  else ok
    CFG-->>CLI: cfg
    CLI->>RES: Resolve(beadsDir, cfg)
    RES->>RES: cfg.GetBackend()
    alt backend == postgres
      RES->>DSN: ParseConnectionTarget(cfg.PostgresDSN)
      DSN-->>RES: host, port, db, user, sslmode
    else backend == dolt
      RES->>RES: cfg.IsDoltServerMode + GetDolt* + doltserver.DefaultConfig
    end
    RES->>LEG: DetectLegacyDoltState(beadsDir, cfg)
    LEG-->>RES: legacyDir, legacyFields
    RES-->>CLI: BackendInfo
  end
  CLI->>OUT: Render(BackendInfo, jsonOutput)
  OUT-->>Op: Repository / Backend / Legacy sections
```

1. Operator runs `bd context` (text or `--json`).
2. CLI resolves the `.beads` directory via the existing
   `selectedNoDBBeadsDir`/walk-up logic — unchanged.
3. CLI calls `configfile.Load(beadsDir)` to load `metadata.json`.
4. Branch a: if file missing, resolver returns
   `BackendInfo{Backend: "unconfigured"}` and the renderer prints
   `Backend: not configured (run bd init)`.
5. Branch b: if parse error, resolver returns
   `BackendInfo{Backend: "unknown", ParseError: …}` and the renderer
   prints the parse error so the operator knows to fix the file.
6. Branch c (normal path): resolver inspects `cfg.GetBackend()`.
7. If `backend=postgres`, resolver calls
   `dsn.ParseConnectionTarget(cfg.PostgresDSN)` to extract host, port,
   database, user, sslmode. No DB connect.
8. If `backend=dolt`, resolver calls existing `cfg.IsDoltServerMode`
   and `cfg.GetDolt*` accessors plus `doltserver.DefaultConfig` for
   the runtime port — same logic context_cmd.go runs today.
9. Resolver runs `DetectLegacyDoltState` to see if `.beads/dolt`
   exists or any `dolt_*` field is populated while backend=postgres.
10. Resolver returns the unified `BackendInfo` struct.
11. Renderer prints text (`Backend:` block with `type`, `mode`,
    `host`, `port`, `database`, `user`, `sslmode`/`data dir` as
    appropriate) plus a `Legacy:` block if any legacy artifacts
    were detected, or emits the JSON shape verbatim.

---

## 8. End-to-end action — `bd doctor` Postgres health

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  autonumber
  participant Op as Operator
  participant DOC as bd doctor
  participant RES as ResolveBackendInfo
  participant ENV as BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD
  participant CMP as dsn.Compose
  participant PG as Postgres
  participant OUT as Renderer

  Op->>DOC: bd doctor [--json]
  DOC->>RES: Resolve(beadsDir, cfg)
  RES-->>DOC: BackendInfo{Backend: postgres, Host, Port, Database, User}
  DOC->>ENV: read BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD
  alt env empty
    DOC->>OUT: warn "no BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD; relying on .pgpass / peer auth"
  end
  DOC->>CMP: Compose(strippedDSN, password)
  CMP-->>DOC: full DSN (in-process only, never logged)
  DOC->>PG: pgxpool.New(ctx, fullDSN) with 3s timeout
  alt connect fails
    PG-->>DOC: error
    DOC->>OUT: FAIL "postgres unreachable: host=... port=... err=..."
  else connect ok
    DOC->>PG: SELECT current_setting('server_version_num')
    PG-->>DOC: "140012"
    DOC->>PG: SELECT value FROM bd_metadata WHERE key='_project_id'
    PG-->>DOC: project_id
    alt mismatch with metadata.json
      DOC->>OUT: FAIL "project_id drift; pointing at wrong PG database"
    else match
      DOC->>OUT: PASS "postgres healthy: 14.0.12 at host:port/database"
    end
  end
  DOC->>OUT: Render full doctor report (incl. backend block in --json)
```

1. Operator runs `bd doctor`.
2. Doctor calls the resolver and gets `BackendInfo`.
3. Doctor reads `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD`. Empty is a warning, not a
   failure (peer auth / `.pgpass` may still allow connection).
4. `dsn.Compose` reconstructs the full DSN in process — never logged
   or written.
5. Doctor opens a 3 s pgx pool. Failure → doctor FAIL with redacted
   target.
6. Doctor runs the version query (`current_setting('server_version_num')`)
   to confirm PG ≥ 14.
7. Doctor reads `_project_id` from the database (the same value
   `runPostgresInit` writes at `cmd/bd/init_postgres.go:115`).
8. Doctor compares against `metadata.json` `project_id`. Mismatch →
   FAIL: the rig is pointing at a different PG database than was
   originally provisioned. This is the cross-project leak check
   (GH#2372) lifted from init into doctor.
9. On match, doctor renders PASS with version + redacted target.
10. The `--json` doctor report gains a top-level `backend` block
    suitable for CI scrapers and observability dashboards.

---

## 9. Security controls

| Concern               | Control                                                                                                                                  |
|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Password in output    | `dsn.RenderRedacted` always re-parses + re-marshals via `pgconn.ParseConfig`/`ConfigToConnString` with empty password. JSON output never includes raw DSN, only host/port/db/user/sslmode |
| Password in logs      | Doctor FAIL messages render the redacted target only. Pgxpool errors are wrapped to drop the upstream pgconn message verbatim (already pattern in `dsn.Strip`) |
| Password at rest      | Already enforced: `runPostgresInit` calls `dsn.Strip` at `cmd/bd/init_postgres.go:43` before persisting. No change                       |
| Password in env dump  | Doctor / context / info do **not** emit `os.Environ()`. If we ever add an "env capture" mode for support bundles, exclude `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` and `BEADS_DOLT_PASSWORD` |
| Project-ID drift      | Doctor health check compares `metadata.json` `project_id` to DB `_project_id`. Mismatch → FAIL                                           |
| Hand-edited DSN       | Defence in depth: `dsn.RenderRedacted` always re-strips. If `pgconn.ParseConfig` fails on a malformed DSN, surface the parse error, do not echo the input |
| TLS mode visibility   | sslmode is emitted as a separate field; reviewers can see at a glance whether prod is `disable`, `require`, `verify-full`                |

---

## 10. Integrations / observability

| System              | Direction | Protocol | Auth                          | Notes                                                                                |
|---------------------|-----------|----------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Postgres backend    | bd → PG   | pgx + TLS | password env / .pgpass / peer | Existing connection. Health check piggy-backs on the same pool path                  |
| Dolt sql-server     | bd → Dolt | MySQL wire | password env / credentials file | Existing                                                                          |
| `gc bd` wrapper     | shell     | n/a      | n/a                           | Inherits `bd context`/`bd doctor` truthful output by default                         |
| `gc rig list/status` | gc → rig | exec `bd context --json`      | n/a              | Architectural hint only — `gc` should consume the new `BackendInfo` JSON shape       |
| CI / observability  | scrape    | exec `bd doctor --json`       | n/a              | New top-level `backend` block enables backend-aware dashboards                       |

---

## 11. Risks

| Risk                                                                                       | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation                                                                                                              |
|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|--------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| JSON shape change for `bd context --json` breaks downstream scrapers                       | M          | M      | Add new fields, never rename existing. Keep `dolt_mode`, `server_host`, `server_port`, `database`, `data_dir` populated for Dolt — only the top-level `backend` field changes from constant `dolt` to resolved value |
| Doctor PG ping adds latency on every doctor run                                            | M          | L      | 3 s timeout. Can be skipped via existing `--quick` family of flags (or add `--skip-pg-ping`)                            |
| Password leak via `pgxpool` error containing the user-supplied DSN                         | L          | H      | Wrap pool errors at the doctor / store_factory boundary; render only redacted target. Test specifically for this leak  |
| `_project_id` drift check fails for rigs that legitimately share a Postgres database       | M          | M      | The current `runPostgresInit` already supports this: it adopts an existing `_project_id` from the DB. Doctor inherits that — drift only means the in-rig metadata.json and DB disagree, which IS a real bug |
| Stale `.beads/dolt` rendered as legacy is interpreted as "I should delete it"              | M          | M      | Doctor REMEDIATION text says "Verify Postgres is healthy via `bd doctor`, then archive: `bd dolt archive` (Dolt skill) or `mv .beads/dolt .beads/dolt.legacy.<date>`". Do NOT auto-delete |
| Operator hand-edits `metadata.json` to switch backend without `bd init`                    | L          | M      | Resolver respects whatever the file says. Doctor's project_id drift check will surface the inevitable failure. Document this is unsupported |
| `gc bd doctor` (a different rig's wrapper) interprets `bd doctor --json` differently       | L          | L      | This bead defines the JSON shape and its stability contract; gc skill consumers can be updated independently            |

---

## 12. Trade-offs and alternatives considered

### Alt A: Add `bd backend status` and leave existing surfaces alone

**Considered.** Cheaper to ship; one new command, one resolver, no edits
to context/info/where/doctor.

**Rejected.** The bead's complaint is that the existing surfaces lie.
Adding a *new* surface that tells the truth doesn't help — operators
will run `bd context` first because that's what they know. Fix the
existing surfaces; the new `bd backend status` is a bonus, not a
substitute.

### Alt B: Resolver returns a string only ("dolt" / "postgres")

**Considered.** Smaller blast radius.

**Rejected.** Most surfaces need host/port/database/data-dir as well.
Returning a string forces every surface to re-implement the field
extraction. The whole point is to centralize the resolution.

### Alt C: Make `bd dolt status` polymorphic (works for postgres too)

**Considered.** Avoids the new command.

**Rejected.** `bd dolt` is a Dolt-namespaced subtree. Hijacking
`bd dolt status` to print Postgres info will confuse anyone reading
help text. Better to add `bd backend status` and keep `bd dolt
status` Dolt-only with a friendly redirect message when run on a
Postgres workspace.

### Alt D: Auto-delete stale `.beads/dolt` when migration is detected

**Strongly rejected.** Data deletion belongs to a deliberate operator
action with explicit confirmation. Surface the legacy state, suggest
the remediation, do not act. The mayor's verification on 2026-05-08
intentionally preserved old state; we honor that.

### Alt E: Read `city.toml [beads] backend` as the truth source

**Rejected.** `bd` is the rig's tool; `city.toml` is `gc`'s view of
the city. They can disagree (e.g. operator manually re-inits a rig as
postgres while city.toml still says dolt). The right answer is: each
tool reads its own config; `gc bd doctor` (when it exists) cross-
checks them.

### Alt F: Postgres connection details parsed lazily on each surface

**Rejected.** That is what we have today, and that is why every
surface gets it slightly wrong. Centralize.

---

## 13. Acceptance criteria (for the builder)

A builder follow-up has shipped this work when:

1. `internal/configfile.ResolveBackendInfo` exists, returns the struct
   above, has unit tests covering: dolt-embedded, dolt-server (TCP),
   dolt-server (Unix socket), postgres (valid DSN), postgres (DSN parse
   error), missing metadata.json, malformed metadata.json, postgres
   with stale `.beads/dolt`, postgres with stale `dolt_*` fields.
2. `internal/storage/postgres/dsn.RenderRedacted` and
   `dsn.ParseConnectionTarget` exist with unit tests asserting no
   password leaks across malformed / valid / hand-edited inputs.
3. `cmd/bd/context_cmd.go:49` no longer hardcodes the backend; the new
   `BackendInfo` flows into `ContextInfo`. Text and `--json` output
   include resolved backend, mode, host, port, database, user,
   sslmode/data_dir.
4. `cmd/bd/info.go:57` no longer hardcodes `"mode": "direct"`. For
   Postgres, `"mode": "postgres"` and `"connection_target":
   "host:port/database"` (no `database_path`). For Dolt server,
   `"mode": "server"` and host/port. For Dolt embedded, `"mode":
   "embedded"` and `"database_path"` retained.
5. `cmd/bd/where.go` includes a `data lives in:` line that renders
   `host:port/database` for Postgres / Dolt server and the data dir
   path for Dolt embedded.
6. `cmd/bd/dolt.go` `bd dolt show` and `bd dolt status` exit `0` with
   a message `backend is postgres — try 'bd backend status'` when
   run on a Postgres workspace, both text and `--json`.
7. `cmd/bd/backend.go` (new) defines `bd backend status` and
   `bd backend status --json`. Output equals `BackendInfo` plus a
   live `healthy` boolean from the same probe `bd doctor` runs.
8. `cmd/bd/doctor.go` runs `CheckPostgresHealth` when backend is
   postgres. `bd doctor --json` includes a top-level `backend` block.
   `bd doctor` prints PASS/FAIL with the redacted Postgres target.
9. Stale-state detection: a workspace with `.beads/dolt` present and
   `backend=postgres` shows it as `Legacy: dolt directory present at
   <path> (inactive — backend is postgres)` in `bd context` and as a
   doctor INFO entry, NEVER as a doctor FAIL.
10. Password redaction tests: for every `*_test.go` file touched in
    this change, add a test that captures the command's combined
    stdout/stderr and asserts the fixture password (e.g.
    `s3cretP@ss`) does not appear. This is a defence-in-depth gate.
11. JSON compatibility tests: `bd context --json` for an unchanged
    Dolt embedded workspace emits a JSON object that is a *superset*
    of the pre-change shape — old keys still present with old values.
12. `golangci-lint run ./...` passes (baseline warnings tolerated).
    `go test ./...` passes.

---

## 14. Suggested test plan (regression prevention)

1. **Unit, configfile.** `TestResolveBackendInfo_Matrix` — table test
   over all 9 combinations listed in (1) above.
2. **Unit, dsn.** `TestRenderRedacted_NeverLeaksPassword` — fuzz
   inputs (valid DSN, malformed, hand-edited with embedded password,
   double-encoded password) and assert the output never contains the
   original password substring.
3. **Unit, info.** `TestInfoMode_BackendMatrix` — Dolt embedded =
   "embedded"; Dolt server = "server"; Postgres = "postgres". Drop
   the hardcoded "direct".
4. **Unit, context.** `TestContextBackendField_BackendMatrix` —
   verifies top-level `backend` is no longer always "dolt".
5. **Unit, dolt.** `TestDoltStatus_RedirectsForPostgres` and
   `TestDoltShow_RedirectsForPostgres` — exit 0, friendly message,
   no Dolt fields populated.
6. **Unit, where.** `TestWhere_DataLivesIn` — for each backend
   matrix, the rendered `data lives in:` value matches expectations.
7. **Integration, doctor.** `TestDoctor_PostgresHealth_HappyPath`
   spins up an embedded testcontainer or uses the existing test PG
   harness; asserts FAIL on bad host, PASS on reachable, FAIL on
   project_id drift.
8. **Regression, legacy detection.** `TestLegacyDoltDir_NotFlaggedAsLive`
   — create `.beads/dolt` directory, `metadata.json` with
   backend=postgres, run `bd context` and `bd doctor`, assert
   nowhere does it report Dolt as live.
9. **Regression, JSON superset.** `TestBdContextJSON_Compatibility` —
   golden fixture from current `bd context --json` for a Dolt
   embedded workspace. After the change, the new output must
   contain every key from the golden file with the same value.
10. **Smoke, dogfood.** Run `bd context`, `bd info`, `bd where`,
    `bd doctor`, `bd backend status` against `gm_beads`,
    `gascity_ga`, `projectwrenunity`, `mcdclient_mc`, `beads_be` on
    127.0.0.1:5433 and `.beads.bak-2026-05-06-prePG` (Dolt). Capture
    output verbatim; eyeball that no surface lies. This is the
    smoke test that would have caught the original bug.

---

## 15. Guardrails (downstream agents)

- **Designer:** any new commands or output formats land in
  `cmd/bd/`. Do not add a separate Postgres CLI subtree (e.g.
  `cmd/bd/postgres/`) — `bd backend status` is the single generic
  surface; backend-specific subcommands stay under `bd dolt`.
  Postgres-specific helpers, if any, live in
  `internal/storage/postgres/`.
- **Designer:** the `BackendInfo` struct is the cross-package
  contract. It belongs in `internal/configfile` (lives with the
  Config it derives from). Importing `configfile` from `cmd/bd/`
  matches the existing pattern.
- **Builder:** never log, render, or store
  `BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or any composed full DSN. Use
  `dsn.RenderRedacted` for any output path.
- **Builder:** do not change the `metadata.json` schema (no new
  fields, no removed fields) in scope of this work. The resolver
  reads what's already there. New fields are be-zdhe4l's concern.
- **Reviewer:** the password-leak defence-in-depth tests are
  non-negotiable. Every new test file touching reporting must
  include one.

---

## 16. Out of scope (for explicit hand-off)

- Postgres host/port/db/user **override mechanisms** (env vars, CLI
  flags). Defer to **be-zdhe4l** which is the configuration UX bead.
- Auto-cleanup of legacy `.beads/dolt` directories. Deletion is
  always an explicit operator action.
- `gc rig list/status` aggregation across rigs. That's `gc`'s
  surface; it just consumes `bd backend status --json`.
- `gc bd doctor` cross-check between `city.toml` and rig
  `metadata.json`. Separate work item.
- Dolt → Postgres data migration tooling (already covered by the
  export → init → import path documented in `cmd/bd/init.go`).

---

## 17. Hand-off checklist

| Item                                                | Owner              | Bead label        |
|-----------------------------------------------------|--------------------|-------------------|
| Implement `configfile.ResolveBackendInfo`           | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Implement `dsn.RenderRedacted` + `ParseConnectionTarget` | designer → builder | needs-design |
| Wire `bd context` to resolver                       | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Wire `bd info` to resolver                          | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Wire `bd where` to resolver                         | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Add `bd backend status` command                     | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Add Postgres branch to `bd doctor`                  | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Friendly redirect for `bd dolt status`/`show` on PG | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Stale-state detection helper + rendering            | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Defence-in-depth password leak tests                | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| JSON-superset compatibility test for `bd context`   | designer → builder | needs-design      |
| Smoke run against five PG-backed and one Dolt-backed rig before close | builder | needs-design |
acceptance_criteria: Architecture identifies every user-facing status/info/context path that can misreport Dolt during a Postgres-backed migration; proposes source-of-truth rules for backend, host, database, health, and stale legacy Dolt dirs; defines tests/doctor checks to prevent regressions.
