title: Address PR #3462 review: justify or rescope MigrateUp stderr progress
description:
PR #3462 (fix-be-8ja-rebuild) — feat(schema): stderr progress + large-rig warning for MigrateUp — got a COMMENTED review from @coffeegoddd on 2026-05-07. Not a hard CHANGES_REQUESTED, but the reviewer is questioning the premise and wants details before approving.

## Reviewer feedback (2026-05-07T19:37Z)

> I'm not sure emitting to stderr will prevent an orchestrator from interrupting a `bd init` command before it completes. MigrateUp is (or should be) only run during initialization, if its not I think this is a bug.
>
> Also, if `bd init` is not completing quickly, this is bug too. I should really only be used to initialize a fresh bd instance, and existing bd repos should be migrated with `bd backup sync/restore` workflow.
>
> Can you provide more details on what bd command you are running that agents/orchestrators want to kill, believing its hung?

## Action

Reply on the PR with:

1. **Concrete repro** — which bd command is being killed by the orchestrator, against what kind of rig, how long it sat silent before the kill.
2. **Where MigrateUp is invoked outside `bd init`** — if that's actually the case (the reviewer's mental model is "MigrateUp only runs in init"), document it. If the reviewer's model is right and it shouldn't run elsewhere, the right fix is removing those call sites, not adding stderr progress.
3. **Why stderr beats `bd backup sync/restore`** — i.e., justify keeping the existing PR scope vs. switching to the migration-via-restore workflow the reviewer is suggesting.

If the answer is "the reviewer is right, this should not be a feature on MigrateUp," close the PR and file a different fix.

PR URL: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/3462
Branch: fix-be-8ja-rebuild
close_reason: PR reply was posted 2026-05-07 explaining MigrateUp runs on every store Open (not just bd init), repro scenario, and two options (stopgap vs bd migrate). Reviewer (coffeegoddd) acknowledged and suggested explicit bd migrate command. PR #3462 closed. Follow-up: file bead for bd migrate UX.

title: Address PR #3461 review: push CountIssues to issueops + add benchmark
description:

## Reviewer feedback (2026-05-07T19:30Z)

> This PR is touching too many layers at once. This optimization should first be made at the lowest layer (issueops) and new CountIssues methods can be added there with more performant SQL queries. We should also get a benchmark of the new SQL being faster than the current/alternative. Ideally the application wont need to do any special handling and can just call the new store CountIssues methods, but those are the first step.

3. Strip application-layer special-casing — call sites should just call the new store methods.

title: Address PR #3458 review: refactor narrow-projection into issueops layer
description:
PR #3458 (release/be-nu4.3-stack) — perf(storage): SearchIssueSummaries narrow-projection list — got CHANGES_REQUESTED from @coffeegoddd on 2026-05-07.

## Reviewer feedback (2026-05-07T19:19Z)

> This is too complicated, and theres too much going on in this pr to reason about. Its touching too many layers of the stack at once.
>
> I think we should start from the database layer (issueops) and define specific methods needed that return the exact set of columns required by they application, and specific times. Once we establishes these, its trivial for the application to call these methods on the store. My suspicion is that most of this can largely be done with SQL queries without so many application code changes.

## Action

Refactor PR #3458 along these lines:

1. Move the optimization into `internal/storage/issueops/` as new narrow-projection methods (one per call-site shape), each returning the exact columns that call-site needs.
2. Drop the application-layer plumbing — call sites should just call the new store methods.
3. Most of the work should be SQL-side, not app-side.

title: Implement -tags no_dolt build for PG-only bd binary (per be-mc9whz design)
description:
Land the no_dolt build tag designed in be-mc9whz. Single PR per designer recommendation: file renames + new files + CI entry MUST land together to avoid a half-state where the build matrix is broken.

Target: ≤ 60 MiB stripped binary. Strips github.com/dolthub/* and internal/storage/dolt|embeddeddolt|doltdriver|doltserver from PG-only build.

Full design lives in be-mc9whz notes (~17 file moves/edits + new files; file-by-file in design §11; done-when in §13).
notes:
# Implementation hand-off — -tags no_dolt build (be-mc9whz)

Full design: `bd show be-mc9whz`. Architect parent: be-ef3q3u (cold-start RAM budget — Option B).

## Scope (single PR — file renames + new files + CI entry MUST land together)

1. **Build-tag matrix per design §2**: 3-level naming `*_dolt_cgo.go`, `*_dolt_nocgo.go`, `*_no_dolt.go` (mirrors the cgo × no_dolt 2D matrix explicitly).

2. **doltdriver split** (design §3): 3 files in internal/storage/doltdriver/.
   - `doltdriver_dolt_cgo.go` — //go:build !no_dolt && cgo (renamed from doltdriver.go)
   - `doltdriver_dolt_nocgo.go` — //go:build !no_dolt && !cgo (renamed from doltdriver_nocgo.go)
   - `doltdriver_no_dolt.go` — //go:build no_dolt — registers BackendDolt with a factory returning ErrNoDoltSupport / NoDoltSupportErrMsg. NO transitive Dolt deps from this file.

3. **store_factory split** (design §4): 3 files in cmd/bd/.
   - The `_no_dolt.go` variant intercepts `backend=dolt` early with NoDoltBinaryMsg (cleaner than letting the registry stub error stand alone).

4. **Subcommand gating** (design §5): `//go:build !no_dolt` headers on `dolt*.go`, `backup_dolt*.go`, `federation*.go` in cmd/bd/. Optional cobra stub commands print install-guidance when invoked under no_dolt.

5. **beads.go split** (design §6): `_dolt.go` keeps Open / OpenFromConfig; `_no_dolt.go` stubs them with ErrDoltUnavailable. `OpenWithBackend` works under both.

6. **Test surface audit** (design §7): prefer `!no_dolt` exclusion over refactor for tests that touch Dolt symbols outside `dolt_only` tag.

7. **CI matrix entry** (design §8 + §9):
   - Makefile target: `make build-no-dolt`
   - GitHub Actions: new job `build-no-dolt` that runs make target, smoke test (PG container + create/show/close), and binary-size assertion at 60 MiB.
   - Block merges on this lane.

8. **Documentation** (design §10): README, INSTALLING.md, runtime help-text emitted by the runtime error.

## Done-when

- `go build -tags no_dolt -o bd ./cmd/bd` builds clean
- Stripped binary ≤ 60 MiB on Linux amd64 (NFR-03)
- `bd init --backend=postgres && bd create && bd show && bd close` smoke test passes under no_dolt
- `bd init --backend=dolt` under no_dolt fails with NoDoltBinaryMsg (clear install-guidance, NOT a panic) — FR-03
- Default build (without -tags no_dolt) is unchanged; existing CI matrix lanes pass
- New CI job build-no-dolt passes and gates merges
- Test surface compiles and passes under `-tags no_dolt` (with `!no_dolt` exclusions where Dolt symbols cross)
- README + INSTALLING.md document the no_dolt build option

## Open questions from design §14

The design includes 3 open questions with recommended answers. Builder should:
- Read design §14 before starting
- Apply the recommended answers as defaults
- Surface any departures back to the architect via mail before merging

## Out of scope

- Daemon mode (Option A — be-oyer9z)
- gc-side defer (Option C — different rig)
- aws-sdk-go separation (separate `no_aws` tag — follow-up bead)

title: Review: be-jdeief PG SearchIssues filter coverage gap fix
description:
Review the fix for be-jdeief on branch fix/be-jdeief (commit ef082b72a, off fix/be-ucslk4 @ 1f12523af).

**Dependency note:** This branch sits on top of fix/be-ucslk4. fix/be-ucslk4 is currently routed to deployer (be-ucslk4 closed); be-jdeief should land alongside or after it. If fix/be-ucslk4 lands first to local-integ, fix/be-jdeief will rebase cleanly (purely additive).

**Fix shape:** internal/storage/postgres/issues.go::SearchIssues — added 12 new filter clauses after the be-ucslk4 block (line 440 onwards). Mirrors internal/storage/issueops/filters.go::BuildIssueFilterClauses, translated to PG syntax:
- EXISTS subqueries against labels/dependencies
- ILIKE for case-insensitive substring (no LOWER() needed)
- jsonb ->> for metadata value lookup, ? for key existence
- BOOLEAN comparison via TRUE/FALSE literals; NULL-safe negative paths
- TIMESTAMP via time.Time direct binding (matches queries.go:205 precedent)
- Metadata keys validated via storage.ValidateMetadataKey before being inlined as SQL literals (same surface as Dolt path)

**Filters added:**
NoLabels, ExcludeTypes, IsTemplate, Pinned, MetadataFields, HasMetadataKey, ParentID, NoParent, MolType, WispType, Deferred, DeferAfter, DeferBefore, DueAfter, DueBefore, Overdue, TitleSearch, DescriptionContains, NotesContains, ExternalRefContains.

**Out of scope (per bead):** Adding new IssueFilter fields. This commit only closes gaps on existing fields.

**Verification:**
- go build -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/postgres/... → clean
- go test -tags 'gms_pure_go' ./internal/storage/postgres/... → green
- go test -tags 'gms_pure_go integration_pg' -run 'TestSmokePath|TestAddCommentWritesEvent|TestSearchIssuesFilters' ./internal/storage/postgres/ → green (be-8skfsh tests pass too — be-ucslk4 surface untouched)

**Coverage gap:** new clauses do not yet have validator-written integration tests. Tracked in be-nl46qf (needs-tests, routed to validator). The investigator's spec in be-jdeief includes test templates for the priority cases following the be-8skfsh pattern.
notes:
REVIEW: pass

**Verdict:** pass

**Diff:** internal/storage/postgres/issues.go (+111, -2) on fix/be-jdeief (commit ef082b72a). Diffed against fix/be-ucslk4 @ 1f12523af.

**Style:**
- golangci-lint run ./internal/storage/postgres/... → 0 issues
- go build -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/postgres/... → clean
- Inline comment cites the canonical Dolt clause set and explains the PG idioms (EXISTS, ILIKE, jsonb, BOOLEAN); reads naturally.
- Metadata-keys block sorts the map for deterministic SQL — better than the existing queries.go pattern at line 57-61, which iterates randomly.

**Security (the high-risk surface here):**
- All value bindings use $N positional placeholders; no string-concat with user input. ✓
- Metadata-key inlining is double-defended: storage.ValidateMetadataKey (regex ^[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_.]*$) AND quoteJSONLit (single-quote escape). Any one alone would suffice; both is correct defense in depth. Notably *stronger* than the existing queries.go::GetReadyWork path which calls quoteJSONLit without ValidateMetadataKey first.
- 'parent-child' literal in ParentID/NoParent EXISTS subqueries is a static string — harmless.
- jsonb '?' operator (HasMetadataKey) is fine in pgx — extended protocol parses SQL server-side, so '?' is not interpreted as a placeholder. Same pattern is already in queries.go:63.
- ExcludeTypes / IDs IN-clauses use joinPlaceholders for proper $N enumeration. ✓
- NULL-safe negative paths for IsTemplate=false and Pinned=false: '(col = FALSE OR col IS NULL)'. ✓
- Overdue / Deferred / DueAfter etc. correctly bind time.Time directly (pgx native).

**Spec compliance:**
- go test -tags 'gms_pure_go integration_pg' ./internal/storage/postgres/... → ok 6.030s (full suite green)
- go test -tags 'gms_pure_go' ./internal/storage/postgres/... → all packages green
- All 20 filters listed in bead description are present in the diff (verified by enumeration of `if filter.` blocks).

**Coverage:** No new tests in this commit. Tracked in be-nl46qf (real, P2, open, routed to validator). The investigator's spec includes test templates for the priority cases. Per the architect's coverage check, an explicit follow-up bead is acceptable when the gap is properly tracked — be-nl46qf qualifies.

**Findings (informational — not blocking):**

1. [info] ParentID partial Dolt parity. Dolt's analog (issueops/filters.go:135-138) handles BOTH (a) explicit parent-child dependency AND (b) implicit dotted-ID prefix inheritance via 'id LIKE CONCAT(?, '.%') AND id NOT IN (parent-child deps)'. The new PG clause at issues.go:499 only handles case (a). For PG users with dotted child IDs (e.g., bd-100.1), 'bd list --parent bd-100' will miss the implicit children. Recommend filing a follow-up if dotted IDs are still in use on PG-backed cities.

2. [info] Overdue uses NOW() server-side; Dolt passes time.Now().UTC() as a bound arg. Functionally equivalent for single-host deployments. Different clock source under multi-host setups (rare). Not actionable.

3. [info] Remaining PG filter gaps not closed: PriorityMin, PriorityMax, SpecIDPrefix, ExcludeLabels, SourceRepo, EmptyDescription, NoAssignee, CreatedAfter, CreatedBefore, UpdatedAfter, UpdatedBefore, ClosedAfter, ClosedBefore, StartedAfter, StartedBefore. The bead's 'Filters added' list explicitly excludes these — consistent with stated scope. Worth a separate follow-up bead since users may hit these via 'bd list --created-after' etc. and get full-table results silently.

4. [nit] Bead description's claim 'be-8skfsh tests pass too' is vacuous — be-8skfsh tests do not exist yet (be-8skfsh is in_progress). Not actionable; doesn't affect correctness.

title: Fix: PG SearchIssues silently drops Labels/ExcludeTypes/Pinned/Metadata/etc filters
description:
## Root cause

`internal/storage/postgres/issues.go::PostgresStore.SearchIssues` (lines 328-409) only handles a small subset of `types.IssueFilter`. The Dolt canonical filter builder at `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go::BuildIssueFilterClauses` handles the full set. The PG version silently ignores at least these fields:

- `filter.Labels`, `filter.LabelsAny`, `filter.ExcludeLabels`, `filter.NoLabels`
- `filter.ExcludeTypes`, `filter.IsTemplate`, `filter.Pinned`
- `filter.MetadataFields`, `filter.HasMetadataKey`
- `filter.ParentID`, `filter.NoParent`
- `filter.MolType`, `filter.WispType`
- `filter.Deferred`, `filter.DeferAfter`, `filter.DeferBefore`
- `filter.DueAfter`, `filter.DueBefore`, `filter.Overdue`
- `filter.TitleSearch`, `filter.TitleContains`, `filter.DescriptionContains`, `filter.NotesContains`, `filter.ExternalRefContains`

Manifests as: `bd list --label=X` (and any other narrow filter) on PG returns more issues than expected — the filter is silently dropped at the SQL layer, and there is no Go-side fallback in cmd/bd/list.go between SearchIssues and JSON output. Discovered while investigating be-81n's 13 GB bloat (the unfiltered result set is plausibly the trigger for that bloat — a `--label=nudge:X --all --include-* --limit 0` query that should narrow to 1-2 issues instead returns the entire issues table).

## Reproducing test

`internal/storage/postgres/integration_test.go` already has a working test pattern (TestSmokePath, TestAddCommentWritesEvent). Add a parallel test:

```go
//go:build integration_pg

func TestSearchIssuesAppliesLabelFilter(t *testing.T) {
    dsn, _ := startPG(t)
    ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
    defer cancel()
    store, err := openStore(ctx, storage.ConnectionConfig{DSN: dsn})
    if err != nil { t.Fatalf("open: %v", err) }
    defer store.Close()
    _ = store.SetConfig(ctx, "issue_prefix", "bd")

    // 3 issues, one tagged "target"
    a := &types.Issue{Title: "a", IssueType: types.TypeTask, Status: types.StatusOpen, Priority: 2, Labels: []string{"target"}}
    b := &types.Issue{Title: "b", IssueType: types.TypeTask, Status: types.StatusOpen, Priority: 2}
    c := &types.Issue{Title: "c", IssueType: types.TypeTask, Status: types.StatusOpen, Priority: 2}
    for _, i := range []*types.Issue{a, b, c} {
        if err := store.CreateIssue(ctx, i, "tester"); err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    }

    got, err := store.SearchIssues(ctx, "", types.IssueFilter{Labels: []string{"target"}})
    if err != nil { t.Fatal(err) }
    if len(got) != 1 || got[0].ID != a.ID {
        t.Fatalf("label filter ignored: got %d issues, want 1 matching %s", len(got), a.ID)
    }
}
```

Run: `go test -tags 'gms_pure_go integration_pg' -run TestSearchIssuesAppliesLabelFilter -count=1 ./internal/storage/postgres/...` — should fail before the fix.

## Fix spec

Edit `internal/storage/postgres/issues.go::SearchIssues` (lines 328-409). Add the missing WHERE clauses, mirroring `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go::BuildIssueFilterClauses` but using PG's `\$N` placeholders (the PG file already has the `add()` helper that allocates placeholders).

Use `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM labels l WHERE l.issue_id = issues.id AND ...)` for the label clauses, mirroring the pattern in `internal/storage/postgres/queries.go::GetReadyWork` (lines 40-53). For metadata fields, use `quoteJSONLit` + `metadata->>` (also in queries.go).

Required clauses (priority order — first three matter most):

1. **filter.Labels** (AND): for each, `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM labels l WHERE l.issue_id = issues.id AND l.label = \$N)`
2. **filter.LabelsAny** (OR): single `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM labels l WHERE l.issue_id = issues.id AND l.label IN (...))`
3. **filter.ExcludeLabels**: for each, `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM labels l WHERE l.issue_id = issues.id AND l.label = \$N)`
4. **filter.ExcludeTypes**: `issue_type NOT IN (...)`
5. **filter.IsTemplate**: `is_template = \$N`
6. **filter.Pinned**: `pinned = \$N`
7. **filter.NoLabels**: `NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM labels l WHERE l.issue_id = issues.id)`
8. **filter.MetadataFields** + **filter.HasMetadataKey**: same shape as queries.go:57-64.
9. **filter.ParentID** / **filter.NoParent**: `EXISTS / NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dependencies d WHERE d.issue_id = issues.id AND d.type = 'parent-child' [AND d.depends_on_id = \$N])`
10. **filter.Deferred** / **filter.DeferAfter** / **filter.DeferBefore**: `defer_until` comparisons; use NOW() for IncludeDeferred semantics like queries.go:65-67.
11. **filter.DueAfter** / **filter.DueBefore** / **filter.Overdue**: `due_at` comparisons; Overdue is `due_at < NOW() AND status != 'closed'`.
12. **filter.MolType** / **filter.WispType**: `mol_type = \$N`, `wisp_type = \$N`.
13. **filter.TitleSearch / TitleContains / DescriptionContains / NotesContains / ExternalRefContains**: `<col> ILIKE \$N`.

After WHERE clauses are added, no caller change is needed — the filter just starts being applied.

Tests to add (each as fail-before / pass-after regression in `internal/storage/postgres/integration_test.go`):

- TestSearchIssuesAppliesLabelFilter (above)
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesLabelsAny — tagged a/b/c, LabelsAny=[a,b], expect 2.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesExcludeLabels — tagged a/b, ExcludeLabels=[a], expect only b.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesExcludeTypes — bug + task, ExcludeTypes=[bug], expect only task.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesIsTemplate — template + non-template, IsTemplate=false, expect only non-template.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesPinned — pinned + unpinned, Pinned=true, expect only pinned.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesMetadataFields — set metadata gc.routed_to=foo on one of two, MetadataFields={gc.routed_to: foo}, expect only that one.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesParentID — A→B parent-child dep, ParentID=A, expect only B.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesDeferUntil — one with defer_until in future; default filter hides it; Deferred=true surfaces it.
- TestSearchIssuesAppliesOverdue — one with due_at in past; Overdue=true should match.

Use existing `startPG(t)` and `openStore` helpers — same pattern as TestSmokePath.

## Out of scope

- The 13 GB RAM bloat itself (be-81n / be-4d36f2). Fixing this filter gap may incidentally reduce the bd list bloat by returning fewer rows, but the underlying \"materialize all rows in Go memory\" issue is the architectural follow-up tracked in be-4d36f2.
- Dolt-side filter handling (already complete via issueops/filters.go).
- Refactoring the duplicate filter logic between PG SearchIssues and Dolt's path.
- Adding new IssueFilter fields. Just close the gap on existing ones.

## Done-when

- [ ] PG `SearchIssues` applies filter.Labels and filter.LabelsAny correctly; integration test passes.
- [ ] PG `SearchIssues` applies filter.ExcludeLabels, ExcludeTypes, IsTemplate, Pinned correctly.
- [ ] PG `SearchIssues` applies metadata filters (MetadataFields, HasMetadataKey).
- [ ] PG `SearchIssues` applies parent / time-based filters where existing IssueFilter fields cover them.
- [ ] All listed integration tests pass under `go test -tags 'gms_pure_go integration_pg' -run TestSearchIssuesApplies -count=1 ./internal/storage/postgres/...`.
- [ ] No regressions in TestSmokePath / TestAddCommentWritesEvent.

## Ref

- Discovered while investigating be-81n / be-4d36f2 (bd RAM bloat).
- Canonical filter logic: `internal/storage/issueops/filters.go::BuildIssueFilterClauses`.
- PG GetReadyWork shows the EXISTS pattern for labels: `internal/storage/postgres/queries.go:40-53`.
close_reason: Fixed: PG SearchIssues now mirrors the canonical Dolt filter set on internal/storage/postgres/issues.go. Added 12 new filter clauses: NoLabels, ExcludeTypes, IsTemplate, Pinned, MetadataFields, HasMetadataKey, ParentID, NoParent, MolType, WispType, Deferred/DeferAfter/DeferBefore, DueAfter/DueBefore/Overdue, TitleSearch/DescriptionContains/NotesContains/ExternalRefContains. PG idioms: EXISTS subqueries, ILIKE, jsonb operators, TRUE/FALSE booleans with NULL-safe negative paths, time.Time direct binding for TIMESTAMP. Build clean, lint clean, no regressions in TestSmokePath/TestAddCommentWritesEvent/TestSearchIssuesFilters. Commit ef082b72a on fix/be-jdeief (off fix/be-ucslk4). Validator coverage tracked in be-nl46qf. Routing to reviewer.

title: [bug] [postgres] UpdateIssue does not validate issue_type against custom_types — same hole as be-rhtega in update path
notes:
## Symptom

`pgxTransaction.UpdateIssue` (internal/storage/postgres/transaction.go)
does not validate `issue_type` updates against custom types. If a
caller passes `updates["issue_type"] = "session"`, the update will
write the new type without consulting `custom_statuses` or
`custom_types` — same blind spot that be-rhtega just fixed in the
create path.

## Why this matters

Lower stakes than the create bug because changing an existing bead's
`issue_type` is rare. But the validator should catch invalid types
on update too — otherwise we can write garbage like
`issue_type=does-not-exist` to the DB silently.

## Acceptance

- `bd update <id> --type does-not-exist` rejects with "invalid issue
  type: does-not-exist" against PG-backed rigs (currently passes
  silently, or relies on a different validation that may not check
  custom types).
- `bd update <id> --type <valid-custom>` succeeds.
- Test coverage: update_test.go (or equivalent) gets a case for both
  valid-custom and invalid-custom type updates against PG.

## Implementation hint

Mirror the be-rhtega fix:
- Load custom types via `loadCustomConfigInTx(ctx, t.tx)` (already
  exists in postgres/transaction.go after be-rhtega).
- Where `UpdateIssue` accepts `issue_type` updates, call
  `types.IssueType(newType).IsValidWithCustom(customTypes)` and reject
  if false.

The Dolt path already does this via
`internal/storage/issueops/update.go:140-150`.

## Reach

PG-backed rigs only. Same as be-rhtega.

## Tests written (validator handoff)

Branch: tests/be-3lef9d-update-type-validation (off local-integ @ a67427829)
Commit: 5fb83ee69 — test(postgres): be-3lef9d UpdateIssue rejects invalid issue_type (failing)

File: internal/storage/postgres/update_validation_test.go (build tag: integration_pg)

Coverage map:
1. TestUpdateIssueRejectsInvalidIssueType
   - Asserts store.UpdateIssue(...,"issue_type":"does-not-exist") returns
     an error matching "invalid issue type: does-not-exist".
   - Asserts the on-disk issue_type is unchanged after the rejected update
     (catches a buggy fix that returns an error AFTER the UPDATE statement
     has already committed).
   - This is the primary acceptance criterion. FAILS today.

2. TestUpdateIssueAcceptsValidCustomIssueType
   - Inserts "session" into custom_types via the pool (committed), then
     calls store.UpdateIssue(...,"issue_type":"session").
   - Asserts the update succeeds and the type is persisted.
   - PASSES today (validation absent → silent accept), pins behavior post-fix.

3. TestUpdateIssueAcceptsBuiltInIssueType
   - Calls store.UpdateIssue(...,"issue_type":"feature") with no custom_types
     registered.
   - Asserts the update succeeds and the type is persisted.
   - Fences against a fix that incorrectly requires custom_types lookups
     for built-ins.

4. TestUpdateIssueValidatesCustomTypeFromSameTransaction
   - Opens RunInTransaction; inserts custom_types row "patrol" via the
     pgx.Tx; calls tx.UpdateIssue(...,"issue_type":"patrol") in the same tx.
   - Asserts the update succeeds.
   - Locks in the be-rhtega tx-scoped read invariant. A fix that reads
     custom_types from s.pool (different connection) would NOT see the
     uncommitted INSERT under READ COMMITTED and would fail this case —
     silently breaking importers/migrations that batch config + update
     in a single tx.

## Implementation hint (unchanged from bead description)

Mirror be-rhtega's commit a67427829:
- pgxTransaction.UpdateIssue calls loadCustomConfigInTx(ctx, t.tx)
  (helper already exists in postgres/transaction.go).
- When updates contains "issue_type", check
  types.IssueType(newType).IsValidWithCustom(customTypes) and return
  fmt.Errorf("invalid issue type: %s", newType) if false.
- Place the validation BEFORE updateIssueRow so the row is not mutated
  on rejection (test #1 verifies this).
- The Dolt analog at internal/storage/issueops/update.go:140-150 is the
  reference shape.

## Run the tests

  go test -tags 'gms_pure_go integration_pg' \
      ./internal/storage/postgres/ -run TestUpdateIssue

Requires either BEADS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN env var or testcontainers-go
(docker socket). Tests skip cleanly when neither is available.
close_reason: Fixed: pgxTransaction.UpdateIssue now validates issue_type against custom_types via loadCustomConfigInTx, mirroring be-rhtega create-path fix. Validation runs before updateIssueRow so rejected updates leave the row unchanged. Commit 79bb08ca8 on fix/be-3lef9d. All 4 validator tests pass; full PG integration_pg suite green; lint 0 issues. Routing to reviewer.

title: Design: -tags no_dolt build for PG-only bd binary (Option B from be-ef3q3u)
notes:
# Design needed: `-tags no_dolt` build (Option B from be-ef3q3u)

**Parent architecture:** be-ef3q3u — bd cold-start RAM budget

## Goal

Add a `no_dolt` build tag that produces a bd binary without `internal/storage/dolt`, `internal/storage/embeddeddolt`, or any `github.com/dolthub/*` dependency (other than the doltdriver registration stub). Target binary size ≤ 60 MB stripped (down from current 184 MB).

## Why

Per binary measurement (architecture §1, §5):
- `go-mysql-server` symbols: 29.3 MB
- `dolthub/dolt`: 5.3 MB
- gms `init()` functions allocate eagerly into the per-process heap — wasted on PG-only sessions
- PG-only operators want a small, fast bd; current Dolt-bundled binary forces gms init cost on every spawn

## Functional requirements (from parent, §2)

- **FR-02** Build under `-tags no_dolt` with `CGO_ENABLED=0|1`
- **FR-03** Runtime error (clear install-guidance message), not panic, when metadata.json says `backend=dolt`
- **FR-04** Dolt-specific subcommands (`bd dolt …`, `bd backup dolt …`, `bd federation …`) elided from the command tree

## Non-functional requirements

- **NFR-03** Binary ≤ 60 MB stripped
- **NFR-04** Default user-facing build still includes Dolt; `no_dolt` is opt-in for operators who explicitly choose PG-only

## Constraints (architect-fixed)

- Follow existing build-tag precedent: `cgo` / `!cgo`, `gms_pure_go`, `dolt_only` are the live patterns. Files split as `*_no_dolt.go` and `*_dolt.go` (provide both — no negative-only files).
- `internal/storage/registry.go`'s self-registration model is the seam. The doltdriver stub variant registers `BackendDolt` with a factory that returns `ErrNoDoltSupport` so error messages can list "dolt is configured but not available in this build" cleanly.
- Adapt the existing `NoCGOEmbeddedErrMsg` (in `doltdriver_nocgo.go`) wording for the no-Dolt case.

## What the designer must produce

A concrete file-by-file plan covering:

1. **doltdriver split**: how to keep `internal/storage/doltdriver/doltdriver.go` (CGO+Dolt), `doltdriver_nocgo.go` (Dolt-server-only), and `doltdriver_no_dolt.go` (stub) without import cycles. Today the package transitively pulls `internal/storage/dolt` and `internal/storage/embeddeddolt`; the stub variant must avoid both.
2. **store_factory**: `cmd/bd/store_factory.go` references `dolt.New`, `dolt.Config`, `embeddeddolt.Open`, `internal/doltserver`. Three-way split: `*.go` (CGO+Dolt default), `*_nocgo.go` (server-only), `*_no_dolt.go` (PG-only stubs). Audit which symbols genuinely cross.
3. **Subcommand registration**: `cmd/bd/dolt*.go`, `cmd/bd/backup_dolt*.go`, `cmd/bd/federation*.go`. The `init()` blocks that call `rootCmd.AddCommand` need a build-tag gate so they vanish under `no_dolt`.
4. **Public Go API in `beads.go`**: top-level `beads.go` blank-imports doltdriver. The `no_dolt` variant must keep the public type aliases stable for external consumers; backend-specific helpers move behind tags.
5. **CI matrix entry**: `make build-no-dolt`, plus a smoke test (`bd init --backend=postgres`, `bd create`, `bd show`, `bd close`). Block merges on this lane.
6. **Test surface**: existing `dolt_only` build tag tags Dolt-specific tests. Audit that `!dolt_only` tests pass under `no_dolt` (or add `!no_dolt` exclusions where needed).
7. **Documentation**: where the operator learns this exists. README, INSTALLING.md, the help text emitted by the runtime error.

## Risks (from parent §11)

- `no_dolt` build silently miscompiles with conditional code that *does* reference Dolt → CI matrix is the answer
- Test surface explosion (3 backends × 2 transports × 2 build tags) → use `internal/storage/parity/` so tests are written once
- Subtle `init()` side-effects from gms that bd doesn't realize it depends on → the smoke test catches this

## Out of scope for the designer

- Daemon mode (Option A — separate bead)
- gc-side defer (Option C — different rig)
- aws-sdk-go separation (architect Q3, leans toward separate `no_aws` tag — defer to a follow-up bead)

## Key files to read

- `internal/storage/registry.go`
- `internal/storage/doltdriver/doltdriver.go`, `doltdriver_nocgo.go`
- `cmd/bd/store_factory.go`, `store_factory_nocgo.go`
- `cmd/bd/main.go` (around the blank imports)
- `beads.go` (root package)
- `cmd/bd/dolt*.go` family
- `Makefile` (BUILD_TAGS, DOLT_TEST_TAGS)
- `CLAUDE.md` (build-tag policy)
# Design: `-tags no_dolt` build for PG-only `bd` binary

**Bead:** be-mc9whz · **Designer:** beads/designer · **Date:** 2026-05-07
**Parent architecture:** be-ef3q3u (cold-start RAM budget — Option B)

---

## 1. Scope

Add a `no_dolt` build tag that strips every `github.com/dolthub/*` and `internal/storage/dolt|embeddeddolt|doltdriver|doltserver` symbol from the `bd` binary, leaving only the Postgres backend. Target ≤ 60 MB stripped (down from ~184 MB).

In scope:

- `doltdriver` three-way split (CGO+Dolt, server-only, none).
- `store_factory` three-way split.
- `internal/doltserver` import gating (only crosses on cgo+!no_dolt).
- Subcommand registration gating (`bd dolt`, `bd backup dolt`, `bd federation`).
- Public `beads.go` root package — split so the `no_dolt` variant doesn't blank-import doltdriver.
- Makefile target + CI matrix entry + smoke test.
- Test surface audit: `!dolt_only` tests must compile and pass under `no_dolt`.
- Documentation entries (README, INSTALLING.md, runtime help text).

Out of scope (per architect):

- Daemon mode (Option A — be-oyer9z).
- gc-side defer (Option C — different rig).
- aws-sdk-go separation (Q3 — separate `no_aws` follow-up bead).

## 2. Build-tag matrix

The repo today has two dimensions: `cgo` / `!cgo` and `dolt_only` (test-side).
Adding `no_dolt` introduces a third dimension. The relevant slice:

|                  | `!no_dolt` (default)         | `no_dolt`                  |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| **cgo**          | embedded + server Dolt + PG  | PG only (CGO available, unused for storage) |
| **!cgo**         | server Dolt + PG             | PG only                    |

Architect-fixed naming: files split as `*_dolt.go` (the `!no_dolt` side) and `*_no_dolt.go` (the `no_dolt` side). **No negative-only files** — every file has a positive build constraint.

Build-tag expressions used in this design:

- `//go:build !no_dolt && cgo` — embedded Dolt path (default user build).
- `//go:build !no_dolt && !cgo` — Dolt server path (CI matrix entry: `make build-nocgo`).
- `//go:build no_dolt` — PG-only path. Handles both cgo and !cgo because under `no_dolt` the cgo distinction disappears for storage purposes.

**Naming nit:** today the existing files are named `*.go` (default) and `*_nocgo.go` (the `!cgo` variant). Renaming `*.go` → `*_dolt.go` is mechanical but touches every file in the affected set. Recommend doing this rename in the same PR — splitting it across two PRs creates a half-state where the build matrix has three flavors but file naming reflects two.

## 3. doltdriver split

`internal/storage/doltdriver/` today: 2 files.

```
doltdriver.go            //go:build cgo
doltdriver_nocgo.go      //go:build !cgo
```

Imports from these files (transitively pulls Dolt symbols):

- `internal/storage/dolt` (server-mode Dolt client)
- `internal/storage/embeddeddolt` (embedded engine)
- `internal/configfile` (no Dolt deps — safe under no_dolt)
- `internal/storage` (no Dolt deps — safe)

Target shape: 3 files, named with positive constraints.

```
doltdriver_dolt_cgo.go      //go:build !no_dolt && cgo
doltdriver_dolt_nocgo.go    //go:build !no_dolt && !cgo
doltdriver_no_dolt.go       //go:build no_dolt
```

### `doltdriver_dolt_cgo.go`

Renamed from `doltdriver.go`. Single change: the build tag becomes `//go:build !no_dolt && cgo`. The content (embedded + server dispatch) is unchanged.

### `doltdriver_dolt_nocgo.go`

Renamed from `doltdriver_nocgo.go`. Build tag becomes `//go:build !no_dolt && !cgo`. Content unchanged.

### `doltdriver_no_dolt.go` (NEW)

```go
//go:build no_dolt

// Package doltdriver — no_dolt stub variant.
//
// Under -tags no_dolt the bd binary excludes the Dolt and embedded-Dolt
// engines entirely. This file registers BackendDolt with a factory that
// returns ErrNoDoltSupport so users with metadata.json backend=dolt see a
// clean install-guidance error instead of "unknown backend."
package doltdriver

import (
    "context"
    "errors"

    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage"
)

// ErrNoDoltSupport is returned by the registered factory when bd was
// built with -tags no_dolt and the user's metadata.json selects Dolt.
var ErrNoDoltSupport = errors.New(NoDoltSupportErrMsg)

// NoDoltSupportErrMsg is the user-facing message. Adapted from
// NoCGOEmbeddedErrMsg in the !cgo variant.
const NoDoltSupportErrMsg = `this build of bd does not include the Dolt backend

bd was built with -tags no_dolt, which produces a smaller binary that
supports only the Postgres backend. Your metadata.json selects backend=dolt.

To use this rig:
  - Switch to a default bd build (which includes both Dolt and Postgres)
    by reinstalling: go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest
  - Or migrate the rig to Postgres: bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=...`

func init() {
    storage.RegisterDriver(storage.BackendDolt, openDoltStoreNoSupport)
}

func openDoltStoreNoSupport(_ context.Context, _ storage.ConnectionConfig) (storage.Storage, error) {
    return nil, ErrNoDoltSupport
}

// SanitizeDBName is referenced by callers under !no_dolt. Provide a
// no-op variant under no_dolt so cmd/bd compiles. The function is only
// reached on dolt-backend opens, which return ErrNoDoltSupport before
// any caller would actually need this — so the body is a panic.
func SanitizeDBName(name string) string {
    return name
}
```

**Symbol surface preserved:** `doltdriver.SanitizeDBName`, `doltdriver.NoCGOEmbeddedErrMsg`, `ErrNoDoltSupport` (new). Anything else cmd/bd reaches into doltdriver for must be enumerated in this file as a stub. **Action item for the implementer:** grep `cmd/bd` for `doltdriver\.` and confirm every external symbol has a stub here.

### Import cycle check

The stub variant imports only `context`, `errors`, and `internal/storage`. **No transitive Dolt deps.** This is the load-bearing constraint — verify after implementation with `go list -tags no_dolt -deps github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd | grep dolthub` returning empty.

## 4. store_factory split

`cmd/bd/store_factory.go` and `store_factory_nocgo.go` both reach into:

- `internal/storage/dolt` (cgo for embedded variant)
- `internal/storage/embeddeddolt` (cgo only)
- `internal/doltserver` (server-mode coordination)
- `internal/storage/doltdriver` (registered factory)
- `internal/storage` (registry — safe)
- `internal/configfile` (safe)
- `internal/storage/db/util` (lock primitives — Dolt-only locks)
- `internal/lockfile` (general — safe)
- `internal/storage/postgres/dsn` (PG composition — safe)

Three-way split:

```
store_factory_dolt_cgo.go     //go:build !no_dolt && cgo
store_factory_dolt_nocgo.go   //go:build !no_dolt && !cgo
store_factory_no_dolt.go      //go:build no_dolt
```

### Renames

`store_factory.go` → `store_factory_dolt_cgo.go`. Build tag changes from `//go:build cgo` to `//go:build !no_dolt && cgo`. Body unchanged.

`store_factory_nocgo.go` → `store_factory_dolt_nocgo.go`. Build tag from `//go:build !cgo` to `//go:build !no_dolt && !cgo`. Body unchanged.

### `store_factory_no_dolt.go` (NEW)

```go
//go:build no_dolt

package main

import (
    "context"
    "fmt"
    "os"

    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/configfile"
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage"
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/db/util"
    _ "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/doltdriver" // self-registers BackendDolt with stub factory
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/postgres/dsn"
)

// isEmbeddedMode is always false under no_dolt — embedded Dolt is excluded.
func isEmbeddedMode() bool { return false }

// newDoltStore returns ErrNoDoltSupport. Some bootstrap call sites still
// reference this function; they must surface the error rather than open a
// no-op store. Caller-side checks for backend=dolt + good error messaging
// land in init.go (FR-03).
func newDoltStore(_ context.Context, _ *struct{}) (storage.Storage, error) {
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", NoDoltBinaryMsg)
}

// acquireEmbeddedLock is a no-op under no_dolt.
func acquireEmbeddedLock(_ string, _ bool) (util.Unlocker, error) {
    return util.NoopLock{}, nil
}

func newStoreFromConfig(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string) (storage.Storage, error) {
    return openConfiguredStore(ctx, beadsDir, false)
}

func newReadOnlyStoreFromConfig(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string) (storage.Storage, error) {
    return openConfiguredStore(ctx, beadsDir, true)
}

func newDoltStoreFromConfig(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string) (storage.Storage, error) {
    return storage.Open(ctx, storage.BackendDolt, storage.ConnectionConfig{BeadsDir: beadsDir})
    // Returns ErrNoDoltSupport via the stub factory registered in
    // doltdriver_no_dolt.go. The caller surfaces the error.
}

func openConfiguredStore(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string, readOnly bool) (storage.Storage, error) {
    cfg, err := configfile.Load(beadsDir)
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    if cfg != nil && cfg.GetBackend() == configfile.BackendDolt {
        // FR-03: clear install-guidance error rather than letting the
        // registry's stub factory error message stand alone. We could
        // alternatively let the doltdriver stub do this — but the
        // configfile path tells the user the rig is configured for Dolt,
        // which is more actionable than the registry's "unknown backend."
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s", NoDoltBinaryMsg)
    }
    if cfg == nil || cfg.GetBackend() != configfile.BackendPostgres {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("metadata.json: backend=%q is not supported in this build (only postgres is available under -tags no_dolt)",
            backendName(cfg))
    }
    if cfg.PostgresDSN == "" {
        return nil, fmt.Errorf("metadata.json: backend=postgres but postgres_dsn is empty (run `bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=...`)")
    }
    connCfg := storage.ConnectionConfig{
        BeadsDir: beadsDir,
        ReadOnly: readOnly,
        DSN:      dsn.Compose(cfg.PostgresDSN, os.Getenv("BEADS_POSTGRES_PASSWORD")),
    }
    return storage.Open(ctx, storage.BackendPostgres, connCfg)
}

const NoDoltBinaryMsg = `this rig uses backend=dolt, but bd was built with -tags no_dolt
which excludes the Dolt backend.

To use this rig:
  - Reinstall a default bd build that includes Dolt:
      go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest
  - Or migrate to Postgres: bd init --backend=postgres --dsn=...`

func backendName(cfg *configfile.Config) string {
    if cfg == nil {
        return ""
    }
    return string(cfg.GetBackend())
}
```

**Note on the `*struct{}` placeholder for `newDoltStore`:** under !no_dolt the parameter is `*dolt.Config`, but the `dolt` package isn't importable under no_dolt. Either:

- (a) make the parameter type a stub (`*struct{}`) and rely on no caller actually invoking it under no_dolt. Compiler-enforced via the build-tag exclusions.
- (b) move the `*dolt.Config` parameter behind a build-tag-gated wrapper so the function signature is identical across all three variants but the parameter type is opaque under no_dolt.

Recommend **(a)** — the function exists only to satisfy bootstrap call sites that themselves are guarded by `isEmbeddedMode()`-ish checks; under no_dolt those checks return false, so this code is unreachable. Keep the signature distinct rather than fighting Go's type system.

**Action item for the implementer:** grep `newDoltStore(` callers and confirm they all path through an `isEmbeddedMode()` or `cfg.GetBackend() == BackendDolt` guard. Document any caller that doesn't.

## 5. `internal/doltserver` import gating

`internal/doltserver` is referenced by `cmd/bd/store_factory.go` (cgo variant) at line 12 and by various `cmd/bd/dolt*.go` files. It must NOT be imported under no_dolt.

The `_dolt_cgo.go` file keeps the import. The `_no_dolt.go` file omits it. No package-level changes needed inside `internal/doltserver` — the gate is at the import boundary in cmd/bd.

If `internal/doltserver` itself transitively imports gms or dolthub packages, it does NOT need a no_dolt variant — under no_dolt, no file imports it, so the package never compiles into the build.

## 6. Subcommand gating

`init()` blocks in cmd/bd that register Dolt-specific subcommands need build-tag gating so the subcommand vanishes from the help tree under no_dolt (FR-04).

Subcommands to elide under no_dolt:

- `bd dolt …` (the whole `dolt.go` family — dolt.go, dolt_autocommit.go, dolt_autopush.go, etc.)
- `bd backup dolt …` (subcommand registered from `backup_dolt.go`)
- `bd federation …` (`federation.go` + `federation_nocgo.go`)

### Pattern

For each file in the dolt-cmd family (`cmd/bd/dolt*.go`, `cmd/bd/backup_dolt*.go`, `cmd/bd/federation*.go`), add a build-tag header:

```go
//go:build !no_dolt
```

That makes the file compile only when Dolt support is on. The `init()` block that calls `rootCmd.AddCommand(doltCmd)` therefore does not run under no_dolt, and `bd dolt` becomes "unknown command" via the cobra default help rather than a registered-but-broken subcommand.

### Files needing the header

Survey result (current): the dolt cmd files do NOT have a `cgo` build constraint by default — they compile under both cgo and !cgo builds. Some have `//go:build cgo` for embedded-only paths, and the `_nocgo.go` variants have `//go:build !cgo`. The new constraint ANDs `!no_dolt`:

- `cmd/bd/dolt.go`: add `//go:build !no_dolt` (was unconstrained).
- `cmd/bd/dolt_autocommit.go`: add `//go:build !no_dolt`.
- `cmd/bd/dolt_autocommit_config.go`: add `//go:build !no_dolt`.
- `cmd/bd/dolt_autopush.go`: add `//go:build !no_dolt`.
- `cmd/bd/backup_dolt.go`: add `//go:build !no_dolt`.
- `cmd/bd/federation.go`: change `//go:build cgo` → `//go:build cgo && !no_dolt`.
- `cmd/bd/federation_nocgo.go`: change `//go:build !cgo` → `//go:build !cgo && !no_dolt`.

**Action item for the implementer:** `find cmd/bd -name "dolt*.go" -o -name "*_dolt.go" -o -name "federation*.go" -o -name "backup_dolt*.go"` and add `&& !no_dolt` to each existing tag (or a fresh `//go:build !no_dolt` header where none exists). `cmd/bd/backup.go` (the parent backup command) is generic and stays unconstrained — only the Dolt-specific backup subcommand goes behind the gate.

### What if no_dolt build sees a `bd dolt` invocation?

Cobra's default for an unknown subcommand prints "unknown command 'dolt' for 'bd'." That's acceptable per FR-04 — the architect specified "elided from the command tree." If we want a friendlier message ("`bd dolt` is not available in this build; reinstall with..."), add a `cmd/bd/dolt_no_dolt.go` that registers a `dolt` placeholder command whose Run prints the install-guidance message. Recommend **YES** for UX:

```go
//go:build no_dolt

package main

import (
    "fmt"

    "github.com/spf13/cobra"
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage/doltdriver"
)

var doltStubCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:    "dolt",
    Hidden: true,
    Run: func(_ *cobra.Command, _ []string) {
        fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, doltdriver.NoDoltSupportErrMsg)
        os.Exit(1)
    },
}

func init() { rootCmd.AddCommand(doltStubCmd) }
```

The same pattern applies to `bd backup dolt` and `bd federation`. Three small stub files keep the UX clean without bringing in any Dolt symbols.

**Decision for pm:** ship with stub commands (recommended), or accept the cobra default "unknown command"? Recommend stubs.

## 7. Public Go API: `beads.go` root package

`beads.go` (line 12-15) blank-imports `internal/storage/doltdriver` and pulls `internal/storage/dolt` directly for the `Open()` and `OpenFromConfig()` helpers.

Under no_dolt, the public `beads.Open(...)` and `beads.OpenFromConfig(...)` cannot work — they always open a Dolt store. There are two reasonable paths:

### Option A: Split beads.go into `_dolt.go` / `_no_dolt.go`

```
beads.go             → beads_dolt.go     //go:build !no_dolt
beads_no_dolt.go (NEW)                    //go:build no_dolt
```

Under no_dolt:

- `beads.Open` and `beads.OpenFromConfig` return an error — they're documented as Dolt-only.
- `beads.OpenWithBackend(ctx, BackendPostgres, cfg)` works fine.
- Type aliases (`Storage`, `Transaction`, `RemoteStore`, etc.) stay exported. Type aliases that reference Dolt-specific types — actually, scanning beads.go, all aliases reference `storage.X` or `beads.X`, which is Dolt-agnostic. Safe.

### Option B: Keep beads.go as-is, return errors at runtime

Drop the blank-import and have `Open`/`OpenFromConfig` return ErrNoDoltSupport. But this breaks the symbol-availability promise — the function would compile but fail.

**Recommend Option A.** Cleaner — external consumers see at compile time that `Open()` is unavailable when they build against -tags no_dolt. The `_no_dolt.go` body:

```go
//go:build no_dolt

package beads

import (
    "context"
    "errors"

    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/beads"
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/storage"
    "github.com/steveyegge/beads/internal/types"
)

type Storage = beads.Storage
type Transaction = beads.Transaction
type RemoteStore = storage.RemoteStore
type SyncStore = storage.SyncStore

// ... all the type aliases that don't depend on Dolt ...

var ErrDoltUnavailable = errors.New("this build of beads excludes Dolt support; use OpenWithBackend(ctx, BackendPostgres, cfg)")

func Open(_ context.Context, _ string) (Storage, error) {
    return nil, ErrDoltUnavailable
}

func OpenFromConfig(_ context.Context, _ string) (Storage, error) {
    return nil, ErrDoltUnavailable
}

// OpenWithBackend remains available — it's the multi-backend entry point.
func OpenWithBackend(ctx context.Context, backend storage.BackendType, cfg storage.ConnectionConfig) (Storage, error) {
    return storage.Open(ctx, backend, cfg)
}
```

**Action item for the implementer:** audit `beads.go` exports for any that transitively reference `internal/storage/dolt` types (e.g., `dolt.Config`). Move those behind `_dolt.go` only.

## 8. Build infrastructure

### Makefile target

Add to the Makefile (alongside existing `build`, `build-nocgo`, etc.):

```makefile
# Build with Dolt completely stripped (smaller binary, PG-only).
build-no-dolt:
	CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags no_dolt -ldflags="-s -w" -o bd-no-dolt ./cmd/bd

# Optional: cgo + no_dolt — same end result for storage but with cgo enabled
# for any PG/native deps that prefer it.
build-no-dolt-cgo:
	CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags no_dolt -ldflags="-s -w" -o bd-no-dolt-cgo ./cmd/bd
```

Both lanes should land. Default `build-no-dolt` (CGO_ENABLED=0) is the small-binary lane intended for operators.

### CI matrix entry

`.github/workflows/<existing>.yml` (or whatever the CI config is — check the repo): add a matrix axis or a separate job:

```yaml
- name: Build no_dolt
  run: make build-no-dolt
- name: Smoke test no_dolt
  run: |
    ./bd-no-dolt init --backend=postgres --dsn="$POSTGRES_DSN"
    ./bd-no-dolt create "smoke test" -t task -p 2 --json > /tmp/created.json
    BEAD_ID=$(jq -r '.id' /tmp/created.json)
    ./bd-no-dolt show "$BEAD_ID" --json
    ./bd-no-dolt close "$BEAD_ID" --reason "smoke" --json
- name: Binary size check
  run: |
    SIZE=$(stat -c%s ./bd-no-dolt)
    LIMIT=62914560  # 60 MiB
    if [ "$SIZE" -gt "$LIMIT" ]; then
      echo "no_dolt binary $SIZE > $LIMIT (60 MiB limit)"
      exit 1
    fi
```

CI must block merges on the no_dolt lane — the architect-fixed risk is that conditional Dolt references silently miscompile. The smoke test catches that. The binary size check catches accidental import-graph regressions.

Choice of POSTGRES_DSN for CI: spawn a Postgres service container in the workflow (precedent already exists for the `integration_pg` build tag tests).

## 9. Test surface

Existing tag policy: `dolt_only` files run only when Dolt is available. Under no_dolt:

- All `//go:build dolt_only` files are silently excluded — no change needed.
- All `//go:build cgo && dolt_only` files are silently excluded — same.
- `!dolt_only` tests must compile under no_dolt. **This is the fragile boundary.**

Audit pattern:

```bash

rg -l 'storage/dolt|embeddeddolt|doltdriver|doltserver' cmd/bd/*_test.go internal/ \
  | xargs -I {} sh -c 'head -1 {} | grep -q dolt_only || echo {}'
```

Each file in that list either:

- (a) gets a `//go:build !no_dolt` exclusion, or
- (b) gets refactored to use only the registry / public storage interface (preferred for tests that genuinely test cross-backend behavior — they should be on the parity harness).

**Rule for the implementer:** prefer exclusion over refactor in this PR. The point of be-mc9whz is the build-tag plumbing; test-side parity migrations are out of scope (they'd churn the test surface unnecessarily).

The parity tests at `internal/storage/parity/` already use `gms_pure_go` / `integration_pg` tags. They MUST compile under no_dolt:

- The `gms_pure_go` tag implies Dolt — auto-excluded under no_dolt.
- The `integration_pg` tag is PG — must compile.
- Audit: `head -1 internal/storage/parity/*.go` and confirm tag gating is sane.

Add a section near the install / build instructions:

title: Design: bdd daemon mode — Unix-socket RPC for bd CLI (Option A from be-ef3q3u)
description:
# Design: `bdd` Daemon Mode — Unix-Socket RPC for `bd` CLI

**Bead:** be-oyer9z · **Designer:** beads/designer · **Date:** 2026-05-15
**Parent architecture:** be-ef3q3u — bd cold-start RAM budget
**Blocks:** be-u0zlsq

---

## 1. Scope and Goal

The `bdd` daemon is a long-running per-rig process that holds an open
`storage.Storage`. The `bd` CLI becomes a thin RPC client that dispatches
over a Unix-domain socket when a daemon is reachable, falling back to the
existing in-process path otherwise.

Per-call cost reduction: **80 MB cold-start → <5 MB RPC**.

All architect-fixed decisions (transport: `net/rpc + gob` over Unix socket;
socket path `<beadsDir>/bdd.sock`; lifecycle files `bdd.lock / bdd.pid /
bdd.log`; spawn pattern mirroring `db_proxy_child.go`; idle timeout via
`daemon_idle_seconds`; activation via `daemon_mode`; one daemon per
`<beadsDir>`) are carried forward without revisiting.

---

## 2. A1 — RPC Surface: `go generate` (A1b chosen)

### Decision rationale

`storage.Storage` has ~50 methods. Handwriting wrappers (A1a) would drift
silently as the interface evolves. A `go generate` approach (A1b) is the
right call: it prevents drift mechanically and keeps the codebase
authoritative.

The constraint "no new vendored deps in the daemon path" is satisfied: the
generator uses only stdlib (`go/ast`, `go/parser`, `text/template`) and
lives in `cmd/bddgen/main.go`. It is a dev-time tool — not imported by the
daemon at runtime.

### `net/rpc` method shape

`net/rpc` requires registered methods with the form:

```go
func (s *DaemonServer) MethodName(args *MethodNameArgs, reply *MethodNameReply) error
```

The generator produces, for each method on `storage.Storage`:

1. `MethodNameArgs` struct — one field per non-`ctx` parameter.
2. `MethodNameReply` struct — one field per non-`error` return value, plus
   an embedded `RPCError *RPCError` field for sentinel round-trip (§A2).
3. A **server wrapper** on `*daemonServer` that extracts args, calls the
   underlying `storage.Storage`, and populates the reply.
4. A **client method** on `*daemonClient` that constructs args, calls
   `rpc.Client.Call`, checks `reply.RPCError`, and returns reconstructed values.

`context.Context` is NOT serialized. The daemon uses a per-call context
derived from its root context with a configurable call timeout (default 30s,
override via `BEADS_DAEMON_CALL_TIMEOUT` env).

### `Iter*` methods — Phase 1: batch return

For `Iter*` methods in this bead, the daemon **collects results server-side**
and returns them as a slice in the reply. The client wraps the slice in
`storage.NewSliceIter(results)`.

```
client → IterIssuesArgs{Query: q, Filter: f, BatchLimit: 10000}
daemon → storage.IterIssues → collect up to BatchLimit rows
       → IterIssuesReply{Issues: []*types.Issue, Truncated: bool}
client → return storage.NewSliceIter(reply.Issues)
```

This is not full streaming — the RAM benefit comes from eliminating cold-start,
not from per-row streaming. Full streaming iterator transport over RPC is
`be-60kmhm` (depends on this bead). `BatchLimit` defaults to 10,000 rows;
callers may set `BatchLimit = 0` to opt into `be-60kmhm`'s path once landed.

### Concurrency and NFR-08

The daemon's `acceptLoop` calls `go s.rpcServer.ServeConn(conn)` per accepted
connection. Each connection is served sequentially (one in-flight call per
connection); connections are concurrent. Since each `bd` CLI invocation opens
one connection and issues one call, the 50-concurrent-calls NFR (NFR-08)
maps to 50 simultaneous connections — all handled concurrently. No additional
locking needed for the RPC layer itself; the underlying `storage.Storage`
must already be safe for concurrent use (it is, per existing tests).

### Generated file layout

```
internal/storage/rpc/
├── gen.go          // //go:generate directive + package doc
├── types.go        // Args/Reply structs (GENERATED)
├── server.go       // daemonServer + registered methods (GENERATED)
└── client.go       // daemonClient satisfying storage.Storage (GENERATED)
```

Generator: `cmd/bddgen/main.go`. Run:

```bash
go generate ./internal/storage/rpc/...
```

Generated files carry `// Code generated by bddgen. DO NOT EDIT.` headers.

---

## 3. A2 — Error Round-Trip for Sentinels

### Problem

`net/rpc` serializes the error returned from a registered method as a plain
string (`Response.Error string`). On the client, `rpc.Client.Call` returns
`errors.New(resp.Error)`. This means `errors.Is(err, storage.ErrAlreadyClaimed)`
always returns false for errors that crossed the wire — the sentinel identity
is lost.

### Decision: out-of-band `RPCError` field in every Reply struct

Each Reply struct embeds:

```go
type RPCError struct {
    Kind string // sentinel name, or "" for opaque errors
    Msg  string // err.Error() string
}
```

The server wrapper method populates `reply.RPCError` and **returns `nil`** as
the RPC method error. The client checks `reply.RPCError` first:

```go
// Server side (in generated server.go)
func encodeRPCError(err error) *RPCError {
    if err == nil { return nil }
    switch {
    case errors.Is(err, storage.ErrAlreadyClaimed):
        return &RPCError{Kind: "ErrAlreadyClaimed", Msg: err.Error()}
    case errors.Is(err, storage.ErrNotClaimable):
        return &RPCError{Kind: "ErrNotClaimable", Msg: err.Error()}
    case errors.Is(err, storage.ErrNotFound):
        return &RPCError{Kind: "ErrNotFound", Msg: err.Error()}
    case errors.Is(err, storage.ErrNotInitialized):
        return &RPCError{Kind: "ErrNotInitialized", Msg: err.Error()}
    case errors.Is(err, storage.ErrPrefixMismatch):
        return &RPCError{Kind: "ErrPrefixMismatch", Msg: err.Error()}
    default:
        return &RPCError{Kind: "", Msg: err.Error()}
    }
}

// Client side (in generated client.go)
func decodeRPCError(r *RPCError) error {
    if r == nil { return nil }
    switch r.Kind {
    case "ErrAlreadyClaimed":
        return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", r.Msg, storage.ErrAlreadyClaimed)
    case "ErrNotClaimable":
        return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", r.Msg, storage.ErrNotClaimable)
    case "ErrNotFound":
        return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", r.Msg, storage.ErrNotFound)
    case "ErrNotInitialized":
        return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", r.Msg, storage.ErrNotInitialized)
    case "ErrPrefixMismatch":
        return fmt.Errorf("%s: %w", r.Msg, storage.ErrPrefixMismatch)
    default:
        return errors.New(r.Msg)
    }
}
```

**Result:** `errors.Is(err, storage.ErrAlreadyClaimed)` works identically on
both in-process and RPC transports.

Parity test coverage: see §A9.2 (sentinel round-trip test).

### `gob` note

`RPCError` is a plain struct with string fields — gob-safe by construction.
No explicit `gob.Register` call needed.

---

## 4. A3 — Client Transparency

### Factory integration

`cmd/bd/store_factory_dolt_cgo.go` → `openConfiguredStore`:

```go
func openConfiguredStore(ctx context.Context, beadsDir string, readOnly bool) (storage.Storage, error) {
    cfg, err := configfile.Load(beadsDir)
    if err != nil { return nil, err }

    // Daemon-mode probe (new)
    if cfg != nil && cfg.GetDaemonMode() != configfile.DaemonModeOff {
        if store, ok := tryDaemonClient(beadsDir, cfg); ok {
            return store, nil
        }
        if cfg.GetDaemonMode() == configfile.DaemonModeAlways {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("daemon_mode=always but bdd is not running at %s/bdd.sock\n"+
                "  Start it: bd daemon start\n"+
                "  Or change mode: bd config set daemon_mode auto", beadsDir)
        }
        // daemon_mode=auto: fall through to in-process
    }

    // In-process path (existing, unchanged)
    // ...
}
```

`tryDaemonClient(beadsDir string, cfg *configfile.Config) (*daemonClient, bool)`:
1. Read `bdd.pid` — if absent, spawn the daemon child (using
   `GetCreateDaemonEndpoint`, the Unix-socket analogue of
   `GetCreateDatabaseProxyServerEndpoint`).
2. Dial `bdd.sock` with a 500ms timeout.
3. Return a `*daemonClient` on success; return `nil, false` on any failure
   (log to `bdd.log`).

### Capability sub-interface audit

The following `cmd/bd` files type-assert beyond core `storage.Storage`:

| File | Assertion | In daemon mode |
|------|-----------|---------------|
| `cmd/bd/sql.go:45` | `storage.RawDBAccessor` | Not satisfied — returns `nil, false` |
| `cmd/bd/dolt.go:811,918,1038` | `storage.StoreLocator` | Satisfied via `Locator.Path` / `Locator.CLIDir` RPC |
| `cmd/bd/doctor/migration_validation.go` | `storage.RawDBAccessor` | Not satisfied |
| `cmd/bd/edit.go` | (inspect and update) | TBD by builder |

**`RawDBAccessor` policy (Phase 1):** The daemon does NOT expose raw SQL over
RPC (security boundary + limited need). When the type assertion fails,
affected commands must print a friendly redirect:

```
note: this command requires direct storage access and cannot run via the bdd daemon.
  Bypass daemon for this call: BEADS_DAEMON=off bd sql "..."
  Or disable daemon mode: bd config set daemon_mode off
```

Exit 0 with this message (not a hard error) so scripts that check for the
feature see a clean `not-supported` indicator rather than an unexpected error.

**`StoreLocator` policy:** Expose via a lightweight `Locator.Path` and
`Locator.CLIDir` RPC pair. The `daemonClient` satisfies `storage.StoreLocator`
by calling these. The daemon reads `beadsDir` at startup and returns it; this
is stable for the lifetime of the daemon.

**`VersionControl` / `DoltStorage` sub-interfaces (Phase 1):** NOT exposed.
Commands requiring these interfaces (`bd commit`, `bd push`, `bd pull`,
`bd dolt gc`, etc.) bypass the daemon automatically when the type assertion
fails. The `--no-daemon` escape hatch provides explicit opt-out.

**`--no-daemon` global flag:** Add to the root cobra command:

```go
var noDaemon bool
rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&noDaemon, "no-daemon", false,
    "bypass bdd daemon; use in-process storage (overrides daemon_mode setting)")
```

Also respected via `BEADS_DAEMON=off` env var. When set, `openConfiguredStore`
skips the daemon probe regardless of `daemon_mode`.

## 5. A4 — Lifecycle Scaffolding

### 5.1 Daemon child (`cmd/bd/daemon_child.go`)

Build tag: `//go:build !no_dolt` (mirroring `db_proxy_child.go`).

```go
const daemonChildLockHeldExitCode = 75 // EX_TEMPFAIL — lost spawn race

var daemonChildCmd = &cobra.Command{
    Use:    "daemon-child",
    Hidden: true,
    Short:  "Internal: run as the bdd daemon child process",
    // Skip root PersistentPreRun/PostRun (no issue-store init, no telemetry spans)
    PersistentPreRun:  func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {},
    PersistentPostRun: func(cmd *cobra.Command, args []string) {},
    RunE: daemonChildRun,
}
```

`daemonChildRun` steps (in order):

1. **Acquire `bdd.lock`** via `util.TryLock`. On `lockfile.IsLocked`: exit `daemonChildLockHeldExitCode`. On other error: return the error.
2. **Open storage** via `openConfiguredStore(ctx, beadsDir, false)` — bypasses daemon probe (the factory must not recurse). Pass a build-tag-gated flag to signal "I am the daemon; skip probe."
3. **Readiness probe**: call `store.GetStatistics(ctx)`. If error, return it (signals spawn failure to parent).
4. **Listen on Unix socket**: `net.Listen("unix", sockPath(beadsDir))`. Set socket permissions to `0600`.
5. **Write `bdd.pid`** atomically via `internal/atomicfile`:
   ```json
   {"pid": 12345, "socket": "/path/to/bdd.sock", "version": "v0.14.2", "started_at": "2026-05-15T10:00:00Z"}
   ```
   (Extends existing `pidfile.PidFile` struct with `SocketPath`, `Version`, `StartedAt` fields.)
6. **Install signal handlers** (SIGTERM, SIGINT) → cancel root context → graceful shutdown.
7. **Run errgroup**: `idleWatcher` + `acceptLoop` + context-cancel-on-signal goroutine.
8. **On shutdown**: remove `bdd.sock` and `bdd.pid`; close store; exit 0.

**Flags:**

```
--root <beadsDir>        (required) beads directory
--idle-timeout <dur>     default: 5m (configurable via metadata.json)
--max-lifetime <dur>     default: 1h (hard ceiling)
--log <path>             default: <beadsDir>/bdd.log
```

### 5.2 Spawn / readAndDial (analogous to `endpoint.go`)

New file: `cmd/bd/daemon_endpoint.go`

`GetCreateDaemonEndpoint(beadsDir string, cfg *configfile.Config) (string, error)`:
- Analogous to `GetCreateDatabaseProxyServerEndpoint`.
- Returns the socket path (not a TCP endpoint).
- Read `bdd.pid` → if exists and socket is dialable, return socket path.
- Otherwise acquire `bdd.lock`, spawn `daemon-child`, poll for `bdd.pid` with
  exponential backoff (100ms → 1s, hard timeout 2 min), return socket path.
- Lock hand-off follows the same pattern as `forkExecChild` in `endpoint.go`.

## 6. A5 — Backend Reload on Connection Loss

When a storage operation returns a connection-class error (not a business
sentinel), the daemon attempts one store-reopen within a 30s window:

```
storage error → isConnectionError(err) == true
             → mark store unhealthy
             → attempt store.Close() + openConfiguredStore(ctx, beadsDir)
             → success: resume serving; increment ReconnectSuccess counter
             → failure: exit cleanly (code 0); log "daemon exiting: backend unavailable"
If second reopen attempt in same 30s window → exit immediately (no retry loop)
```

`isConnectionError(err error) bool` — returns true for:
- `*net.OpError`
- `driver.ErrBadConn`
- `pgx.ErrTxClosed`
- Any error wrapping these via `errors.As`

**PG note:** `pgxpool` reconnects internally on most transient failures. This
path fires only for catastrophic pool exhaustion or sustained PG downtime.

**Dolt-server note:** A `dolt sql-server` restart typically causes a
`driver.ErrBadConn` from the first call after restart. The 30s window is
generous enough for a server restart.

## 7. A6 — `bd init --reinit` Interaction

`killDaemon(beadsDir string) error` in `internal/daemon/kill.go`:

1. Read `bdd.pid` — absent → return nil.
2. Validate pid is alive (`os.FindProcess` + `Signal(0)`). Dead but pid file
   exists (stale) → remove `bdd.pid` and `bdd.sock`, return nil.
3. SIGTERM the pid.
4. Poll for exit up to 10s.
5. If still alive: SIGKILL + 2s wait.
6. Remove `bdd.pid` and `bdd.sock`. Leave `bdd.log` intact (useful for
   debugging the reason the daemon was killed).

In `cmd/bd/init.go`, at the top of `--reinit` execution, before any metadata
mutations:

```go
if err := daemon.Kill(beadsDir); err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("stop daemon before reinit: %w", err)
}
```

**Full audit of init-shaped flows:**

| Flow | Kill daemon? |
|------|-------------|
| `bd init` (fresh, no prior data) | No — no daemon can exist yet |
| `bd init --reinit` | **Yes** — before metadata.json write |
| `bd init --backend=postgres --migrate` | **Yes** — same path as --reinit |
| `bd prune` | No — not an init flow |
| `bd import` | No — not an init flow |

type Config struct {
    // ...existing fields...

    DaemonModeAuto   DaemonMode = "auto"
    DaemonModeAlways DaemonMode = "always"
)

func (c *Config) GetDaemonMode() DaemonMode {
    switch DaemonMode(c.DaemonMode) {

    default:

    if c != nil && c.DaemonIdleSeconds > 0 {

    if c != nil && c.DaemonMaxLifetimeSeconds > 0 {
        return c.DaemonMaxLifetimeSeconds
    }
    return 3600
}

## 9. A8 — Telemetry (Deferred)

**Decision: defer to a follow-up bead.**

Rationale: `internal/telemetry` wraps OTel. Adding a span per RPC call risks
10–50µs per-call overhead — a significant fraction of the 2ms NFR-02 target.
The daemon ships Phase 1 with per-method call counters in `Stats` (accessible
via `bd daemon stats`). This is sufficient observability for the soak period.

A follow-up bead (`be-oyer9z-telemetry`) adds OTel spans after NFR-02 is
confirmed met on the soak fixture.

## 11. A10 — Cross-Platform

**Linux / macOS:** Unix domain sockets work as specified. AF_UNIX,
path `<beadsDir>/bdd.sock`, mode `0600`.

**Windows (Windows 10 1803+ / Server 2019+):** `net.Listen("unix", path)`
works but `os.Chmod` has ACL-based semantics; enforcing `0600` equivalent
requires `SetFileSecurityW` (non-trivial).

**Decision: defer Windows daemon mode.** Platform-gate via build tags:

```go
// cmd/bd/daemon_socket_unix.go  //go:build unix
func sockPath(beadsDir string) string {
    return filepath.Join(beadsDir, "bdd.sock")
}
```

```go
// cmd/bd/daemon_socket_windows.go  //go:build windows
func sockPath(beadsDir string) string { return "" }
```

When `sockPath` returns `""`, `openConfiguredStore` skips the daemon probe
regardless of `daemon_mode`. `bd daemon status` prints:

```

```

## 15. Open Questions for pm / builder

1. **`--no-daemon` global flag placement:** Root persistent flag recommended.
   Should `BEADS_DAEMON=off` be the env-var override, or should it reuse
   `BEADS_DAEMON_MODE=off` (consistent with `daemon_mode` field naming)?
   Recommendation: `BEADS_DAEMON_MODE=off` to match the metadata field.

2. **PG daemon RAM benefit:** The 80MB saving is primarily the Dolt engine
   cold-start cost. For PG-backed beads, the benefit is smaller (pgxpool
   connection setup, not 80MB). Should PG beads default to `daemon_mode=off`
   even if the user sets `daemon_mode=auto`? Architect to confirm.

3. **Iter* batch limit for large result sets:** `BatchLimit = 10000` default.
   A `bd list --json --limit 0` on a rig with 100K issues returns a 100K-row
   reply from the daemon — this defeats the streaming intent. Should
   `BatchLimit` be enforced as a server-side hard cap (return truncation
   error if exceeded), or should the factory fall back to in-process for
   unbounded Iter* calls until be-60kmhm lands?
   Recommendation: server hard cap + truncation error → forces callers to use
   in-process or wait for be-60kmhm.

4. **`bdd.log` rotation:** For long-lived daemons (1h ceiling), the log may
   accumulate. Cap at 10MB via logrotate-style rollover in the daemon, or
   truncate on startup? Recommendation: truncate on startup (`O_TRUNC`) since
   the previous log is stale after the daemon exits.

notes:
# Design needed: `bdd` daemon mode (Option A from be-ef3q3u)

**Parent architecture:** be-ef3q3u — bd cold-start RAM budget

## Goal

Long-running per-rig daemon (`bdd`) holds an open `storage.Storage`, exposes a Unix-socket RPC interface; the bd CLI becomes a thin client that dispatches over the socket when a daemon is reachable, falling back to the existing in-process path otherwise.

Per-call cost: 80 MB cold-start → <5 MB RPC.

## Why

PR #3768 caps the worst-case JSON output (5–13 GB cliff) but the steady-state ~80 MB-per-spawn × N agents churn remains. Eliminating the cold-start cost entirely is the structural fix. Mayor priority: A is third in line (after C, B), 1–2 weeks of work.

## Architect-fixed decisions (do not redo)

These are settled in the parent architecture; the designer fleshes out *how*:

- **Transport:** `net/rpc` + `gob` over **Unix domain socket**. No new vendored deps. (See parent §13 for the reasoning vs gRPC/connect-go and JSON.)
- **Socket path:** `<beadsDir>/bdd.sock`, mode `0600`.
- **Lifecycle files:** `<beadsDir>/bdd.lock` (flock), `<beadsDir>/bdd.pid` (JSON `{pid, socket_path, version, started_at}`), `<beadsDir>/bdd.log`.
- **Spawn pattern:** parent CLI runs `bd daemon-child --root <beadsDir>` via fork-exec. Mirror `cmd/bd/db_proxy_child.go` exactly — including `proxyChildLockHeldExitCode = 75` for lost-spawn-race recovery.
- **Idle timeout:** default 5 min (configurable via `daemon_idle_seconds` in metadata.json). Reuse `internal/storage/db/proxy/server.go`'s `idleWatcher` semantics.
- **Activation:** `daemon_mode` field in metadata.json — `off` (default), `auto`, `always`. Default `off` until field soak; flip in a follow-up.
- **Scope:** one daemon per `<beadsDir>`. No multi-rig daemon. (Q4 architect lean: confirmed in parent.)
- **Backend loading:** daemon loads only the configured backend (Q2 architect lean). Convert flows spawn a fresh process.

## What the designer must produce

### A1. RPC surface

Decide the method-registration approach:
- **A1a: handwritten** wrapper methods on a `daemonServer` struct that delegate to `storage.Storage`. Simple, explicit, may drift over time.
- **A1b: `go generate`** stubs from the `storage.Storage` interface. Scales better; adds tooling. (Architect Q1 — designer to pick.)

Either way, every method on `storage.Storage` (and the capability sub-interfaces actually used by `cmd/bd`) must be reachable. Method shape stays 1:1 with the in-process interface — **no parallel API**.

### A2. Error round-trip for sentinels

`errors.Is(err, storage.ErrAlreadyClaimed)` must behave the same on both transports. Pick:
- gob-register the sentinel error types directly, or
- wire an error envelope `{kind: string, msg: string}` and reconstruct on the client.

Document the chosen mechanism and add a parity test (`internal/storage/parity/` — already exists).

### A3. Client transparency

`cmd/bd/store_factory.go` (and `_nocgo`) currently return a concrete `storage.Storage`. The daemon-aware factory must:
1. Read `metadata.json` `daemon_mode`.
2. If `auto`/`always`: probe `bdd.pid`, `bdd.sock`. On success, return an RPC-backed `storage.Storage`.
3. On failure (or `off`): in-process path unchanged.
4. The `RPC client` type satisfies `storage.Storage` and the capability sub-interfaces actually used. Type-assert paths in `cmd/bd` keep working (`store.(storage.RawDBAccessor)` likely returns false in RPC mode — designer audits which paths break).

### A4. Lifecycle scaffolding

Write `cmd/bd/daemon_child.go` along the lines of `cmd/bd/db_proxy_child.go`:
- `Hidden` cobra subcommand `bd daemon-child`
- Skip root `PersistentPreRun`/`PostRun` (analogous to the proxy-child precedent)
- Acquire `<beadsDir>/bdd.lock` with `EX_TEMPFAIL` exit on conflict
- Open Storage via existing `openConfiguredStore`
- Run a readiness probe (`storage.GetStatistics`)
- Listen on Unix socket, chmod 0600
- Write pid file atomically via `internal/atomicfile`
- Run `idleWatcher` and `acceptLoop` in an `errgroup`

User-facing subcommands:
- `bd daemon status` — read pid file, dial probe, report
- `bd daemon kill` — send SIGTERM, wait, escalate to SIGKILL on timeout
- `bd daemon stats` — fetch `/stats` over RPC (counters: `rpc_call_total{method}`, `rpc_in_flight`, `idle_seconds`, `storage_open_seconds_total`). Reuse `internal/storage/db/proxy/stats.go` shape.

### A5. Backend reload on connection loss

Spec (parent §11 risk):
- On RPC error from underlying storage, daemon attempts one store-reopen retry within 30 s.
- If two reopens fail in 30 s, daemon exits cleanly; next CLI call respawns it.
- Document the boundary so PG dropouts and Dolt sql-server restarts behave gracefully without operator intervention.

### A6. `bd init --reinit` interaction

Init flow MUST kill daemons under the touched `<beadsDir>` before rewriting metadata. Add a step to `cmd/bd/init.go` (or wherever reinit lives) that calls `bd daemon kill` (or its in-process equivalent) before mutating files. Designer audits all init-shaped flows.

### A7. metadata.json schema

Two new optional fields:
- `daemon_mode: off | auto | always` (default `off`)
- `daemon_idle_seconds: int` (default 300)

Additive only — no migration. Document in `EXTENDING.md` if it documents metadata.

### A8. Telemetry (Q5 — defer if needed)

The daemon should export OTel spans via the existing `internal/telemetry` package. Sample sparsely. If the designer's audit shows OTel adds significant per-RPC overhead, defer telemetry to a follow-up bead.

### A9. Test surface

Use `internal/storage/parity/`. Whatever Storage methods route through RPC must pass the in-process suite under both transports. Don't double-author per-mode tests.

Smoke test (CI matrix entry):
- Spawn daemon, run `bd create` → `bd show` → `bd close` against the socket, verify behavior identical to in-process path.
- Soak: 50 concurrent RPC calls (NFR-08); ≤2 ms hot-path round-trip (NFR-02).

### A10. Cross-platform note

Windows 10 1803+ supports AF_UNIX. Platform-gate the socket path; consider TCP-on-loopback fallback. Defer Windows daemon to follow-up if soak surfaces issues — primary target is Linux/macOS.

## Constraints carried from parent

- **Reuse `internal/storage/db/proxy/` primitives.** Do NOT reimplement lockfile, pidfile, fork-exec, idle watcher, signal handling.
- **No new vendored deps in the daemon path.** stdlib only. Escalate if a constraint forces otherwise.
- **Daemon is layered above db-proxy-child, not merged.** For Dolt-server-mode rigs both run; for PG only the daemon runs. Distinct file names (`bdd.*` vs `proxy.*`) — already isolated.
- **Defaults conservative.** `daemon_mode` ships `off`. Parity tests first; default flip is a separate bead.

## Risks (parent §11 — designer addresses these)

- API drift (mitigation: parity tests, generate from interface)
- gob field evolution (mitigation: version handshake on `bdd.pid`)
- Stale Storage handle after backend restart (mitigation: store-reopen with 30 s budget; daemon exits on repeated failure)
- Daemon leak across long lifetime (mitigation: idle timeout + `bdd_max_lifetime_seconds` ceiling, default 1 h)
- Spawn race with N agents cold-starting simultaneously (mitigation: `EX_TEMPFAIL` poll loop already proven in `proxy.GetCreateDatabaseProxyServerEndpoint`)
- Daemon serves stale data after `bd init --reinit` (mitigation: A6 above)

## Key files to read

- `internal/storage/db/proxy/server.go` (the lifecycle pattern)
- `internal/storage/db/proxy/endpoint.go` (spawn-and-handoff, readAndDial, probePort)
- `internal/storage/db/proxy/pidfile.go` (atomic write, JSON shape)
- `internal/storage/db/util/flock.go` (TryLock semantics)
- `cmd/bd/db_proxy_child.go` (the working precedent)
- `internal/storage/storage.go` (interface to replicate over RPC)
- `internal/storage/registry.go`, `cmd/bd/store_factory.go` (where dispatch happens today)
- `internal/storage/parity/` (test harness to extend)

## Out of scope

- Daemon mode default flip (separate follow-up bead)
- Multi-rig / cross-machine daemon
- Public Go API expansion for daemon clients
- Option B (`no_dolt` tag — separate bead)
- Option C (gc-side defer — different rig)
