title: Review: be-zjv6 tier-aware compat migrations (PR #3540 fix)
description:
## Review target

Commit: `145a67a4` on branch `be-xtf-readme` (builder worktree).

Source bead: be-zjv6 (closed). Investigation: be-4m8o (closed).
Original PR: #3540 (`release/be-n6n`, currently buggy at HEAD ca7d7bdd).

## What changed

- `internal/storage/dolt/migrations/runner.go` — `CompatTier` enum,
  `Tier` field on `CompatMigration`; 17 entries tier-annotated (16 drift,
  1 backfill); `RunCompatMigrations` skip-check gated only on backfill
  tier; doc updated.
- `internal/storage/dolt/compat_migrations_test.go` —
  `TestRunCompatMigrationsSkipsWhenUpToDate` rewritten to assert backfill
  gate via custom_types deletion; docstrings updated.

## Verification done

- Build clean (`gms_pure_go`).
- `go test -count=1 -run TestRunCompatMigrations ./internal/storage/dolt/` PASS.
- migrations subpackage PASS.
- `TestEmbeddedOpenRunsCompatMigrations` PASS (the PR #3540 CI failure).
- `golangci-lint run --build-tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/dolt/...` 0 issues.

## Pre-existing failures (not introduced)

Full `./internal/storage/dolt/...` run reports pre-existing failures in
`TestApplyConfigDefaults_*` and `TestPrePushFSCK_UnopenableDB` — same set
the validator flagged in their gm-wisp-alq mail re: be-bpb. None of those
touch compat-migration code paths.

## Hand-off scope

Reviewer: confirm tier semantics + test rewrite are correct. After PASS,
deployer integrates onto `release/be-n6n` (cherry-pick the commit) and
posts the PR reply enumerating the regression and the fix per the
be-zjv6 done-when checklist.
notes:
## Reviewer verdict: PASS (2026-04-30, reviewer-gm-po6pox3)

Commit `145a67a4` on `be-xtf-readme` reviewed against be-zjv6 spec.

### Findings

- 0 blockers, 0 high, 0 medium, 0 low.

### Spec compliance

- `runner.go`: `CompatTier` enum + `Tier` field added; 16/17 entries
  CompatTierDrift, only `backfill_custom_tables` is CompatTierBackfill;
  gate is `if m.Tier == CompatTierBackfill && applied[m.Name]`. Matches
  the spec textually.
- `compat_migrations_test.go`: `TestRunCompatMigrationsSkipsWhenUpToDate`
  rewritten to assert backfill gate via `DELETE FROM custom_types` +
  post-call recount (count must remain 0). Docstrings updated on both
  tests to reflect tier-aware semantics. Matches spec.
- Files explicitly out of scope (`embeddeddolt/compat_migrations_test.go`,
  `release-gates/be-n6n-gate.md`) untouched. ✓

### Style

- `CompatTier` enum is well-named, well-documented, with `iota` semantics
  matching Go convention.
- `RunCompatMigrations` doc updated to explain the tier-aware gate.
- Positional struct literals in `compatMigrationsList` are tight but
  acceptable for a 3-field struct; field labels would be a nit, not a
  blocker.

### Security (OWASP walk on the diff)

- No injection: `m.Name` is sourced from a hard-coded list, not user
  input; the `INSERT IGNORE` uses parameterized `?`.
- No new auth/access-control surface.
- No new file I/O, deserialization, or external calls.
- No sensitive data exposure.
- Defense in depth: tier classification + each migration's internal
  idempotency check = two layers.

### Verification I re-ran (builder worktree, commit 145a67a4)

- `go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...` clean.
- `go test -tags gms_pure_go -count=1 -run TestRunCompatMigrations ./internal/storage/dolt/` PASS (0.121s).
- `go test -tags gms_pure_go -count=1 ./internal/storage/dolt/migrations/...` PASS (0.065s).
- `BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test -tags gms_pure_go -count=1 -run TestEmbeddedOpenRunsCompatMigrations ./internal/storage/embeddeddolt/` PASS (0.207s) — confirms the PR #3540 regression is repaired.
- `go vet -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/dolt/...` clean.
- `golangci-lint run --build-tags gms_pure_go ./internal/storage/dolt/...` 0 issues.

### Coverage

- New test directly exercises the backfill gate (decision logic on the
  changed line).
- `TestEmbeddedOpenRunsCompatMigrations` exercises drift-tier behavior
  (017 always runs even with tracking row present).
- Combined, the two tests cover both branches of the new
  `if m.Tier == CompatTierBackfill && applied[m.Name]` decision. Authors
  thought about testing — outcome (a).

### Pre-existing failures (acknowledged, not introduced)

`./internal/storage/dolt/...` full run still shows the
`TestApplyConfigDefaults_*` / `TestPrePushFSCK_UnopenableDB` set already
flagged by validator gm-wisp-alq on be-bpb. None touch compat-migration
code paths; not blocking this review.

### Perf trade-off (acknowledged)

Fast-path savings change from "30 → 3 SQL roundtrips" to "30 → ~17"
because drift-tier idempotency checks still run. This is the deliberate
trade-off documented in the bead and the runner doc comment. If gas-city
contention re-surfaces, the follow-up is an introspection cache or
fingerprint sentinel — out of scope for this fix.

title: dolt journalWriter.flush panic during 10K seed (D4v2 bench-infra blocker, cross-rig)
description:
# Upstream dolt panic blocking D4v2 (be-eei) write-bench gate

The D4v2 schema migration (be-s54 / be-nx7 / cfd38cda) cannot be measured
against be-eei §8 guardrail 5 (`-count=5` write-bench at 10K) because the
Dolt SQL server panics in `journalWriter.flush` during seed. Two days of
attempts (2026-04-25 → 2026-04-26) all crashed mid-seed.

This bead is cross-rig — the root cause sits in `dolthub/dolt` itself,
not in beads' test harness. Beads' own testmain ordering bug
(`BEADS_TEST_EXTERNAL_DOLT_PORT`) is fixed on validator branch
`tests/be-s9d-testmain-external-port` (commit 27a4f1f8), so the
host-resident dolt sql-server fallback path is reachable; what dies is
the dolt server itself.

## Symptom class

**Client-side (test process):**
```
[mysql] packets.go:58 read tcp 127.0.0.1:NNNN->127.0.0.1:33099: i/o timeout
--- FAIL: BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-16
    dolt_benchmark_test.go:1359: create perms batch 1500: failed to insert
        issue sum-perm-1862: insert issue into issues: invalid connection
    dolt_benchmark_test.go:78: drop bench database
        "benchdb_3050966_1bac75065b63f1e2": context deadline exceeded
```
(Captured 2026-04-26 in `/var/tmp/be-s9d/pre-d4v2-create-update.txt`.)

**Server-side panic** (from prior session-resume notes — original log
`/tmp/be-s9d-dolt-fresh.log` lost on host reboot, /tmp is tmpfs):
- panic in `journalWriter.flush` during seed insert burst
- documented at be-s9d session-resume note 2026-04-25T17:55, again
  2026-04-27T01:25
- recurrent across attempts on 2026-04-25 and 2026-04-26
- not reproduced in this bead — a fresh repro requires another ~30-50 min
  bench attempt and is requested as part of the investigator's intake.

## Reproduction (suggested)

1. Build the pre-D4v2 baseline + HEAD worktrees per be-s9d session notes
   (artifacts left at `/var/tmp/be-s9d/{head,pre-d4v2}/` as of
   2026-04-26 11:27).
2. Start a host-resident dolt sql-server on port 33099 against a
   fresh dolt repo (e.g. `/var/tmp/be-s9d/dolt/`).
3. Set `BEADS_TEST_EXTERNAL_DOLT_PORT=33099` and run:
   ```
   go test -tags gms_pure_go -bench='BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K' \
       -benchtime=1x -count=5 -timeout=4h \
       ./internal/storage/dolt -run='^$'
   ```
4. Server typically dies between 1500-4500 inserts of the 10K seed.
   Stack should land in `journalWriter.flush` (NBS / journal subsystem).

## Environment

- **Dolt version:** `github.com/dolthub/dolt/go v0.40.5-0.20260326074512-005921bdd8ca`
  (pinned in `go.mod`; pseudo-version, ~Mar 2026 dolt main).
- **Rig:** beads (`/home/jaword/projects/beads`).
- **Host:** AMD Ryzen 9 8945HS, 32G RAM (per host-update.txt).
- **Storage:** `/var/tmp/be-s9d/` on nvme0n1p8 (~36G free); `/tmp` is
  tmpfs and MUST NOT be used for the dolt data dir per
  operator-constraint comment on be-s9d 2026-04-26.
- **Build tag:** `gms_pure_go` (mandatory per CLAUDE.md).
- **Beads-side workaround:** `BEADS_TEST_EXTERNAL_DOLT_PORT` ordering
  fix on validator branch `tests/be-s9d-testmain-external-port`
  (HEAD 27a4f1f8). Does NOT fix the upstream panic.

## Why this is upstream

- Failure happens server-side (dolt-process exit + i/o timeout on the
  client). The beads test harness only observes the corpse.
- Same panic location (`journalWriter.flush`) reported across multiple
  attempts on different dolt repos / different runs.
- Symptom is independent of beads' own write paths — it triggers in
  the same NBS journal flush regardless of which test seeds the rows.

## Out-of-scope for this bead

- Re-running the bench at 10K (that's the architect re-escalation
  bead's territory once dolt is fixed or methodology changes).
- Patching beads to seed in smaller batches as a workaround (would be
  hiding an upstream bug — should be decided by architect via
  re-escalation, not implemented unilaterally).

## Linked context

- Discovered-from: be-nx7 (D4v2 review, REQUEST-CHANGES on missing
  write-bench evidence)
- Sister bead: be-s9d (10K write-bench measurement, blocked on the
  same upstream panic)
- Architect spec: be-eei §8 guardrail 5 + NFR-D4-3 (gate that cannot
  be evaluated)
notes:
## Deep-investigator notes (deep-investigator, 2026-05-02)

**Status**: panic does NOT reproduce on current host + system dolt
v1.86.6. Original "panic in journalWriter.flush" framing was a
misdiagnosis — what looked like a dolt bug is dolt **deliberately
crashing** because of an underlying I/O error from the bench host
itself. Closing as resolved with full evidence; be-6e8s is unblocked.

### Key finding (cross-rig: beads → dolt)

The dolt panic is intentional behavior. Source:

- `dolt:go/store/nbs/journal_writer.go:541-549` — `journalWriter.flush`
  calls `dherrors.Fatalf(behavior, "%w: error writing to database
  journal file", err)` when `wr.journal.WriteAt(wr.buf, wr.off)`
  returns an error.
- `dolt:go/libraries/utils/errors/panic.go:30-49` — `Fatalf` with
  `FatalBehaviorCrash` launches a goroutine that **panics** with the
  full `debug.Stack()` and the underlying error message. The original
  goroutine sleeps forever. (This is why the panic stack always points
  at `journalWriter.flush` regardless of which write was upstream.)
- `dolt:go/libraries/doltcore/sqle/database.go:201-210` — every Dolt
  database registered with the SQL engine is configured for
  `FatalBehaviorCrash` ("These are local databases and it isn't
  necessarily safe to continue operating after an I/O on the write
  path"). So the dolt sql-server crashes on any journal-write error.
- Mechanism introduced: `dolt:0fc9dccc1` (PR #10429, "go/store/nbs:
  For local databases, crash on fatal I/O errors during writes",
  Aaron Son, 2026-02-04). System dolt v1.86.6 (currently at
  /usr/local/bin/dolt) and every v1.86.x in between contains it.

So the panic is dolt **correctly** reporting that an underlying
write/fsync failed. The actual "bug" is whatever was causing the
WriteAt to return an error in the bead-time environment.

### Reproduction attempt — passes cleanly

Re-ran the exact spec from be-6e8s on this host and current dolt:

- Host: AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395, 32G RAM, **/dev/nvme0n1p8 = 410G free**
  (vs 36G in bead environment).
- System dolt: `dolt version 1.86.6` (released 2026-04-27, after
  bead was filed; contains all NBS commits up to that tag).
- Beads worktree: `tests/be-s9d-testmain-external-port` (commit
  27a4f1f8, has cfd38cda D4v2 migration + the testmain
  external-port ordering fix; uses `BEADS_TEST_EXTERNAL_DOLT_PORT`).
- Build tag: `gms_pure_go`.
- External dolt sql-server on `127.0.0.1:33099`, data dir
  `/var/tmp/be-8xg9/dolt/`. Stderr persisted to
  `/var/tmp/be-8xg9/dolt-stderr.log` (so a panic stack would
  survive the process exit, unlike the original /tmp tmpfs runs).

Results (full logs in `/var/tmp/be-8xg9/`):

```
BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   22753882 ns/op
BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   20896644 ns/op
BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   22247807 ns/op
BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   22865700 ns/op
BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   26761574 ns/op
PASS  (7:25 wall, all 5 samples clean)

BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   17760950 ns/op
BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   28456198 ns/op
BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   17975971 ns/op
BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   22450374 ns/op
BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K-32   1   16294532 ns/op
PASS  (7:43 wall, all 5 samples clean)
```

Total: 11 fresh 10K-row seeds (~110K seeded inserts) + 10 timed
bench iterations. Zero panics. Dolt sql-server stayed up the whole
time, RSS stable around 95M, stderr clean except for the unrelated
secure_file_priv warning emitted at startup.

### Why the bead-time environment failed and this one didn't

Highest-confidence drivers (in approximate order):

1. **Disk pressure.** The 2026-04-26 operator note flagged 36G free
   on `/var/tmp`; today the same partition has 410G. Each 10K seed
   in the bench is small in steady state (the bench dropBenchDB drops
   the per-iteration database, so /var/tmp/be-8xg9/dolt was 116K at
   end of run), but during seed dolt accumulates uncommitted journal
   pages that periodically fsync. Under disk pressure or with
   accumulated uncommitted data from prior abandoned runs in the
   same data dir, fsync can ENOSPC, which trips `Fatalf(crash)`. The
   original session-resume notes referenced earlier crashed dolt
   processes leaving stale data in `/tmp/be-s9d-bench-dolt/` —
   exactly the accumulation pattern that pushes a 36G-free disk
   over.
2. **Tmpfs RAM pressure (early attempts).** Some of the original
   attempts used `/tmp` (tmpfs, 16G cap) before the operator
   constraint moved everything to `/var/tmp`. mmap-backed dolt
   writes against tmpfs under RAM pressure can fail with EIO/ENOMEM
   on the fsync path, again tripping the crash-on-fatal-IO. The
   `/tmp/be-s9d-dolt-fresh.log` referenced in the bead is itself
   from a tmpfs-backed run (pre-relocation) — that log was lost on
   reboot, which is also consistent with a tmpfs-backed data dir.
3. **Dolt minor-version churn.** Bead-time dolt was likely
   v1.86.0–v1.86.4 (Apr 6–22 tags); current is v1.86.6 (Apr 27). I
   walked `git log v1.86.0..v1.86.6 -- go/store/nbs/` in the dolt
   reference clone; there are NBS GC and journal-locking fixes in
   that range (e.g. `ccf7bde20` "Fix a rare race condition", but
   that's a deadlock not a panic) but nothing that would change the
   FatalBehaviorCrash semantics or directly fix a write-path EIO.
   Version drift is plausibly contributory but I can't pin a single
   smoking-gun commit. The mechanism itself is unchanged from
   bead-time.

### Disproven alternative hypothesis

**"The panic is a deterministic dolt bug at 10K seed regardless of
host."** Disproven: 110K successful seeded inserts on this host with
zero panics, on a dolt build that contains the FatalBehaviorCrash
mechanism. Whatever was wrong was environmental.

I considered but did not pursue:

- Looking for a specific dolt commit that "fixed" it — there is
  nothing to fix in dolt; the crash is dolt correctly refusing to
  continue after an I/O error.
- Adding a knob to disable FatalBehaviorCrash for benches —
  intentionally upstream-rejected design choice, would mask real
  data-integrity risks. (Per dolt commit message: "If an fsync
  fails, ... it is not safe for the server to keep running.")

### Cross-rig sweep of in-flight work (per playbook step 2)

- `gastownhall/beads` recent main commits (since 2026-04-25):
  PR #3435 (`f4c46d91`, 2026-04-27) bumped the dolt go.mod pin from
  `v0.40.5-0.20260326074512-005921bdd8ca` →
  `v0.40.5-0.20260422221605-73fcb4a868c2`. Routine bump, not
  triggered by this bead. **The pin is irrelevant for the panic
  path** — the panic is in the EXTERNAL `dolt sql-server` process
  (system v1.86.6), not in beads' embedded-dolt module. The bench
  harness uses `BEADS_TEST_EXTERNAL_DOLT_PORT` which connects via
  the MySQL driver; the embedded `dolthub/dolt/go` import is for
  in-process usage and not on this code path.
- No open beads PR addresses the panic.
- No open dolt PR addresses the panic.

### Files to touch / fix spec

**No code fix is needed in any rig.** The dolt FatalBehaviorCrash
mechanism is correctly designed; the bead-time triggers no longer
apply.

For be-6e8s (post-land verification, downstream of this bead),
builder action is straightforward — set up the same environment I
used and run the spec:

- Worktree from origin/main + cherry-pick `cfd38cda` (D4v2 migration)
  + `27a4f1f8` (testmain external-port). Or run the bench directly on
  `tests/be-s9d-testmain-external-port` for the HEAD numbers, plus a
  parallel pre-D4v2 worktree for the baseline numbers.
- Reuse the dolt-server setup at /var/tmp (any path on
  /dev/nvme0n1p8 is fine now — 410G free). Init a fresh repo, write
  the same `config.yaml` (autocommit: false, port 33099,
  max_connections: 200 was sufficient).
- Persist server stderr to a non-tmpfs path before starting (the
  bead's original logs were lost because /tmp is tmpfs on this
  host). Operator constraint comment from 2026-04-26 still applies.
- Run `BenchmarkCreateIssue_Existing10K` and
  `BenchmarkUpdateIssue_Existing10K` with `-count=5 -benchtime=1x`
  against both pre-D4v2 and HEAD. ~7-8 min wall per bench-class
  per worktree on this host.
- benchstat -geomean each pair, attach to be-6e8s per its
  acceptance criteria.

### Proof gate self-assessment

- [✓] Captured artifact: full bench output for both bench-classes
  at -count=5 (5 clean samples each), persisted dolt server stderr,
  matching the bead's repro spec. Files at
  `/var/tmp/be-8xg9/bench-{create,update}-{stdout,stderr}.log` and
  `/var/tmp/be-8xg9/dolt-stderr.log`. The "non-failure" is the
  proof: the failure mode no longer manifests under spec-matching
  conditions.
- [✓] Exact source line: `dolt:go/store/nbs/journal_writer.go:544`
  (the panic site), `dolt:go/libraries/utils/errors/panic.go:38`
  (the Fatalf mechanism), `dolt:go/libraries/doltcore/sqle/database.go:210`
  (the SetCrashOnFatalError call that registers it).
- [✓] Disproved at least one alternative hypothesis: see above
  ("deterministic dolt bug at 10K seed").
- [✓] Checked recent commits and PRs: see Cross-rig sweep above.
- [✓] Fix spec: no code fix needed; builder instructions for be-6e8s
  named above.

### Disposition

Closing be-8xg9 as resolved (no longer reproducible). Per be-6e8s's
deadline trigger (b) — "be-8xg9 is resolved" — closing this bead
**starts the be-6e8s clock if migration 0033 has not yet landed**.
(Migration 0033 / cfd38cda is NOT yet on origin/main; the deadline
clock for be-6e8s now hinges on this resolution.) Builder picks up
be-6e8s through normal routing and runs the bench per the spec
above; my numbers above are not a replacement for be-6e8s's
benchstat -geomean comparison but should cut setup time
substantially.

title: gc mail send timing out at session-list step (likely be-vzu N+1)
description:
## Symptom

`gc mail send <recipient>` consistently times out after 120s with:

  gc mail send: listing live sessions: bd list: timed out after 120s
  gc mail send: unknown recipient "beads/builder": resolving configured named session "beads/builder": listing session beads: bd list: timed out after 120s

Observed in beads/deployer-1 worktree on 2026-04-25 at ~16:45 PT while
attempting to mail beads/builder and mayor about two failed deploys.

## Likely root cause

The `bd list` invocations made by gc mail (to enumerate live sessions
and to resolve the recipient) hit the same N+1 wisp-membership-check
bug that be-vzu is supposed to fix — which itself is currently
needs-deploy-blocked (be-x35) and routed back to the builder for a
trivial signature-drift rebase. The fix is queued behind itself.

## Why it matters now

Until be-vzu (and probably be-pq5 — same builder branch) ships, every
deployer or mayor wishing to send mail will hit this. KDE notify still
works, but the in-cluster mail surface is degraded.

## Resolution

Untangle the be-vzu / be-s54 / be-pq5 builder stack. Once be-vzu lands
on main, gc mail should recover automatically (no separate code change
needed in the gc tooling).

If untangling takes more than a day, consider a stopgap: have gc mail
fall back to a fast path (e.g., direct file write to the recipient's
mail dir) when `bd list` exceeds a threshold.
notes: Builder check 2026-05-20: be-vzu/be-pq5/be-s54 beads not found (likely closed/merged). PRs #4001-#4004 and #4008 merged after bead was created (2026-04-25) with perf fixes for bd ready/list/deps. Quick check: 'bd list --wisp-type=heartbeat --limit=5' runs in 0.07s locally. Recommend deployer verify 'gc mail send' in their worktree before closing.

title: Cross-rig: cleanup 19GB gc-management dolt store + investigate __gc_probe autostats bloat
description:
Rig investigator handoff. Original bead: be-2cf.

## Summary

Investigated be-2cf ("beads dolt store is 19GB"). Real breakdown differs sharply from the bead's hypothesis. Some causes are **in beads** (handed off to beads/builder via separate bead). Some causes live **outside the beads rig** and need cross-rig action — this is that handoff.

## Confirmed sizes (`/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt`, total 19GB)

| Path | Size | Story |
|---|---|---|
| .dolt_dropped_databases/benchdb_*_* | **9.3GB** | 27 orphan dropped DBs from beads bench tests (DROP without PURGE — beads bug, fix landing in beads/builder bead) |
| be/.dolt/git-remote-cache/.../repo.git/objects/pack/ | **6.2GB** | **single bare clone** of github.com/gastownhall/beads.git (NOT history bloat — bead's hypothesis was wrong). noms is only 3.4MB. |
| __gc_probe/.dolt/stats/.dolt/noms | **2.0GB** | autostats noms on a probe schema whose source data is 28KB. 70000x ratio — looks like a Dolt-side runaway autostats bug, but the schema is created by gc-management's startup probe (NOT beads). |
| gascity/.dolt/git-remote-cache/.../repo.git | **644MB** | bare clone of github.com/gastownhall/gascity.git — same pattern as be |
| gascity/.dolt/noms | 19MB | actual issue data |
| gm/.dolt/noms | 316MB | actual city data (no git-remote-cache) |
| Others | <30MB | mc, projectwrenunity |

## What needs cross-rig action

### 1. Reclaim the 9.3GB of dropped benchdb_* now (operational)

Even after the beads/builder fixes the bench leak (so future runs don't accumulate), the **existing 27 orphan DBs in gc-management/.beads/dolt/.dolt_dropped_databases/ won't go away** until someone runs:

```sql
CALL DOLT_PURGE_DROPPED_DATABASES();
```

against the gc-management dolt server (port 28231 per /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.gc/runtime/packs/dolt/dolt-config.yaml). Followed by `dolt gc` to compact noms.

This is a **gc-management operational task**, not beads code — the data dir is owned by gc-management.

### 2. __gc_probe stats bloat (architectural — gc-management)

`__gc_probe` is a startup-probe schema created by gc-management (no references to it in beads source). Its source data is 28KB but `.dolt/stats/.dolt/noms` is **2GB**. Two questions for whoever owns gc-management's dolt-pack startup probe:

- Why does the probe schema persist between starts? (looks like it's never dropped — date stamp Apr 24 09:17)
- Why is autostats generating 2GB of noms on a near-empty schema? (Dolt server config has `auto_gc_behavior.enable: true` but autostats is separate from auto_gc.)

Likely fix: gc-management should DROP `__gc_probe` after the probe completes, and PURGE on startup. Or set `statistics: enable: false` for probe-only schemas. (Beads' `bd dolt` doesn't manage this schema.)

### 3. git-remote-cache growth (informational — design discussion)

The 6.2GB `be` and 644MB `gascity` git-remote-caches are **legitimate** — dolt's git-remote provider keeps a bare clone of the upstream git repo for sync. Each pack is one consolidated pack file from `git fetch`, not orphaned tmp_pack garbage.

beads/builder will:
- Add a `bd dolt cache prune` CLI to wipe these caches on demand (next sync re-fetches)
- Document this size expectation in beads docs

But the **broader question** is whether gc-management should switch its sync transport away from git-remote (e.g., DoltHub, custom remotesapi) to avoid mirroring entire upstream Git histories on every operator's machine. That's a gc-management/architecture call, not a beads call.

### 4. test_setupshared_d1a7c740 (was in bead, no longer on disk)

Bead mentioned a `test_setupshared_d1a7c740` schema. It's not currently present in /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/. Either already cleaned, or the bead was looking at a different snapshot. No action — flagging in case a stale-DB scan re-detects it.

## Trail leaves the rig

The investigation lives squarely in /home/jaword/projects/beads/ for the bench-leak code fix (handed off to beads/builder). The **operational cleanup** of /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/ AND the __gc_probe code root-cause are in gc-management — that's where this needs to land.

## Memorized prerequisite

The user's `project_dolt_cleanup_two_phase` memory is the right procedure:
1. `DROP DATABASE` (already happened for the 27 benchdbs)
2. `CALL DOLT_PURGE_DROPPED_DATABASES()` (this is what's missing — would reclaim 9.3GB)
3. `dolt gc` (compact noms after)

Run these against the gc-management dolt server (127.0.0.1:28231) after confirming nothing is mid-write.

## Reproducer commands (read-only, safe)

```bash
# Total store size
du -sh /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt
# Per-schema
du -sh /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/*
# Dropped DBs waiting for purge
du -sh /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/.dolt_dropped_databases
ls /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/.dolt_dropped_databases | wc -l
# git-remote-cache for be schema
du -sh /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/be/.dolt/git-remote-cache
# autostats bloat
du -sh /home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/__gc_probe/.dolt/stats
# Live schema sizes via mysql client (port 28231 = prod gc-management server)
mysql -h 127.0.0.1 -P 28231 -u root -e "USE be; SELECT table_name, table_rows, ROUND(data_length/1024/1024,2) AS mb FROM information_schema.tables WHERE table_schema='be' ORDER BY data_length DESC;"
```
notes:
## Deep-investigator findings (2026-05-02)

Re-investigated be-hvl. **State has changed substantially since the bead
was filed (2026-04-25)** — most concerns are resolved or in flight.

### Total store: 19GB → 9.0GB (10GB reclaimed since bead filed)

Captured artifact: `/tmp/be-hvl-artifacts/store-state-2026-05-02.txt`.

| Path | Bead said (Apr 25) | Now (May 2) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.dolt_dropped_databases` | 9.3GB (27 benchdb_*) | empty (0 entries) | **DONE** |
| `__gc_probe/.dolt/stats` | 2.0GB | 6.7MB | masked by lottery shift, see below |
| `be/.dolt/git-remote-cache` | 6.2GB | 6.2GB | unchanged (legitimate) |
| `gascity/.dolt/git-remote-cache` | 644MB | 644MB | unchanged (legitimate) |
| `gm/.dolt/noms` | 316MB | **2.0GB** | new growth; out of scope, see "Aside" |

### Item 1: 9.3GB benchdb cleanup — DONE

`/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/.dolt_dropped_databases/`
is empty as of 2026-04-30 13:16. The 27 orphan benchdbs were purged.
No further operational action needed for this bead.

(beads-side bench-leak fix per the bead's earlier handoff is a separate
work item; this bead's operational ask is resolved.)

### Item 2: __gc_probe autostats bloat — IN FLIGHT, NOT YET FIXED

**Important:** the small `__gc_probe` size on disk today is masking,
not resolving, the bug.

- The fix is **gascity PR #1358** (`release/ga-hivi-probe-user-db`,
  ga-42gi), OPEN since 2026-04-27, all CI green, no review decision yet.
  Diff: `cmd/gc/dolt_sql_health.go` — replaces hard-coded
  `__gc_probe.__probe` writes with `<first user db>.__probe`.
- The deployed production binary `/home/jaword/go/bin/gc` is built from
  gascity `f5527f452937+dirty` (May 1 14:38), which does **not** include
  the ga-42gi commit. Verified via `go tool nm` — no
  `managedDoltSelectUserDatabase` symbol.
- Old probe code lines on origin/main: `gascity:cmd/gc/dolt_sql_health.go:36-39`:
  ```go
  "CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS " + managedDoltProbeDatabase,
  "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS " + managedDoltProbeDatabase + ".__probe (k INT PRIMARY KEY)",
  "REPLACE INTO " + managedDoltProbeDatabase + ".__probe VALUES (1)",
  ```
  with `managedDoltProbeDatabase = "__gc_probe"`.
- Live state: `dolt_stats_enabled=ON`, `dolt_stats_paused=OFF`. Autostats
  is currently sized at `be/.dolt/stats: 12M` and `__gc_probe/.dolt/stats:
  6.7M`. The lottery has shifted to `be` for now, but Dolt's
  statspro election is non-deterministic — if it shifts back to
  `__gc_probe`, the 2GB bloat will recur.
- Sidelight: `be.__probe` was created by a `bd: batch commit by Jim
  Wordelman (+ __probe)` at 2026-05-01 15:59:18. The only code that
  writes a `__probe` table to a non-`__gc_probe` schema is the FIXED
  branch — verified that `/home/jaword/quad341-claude/go/bin/gc`
  contains the `managedDoltSelectUserDatabase` symbol (7 occurrences).
  So the fix has been exercised against this live store from a dev
  binary, but not from the deployed one.

**Verdict:** PR #1358 is the right fix. No new code to write or hand off.
What's needed is **review + merge + redeploy** of #1358.

### Item 3: git-remote-cache (6.2GB `be` + 644MB `gascity`) — unchanged

Per the rig investigator's original analysis these are legitimate bare
clones, not history bloat. beads/builder is adding `bd dolt cache prune`
as a CLI workaround. The deeper "what's the right sync transport"
question (DoltHub vs git-remote) is gc-management architecture; not
opening a new bead unless mayor wants one — the original investigator's
framing was "informational / design discussion", and item 3 has no
mandatory action.

### Item 4: test_setupshared_d1a7c740 — NO-OP

Confirmed not present in `/home/jaword/projects/gc-management/.beads/dolt/`.
No action needed.

### Aside (out of scope, not opening a bead): gm/.dolt/noms grew 6x

`gm/.dolt/noms` was 316MB (per bead, Apr 25) and is now 2.0GB. Likely
explanation is normal beads write traffic — `dolt.log` shows heavy
`connectionDb=gm` activity ("nothing to commit" warnings every few
seconds) consistent with the `bd: batch commit by ...` cadence, and
`information_schema.tables` shows gm.events at 34,776 rows / 6.6GB
data_length and gm.issues at 3,108 rows / 1.4GB data_length. Not
investigating further here — flagging in case it crosses an alert
threshold for someone owning city growth budget.

### Disproven hypothesis

"The autostats issue is fully resolved" — disproven. Deployed binary
still hosts probe at `__gc_probe`, autostats remains enabled, and the
lottery is non-deterministic. Today's small `__gc_probe` is incidental.

### Cross-rig action items routed by this bead — closed disposition

notes:
# Reviewer handoff — DB-recovery edition

## Context recovery
Original work bead be-8ja was lost when the beads database was re-initialized mid-session at ~04:46 UTC (21:46 local 2026-04-23). This bead is a best-effort handoff using the commit + my recollection of the spec.

## The work
Sibling of D4 (was be-nu4.4.1 in the lost DB). Adds stderr progress output and a large-rig warning to the shared migration runner so operators don't ^C a slow index build — the audit on the D4 design noted that index creation on a 49K-row issues table takes ~25-75s with zero terminal output today and the CLI looks hung.

## Commit
- 38f2f1e4 on branch gc-builder-e35c0415a93c.
- Single file: internal/storage/schema/schema.go, +35 insertions.
- Applied on top of 1915d30d (be-3ht fix) which is on top of 5023e0e1 (D3 SearchIssueSummaries).

## What changed in schema.go
1. New package var `progressOut io.Writer = os.Stderr` — unexported, for test-side swap without production API leak.
2. New const `largeRigThreshold = 10000`.
3. In `runMigrations`, after the `len(pending) == 0` early-return:
   - Query `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM issues` once. If err==nil (issues table exists) AND count>10000, emit `Large rig detected (%d issues). This migration may take up to 60 seconds; do not interrupt.\n` to progressOut.
   - A missing issues table (fresh install) scans into err!=nil, treated as count=0, no warning. Intentional — a fresh install has nothing to warn about.
4. In the per-migration loop:
   - `Applying migration %04d: %s…\n` before the Exec (uses new helper humanMigrationName to strip version prefix and .up.sql suffix).
   - `  done (%.1fs)\n` after both Exec and the INSERT IGNORE recording.
5. New helper `humanMigrationName` turns `0033_add_date_indexes.up.sql` into `add_date_indexes`.

## Spec compliance
- stderr only — stdout pipelines unaffected. Verified by call-site audit: every `fmt.Fprintf` in the diff targets progressOut (which defaults to os.Stderr).
- Plain text only — no spinners, no color, no TTY detection. Uses stdlib io/os/time only, no new deps.
- Warning gated on len(pending)>0 (early return at top of runMigrations) AND issues>10000 — fires exactly once per MigrateUp invocation with pending work on a populated rig.

## Gates
- go build ./... — clean
- go vet ./internal/storage/schema/... — clean
- gofmt -l internal/storage/schema/schema.go — clean
- go test ./internal/storage/schema/... — PASS
- BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test ./internal/storage/embeddeddolt/... -run TestSchemaAfterInit — PASS. Progress output visible end-to-end against real migrations (0001→0032 on a fresh DB, 0.0s per trivial migration, no large-rig warning since fresh DB count=0).

## Pre-existing, unrelated test failures
Ran broader suites; the following fail on clean main too (confirmed by `git stash` + re-run):
- cmd/bd/doctor role_test.go (TestCheckBeadsRole_*) — git role config detection, unrelated.
- cmd/bd TestInitCommand — 'Dolt database directory was not created' after `bd init`, unrelated.
- cmd/bd context_binding_integration_test.go and others — 'disk quota exceeded' from /tmp; cleaned up but some rebuilds still fail when /tmp refills during parallel suites.

None touch the migration runner or schema package.

## Unit test — deliberately deferred
Bead acceptance criteria includes a unit test capturing stderr from MigrateUp on fresh DB and on a 12K-row fixture. Per factory split, test authorship is the validator's job; the code is structured to make that trivial (swap progressOut to a *bytes.Buffer, drive MigrateUp through runMigrations's pending path).

## Out of scope (per original bead)
- Migration cancellation/resume protocol.
- TTY-aware fancy output.
- Changes to `bd migrate` command surface.

## Release gate
Do NOT cut a release containing D4 (be-nu4.4.1 in lost DB) until this ships. The inline stderr warning replaces a prose-only release-notes warning — it's the better UX. Independent PR otherwise, may land in parallel.

## One thing to verify
I did not run a manual 12K-row smoke test to see the large-rig warning fire in anger — the test infrastructure needed for that is the same validator suite this bead defers. A reviewer who can cheaply stand one up should confirm the format matches the spec byte-for-byte.

**Verdict: PASS** (proceed to deploy via PR #3780)

## Personas summary

- **Engineering Manager** — clean stdlib-only diff, no new deps, gofmt/vet clean at 38f2f1e4, well-scoped (single file +35 lines).
- **Principal Engineer** — design is right: unexported `progressOut` package var enables test-side swap without leaking a production setter; warning text matches spec byte-for-byte; helper extraction (in PR #3780 / 101ea7770) keeps runMigrations focused.

Output is non-sensitive operational metadata to stderr only — `bd --json | jq` pipelines unaffected (validated by TestProgressOutDefaultsToStderr). The author thought about testing — the architecture *deliberately* enables it via the unexported `progressOut` var. Validator-side coverage exists in PR #3780:

title: dolt-auto-commit defaults to ON — should default to OFF for server mode
description:
attached_molecule: dolt-test-wisp-71h6
attached_at: 2026-02-09T00:16:18Z
dispatched_by: mayor

dolt_autocommit_config.go:18 defaults to ON when dolt.auto-commit is unset. This means every bd write fires DOLT_COMMIT('-Am', ...) even in server mode with branch-per-polecat where individual commits are unnecessary.

Under concurrent load (16+ polecats), this causes manifest update contention and the Dolt server enters read-only mode.

Fix: Default should be OFF for dolt-native sync mode (or at minimum for server mode). Let callers opt-in to auto-commit rather than opt-out.

File: cmd/bd/dolt_autocommit_config.go:15-28
Related: gt-5cc2p (gastown sling should pass --dolt-auto-commit=off)
notes: Changed default dolt-auto-commit from ON to OFF in getDoltAutoCommitMode() (dolt_autocommit_config.go:18). Callers now opt-in via --dolt-auto-commit=on or config key dolt.auto-commit=on. Prevents manifest contention under concurrent polecat load.

title: BD_BRANCH checkout fails hard if branch does not exist, no auto-create
description:
attached_args: P1 fix: BD_BRANCH checkout fails hard if branch doesn't exist. Need auto-create behavior. Part of convoy hq-cv-rmqgu.
dispatched_by: beads/crew/emma

When BD_BRANCH is set in internal/storage/dolt/store.go (line 347-356), the code runs CALL DOLT_CHECKOUT(?) which fails immediately if the branch does not exist. The entire bd process exits with an error, and the polecat cannot work.

Gas Town sets BD_BRANCH to isolate polecat writes to separate Dolt branches. If the branch does not exist (race condition, Gas Town bug, or cleanup that ran too early), the polecat fails to start entirely.

Suggested fix: Try checkout first, then auto-create from current branch if not found. This makes the system self-healing - polecats create their own branches if they do not exist, eliminating the dependency on Gas Town pre-creating branches.

Location: internal/storage/dolt/store.go:347-356
close_reason: Auto-create branch on checkout failure. Try DOLT_CHECKOUT first, if branch missing, DOLT_BRANCH to create from current HEAD, then retry checkout.

title: Epic: Rip out SQLite/JSONL — Dolt-only Beads
description:
## Rip out SQLite/JSONL/daemon — make Beads Dolt-only

Plan of record (agreed Feb 7, 2026):

### Phase 1: v0.50.0 — Dolt is the default (Wed Feb 11)
- bd init defaults to --backend dolt
- SQLite still works but prints deprecation warning
- Co-launch with Dolt-in-Git blog post
- Blog post educating users about the transition

### Phase 2: v0.51.0 — SQLite removed (~Feb 21)
- Remove internal/storage/sqlite/ entirely
- Remove JSONL-as-sync-mechanism (autoflush, autoimport, 3-way merge, sync_base)
- Remove the daemon (its primary purpose was SQLite-JSONL auto-sync)
- Remove git hooks for JSONL sync
- Remove bd migrate (after transition window)
- Remove belt-and-suspenders and git-portable sync modes
- Remove SQLite corruption recovery paths
- Point users to Jeffrey Emanuel's Beads Classic (Rust) for SQLite/JSONL

### Phase 3: v0.52+ — Dolt-native cleanup (March)
- Remove any remaining JSONL-as-sync code
- JSONL becomes export-only format, not a sync path

### What to KEEP
- bd export --format jsonl (human-readable export, debugging, interop)
- Simplified bd import for one-time data ingestion (no 3-way merge)
- Bootstrap from JSONL (transition period only)

### Estimated code removal
~30-40% of codebase. Major wins in reduced test matrix and feature complexity.

### Escape hatch
Jeffrey Emanuel maintains Beads Classic (Rust): https://github.com/Dicklesworthstone/beads_rust
Compatible implementation for users who prefer SQLite/JSONL architecture.

title: bug: "connection refused" classified as non-retryable in Dolt retry logic
description:
In storage/dolt/store.go:99, "connection refused" errors are classified as non-retryable. When the Dolt server crashes and comes back, every bd operation fails immediately with no retry instead of backing off and waiting for recovery. This is the root amplifier of the cascading failure — a transient server outage becomes a permanent failure for all in-flight operations.

Fix: Move "connection refused" to the retryable error list in isRetryableError(), with exponential backoff. Also consider adding a short grace period for server restart scenarios.

File: internal/storage/dolt/store.go:99 (isRetryableError function)
Compare: Lines 86-97 show other errors that ARE retried (bad connection, broken pipe, connection reset).
close_reason: Moved 'connection refused' from non-retryable to retryable in isRetryableError(). Server restarts are transient and will recover within the 30s backoff window.

title: bd should fail-fast if metadata says dolt_mode=server but server unreachable
description: When metadata.json contains dolt_mode=server, bd should attempt a TCP connection to the configured Dolt server port before proceeding. If the server is unreachable, bd should fail immediately with a clear error message pointing the user to 'gt dolt start', rather than silently falling back to creating a local database. This is the bd-side fix for the split-brain risk described in gt-ceq7b. The gt-side fix (doctor check, auto-start in gt dolt migrate) is being implemented separately.
close_reason: Fixed: added fail-fast TCP pre-check in dolt.New() before MySQL protocol initialization, with clear error pointing to gt dolt start

title: Daemon: reEstablishWatch blocks fsnotify event loop
description:
attached_molecule: dolt-test-wisp-dm7o
attached_at: 2026-02-09T01:33:44Z
dispatched_by: mayor

daemon_watcher.go:202-203 calls reEstablishWatch directly from fsnotify event loop goroutine. reEstablishWatch sleeps with exponential backoff (up to 750ms total). During this time the event loop is blocked and cannot process other events. If fsnotify buffer fills, events are dropped. Fix: run reEstablishWatch in a separate goroutine.
notes: Fixed: moved reEstablishWatch call from synchronous inline in fsnotify event loop to a separate goroutine tracked by fw.wg. Prevents blocking event processing during exponential backoff retries (up to 750ms).

title: Daemon: Channel leak in select loop via repeated make(chan time.Time)
description:
attached_molecule: dolt-test-wisp-gvvw
attached_at: 2026-02-09T01:33:25Z
dispatched_by: mayor

daemon_event_loop.go:147 and :171 use inline IIFEs that call make(chan time.Time) on every select iteration when ticker is nil. Each iteration allocates an unbuffered channel never closed or GCd. Over long-running daemon this accumulates garbage. Fix: create never-fire channels once before loop, or use nil channel directly in select (nil channel blocks forever).
notes: Replaced inline IIFEs calling make(chan time.Time) on every select iteration with pre-allocated nil channel variables. A nil <-chan time.Time blocks forever in select, providing the same never-fire behavior without per-iteration garbage allocation.

title: Security: path traversal in RPC export handler
description: internal/rpc/server_export_import_auto.go accepts user-supplied JSONLPath (line 25-32 via ExportArgs) with zero path validation. The path flows to os.CreateTemp (line 142), os.Rename (line 190), and os.Chmod (line 198), enabling arbitrary file write to any path the process can access. No canonicalization, no symlink detection, no workspace containment check. Fix: validate that JSONLPath resolves within the workspace directory.

title: Security: shell command injection via sh -c in import.go
description: cmd/bd/import.go:662 uses exec.Command("sh", "-c", cmd) where cmd is built via fmt.Sprintf with file paths (lines 638, 714). If a filename contains shell metacharacters (;, |, $, backticks), this enables command injection. The relPath is normalized via filepath.Rel() but that does not strip shell-special characters. Fix: refactor to use exec.Command with individual arguments instead of sh -c.
close_reason: Closed

title: Sync: bd sync --resolve --ours/--theirs doesnt apply strategy
description: In sync.go:1061-1094, resolveSyncConflicts iterates over conflicts and determines winner based on strategy (ours/theirs/newest) but only PRINTS the result. It never modifies any issues. Then at line 1102, MergeIssues is re-run with the original unmodified base/local/remote inputs, which re-applies default LWW merge ignoring the user strategy. The --ours and --theirs flags effectively do nothing for automated resolution. Only --manual works correctly because it uses a separate interactive path.
close_reason: Fixed: resolveSyncConflicts now collects strategy winners and overrides MergeIssues result for conflicting issues

title: Sync: merge.go conflict error check can panic on short error

If the error message is shorter than 20 characters, this panics with index out of range. Should use strings.HasPrefix instead. Example trigger: any merge.Merge3Way error with a short message like 'parse error'.

title: migrate dolt uses hardcoded database name causing cross-rig contamination
description:
attached_molecule: dolt-test-wisp-917
attached_at: 2026-02-07T05:08:10Z
dispatched_by: mayor

In cmd/bd/migrate_dolt.go line 139: cfg.Database = "dolt" is hardcoded. When multiple rigs on the same Dolt server each run bd migrate dolt, they all connect to the same database named 'dolt', causing cross-rig contamination (gastown sees beads issues and vice versa).

Fix: Use the rig's issue prefix as the database name. E.g., gastown (prefix 'gt') gets database 'beads_gt', beads (prefix 'bd') gets database 'beads_bd'. The prefix is already available during migration (it's read from the SQLite config table).

Also update store.go default (line 126) to derive the database name from the prefix in metadata.json or config, rather than defaulting to 'beads'.

Reproduction: On lab VM migration-test-lab, run bd migrate dolt in two different rigs sharing the same Dolt server on port 3307. The second rig's issues appear in the first rig's listing.

Related: bd-73cf5 (cross-rig contamination detection) detected this but didn't fix the root cause.
notes: Fixed: migrate_dolt.go and init.go now derive Dolt SQL database name from issue prefix (beads_<prefix>). Also backtick-quoted CREATE DATABASE in store.go for safety with special characters in prefixes.

title: bd ledger: Export agent capability/completion history
description:
attached_molecule: bd-wisp-infj9
attached_at: 2026-02-06T03:48:09Z
dispatched_by: mayor

## Summary

Add a `bd ledger` command that exports agent completion history as a structured report. This is the "Capability Ledger" — a permanent record of what agents have accomplished, used for tracking capability over time.

## What It Exports

For each agent (polecat/crew member), extract:
- Issues worked on (hooked/assigned)
- Completion status (closed, rejected, abandoned)
- MRs created and their outcomes (merged, rejected, conflicts)
- Time from hook to completion
- Lines changed (from git diff stats if available)
- Quality signals: first-attempt merge vs retry count

## Output Formats
- `bd ledger` — human-readable summary table
- `bd ledger --json` — machine-readable JSON
- `bd ledger --csv` — CSV export for spreadsheets
- `bd ledger --agent=<name>` — filter to specific agent
- `bd ledger --rig=<name>` — filter to specific rig
- `bd ledger --since=<date>` — time window filter

## Data Sources
- Agent beads (type=agent, labels=gt:agent)
- Issue assignee/owner fields
- Merge request beads (labels=gt:merge-request) and their status
- Close reasons and notes

## Example Output
```
Agent Capability Ledger — gastown
═══════════════════════════════════
Agent      Completed  Rejected  Avg Time  Lines Changed
furiosa    12         1         22m       +1847/-312
gus        8          0         18m       +923/-156
obsidian   15         2         31m       +2104/-891
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] bd ledger shows completion history per agent
- [ ] Filters by agent, rig, date range
- [ ] JSON and CSV export formats
- [ ] Handles cross-rig agent work (same agent, different rigs)

title: Remove embedded Dolt mode from bd — server-only
description:
attached_molecule: bd-wisp-x50u6
attached_at: 2026-02-05T21:43:20Z
dispatched_by: mayor

## Summary

With server mode live and daemon-managed, embedded mode is dead code. Remove it entirely.

## What Gets Removed

1. **go-dolt embedded driver** (go.mod) — largest dep, ~100MB of binary
2. **access_lock.go** — entire file (advisory flock layer)
3. **Embedded connection path** in store.go — openEmbeddedConnection(), withEmbeddedDolt(), UOW1/UOW2
4. **Server→embedded fallback** in factory_dolt.go — isServerConnectionError() fallback
5. **JSONL bootstrap** in factory_dolt.go — bootstrapEmbeddedDolt(), hasDoltSubdir()
6. **isReadOnlyCommand()** in main.go — server handles concurrency natively
7. **Semaphore hacks** — MaxConcurrentBd (G1/G5)
8. **Lock timeout config** — 5s/15s read/write timeouts
9. **CGO build tags** — no longer needed

## Impact

- Binary: ~120MB → ~20MB (no embedded Dolt engine)
- Build: ~90s → ~15s (pure Go, no CGO)
- store.go: two code paths → one (server only)
- ~300 lines of lock-related code removed

## Design doc

See Part 11 of gastown/mayor/rig/docs/design/dolt-storage.md
notes: Implemented: Removed embedded Dolt driver (dolthub/driver), CGO build tags, access locks, bootstrap code, nocgo stubs, go-icu-regex vendored dep. 97 files changed, +281/-5746 lines. Binary reduced ~120MB to 44MB. All non-Dolt tests pass. Dolt integration tests skip gracefully when no server running.
close_reason: Already merged to beads main as e5330641.

title: Skip CREATE DATABASE for read-only commands
description:
attached_molecule: bd-wisp-r3688
attached_at: 2026-02-05T18:13:54Z
dispatched_by: mayor

## Root Cause

In internal/storage/dolt/store.go:242-246, even read-only commands (list, show, ready, etc.) execute UOW1: CREATE DATABASE IF NOT EXISTS. This is a WRITE operation that acquires Dolt's exclusive noms LOCK, even though the advisory lock correctly uses a shared flock for read-only mode. This serializes all readers unnecessarily.

## Fix

Wrap UOW1 in a if !cfg.ReadOnly guard, same as UOW2 (line 250). The database must already exist for reads to succeed. If it doesn't, the subsequent query will fail with a clear error anyway.

## Expected Impact

Eliminates the exclusive noms LOCK acquisition for all read-only commands (list, show, ready, stats, blocked, count, search, graph, duplicates, comments, current). Multiple concurrent readers will no longer serialize on Dolt's internal file lock.

## Related: bd-luqt0 (parent lock contention issue)
close_reason: Already fixed on main (74920a8b)

title: Dolt lock contention causes bd commands to hang with many agents
description:
## Problem

With many agents running (7+ beads crew doing PR reviews, plus witnesses, refineries, mayor, deacon), bd commands frequently hang for 15+ seconds and timeout. This causes:

1. gt status, bd list, bd blocked become unusable
2. Agents get confused when commands fail, may take wrong actions
3. Work coordination breaks down

## Root Cause

Dolt uses exclusive locks for writes. The current 15-second timeout means only one bd process can write at a time. Read queries also take write locks. Hooks spawn bd on every prompt, session start, etc.

## Proposed Solutions

### Short-term
1. Add --readonly mode for queries that uses shared lock
2. Batch hook mail checks into single bd call
3. Tune lock timeout (shorter with retry backoff?)

### Medium-term
1. Connection pooling within sessions
2. Query result caching for hooks

## Workarounds

- pkill -f "^bd " to clear stuck processes
- bd --no-daemon --allow-stale <cmd> to bypass coordination
close_reason: Resolved: Migrated to dolt sql-server mode. All 4 databases (hq, beads, gastown, wyvern) served by single server on port 3307. No more file-level locking.

title: Add BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK env var for Dolt lock testing
description:
## Context

The Dolt team is questioning whether the flock-based `dolt-access.lock` in beads is necessary, given that Dolt has its own internal locking mechanism.

## Current Architecture

1. **Dolt's internal lock** - Built into embedded Dolt
2. **`dolt-access.lock` (flock)** - Added by beads in commit `12693685` to prevent zombie bd processes
3. **Old `.beads/sem/slot.*`** - The G5 semaphore that was replaced by flock

## Task

Add an env var `BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK=1` to bypass the flock layer so we can test whether Dolt's internal locking is sufficient for ~50 concurrent workers.

### Implementation

In `internal/storage/dolt/store.go:207`, change:
```go
if !cfg.ServerMode && cfg.OpenTimeout > 0 {
```
to:
```go
if !cfg.ServerMode && cfg.OpenTimeout > 0 && os.Getenv("BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK") == "" {
```

### Testing Plan

1. With `BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK=1`, run concurrent bd commands and verify:
   - No deadlocks or data corruption
   - Dolt's internal lock handles contention correctly
   - Error messages are clear when lock contention occurs

2. If Dolt's lock is sufficient, we can remove the flock layer entirely
3. If not, document what scenarios require the flock layer

## Related

- Commit 12693685: "fix: advisory flock to prevent zombie bd processes from dolt lock contention"
- DOLT-HEALTH-P0.md Phase D work
- Dolt team communication about embedded mode concurrency
close_reason: Added BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK env var check in store.go:207. Set BD_SKIP_ACCESS_LOCK=1 to bypass the flock layer and test if Dolt's internal locking is sufficient.

title: bd creates local .beads in crew directories instead of using routed location
description:
## Problem

When bd runs from a crew directory (e.g., gastown/crew/max/), it creates a local .beads/ directory instead of using the routed rig location (gastown/mayor/rig/.beads/).

## Evidence

After cleaning up all crew .beads directories, they immediately regenerate when agents run bd commands:

```
$ find ~/gt -type d -name '.beads'
/Users/stevey/gt/wyvern/mayor/rig/.beads
/Users/stevey/gt/.beads
/Users/stevey/gt/gastown/crew/max/.beads  <-- SHOULD NOT EXIST
/Users/stevey/gt/gastown/mayor/rig/.beads
/Users/stevey/gt/beads/mayor/rig/.beads
```

## Expected Behavior

bd should:
1. Walk up to find the rig root (has config.json)
2. Route to mayor/rig/.beads/ for that rig
3. Never create .beads/ in crew/polecat/refinery directories

## Related

bd-a4gwx - bd routing broken from crew directories (different symptom, possibly same root cause)
close_reason: Fixed by emma - redirect files in crew dirs route to rig .beads

title: bd routing broken from crew directories - 'no beads database found'
description:
## Problem

Running bd commands from crew directories (e.g., gastown/crew/mel) fails with 'no beads database found' even when the prefix should route to a valid rig.

## Example

```
$ pwd
/Users/stevey/gt/gastown/crew/mel

$ bd show bd-zlih1
Error: no beads database found
```

But the same command works from the rig directory:
```
$ cd /Users/stevey/gt/beads/mayor/rig && bd show bd-zlih1
✓ bd-zlih1 [BUG] ...
```

## Expected Behavior

bd should:
1. Detect the bd- prefix
2. Look up routes.jsonl (in town .beads)
3. Route to beads/mayor/rig/.beads

This used to work before the Dolt migration.

## Likely Cause

The database discovery logic changed during Dolt migration and broke prefix-based routing from non-rig directories.

title: Remove BD_BACKEND env var override - prevents sqlite fallback
description:
## Problem

Polecats can accidentally fall back to sqlite backend via BD_BACKEND=sqlite env var when they hit dolt lock errors. This fragments data across backends.

## Evidence

Polecat furiosa hit dolt lock errors and tried:
```
BD_BACKEND=sqlite bd show gt-wisp-f4d5
```

This would have worked and written to sqlite while other processes use dolt - data fragmentation.

## Related Issue

Also discovered the bd binary wasn't built with CGO, causing:
```
dolt backend requires CGO (not available on this build)
```
This may be fixed now (emma's recent make install) but needs verification.

## Fix

1. Remove BD_BACKEND and BD_DATABASE_BACKEND env var overrides entirely
2. Or: Only allow them when an explicit --i-know-what-im-doing flag is set
3. Ensure Makefile always builds with CGO_ENABLED=1
close_reason: Blocked BD_BACKEND and BD_DATABASE_BACKEND env vars in PersistentPreRun with clear error message. Added checkBlockedEnvVars() + tests. Makefile already has CGO_ENABLED=1.

title: JSONL auto-flush writes despite dolt-native sync mode
description:
dispatched_by: gastown/crew/mel

## Problem

Post-Dolt migration, JSONL files are being actively written to despite `sync.mode: dolt-native` in config.yaml. This mode should mean 'no JSONL, just Dolt commits/push'.

## Evidence

Active JSONL files alongside dolt/ directories (all updated Feb 4 2026):

| Location | Size | Lines |
|----------|------|-------|
| ~/gt/.beads/issues.jsonl | 427KB | 586 |
| ~/gt/gastown/mayor/rig/.beads/issues.jsonl | 178KB | 259 |
| ~/gt/beads/mayor/rig/.beads/issues.jsonl | 863KB | 907 |

All three have `sync.mode: dolt-native` in their config.yaml.

## Root Cause Hypothesis

The `no-auto-flush` setting defaults to `false` (enabled), so even with dolt-native mode, the auto-flush mechanism still writes JSONL after each mutation. The dolt-native mode doesn't properly disable JSONL auto-flush.

## Additional Artifacts Found

### SQLite files:
- ~/gt/deacon/.beads/beads.db (282KB) - has redirect file but beads.db not cleaned
- ~/gt/sky/.beads/beads.backup-pre-dolt-*.db (5.3MB) - backup, maybe intentional

### Migration leftovers in beads-worktrees:
- beads.left.jsonl files
- issues.jsonl.new export artifacts
- Empty interactions.jsonl files

## Fix Needed

1. When sync.mode=dolt-native, auto-flush should be disabled (or skip JSONL write)
2. Clean up existing JSONL files from migrated installations
3. Clean up beads.db from deacon/.beads/
notes: Fixed in commit 69bf2c96. ShouldExportJSONL() now returns false for dolt-native mode. Cleanup of existing JSONL files should be done separately.
close_reason: Fixed in cd9768d4. Verified: bd commands no longer create issues.jsonl in dolt-native mode.

title: bd cleanup --hard should skip tombstone creation for true permanent deletion
description:
## Problem

When using bd cleanup --hard --older-than N --force, the command:
1. Deletes closed issues older than N days (converting them to tombstones with NOW timestamp)
2. Then tries to prune tombstones older than N days (finds none because they were just created)

This leaves the database bloated with fresh tombstones that will not be pruned.

## Expected Behavior

In --hard mode, the deletion should be permanent without creating tombstones, since the user explicitly requested bypassing sync safety.

## Workaround

Manually delete from database: sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'DELETE FROM issues WHERE status=tombstone'

## Fix Options

1. In --hard mode, use a different delete path that does not create tombstones
2. After deleting, immediately prune the just-created tombstones regardless of age
3. Pass a skip_tombstone flag to the delete operation

Option 1 is cleanest - --hard should mean permanent delete without tombstone.

description:
## Problem

Running bd cleanup --force fails with:

Error: failed to create tombstone for bd-okh: sqlite3: constraint failed: CHECK constraint failed: (status = 'closed') = (closed_at IS NOT NULL)

## Root Cause

The database has a CHECK constraint ensuring closed issues have closed_at set and non-closed issues do not. When bd cleanup tries to convert a closed issue to a tombstone, this constraint fails.

## Impact

- 722 closed issues cannot be cleaned up
- Blocks routine maintenance

## Investigation Needed

1. Check the bd-okh record in the database
2. Determine if this is data corruption or a bug in tombstone creation

## Proposed Solutions

1. If data corruption: Add a bd doctor --fix check that repairs status/closed_at mismatches
2. If code bug: Fix the tombstone creation to properly handle the constraint

## Files to Investigate

- internal/storage/sqlite/sqlite.go - DeleteIssue / tombstone creation
- Schema CHECK constraint definition

## Acceptance Criteria

- Identify root cause (data vs code bug)
- bd cleanup --force completes successfully
- bd doctor detects status/closed_at mismatches

title: bd cleanup should also prune expired tombstones
description:
## Problem

bd cleanup deletes closed issues (converting them to tombstones) but does NOT prune expired tombstones. Users expect 'cleanup' to do comprehensive cleanup.

## Current Behavior

1. bd cleanup --force converts closed issues to tombstones
2. Expired tombstones (>30 days) remain in issues.jsonl  
3. User must separately run bd compact to prune tombstones
4. bd doctor warns about expired tombstones: Run bd compact to prune

## Expected Behavior

bd cleanup should also prune expired tombstones from issues.jsonl.

## Impact

With v0.30.0 making tombstones the default migration path, this UX gap becomes more visible. Users cleaning up their database should not need to know about a separate bd compact command.

## Proposed Solution

Call pruneExpiredTombstones() at the end of the cleanup command (same function used by compact).

## Files to Modify

- cmd/bd/cleanup.go - Add call to pruneExpiredTombstones after deleteBatch

## Acceptance Criteria

- bd cleanup --force prunes expired tombstones after deleting closed issues
- bd cleanup --dry-run shows what tombstones would be pruned
- JSON output includes tombstone prune results

title: fix: bd onboard hangs on Windows

Parameterize SQLite busy_timeout in store.go
description:
Modify sqlite.New() to accept configurable busy_timeout.

## Current State
`internal/storage/sqlite/store.go` hardcodes:
```go
connStr = "file:" + path + "?_pragma=foreign_keys(ON)&_pragma=busy_timeout(30000)&..."
```

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Add timeout parameter to New()
```go
func New(ctx context.Context, path string, busyTimeout time.Duration) (*SQLiteStorage, error)
```
Pro: Simple, explicit
Con: Changes function signature (breaking change for callers)

### Option B: Options struct pattern
```go
type Options struct {
    BusyTimeout time.Duration // default 30s
}
func New(ctx context.Context, path string, opts *Options) (*SQLiteStorage, error)
```
Pro: Extensible, nil means defaults
Con: More boilerplate

### Recommendation: Option A with default
```go
func New(ctx context.Context, path string) (*SQLiteStorage, error) {
    return NewWithOptions(ctx, path, 30*time.Second)
}

func NewWithOptions(ctx context.Context, path string, busyTimeout time.Duration) (*SQLiteStorage, error)
```

## Acceptance Criteria
- busy_timeout is parameterized in connection string
- 0 timeout means no waiting (immediate SQLITE_BUSY)
- All existing callers continue to work (via default wrapper)

title: Sync protection mechanism resurrects deleted issues
description:
During bd sync, the 'Protecting N issue(s) from left snapshot' logic resurrects issues that are in the deletions manifest, causing UNIQUE constraint failures on subsequent syncs.

## Reproduction
1. Delete an issue with bd delete (creates tombstone + deletions.jsonl entry)
2. Run bd sync - succeeds
3. Run bd sync again - fails with 'UNIQUE constraint failed: issues.id'

## Root Cause
The protection mechanism (designed to prevent data loss during 3-way merge) keeps a snapshot of issues before sync. When importing after pull, it restores issues from this snapshot even if they're in the deletions manifest.

## Observed Behavior
- bd-3pd was deleted and added to deletions.jsonl
- First sync exports tombstone, commits, pulls, imports - succeeds
- Second sync: protection restores bd-3pd from left snapshot
- Import tries to create bd-3pd which already exists → UNIQUE constraint error

## Expected Behavior
Issues in deletions manifest should NOT be restored by protection mechanism.

## Workaround
Manually delete from DB: sqlite3 .beads/beads.db 'DELETE FROM issues WHERE id = "bd-xxx"'

## Files to Investigate
- cmd/bd/sync.go - protection logic
- cmd/bd/snapshot_manager.go - left snapshot handling
- internal/importer/importer.go - import with protection

title: Replace Windows CI full test suite with smoke tests
description:
## Problem

Windows CI tests consistently timeout at 30 minutes despite multiple optimization attempts:
- Split into parallel jobs (cmd vs internal) - still times out
- RAM disk for temp/cache - marginal improvement (~50%)
- RAM disk for workspace - breaks due to t.Chdir() incompatibility with ImDisk

Root cause: Windows I/O is fundamentally 20x slower than Linux:
- NTFS slow for small file operations
- Windows Defender scans every file access
- Git on Windows is 5-10x slower
- Process spawning is expensive

Linux tests complete in ~1.5 min with race detector. Windows takes 30+ min without.

## Current State

- Windows jobs have continue-on-error: true (don't block PRs)
- Tests timeout before completing, providing zero signal
- RAM disk experiments added complexity without solving the problem

## Solution: Smoke Tests Only

Replace full test suite with minimal smoke tests that verify Windows compatibility in < 2 minutes.

### What to Test
1. Binary builds - go build succeeds (already separate step)
2. Binary executes - bd version works
3. Init works - bd init creates valid database
4. Basic CRUD - create, list, show, update, close
5. Path handling - Windows backslash paths work

### Proposed CI Change

Replace test-windows-cmd and test-windows-internal with single smoke test job:
- Build bd.exe
- Run: bd version
- Run: bd init --quiet --prefix smoke
- Run: bd create --title "Windows smoke test" --type task
- Run: bd list
- Run: bd show smoke-001
- Run: bd update smoke-001 --status in_progress
- Run: bd close smoke-001

### Benefits
- Completes in < 2 minutes vs 30+ minute timeouts
- Provides actual pass/fail signal
- Verifies Windows binary works
- Removes RAM disk complexity
- Single job instead of two parallel jobs

### Files to Change
- .github/workflows/ci.yml - Replace test-windows-cmd and test-windows-internal jobs

### Migration Steps
1. Remove test-windows-cmd job
2. Remove test-windows-internal job
3. Add single test-windows job with smoke tests
4. Remove continue-on-error (tests should now pass reliably)
5. Clean up RAM disk remnants from previous attempts

### Context
- Parent issue: bd-5we (Use RAM disk for Windows CI tests)
- RAM disk approach proved insufficient
- This is the pragmatic solution after extensive experimentation

title: bd hooks install fails in git worktrees
description:
When bd is used in a git worktree, bd hooks install fails with 'mkdir .git: not a directory' because .git is a file (gitdir pointer) not a directory. Beads should detect and follow the .git gitdir pointer to install hooks in the correct location. This blocks normal worktree workflows.

## Symptoms of this bug:
- Git hooks don't install automatically
- Auto-sync doesn't run (5-second debounce)
- Hash mismatch warnings in bd output
- Daemon fails to start with 'auto_start_failed'

## Workaround:
Use `git rev-parse --git-dir` to find the actual hooks directory and copy hooks manually:
```bash
mkdir -p $(git rev-parse --git-dir)/hooks
cp -r .beads-hooks/* $(git rev-parse --git-dir)/hooks/
```

title: Auto-compact deletions during bd sync
Add --body-file flag to bd create for reading descriptions from files
description:
## Problem

Creating issues with long/complex descriptions via CLI requires shell escaping gymnastics:

```bash
# Current workaround - awkward heredoc quoting
bd create --title="..." --description="$(cat <<'EOF'
...markdown...
EOF
)"

# Often fails with quote escaping errors in eval context
# Agents resort to writing temp files then reading them
```

## Proposed Solution

Add `--body-file` and `--description-file` flags to read description from a file, matching `gh` CLI pattern.

```bash
# Natural pattern that aligns with training data
cat > /tmp/desc.md << 'EOF'
...markdown content...
EOF

bd create --title="..." --body-file=/tmp/desc.md
```

## Implementation

### 1. Add new flags to `bd create`

```go
createCmd.Flags().String("body-file", "", "Read description from file (use - for stdin)")
createCmd.Flags().String("description-file", "", "Alias for --body-file")
```

### 2. Flag precedence

- If `--body-file` or `--description-file` is provided, read from file
- If value is `-`, read from stdin
- Otherwise fall back to `--body` or `--description` flag
- If neither provided, description is empty (current behavior)

### 3. Error handling

- File doesn't exist → clear error message
- File not readable → clear error message
- stdin specified but not available → clear error message

## Benefits

✅ **Matches training data**: `gh issue create --body-file file.txt` is a common pattern
✅ **No shell escaping issues**: File content is read directly
✅ **Works with any content**: Markdown, special characters, quotes, etc.
✅ **Agent-friendly**: Agents already write complex content to temp files
✅ **User-friendly**: Easier for humans too when pasting long descriptions

## Related Commands

Consider adding similar support to:
- `bd update --body-file` (for updating descriptions)
- `bd comment --body-file` (if/when we add comments)

## Examples

```bash
# From file
bd create --title="Add new feature" --body-file=feature.md

# From stdin
echo "Quick description" | bd create --title="Bug fix" --body-file=-

# With other flags
bd create \
  --title="Security issue" \
  --type=bug \
  --priority=0 \
  --body-file=security-report.md \
  --label=security
```

## Testing

- Test with normal files
- Test with stdin (`-`)
- Test with non-existent files (error handling)
- Test with binary files (should handle gracefully)
- Test with empty files (valid - empty description)
- Test that `--description-file` and `--body-file` are equivalent aliases

title: Fix TestFallbackToDirectModeEnablesFlush deadlock causing 10min test timeout
description:
## Problem

TestFallbackToDirectModeEnablesFlush in direct_mode_test.go deadlocks for 9m59s before timing out, causing the entire test suite to take 10+ minutes instead of <10 seconds.

## Root Cause

Database lock contention between test cleanup and flushToJSONL():
- Test cleanup (line 36) tries to close DB via defer
- flushToJSONL() (line 132) is still accessing DB
- Results in deadlock: database/sql.(*DB).Close() waits for mutex while GetJSONLFileHash() holds it

## Stack Trace Evidence

```
goroutine 512 [sync.Mutex.Lock, 9 minutes]:
database/sql.(*DB).Close(0x14000643790)
  .../database/sql/sql.go:927 +0x84
github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd.TestFallbackToDirectModeEnablesFlush.func1()
  .../direct_mode_test.go:36 +0xf4

While goroutine running flushToJSONL() holds DB connection via GetJSONLFileHash()
```

## Impact

- Test suite: 10+ minutes → should be <10 seconds
- ALL other tests pass in ~4 seconds
- This ONE test accounts for 99.9% of test runtime

## Related

This is the EXACT same issue documented in MAIN_TEST_REFACTOR_NOTES.md for why main_test.go refactoring was deferred - global state manipulation + DB cleanup = deadlock.

## Fix Approaches

1. **Add proper cleanup sequencing** - stop flush goroutines BEFORE closing DB
2. **Use test-specific DB lifecycle** - ensure flush completes before cleanup
3. **Mock the flush mechanism** - avoid real DB for testing this code path  
4. **Add explicit timeout handling** - fail fast with clear error instead of hanging

## Files

- cmd/bd/direct_mode_test.go:36-132
- cmd/bd/autoflush.go:353 (validateJSONLIntegrity)
- cmd/bd/autoflush.go:508 (flushToJSONLWithState)

## Acceptance

- Test passes without timeout
- Test suite completes in <10 seconds
- No deadlock between cleanup and flush operations
close_reason: Made SQLiteStorage.Close() idempotent via CompareAndSwap on the closed flag. Fixed FlushManager cleanup ordering in test. Test suite: 231s -> 103s, WAL checkpoint warnings: 81 -> 0.

title: Git merge driver uses invalid placeholders (%L, %R instead of %A, %B)
description:
## Problem

The beads git merge driver is configured with invalid Git placeholders:

```
git config merge.beads.driver "bd merge %A %O %L %R"
```

Git doesn't recognize `%L` or `%R` as valid merge driver placeholders. The valid placeholders are:
- `%O` = base (common ancestor)
- `%A` = current version (ours)
- `%B` = other version (theirs)

## Impact

- Affects ALL users when they have `.beads/beads.jsonl` merge conflicts
- Automatic JSONL merge fails with error: "error reading left file: failed to open file: open 7: no such file or directory"
- Users must manually resolve conflicts instead of getting automatic merge

## Root Cause

The `bd init` command (or wherever the merge driver is configured) is using non-standard placeholders. When Git encounters `%L` and `%R`, it either passes them literally or interprets them incorrectly.

## Fix

Update the merge driver configuration to:
```
git config merge.beads.driver "bd merge %A %O %A %B"
```

Where:
- 1st `%A` = output file (current file, will be overwritten)
- `%O` = base (common ancestor)
- 2nd `%A` = left/current version
- `%B` = right/other version

## Action Items

1. Fix `bd init` (or equivalent setup command) to use correct placeholders
2. Add migration/warning for existing users with misconfigured merge driver
3. Update documentation with correct merge driver setup
4. Consider adding validation when `bd init` is run
close_reason: Already fixed. The code now uses correct placeholders '%A %O %A %B' (init_git_hooks.go:654). Detection of old %L/%R placeholders is at lines 437-440, and doctor checks/fixes are in doctor/git.go and doctor/fix/merge_driver.go.
