title: bd: local-only Dolt guardrail — persistent no-remote marker + warn/refuse when a dolt remote equals a repo's public git origin
description:
# Architecture: bd local-only Dolt guardrail (be-ax9h1)

## Problem Summary

Recurring city-health incident (gm-x28y5b, gm-4lxazp, today: gascity rig):
an agent "fixes" a `bd dolt push` "non-fast-forward / no-common-ancestor"
failure by running `bd dolt remote add origin <git-origin-url>`, then calling
`DOLT_PULL`. This causes:

1. **CPU churn:** Dolt sql-server hits ~180% CPU from orphaned native-merge
   goroutines. Client timeout does not stop server-side merge.
2. **Data leak:** Private bead state is pushed to the public git origin.

Current mitigation relies on agents reading a `bd remember` memory — fragile.

---

## Requirements

### Functional

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| FR-01 | A per-project config key `dolt.local-only=true` disables `bd dolt push` and `bd dolt pull` with a clear informational message and exit 0 |
| FR-02 | When `dolt.local-only=true`, `bd dolt remote add` refuses with exit 1 and an error message |
| FR-03 | When `dolt.local-only=true`, the auto-adoption path (`adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush`) is a no-op |
| FR-04 | When `dolt.local-only=true`, `maybeAutoPush` is a no-op |
| FR-05 | `bd config set dolt.local-only true` and `bd config unset dolt.local-only` are the canonical on/off controls |
| FR-06 | `bd dolt remote add` refuses (exit 1) when the URL-to-add normalizes to the same URL as the current git origin |
| FR-07 | FR-06 refusal can be overridden with `--allow-git-origin` for intentional git-backed Dolt storage |
| FR-08 | `bd doctor` emits a warning check when any Dolt remote's URL matches the normalized git origin URL |
| FR-09 | `bd doctor` fix guidance for FR-08: `bd dolt remote remove <name>` + optionally `bd config set dolt.local-only true` |

### Non-Functional

| ID | Requirement |
|----|-------------|
| NFR-01 | Exit code for push/pull no-op is **0** — agents must not retry or escalate |
| NFR-02 | Exit code for remote add refusal is **1** — agents should stop the add attempt |
| NFR-03 | No schema changes — config.yaml only |
| NFR-04 | No changes to Dolt sql-server or dolt binary behavior |
| NFR-05 | No auto-detection of "public" vs "private" repos — that's heuristic and fragile |
| NFR-06 | No changes to `bd init` behavior |

---

## Constraints

| Type | Constraint |
|------|-----------|
| Technical | `dolt.*` namespace is already in the `IsYamlOnlyKey` prefix whitelist (`yaml_config.go:92`) — `dolt.local-only` inherits storage in `config.yaml` automatically |
| Technical | `config.GetBool(key)` returns `false` safely when config is not loaded — no guard breach on early init |
| Technical | `bd dolt remote add` already holds `getStore()` open before the guard can check — need to check before `getStore()` or check in-band |
| Business | Existing git-backed Dolt storage setups must keep working via `--allow-git-origin` |
| Operational | The marker must survive `git pull` — `config.yaml` is git-tracked, not gitignored |

---

## Framework Selections

| Layer | Name | Rationale |
|-------|------|-----------|
| Config storage | `config.yaml` via Viper | `dolt.*` prefix already yaml-only; no DB writes needed |
| Config read | `config.GetBool("dolt.local-only")` | Consistent with `isDoltAutoPushEnabled()` pattern |
| CLI flag | `--allow-git-origin` on `bd dolt remote add` | Explicit opt-in; more readable than `--force` for this specific risk |
| Doctor check | `doctorCheck` struct + `convertWithCategory` | Consistent with all existing doctor checks |

---

## Component Layout

```
cmd/bd/dolt.go
  ├── isDoltLocalOnly() bool                  [NEW helper]
  ├── doltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin(url) bool    [NEW helper]
  ├── doltPushCmd.Run                         [MOD: early local-only check]
  ├── doltPullCmd.Run                         [MOD: early local-only check]
  ├── adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush()           [MOD: local-only short-circuit]
  └── doltRemoteAddCmd.Run                    [MOD: local-only + git-origin guards]
       └── init(): add --allow-git-origin flag

cmd/bd/dolt_autopush.go
  └── maybeAutoPush()                         [MOD: isDoltLocalOnly() early return]

cmd/bd/doctor.go (or doctor_dolt.go)
  └── checkDoltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin(path)   [NEW check, warning level]

internal/config/yaml_config.go
  └── YamlOnlyKeys["dolt.local-only"] = true [ADD: explicit entry for discoverability]
```

---

## Data Model

No new database schema. Config stored in `.beads/config.yaml`:

```erDiagram
    BEADS_CONFIG_YAML {
        string dolt_local_only "dolt.local-only = true|false"
        string dolt_auto_push  "existing: dolt.auto-push"
        string sync_remote     "existing: sync.remote"
    }
```

The key is a YAML-only key stored in `.beads/config.yaml`, which is
git-tracked and survives `git pull`. It is NOT stored in the Dolt database
(not pushed to remote, not in SQL schema).

---

## Use Cases

### UC-1: Agent attempts push on a local-only project

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Agent runs bd dolt push] --> B{isDoltLocalOnly?}
    B -- yes --> C[Print: remote sync disabled]
    C --> D[exit 0]
    B -- no --> E[Existing push logic]
```

### UC-2: Agent attempts to add a remote on a local-only project

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Agent runs bd dolt remote add X url] --> B{isDoltLocalOnly?}
    B -- yes --> C[Print error to stderr]
    C --> D[exit 1]
    B -- no --> E{URL matches git origin?}
    E -- yes, no --allow-git-origin --> F[Print error to stderr]
    F --> G[exit 1]
    E -- yes, --allow-git-origin --> H[Proceed with warning]
    E -- no --> I[Existing add logic]
```

### UC-3: bd doctor detects git-origin-as-dolt-remote

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[bd doctor runs] --> B[checkDoltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin]
    B --> C{List dolt remotes}
    C --> D{Get git origin URL}
    D --> E{Normalize + compare}
    E -- match found --> F[Emit statusWarning]
    F --> G[Show fix guidance]
    E -- no match --> H[Emit statusOK]
```

---

## Action Flows

### AF-1: `bd config set dolt.local-only true`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as User/Agent
    participant BD as bd config set
    participant YAML as config.yaml

    U->>BD: bd config set dolt.local-only true
    BD->>BD: IsYamlOnlyKey("dolt.local-only") → true (dolt.* prefix)
    BD->>YAML: Write dolt.local-only: "true"
    BD->>U: Set dolt.local-only = true (in config.yaml)
```

1. User invokes `bd config set dolt.local-only true`
2. `IsYamlOnlyKey` returns true for `dolt.*` prefix — routes to config.yaml
3. Viper writes the key to `.beads/config.yaml`
4. Confirmation printed to stdout

### AF-2: `bd dolt push` with `dolt.local-only=true`

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant U as Agent
    participant BD as doltPushCmd
    participant CFG as config.GetBool

    U->>BD: bd dolt push
    BD->>CFG: GetBool("dolt.local-only")
    CFG-->>BD: true
    BD->>U: stdout: "Remote sync is disabled (dolt.local-only=true)..."
    BD->>U: exit 0
```

1. Agent invokes `bd dolt push`
2. `isDoltLocalOnly()` calls `config.GetBool("dolt.local-only")` → true
3. Print informational message explaining the no-op to stdout
4. Exit 0 — no error, agents must not retry

### AF-3: `bd dolt remote add origin <url>` on local-only project

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Agent
    participant BD as doltRemoteAddCmd
    participant CFG as config.GetBool

    A->>BD: bd dolt remote add origin <url>
    BD->>CFG: GetBool("dolt.local-only")
    CFG-->>BD: true
    BD->>A: stderr: "Error: cannot add remote — dolt.local-only is set"
    BD->>A: exit 1
```

1. Agent invokes `bd dolt remote add origin <url>`
2. `isDoltLocalOnly()` → true
3. Print error to stderr with fix guidance
4. Exit 1 — this is an active refusal, agents should not retry the add

### AF-4: `bd dolt remote add origin <git-origin-url>` (git-origin collision guard)

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant A as Agent
    participant BD as doltRemoteAddCmd
    participant GIT as gitOriginGetURL()
    participant NORM as normalizeRemoteURL()

    A->>BD: bd dolt remote add origin https://github.com/org/repo.git
    BD->>BD: isDoltLocalOnly() → false
    BD->>GIT: gitOriginGetURL()
    GIT-->>BD: https://github.com/org/repo.git
    BD->>NORM: normalizeRemoteURL(git-origin)
    NORM-->>BD: git+https://github.com/org/repo.git
    BD->>NORM: normalizeRemoteURL(requested-url)
    NORM-->>BD: git+https://github.com/org/repo.git
    BD->>BD: urls match, --allow-git-origin not set
    BD->>A: stderr: "Error: URL matches git origin — refusing..."
    BD->>A: exit 1
```

1. Agent tries to add git origin as Dolt remote
2. `isDoltLocalOnly()` passes (not set)
3. Retrieve current git origin URL
4. Normalize both URLs via `normalizeRemoteURL()`
5. Normalized URLs match → `doltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin()` returns true
6. `--allow-git-origin` flag not set → refuse with stderr error
7. Exit 1

### AF-5: `bd doctor` git-origin check

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant BD as bd doctor
    participant ST as DoltStorage.ListRemotes
    participant GIT as gitOriginGetURL()

    BD->>ST: ListRemotes(ctx)
    ST-->>BD: [{name:"origin", url:"git+https://..."}]
    BD->>GIT: gitOriginGetURL()
    GIT-->>BD: https://github.com/org/repo.git
    BD->>BD: normalizeRemoteURL(git-origin) == remote-url?
    BD-->>BD: match
    BD->>BD: Emit statusWarning doctorCheck
```

1. Doctor lists Dolt remotes via storage layer
2. Retrieves git origin URL
3. Normalizes git origin
4. Compares with each remote URL
5. Match found → emit warning with fix guidance

---

## Security Controls

| Control | Mechanism |
|---------|-----------|
| Data leak prevention | `dolt.local-only` prevents any remote add; git-origin guard prevents accidental cloud push |
| Trust boundary | Config.yaml is git-tracked and per-project — agents can read but not silently bypass without `--allow-git-origin` |
| Audit trail | `bd config set` changes are committed to git via `commitBeadsConfig` (existing pattern) |
| No secret exposure | `dolt.local-only` is a boolean flag, not a credential |

---

## Guardrails for Downstream Agents

The following rules apply to builder agents implementing this feature:

1. **Exit codes are load-bearing.** Push/pull no-op MUST exit 0. Remote add
   refusal MUST exit 1. Inverting these breaks agent retry logic.

2. **Check `isDoltLocalOnly()` before calling `getStore()`** in push/pull
   commands, to avoid spinning up the Dolt server unnecessarily.

3. **Doctor check must be warning-level, not error-level.** A dolt remote
   matching git origin is not a broken installation — it's a risky config.
   Using `statusError` would fail CI for legitimately configured projects.

4. **`doltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin()` must handle the case where `gitOriginGetURL()`
   fails (not a git repo, no origin configured).** Return false — don't refuse
   when we can't determine the git origin.

5. **`--allow-git-origin` must be registered in the `init()` function** so
   Cobra parses it correctly. Do not use a global flag; scope it to
   `doltRemoteAddCmd` only.

6. **Do not add `dolt.local-only` to the `sync.*` namespace.** The existing
   `sync.local-only` key in tests is for contributor routing, not for
   dolt push/pull. Keep namespaces separate.

7. **The explicit `YamlOnlyKeys["dolt.local-only"] = true` entry in
   `yaml_config.go` is for discoverability and documentation.** It is not
   required for functional correctness (the `dolt.*` prefix match handles it),
   but omitting it makes the key harder to find during code review.

---

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|------|------------|--------|-----------|
| Agent reads exit 0 as "push succeeded" | Medium | Low | Stdout message says "disabled" explicitly; well-written agents read output |
| `--allow-git-origin` creates bypass loophole | Low | Medium | Requires explicit flag; rare intentional use case documented in help |
| `config.GetBool` called before Viper initialized | Low | Low | Returns `false` safely — no guard breach, just not enforced |
| Doctor check opens second store connection (CPU cost) | Low | Low | Use `sharedStore` pattern already established in `doctor.go:GH#2636` |
| Marker survives after `git stash` resets config.yaml | Very Low | Low | Out of scope — config.yaml manipulation is user-error territory |

---

## Trade-offs & Alternatives Considered

### Alternative A: Memory-based guardrail (current workaround)
The `bd remember dolt-local-only` pattern relies on agents reading memory before
every dolt push. **Rejected:** Does not survive agent restart; not enforced by
the tool itself; already failing (see today's gascity recurrence).

### Alternative B: Refuse `bd dolt remote add` only (no push/pull no-op)
Refuse remote-add but let push/pull error naturally when no remote exists.
**Rejected:** Agents may add the remote via raw dolt CLI (`dolt remote add`)
rather than `bd dolt remote add`. The push/pull guard catches both paths.

### Alternative C: Auto-detect `dolt.local-only` at init time for solo projects
Set the marker automatically when a project is initialized without a remote.
**Rejected:** Too many false positives; users may add a remote later. Opt-in
is safer.

### Alternative D: Warn only on `bd dolt remote add` (no error)
Print a warning but proceed. **Rejected:** The incident shows agents ignore
warnings when they believe they are "fixing" a problem. Exit 1 is required to
stop the add.

### Alternative E: Block `CALL DOLT_PULL` at the SQL layer
Intercept SQL calls to prevent native-merge goroutine creation.
**Rejected:** bd has no interceptor in the Dolt SQL server path; this would
require changes to Dolt itself, which is out of scope for bd 1.0.4.

---

## Implementation Checklist (for builder)

- [ ] Add `isDoltLocalOnly() bool` to `cmd/bd/dolt.go`
- [ ] Add `doltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin(url string) bool` to `cmd/bd/dolt.go`
- [ ] Guard `doltPushCmd.Run` with `isDoltLocalOnly()` (exit 0)
- [ ] Guard `doltPullCmd.Run` with `isDoltLocalOnly()` (exit 0)
- [ ] Guard `adoptGitOriginRemoteForPush()` with `isDoltLocalOnly()` (return false, nil)
- [ ] Guard `doltRemoteAddCmd.Run` with `isDoltLocalOnly()` (exit 1) before `getStore()`
- [ ] Guard `doltRemoteAddCmd.Run` with `doltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin()` (exit 1) — after local-only check
- [ ] Register `--allow-git-origin` flag on `doltRemoteAddCmd` in `init()`
- [ ] Guard `maybeAutoPush()` with `isDoltLocalOnly()` (early return)
- [ ] Add `checkDoltRemoteMatchesGitOrigin(path string) doctorCheck` function
- [ ] Wire new doctor check into `doctor.go` main run loop (after Dolt remotes section)
- [ ] Add `"dolt.local-only": true` to `YamlOnlyKeys` in `yaml_config.go`
- [ ] Update `dolt.go` Long help text for `doltCmd` to document `dolt.local-only`
- [ ] Write integration tests for push/pull no-op behavior
- [ ] Write integration tests for remote add refusal (local-only + git-origin)
- [ ] Write integration test for doctor warning

title: issues/wisps id collision: message->wisp migration leaves dup rows; lookup hard-errors on dual-presence
description:
Symptom: `Error fetching <id>: failed to search issues: id "X" exists in both issues and wisps`. On 2026-05-22 this broke `gc session attach` and `bd show` for ~2091 ids in our HQ city DB (and likely crashed prior mayor sessions, since any colliding-id lookup errors hard).

Root cause: `message`-type beads exist in BOTH the `issues` and `wisps` tables. During the message->wisps migration window (~2026-05-06..05-18) messages were written to both tables and the `issues` copies were never deleted. After 05-18 messages are written to `wisps` only. beads 1.0.4's id resolver queries both tables and hard-errors on any id present in both.

Requested fixes (beads-side; mayor does not change beads code):
1. Migration completeness: when a message is stored as / promoted to a wisp, DELETE the corresponding row from `issues` (and its issue-side children: events/labels/deps). A partial migration must not leave dual rows.
2. Lookup robustness: the id resolver must not hard-error on dual-presence. Prefer the canonical wisp record (or de-dup deterministically) so a single stray dup cannot break session-attach / bd show city-wide.
3. `bd doctor --check validate [--fix]` SKIPS duplicate detection with "requires CGO" on CGO-less builds. On the dolt backend this data-integrity repair should not require CGO -- otherwise the only native repair is unavailable exactly on the production binaries that hit this.

Mitigation already applied to HQ by mayor: deleted the 2091 stale `issues` message rows (canonical copies kept in `wisps`; CASCADE removed 2099 trivial created-events + 4 labels). dolt commit e0lvpmqkr606erkpvp329k4ob27tnknt on the hq DB. Backup at gc-management/.beads/backup/hq-issuewisp-dup-cleanup-2026-05-22/. Rig DBs (gascity/mcdclient/pwu) were unaffected (0 collisions).

Won't recur from new writes (dual-write path stopped 05-18), but the lookup-robustness gap (#2) means any future stray dup re-breaks lookups. Filed by mayor (gc-management); per standing order the beads rig owns the code fix.
notes: Implementation plan: (1) issueops: prefer wisp on dup in search.go, ready_work.go, ready_work_counts.go, search_counts.go, dependency_queries.go; (2) update 3 existing tests that expected hard-error to expect graceful dedup; (3) add CheckCrossTableDuplicates to doctor (no CGO required, uses fix.openDoltDB); add CrossTableDuplicates fix function; wire into validate checks and fix dispatch. Branch: fix/be-iabdi-issuewisp-dup-robustness
close_reason: Implemented all 3 fixes: (1) lookup robustness in 5 issueops merge sites, (2) CGO-free cross-table duplicate doctor check + fix, (3) updated 3 tests to assert wisp-preferred dedup. PR #4163 open at gastownhall/beads.

title: Document schema-skew guard in bd --help and README
description:
# Documentation Design: Schema-Skew Guard in bd --help and README

**Bead:** be-x0rl6  
**Designer:** beads/designer  
**Date:** 2026-05-22  
**Architecture ref:** be-blpg3 §2 (escape hatch), §5 (error copy), §17 Child 2  
**UX ref:** be-wwbsv design

---

## 1. Summary

This document specifies the exact text for three documentation artifacts:
(a) `--ignore-schema-skew` flag description in `bd --help`, (b) the README
section explaining the schema-version guard, and (c) the CHANGELOG entry.
No new documentation files are created — all additions are in existing files.

---

## 2. Flag Help Text

### 2a. Cobra flag registration (main.go)

```go
rootCmd.PersistentFlags().BoolVar(&ignoreSchemaSkew, "ignore-schema-skew", false,
    "Bypass the schema-version guard when the database is ahead of the binary. Sets BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1. Use only when forward migrations are safe for your workload.")
```

**Rendered in `bd --help`:**

```
      --ignore-schema-skew   Bypass the schema-version guard when the database is ahead of the binary. Sets BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1. Use only when forward migrations are safe for your workload.
```

### 2b. Style notes

- Follows the existing flag description pattern: imperative verb phrase, no
  trailing period, explains what the flag does and when to use it.
- Length: 151 chars — cobra wraps at terminal width automatically; no manual
  newlines in the description string.
- Mentions `BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1` so users who see the env var in CI logs
  know it corresponds to this flag.
- Placement: after `--global` and before `--json` in the Flags block (alphabetical
  order within the `i` section). Cobra sorts flags alphabetically so this is
  automatic.

---

## 3. README Section

### 3a. Placement

Add as `### Schema Version Guard` immediately after `### Backup & Migration`
(line 175 in current README.md). It belongs under `## 💾 Storage Modes`
because it is a storage-layer behavior. It appears after Backup & Migration
because it is most relevant when operators are upgrading binaries or moving
databases.

### 3b. Exact text to insert

```markdown
### Schema Version Guard

`bd` checks the database schema version at open time. If the database has been
migrated by a newer binary and an older binary tries to open it, `bd` exits
with an actionable error rather than issuing queries that fail with cryptic SQL
errors:

```
schema version mismatch: database is at v45, binary knows up to v42 (3 migrations ahead)

  Your bd binary is stale. Queries for dropped or renamed columns will fail
  with cryptic SQL errors (e.g. "column X could not be found in any table in scope").

  Rebuild from main:
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd

  Or install the latest release:
    go install github.com/steveyegge/beads/cmd/bd@latest

  To proceed despite the risk (some read commands may still work):
    BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1 bd <command>
    bd --ignore-schema-skew <command>
```

**When this fires:** only when the database schema is *ahead* of the binary
(a newer binary migrated the database; this binary doesn't know those
migrations). Normal upgrades, where the binary migrates the database forward,
are unaffected.

**Escape hatch:** `BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1` (or `--ignore-schema-skew`) bypasses
the guard with a warning on stderr. Use this only if you know the forward
migrations are additive and safe for your specific workload.
```

### 3c. Formatting notes

- The code block uses a triple-backtick fence with no language tag (plain text
  output — no syntax highlighting needed or wanted).
- The nested triple-backtick inside the `### Schema Version Guard` block will
  need to be escaped when inserted into the file. The builder should use four
  backticks for the outer fence:

  ````markdown
  ````
  schema version mismatch: ...
  ````
  ````

  OR change the inner fence to use `~~~` fencing so the outer ```` remains
  triple-backtick. Either approach renders identically on GitHub.

- Bold callouts (`**When this fires:**`, `**Escape hatch:**`) match the style
  used in other README sections (e.g., Storage Modes callouts).
- No emoji — the subsection header does not use an emoji, consistent with the
  existing `### Embedded Mode`, `### Server Mode`, `### Backup & Migration`
  subheadings (only top-level `##` headers use emoji in the current README).

---

## 4. CHANGELOG Entry

### 4a. Placement

Under `## [Unreleased]` → `### Added` section (after existing `### Added`
items, before `### Changed`). This is a net-new feature guard.

### 4b. Exact text

```markdown
- **Schema-version guard**: `bd` now hard-fails at database-open time when the
  database schema is ahead of the binary's embedded migrations. This protects
  against cryptic SQL errors (e.g., `column X could not be found in any table
  in scope`) that occur when an older binary opens a database migrated by a
  newer one. The error message names the exact version mismatch and provides a
  copy-paste rebuild command. Use `--ignore-schema-skew` (or env var
  `BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW=1`) to bypass the guard when you know the forward
  migrations are safe for your workload. Fresh databases and normal
  forward-migration paths are unaffected.
```

### 4c. Style notes

- Follows the existing CHANGELOG bullet style: bold feature name, sentence
  case, no trailing period on the block.
- Mentions both the CLI flag and env var — agents and operators frequently
  encounter one without knowing the other.
- Explicitly names the "not affected" cases to reduce support questions from
  users who upgrade normally.

---

## 5. Documentation Accessibility Audit

### 5.1 Scanability

- README section: three visual anchors — the code block (error output),
  **When this fires:** callout, **Escape hatch:** callout. Users scanning the
  page can extract all relevant facts in under 10 seconds.
- CHANGELOG entry: single bullet, complete in 5–6 lines. No sub-bullets or
  code blocks; easy to scan in the changelog feed.
- Flag help: one-liner in `bd --help`. Complete, no truncation at typical
  terminal widths (80–200 cols). Cobra wraps gracefully at narrow widths.

### 5.2 Copy-paste fidelity

The error message in the README exactly matches `SchemaSkewError.UserMessage()`
output. If the builder changes the message copy, the README must be updated in
the same PR. The be-wwbsv design (§3b) is the canonical source; this document
references it for the code block content.

### 5.3 Discoverability (find this doc when you need it)

Users encountering the error will search for key phrases. The README section
contains:
- `"schema version mismatch"` — exact first line of the error
- `"ignore-schema-skew"` — the flag name
- `"BD_IGNORE_SCHEMA_SKEW"` — the env var

All three appear in README and CHANGELOG, making the section findable via
`grep` or GitHub's search.

### 5.4 Screen-reader / plain-text compatibility

The README section uses no HTML, no image, no table. It renders identically
in `cat README.md` and in GitHub's rendered view. The code block is pre-formatted
text, not an image of text.

---

## 6. What this design does NOT cover

- Implementation of `--ignore-schema-skew` in main.go — builder work (be-wwbsv)
- `bd doctor` output format for schema version status — separate UX item
- `docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` entry — can be added but was not in be-blpg3 §17 scope;
  file a follow-up if wanted
notes:
Derived from be-blpg3 (schema-skew guard architecture).

## Scope
- Add --ignore-schema-skew to bd root command --help (PersistentFlag description)
- Add 'Schema version guard' section in README.md under Maintenance/Configuration:
  - What it is (open-time check; fires when DB schema is ahead of binary)
  - When it fires (exact scenario: binary at vN, DB at vM>N)
  - What to do: rebuild from main, or use --ignore-schema-skew
  - The error message example
- Add changelog entry under next version
close_reason: README Schema Version Guard section + CHANGELOG entry added in PR #4161. Flag description expansion note added to PR #4152.

# Daily standup — plain-English status for mayor

You are the rig PM. Mayor reads this in the morning. Write the brief and close this bead.

## Format (use this exact shape)

### What was done (last ~24h)
Concrete bullets. Recent closures, merges, decisions, fixes. Bead IDs go in parens for anchoring, NOT as primary content. Terse bullets, not paragraphs.

### What's in flight
Active arcs, who's working what. Group by theme if multiple. Plain English — a colleague who's been out a day should understand.

### What's blocking
Anything stuck. Why. What needs to move (a decision, a bead, an upstream landing). If nothing is blocking, write "nothing".

### What's next
The things that should land in the next ~24h if all goes well.

### Questions for mayor (optional — omit if none)
ONLY include if you actually need operator input. Don't ask permission for things you can decide yourself. Examples of valid asks:
- A scope/priority/sequencing decision only mayor can make
- A blocker needing operator action (lift a freeze, choose an option from a real set)
- Confirmation when you're about to do something potentially destructive or wide-blast

NOT valid asks (these are PM's call, just decide):
- "Should we revisit retired feature X?" — your call; default is stay-shelved unless evidence forces a revisit
- Internal-system architecture/sequencing decisions that need deep context — your call
- Routine rescheduling, deferring, dropping work — you're empowered

If this section is non-empty, mail mayor after closing the bead:
`gc mail send mayor -s "Re: standup $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" -m "Questions in <bead-id> — please advise"`

## Style

- **Plain English, not bead-ID dumps.** Lead with what's happening; cite beads in parens for anchoring.
- Concrete > abstract. Names of files / commits / branches where relevant.
- You are empowered to revisit, reschedule, drop, or escalate things without permission. Mayor appreciates autonomy. Surface questions only when mayor's perspective genuinely matters.
- Be honest about red flags — if something looks wrong, say so plainly.

## Deliverable

Write the standup into this bead's `notes` (use `bd update <this-bead-id> --notes "..."`).
Then close the bead with a one-line reason like "standup posted".

If you raised mayor-questions in section 5, also send the mail described above.

description:

Title: fix(export): fail on auto-export git add errors (maintainer cherry-pick from PR #4092)
Branch: maintainer/pr-4092-auto-export-errors
Review decision: NONE
Created: 2026-05-22T08:31:51Z  (0d ago)
Last activity: 2026-05-22T08:42:54Z  (0d ago)

Filed by hourly pr-audit. As investigator: read the PR, decide to (a) build a fix per reviewer comments, (b) close as superseded by other work, (c) close as no-longer-wanted, or (d) escalate to the mayor. Close this bead with the chosen path in notes.
notes:
INVESTIGATED & ESCALATED (option d: escalate to mayor).

Root cause of PR #4098 CI red (only failing check: Embedded Dolt Cmd 18/20): a deterministic contract conflict, not flake.
- PR makes auto-export 'git add' failures fatal (export_auto.go:145 returns error -> main.go:1157-1158 FatalError), INCLUDING the gitignored case.
- main's TestEmbeddedPrune/prune_last_issue_removes_gitignored_auto_export (prune_embedded_test.go:112) requires .gitignore=.beads/ + git-add=true -> bd create/close SUCCEED.
- PR's own new TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero (export_auto_test.go:506) requires the SAME setup -> bd create FAIL with 'ignored'.
- Identical preconditions, opposite required outcomes => no single behavior passes both; one test must change = a contract decision.

Proof: CI run 26277292024 / job 77345269683 (artifact); mechanism reproduced locally (git add on gitignored .beads exits 1 'paths are ignored'); both test bodies read at the pinned line numbers; disproved 'mechanical test-fix' by showing logical mutual exclusivity, and 'gitignored is in #3970 threat model' by showing an untracked ignored file is never staged/committed.

Actions: posted full analysis + recommendation on PR https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4098#issuecomment-4517650707 ; mailed mayor (gm-wisp-r8nrr); recorded bd memory pr4098-autoexport-gitadd-gitignore-contract.

Recommendation to maintainer: keep fatal for transient staging failures (locked index = real #3970 repro), make gitignored non-fatal in export_auto.go:143-146, re-point PR's new test at a .git/index.lock trigger. Investigator ready to implement once direction is confirmed.
DECISION (mayor, 2026-05-22): Go with your recommended direction — it's the "main is right, build from there" call.

- PRESERVE main's contract: gitignored .beads + git-add=true must SUCCEED (TestEmbeddedPrune/prune_last_issue_removes_gitignored_auto_export, prune_embedded_test.go:112, stays as-is). An ignored file is never staged/committed, so #3970's stale-blob risk is structurally absent in that case — making it fatal would break the supported gitignored-.beads workflow.
- KEEP fatal for transient/tracked staging failures (locked .git/index — the actual #3970 repro).
- RE-POINT the PR's new test (TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero, export_auto_test.go:506) from the gitignored setup to a .git/index.lock trigger, so it exercises the real failure mode.

Implement on #4098 (our PR, branch maintainer/pr-4092-auto-export-errors); get CI green (Embedded Dolt Cmd 18/20).

BOUNDARY: beads is a contributor repo for us — once green, leave the merge to beads maintainers; do NOT self-merge. Keep maphew (original #4092 author) credited, and add a brief PR comment explaining the contract decision so maphew + maintainers can follow the test re-point.

Thanks for the sharp root-cause — "identical preconditions, opposite required outcomes" was exactly the right framing.

IMPLEMENTED (mayor's directed fix) on PR #4098 branch maintainer/pr-4092-auto-export-errors, commit 1c7bbe2a9 (pushed to fork).

Change: maybeAutoExport (cmd/bd/export_auto.go:144-156) now classifies the gitAddFile error via new pathIsGitIgnored() helper (git check-ignore -q). Gitignored .beads -> benign skip (debug log, command succeeds); all other failures incl. locked .git/index -> fatal as before. gitAddFile's own contract unchanged (still errors on both) so its unit tests untouched. Re-pointed TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero (export_auto_test.go) from gitignored trigger -> held .git/index.lock.

Local verification (CGO_ENABLED=1, BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1): TestEmbeddedPrune/prune_last_issue_removes_gitignored_auto_export PASS (was the shard-18 failure), re-pointed TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero PASS, all TestGitAddFile_* PASS, full TestAutoExport*/TestExport*/TestEmbeddedPrune surface PASS.

PR comment posted (crediting maphew): https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4098#issuecomment-4517873666 . Watching CI on 1c7bbe2a9; will close when green. Not self-merging (beads is contributor repo).
CI GREEN on commit 1c7bbe2a9 (PR #4098): 41/41 checks pass, incl. the previously-failing Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 18/20). Mayor's done-condition met.

EXIT PATH: Implemented mayor's directed fix on the maintainer PR branch (Exit B-style: pushed to our own cherry-pick PR #4098, did NOT self-merge — beads is a contributor repo, merge left to beads maintainers). Reviewer/maintainer follow-up: re-review + merge #4098.

Closing this bead.

title: mpr: gastownhall/beads#4092 held for human merge
notes:
## Reviewer verdict: REQUEST-CHANGES (2026-05-22, reviewer)

PR #4098 — fix(export): fail on auto-export git add errors

### CI Status
One shard failing: Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 18/20)
- **FAIL**: TestEmbeddedPrune/prune_last_issue_removes_gitignored_auto_export (99.09s)

### Findings

**BLOCKER — CI regression (severity: high, confidence: verified):**

File: cmd/bd/prune_embedded_test.go, ~line 112
File: cmd/bd/export_auto.go, line 143-145 (git-add error handling)

The PR converts all git-add failures in maybeAutoExport from warning-and-continue to fatal errors. This breaks the existing test TestEmbeddedPrune/prune_last_issue_removes_gitignored_auto_export, which sets up:
  - .beads/ in .gitignore
  - export.git-add = true
  - Calls bd create — now fails exit status 1

Error from CI:
  prune_embedded_test.go:112: bd create Closed exported task failed: exit status 1
  {"error": "auto-export: git add failed: exit status 1: The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files:\n.beads"}

The contradiction: the new test TestAutoExportGitAddFailureExitsNonZero (added by this PR) expects bd create to FAIL when .beads is gitignored + export.git-add=true. The existing prune test expects bd create to SUCCEED in the same configuration.

title: fix(audit): widen newID() to 16 bytes to eliminate birthday collisions
description:
## Root cause

`internal/audit/audit.go:160-166` — `newID()` returns only 32 bits of randomness:

```go
func newID() (string, error) {
    var b [4]byte
    if _, err := rand.Read(b[:]); err != nil {
        return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to generate id: %w", err)
    }
    return idPrefix + hex.EncodeToString(b[:]), nil
}
```

For the test parameters used in `internal/audit/concurrency_test.go::TestAppend_ConcurrentWritersUniqueIDs` (writers=8 × entriesPerWriter=250 = 2000 IDs), birthday-paradox collision probability is `n(n-1)/(2N) = 2000·1999/(2·2^32) ≈ 4.65×10^-4 ≈ 1 in 2,150 runs`.

This is **not** a torn-write bug or a shared-counter bug — the test's preamble already correctly notes there's no counter. The bug is that 32 random bits is too small for the use case: real-world audit logs in long-running rigs will accumulate many more than 2000 entries, where collisions become near-certain.

## Reproducing test/artifact

The existing test `TestAppend_ConcurrentWritersUniqueIDs` IS the failing test. CI evidence: gastownhall/beads PR #3913 run 26123385619 — "expected 2000 unique returned IDs, got 1999 (duplicate IDs: [int-3f25833f])".

Standalone reproduction (3/5000 collision rate empirically observed, matches model): 8 goroutines × 250 IDs each, 5000 trials → ~3 collisions. Repro code lived in `/tmp/be-tjt9-newid-collision.go` during the investigation.

## Fix spec

**File:** `internal/audit/audit.go`

**Change line 161** from `var b [4]byte` to `var b [16]byte`.

That's it. `hex.EncodeToString` already handles arbitrary byte slices; the returned ID becomes `int-<32hex>` (37 chars total) instead of `int-<8hex>` (12 chars). New space is 2^128 — collision probability for 2000 IDs is ~5×10^-36, vanishing.

**Also update the test's `entriesPerWriter` constant** in `internal/audit/concurrency_test.go:48` from `250` to `1000` (writers*entriesPerWriter = 8000 IDs). With 128-bit IDs and 8000 entries, collision probability is ~9×10^-32, so the test will never flake.

## Verifying the fix

```bash
go test -count=200 -run TestAppend_ConcurrentWritersUniqueIDs ./internal/audit/...
```

Before fix: expected ~1 flake in 200 runs (still rare but visible). After fix with bumped entriesPerWriter: all 200 runs pass.

## Out of scope (do NOT do in this PR)

- Do not rename `int-` prefix. Other code may pattern-match on it.
- Do not modify the on-disk file format. Existing audit logs with the old short IDs remain valid — IDs are opaque strings.
- Do not migrate old entries. Mixed-length IDs in the same log are fine (type is `string`).
- Do not change `idPrefix` or `FileName` constants.
- Do not touch the rest of the audit subsystem (`Append`, `LogFieldChange`, `Path`, `EnsureFile`).

## Done-when

- [ ] `internal/audit/audit.go:161` uses `var b [16]byte`.
- [ ] `internal/audit/concurrency_test.go:48` bumps `entriesPerWriter` to `1000`.
- [ ] `go test -count=200 -run TestAppend_ConcurrentWritersUniqueIDs ./internal/audit/...` passes (no flakes).
- [ ] `go vet ./...` clean.
- [ ] Commit message follows the repo's `fix(audit):` convention with a one-line explanation of the birthday-collision rationale.

## Context

- Investigator bead: be-tjt9
- Surfaced by: PR #3913 CI run 26123385619 (job 76830815971), 2026-05-19
- Reporter (PR author): @quad341

title: Fix: rebase PR #3734 + add --actor to count_embedded_test.go:89 (be-035 actor-assignee guard)
description:
## Origin

Hand-off from beads/investigator. Source bead: be-0nuq (PR #3734 CI failing).

PR: https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/3734
Branch: `release/be-07y-gate`
Title: fix(close): refuse silent close on actor/assignee mismatch
Author: quad341 (user's own PR; safe to push directly to its branch)

## Root cause (two independent failures on the same CI run)

PR #3734 has two failing CI checks. They have separate root causes, both of which must be fixed for CI to go green.

### Failure 1 — `Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 5/20)` → `TestEmbeddedCount` (15.72s)

The PR introduces a new authority guard in `internal/validation/issue.go::AssigneeMatches(actor, force)`. It's wired into `validateIssueClosable` from `cmd/bd/close.go:135`. The guard refuses `bd close` whenever the actor (default in tests: `"Test"`, from `git config user.name "Test"` set by `bdInit`) doesn't match the bead's assignee, unless `--force` is passed.

`cmd/bd/count_embedded_test.go:89` (PR branch ref `tmp-pr-3734`) — the only pre-existing call site that closes an `--assignee`-set issue without a matching actor:

```go
closedIssue := bdCreate(t, bd, dir, "Count closed one", "--type", "task", "--priority", "2", "--assignee", "alice")
bdClose(t, bd, dir, closedIssue.ID)   // line 89: actor="Test", assignee="alice" → guard refuses
```

Observed CI error (run 25971073954, job 76343330285):

```
count_embedded_test.go:89: bd close ct-7vh failed: exit status 1
    cannot close ct-7vh: assignee is "alice", actor is "Test"; reclaim or use --force to override
```

I scanned every `bdCreate(...,"--assignee",...)` site in `cmd/bd/*_embedded_test.go` on the PR branch. The other `--assignee` creates (in query/search/show/stale/status _embedded_test.go) don't get closed by the test; line 89 is the **only** site that needs an update.

### Failure 2 — `Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 11/20)` → `TestEmbeddedClose/close_json_output` (4.21s)

Known pattern documented in `bd-embedded-test-json-stderr-leak`. Observed CI error:

```
close_embedded_test.go:480: expected valid JSON, got: [
        "title": "JSON close test",
    beads: auto-export warning: no Dolt remote configured.
```

PR #3734's branch was last pushed `2026-05-16T19:39:12Z`; CI ran shortly after at `19:45–19:51`. The omnibus fix PR #3996 (commit `88e13542e`, "test(embedded): split stdout/stderr in all JSON-parsing helpers") landed on main at `2026-05-17T04:21Z` — about 9 hours after PR #3734's CI failed. Rebasing onto current main pulls in the fix and resolves this failure.

(The PR's own diff happens to revert the runCommandBuffers helper across ~40 test files because it forked before that helper existed. Those revert-shaped diffs will go away on rebase.)

## Reproducing artifact / evidence

CI logs from PR #3734's last run, both failed jobs:
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/25971073954/job/76343330285 (Test 5/20)
- https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/actions/runs/25971073954/job/76343330326 (Test 11/20)

PR commits: head `b7a279f2b8`, parent `daf1deb0f1` (both `2026-05-16T19:39:12Z`).

Disproved hypotheses:
- "Actor/assignee guard already landed on main → PR is superseded." DISPROVEN: `grep "reclaim or use --force"` on `origin/main` returns no hits; only on `tmp-pr-3734:internal/validation/issue.go`.
- "Test 11/20 (close_json_output) is the same actor/assignee guard." DISPROVEN: error signature is `expected valid JSON, got: [` followed by `auto-export warning: no Dolt remote configured.` — exact memory match for stderr-leak.

## Fix spec

Imperative. Do these in order.

### Step 1 — Rebase the PR branch onto current main

```bash
cd <rig-root>
git fetch origin
git checkout release/be-07y-gate
git pull --ff-only origin release/be-07y-gate   # in case branch advanced
git rebase origin/main
```

Most conflicts will be in `cmd/bd/*_embedded_test.go` where the PR's `runCommandBuffers → cmd.CombinedOutput()` reverts collide with main's helper. **Resolution rule:** keep main's `runCommandBuffers(t, cmd)` form; drop the PR's CombinedOutput reverts. The PR's intent for those files was already accomplished by omnibus #3996.

Also expect to keep the PR's substantive new code (no conflict expected):
- `cmd/bd/close.go` — adds `actor` to `validateIssueClosable(id, issue, actor, force)` call
- `internal/validation/issue.go` — adds `AssigneeMatches(actor, force) IssueValidator`
- `cmd/bd/close_embedded_test.go` — adds 4 new authority-guard sub-tests (`close_assignee_mismatch_refuses_without_force`, `close_assignee_mismatch_with_force`, `close_same_actor_succeeds`, `close_unassigned_bead_succeeds`)
- `cmd/bd/validation_test.go` and `internal/validation/issue_test.go` — `TestAssigneeMatches`, updated `TestValidateIssueClosable`
- `release-gates/be-07y-gate.md` — gate doc

### Step 2 — Update the one broken call site

Edit `cmd/bd/count_embedded_test.go` line 89 (line number is pre-rebase; post-rebase it will shift if the file's imports differ — find the call by content):

```diff
-	bdClose(t, bd, dir, closedIssue.ID)
+	bdClose(t, bd, dir, closedIssue.ID, "--actor", "alice")
```

Rationale: the test creates an issue assigned to alice and immediately closes it. The cleanest fix mirrors the convention used by the PR's own new tests (`close_embedded_test.go:285,296`): pass `--actor` matching the assignee. Avoid `--force` here — `--force` exists to override authority; the test intent is "alice closes alice's bead", which the guard already permits when actor matches.

### Step 3 — Verify

```bash
# Build with the embedded tag and run the affected tests
CGO_ENABLED=1 BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test -count=1 \
    -run 'TestEmbeddedCount|TestEmbeddedClose' \
    ./cmd/bd/...
```

Both `TestEmbeddedCount` and `TestEmbeddedClose/close_json_output` must pass.

If other sub-tests fail with the same `assignee is X, actor is Y` signature after rebase, treat them the same way (add `--actor` matching the create-time assignee). I scanned and didn't find any other site, but a clean test run is the source of truth.

### Step 4 — Push

```bash
git push --force-with-lease origin release/be-07y-gate
```

(Force-with-lease is required because rebase rewrites SHAs. The PR is the user's own; no external contributors to coordinate with.)

## Out of scope (do NOT do here)

- `bd update --status=closed` does not pass through the new guard. The PR description acknowledges this and explicitly defers it as a separate P2 follow-up. Do **not** add the guard to the update path in this rebase.
- Do **not** broaden the guard's scope (e.g., to add role/owner overrides). The PR description explicitly scopes authority to assignee-only with `--force` override.
- Do **not** add `--force` to `count_embedded_test.go:89`. `--actor "alice"` is the right fix (preserves test intent).
- Do **not** re-apply the runCommandBuffers reverts during rebase conflict resolution — drop them all in favor of main's helper.

## Done-when

- [ ] `release/be-07y-gate` is rebased on current `origin/main` (no `runCommandBuffers → CombinedOutput` reverts remain)
- [ ] `cmd/bd/count_embedded_test.go` line ~89 passes `--actor "alice"` to the `bdClose` call after the `--assignee alice` create
- [ ] `CGO_ENABLED=1 BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 go test -run 'TestEmbeddedCount|TestEmbeddedClose' ./cmd/bd/...` passes locally
- [ ] Branch is force-pushed (`--force-with-lease`) to `origin/release/be-07y-gate`
- [ ] PR #3734 CI shows the two previously-failing checks (`Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 5/20)`, `Test (Embedded Dolt Cmd 11/20)`) now passing
- [ ] No new failures introduced (full embedded suite green or its failures are pre-existing-on-main, not caused by this rebase)
notes: Pre-resolved: PR #3734 now MERGEABLE with 41/41 CI checks passing as of 2026-05-25. No action needed.
close_reason: PR #3734 is MERGEABLE with all CI passing — issue was already resolved before builder could act.

Verified end-to-end via real schema.MigrateUp against a live dolt sql-server: all 6 cols -> longtext, wisps defaults preserved, minimal wisp insert OK, minimal issue insert correctly rejected, idempotent re-run. (Testcontainer suite needs Docker, unavailable locally; CI re-run on new commit is the final gate.)

Flagged to author (non-blocking): branch bundles unrelated perf/count/jira/spike commits (bd-xoi0x/qi4qr/co6m6/wsgws) that could be split out. Left history untouched.

The 12 files in this PR (audit, compact, config, dolt, help_all, init, init_proxied_server, linear, ready, restore, search, sql) correctly use the stderr-JSON variant — none are stdout-JSON commands.

LOW-1 — cmd/bd/config.go line 379: FatalErrorWithHint hint starts with two spaces ('  To migrate: re-init...'). Original code used fmt.Fprintln where those spaces provided visual indent. Now they appear after 'Hint: ' prefix, printing 'Hint:   To migrate: re-init...'. Trim the leading spaces from the hint string.

LOW-2 — ~20 call sites use FatalError with a bare literal and no variadic args (e.g. FatalError('--kind is required')). Safe today (no % chars in any literal), but fragile — a future edit adding % to the message without a matching arg produces garbled output. Consider FatalErrorMessage(msg string) for the non-format cases, or add a vet annotation.

Filed by hourly pr-audit. As investigator: read the PR, decide to (a) build a fix per reviewer comments, (b) close as superseded by other work, (c) close as no-longer-wanted, or (d) escalate to the mayor. Close this bead with the chosen path in notes.
notes:
## Investigation result (closed via Exit B — pushed PR)

**PR #3913 status:** docs-only (CONTRIBUTING_PR_GUIDELINES.md + release-gates/be-z33z-gate.md). No reviewer comments. The CI failure is entirely unrelated to the PR contents.

**Root cause of CI failure:** `TestAppend_ConcurrentWritersUniqueIDs` in `internal/audit/concurrency_test.go` failed with `duplicate IDs: [int-3f25833f]`. The bug is in `internal/audit/audit.go:160-166` — `newID()` drew only 4 random bytes (32 bits). For 2000 IDs, birthday-paradox collision probability is ~5e-4 per run.

**Hypotheses considered:**
- Torn writes (the failure mode of prior fix #3301) — DISPROVEN. That fix is on PR base; the new failure is in-memory `returnedIDs` map collision at concurrency_test.go:104, BEFORE the file scan.
- Counter race — DISPROVEN. No counter exists (test comment confirms).
- Insufficient entropy from 32-bit ID space — CONFIRMED. Math matches observed rate; reproduced 4 dups in 3000 local runs (~0.13%).

**Fix:** PR #4046 (https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4046) — widens `newID()` to 8 bytes (64-bit). After fix: 0 collisions in 3000 runs locally.

**Recommended next steps for mayor:**
1. Merge #4046.
2. Rebase or rerun CI on #3913. Once #4046 lands and the audit fix is in PR #3913's lineage, CI should be reliably green.
3. PR #3913 itself is 93 commits behind main; consider rebasing as part of the green-CI step.

Decision: (a) build a fix per reviewer comments — but the "reviewer" here is CI, and the fix lives in a separate PR for an unrelated bug.
close_reason: Filed PR #4046 (https://github.com/gastownhall/beads/pull/4046) fixing root-cause audit ID collision behind PR #3913's CI flake. See notes for full investigation.

title: UX design: bd init fork-detection flow messaging and output format
description:
Design the CLI UX for the auto-fork-detection path in bd init (bd-umbf Child 1).

Scope: terminal output text, messaging cadence, and whether/what to prompt.

Design questions to resolve:
1. Should the fork-detection flow prompt for confirmation or just auto-configure? (Recommendation: auto, log what was done)
2. What is the exact output text? Should it look like the existing bd init output style or the --contributor wizard?
3. If the user doesn't want auto-routing (wants maintainer mode on a fork), how do they opt out?
4. What is the success message format? (e.g., checkmark + "Contributor routing configured" vs a summary block)
5. Should bd init show a one-liner note about --contributor when fork is NOT detected?

Deliverable: CLI mockup in code-fenced block showing the exact terminal output for the happy path (fork detected) and the opt-out path.
Architecture ref: bd-umbf Child 4.
notes:
# Design: `bd init` Fork-Detection Flow — Messaging and Output Format

**Bead:** be-0ccf34  
**Author:** beads/designer  
**Architecture ref:** bd-umbf Child 4 / Child 1

---

## Design decisions

### Q1 — Auto-configure or prompt?

**Decision: auto-configure, with full audit output.**

Rationale:
- An `upstream` remote is unambiguous evidence of a fork workflow. The user made a deliberate git choice; `bd init` can honour it without asking.
- Prompting violates FR-02 (zero-friction first-time setup). The user already cloned, already added `upstream` — re-confirming intent is patronising.
- The existing `promptForkExclude` already defaults to `[Y/n]` (safe choice). This extends that logic one step: if the answer is almost always yes, don't ask.
- NFR-04 ("explicit over silent") is satisfied by clear audit lines, not by prompting.

Exception: if `--role=maintainer` is passed, fork detection is acknowledged but routing is skipped. The user's explicit intent wins.

---

### Q2 — Output style: integrated init vs wizard

**Decision: integrated into `bd init` output, not the contributor wizard.**

The `--contributor` wizard (`runContributorWizard`) is appropriate when the user consciously opts in and needs to make decisions (planning repo path, push access confirmation). For a fork-detected auto-path, all those decisions are already answered by convention (`~/.beads-planning`, routing mode = auto). A full wizard here is friction disguised as helpfulness.

The fork-detection block follows the existing `▶ / ✓` pattern already used throughout `bd init`. It sits between the core setup steps and the final summary, matching the existing placement of `promptForkExclude`.

---

### Q3 — Opt-out mechanism

**Decision: `--role=maintainer` flag on `bd init` (already exists).**

When `--role=maintainer` is passed:
- Fork is detected and mentioned (transparency)
- Routing auto-config is skipped
- A one-line recovery hint is shown

Post-init reconfiguration:
```
git config beads.role maintainer
bd config set routing.mode ""
```

A one-line mention of `--role=maintainer` appears in the fork-detection output so users who see it unexpectedly can act immediately.

---

### Q4 — Success message format

**Decision: minimal, structured, consistent with the `bd init` summary block.**

Uses the `  ✓ label: value` two-column style already in the final summary. Fork-detection lines are grouped under a `▶` header with 2-space-indented `✓` children — identical to the contributor wizard's step headers, but without the wizard's interactive turns.

---

### Q5 — Hint about `--contributor` when no fork detected?

**Decision: no.**

Standard maintainer init stays clean. `bd help init` already documents `--contributor`. Adding a hint to the mainline output is noise for the majority of users (project maintainers).

---

## Terminal mockups

### Happy path — fork detected (interactive or non-interactive)

```
$ cd ~/projects/my-fork
$ bd init

  Hooks installed to: .beads/hooks/
  ✓ Committed beads files to git
  ✓ Auto-export enabled → .beads/issues.jsonl

▶ Fork detected — configuring contributor routing
  upstream: https://github.com/original/repo

  ✓ Planning repo: ~/.beads-planning
  ✓ Issues will route to planning repo (routing.mode=auto)
  ✓ Sync remote set to upstream
  ✓ Added .beads/ to .git/info/exclude

  To use maintainer mode instead: bd init --role=maintainer

✓ bd initialized successfully!

  Backend: dolt
  Mode:    embedded
  Database: my-fork
  Issue prefix: my-fork
  Issues will be named: my-fork-<hash> (e.g., my-fork-a3f2dd)

Run bd quickstart to get started.
```

Key details:
- The `▶` header and its `✓` children are a self-contained block visually distinct from the surrounding lines.
- The upstream URL is echoed so the user can verify it's the right remote.
- All four actions are listed (planning repo, routing, sync, exclude) — no hidden side-effects.
- Opt-out hint is the last line of the block, not the first. Users who wanted this don't need to read it; users who didn't can act on it.

---

### Opt-out path — `--role=maintainer` on a fork

```
$ cd ~/projects/my-fork
$ bd init --role=maintainer

  Hooks installed to: .beads/hooks/
  ✓ Committed beads files to git
  ✓ Auto-export enabled → .beads/issues.jsonl

  ⚠ Fork detected (upstream: https://github.com/original/repo)
    Contributor routing skipped (--role=maintainer).
    To set up contributor routing later: bd init --contributor

✓ bd initialized successfully!

  Backend: dolt
  Mode:    embedded
  Database: my-fork
  Issue prefix: my-fork
  Issues will be named: my-fork-<hash> (e.g., my-fork-a3f2dd)

Run bd quickstart to get started.
```

Key details:
- `⚠` (warn) not `▶` (action) — nothing was configured, just observed.
- One line says what was skipped and why; one line says how to undo the skip later.
- The block is compact because there's nothing to enumerate.

---

### Edge case — routing already configured (re-init on existing repo)

```
$ bd init

  ⚠ Fork detected (upstream: https://github.com/original/repo)
    Contributor routing already configured → ~/.beads-planning
    Skipping auto-setup. To reconfigure: bd init --contributor

✓ bd initialized successfully!
...
```

The `⚠` signals "I noticed something but took no action" — consistent with the existing warning style.

---

### Non-interactive mode (`CI=true` or stdin not a TTY)

Routing is configured silently. The `--quiet` contract already suppresses informational output. The long description for `bd init` already states "Fork exclude auto-configured when fork detected" — the same applies to routing.

```
$ CI=true bd init

✓ bd initialized successfully!

  Backend: dolt
  Mode:    embedded
  Database: my-fork
  Issue prefix: my-fork
  Issues will be named: my-fork-<hash> (e.g., my-fork-a3f2dd)

Run bd quickstart to get started.
```

---

## Accessibility audit (WCAG 2.1 AA)

### 1.4.1 Use of Color — PASS

Every status signal uses both a Unicode symbol and a semantic color:
- `▶` accent — discovery / step header
- `✓` green/pass — completed action
- `⚠` yellow/warn — informational; no action taken

No information is conveyed by color alone. In a no-color terminal (`NO_COLOR=1` or `--no-color`), the symbols remain meaningful.

### 1.4.3 Contrast — PASS (conditional)

Terminal contrast is theme-dependent. The codebase uses lipgloss styles via `ui.RenderAccent`, `ui.RenderPass`, `ui.RenderWarn` — the same palette already validated across the rest of `bd`. No new colors introduced.

### 2.1.1 Keyboard — PASS

The happy path requires no interaction. The opt-out path uses a command-line flag provided upfront, not a mid-flow prompt.

### 2.4.6 Headings and Labels — PASS

The `▶ Fork detected — configuring contributor routing` header describes the section's purpose. Sub-items use consistent `✓ label: value` format. No ambiguous abbreviations.

### 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions — PASS

The opt-out hint (`To use maintainer mode instead: bd init --role=maintainer`) is a complete, actionable instruction. No ellipsis-terminated fragments.

### Screen-reader / plain-text mode

Strip all ANSI codes; the remaining text reads cleanly:

```
Fork detected — configuring contributor routing
upstream: https://github.com/original/repo

Planning repo: ~/.beads-planning
Issues will route to planning repo (routing.mode=auto)
Sync remote set to upstream
Added .beads/ to .git/info/exclude

To use maintainer mode instead: bd init --role=maintainer
```

All information present. No meaning lost.

---

## Component choices

**Reuse without modification:**

| Symbol | Go expression | Semantic |
|--------|--------------|---------|
| `▶`    | `ui.RenderAccent("▶")` | Step / discovery header |
| `✓`    | `ui.RenderPass("✓")` | Completed action |
| `⚠`    | `ui.RenderWarn("⚠")` | Info / skipped |

No new UI primitives. No new lipgloss styles. The fork-detection block follows the same 2-space indentation under the `▶` header used in `promptForkExclude` and the contributor wizard.

**Placement in init.go flow:**

```
// existing: role prompt → contributor wizard → dolt commit
// NEW: fork-detection block (replaces promptForkExclude + role prompt for fork repos)
// existing: auto-export prompt → hooks install → git commit → final summary
```

The fork-detection block runs after the Dolt database is initialized and committed, before the auto-export prompt. This matches the current placement of `promptForkExclude` (line 1201 in init.go).

---

## What this design does NOT cover

- `bd migrate-personal` UX — bd-umbf Child 3, separate bead
- `bd export --exclude-owner` — bd-umbf Child 2, builder work
- `bd list` cross-repo display — already works via existing hydration
- Error recovery UI (planning repo creation failure) — builder chooses; recommendation is `⚠ auto-routing failed: <error>. Run bd init --contributor to retry.`
close_reason: Design complete - full UX spec for bd init fork-detection in bead notes. Builder bead be-c7696f implemented before design; UX alignment bead pending.

title: bd migrate-personal: relocate pre-existing contributor issues to planning repo
description:
New command: bd migrate-personal

Purpose: one-time migration for contributors who created personal planning issues before routing was configured.

Implementation (cmd/bd/migrate_personal.go):
1. Determine contributor identity via getActorWithGit()
2. Query project DB: SELECT * FROM issues WHERE created_by = identity
3. Show list of found issues with titles; prompt: "Move N issues to ~/.beads-planning? [Y/n]"
4. If yes: read routing.contributor from config; open planning DB at that path
5. For each issue: INSERT into planning DB (including labels, deps, comments); DELETE from project DB
6. Wrap DELETE in transaction; validate planning DB connection before any DELETE
7. Report: "Moved N issues to ~/.beads-planning"

Safety:

notes:
## Review Verdict: request-changes

**Reviewed:** feat/be-nnqp-be-4b63-stats-no-blocked (commit ddf53438c)
**Reviewer:** beads/reviewer
**Date:** 2026-05-17

---

### PASS

- **Build clean**: `go build ./...` passes on feature branch, no new failures vs main.
- **go vet clean**: No issues in changed packages.
- **All BlockedIssues callers nil-guarded**: Grepped cmd/bd/ and internal/ — every dereference of `stats.BlockedIssues` is nil-checked (`status.go:119-124`, `status.go:212`, `examples/library-usage/main.go:116`).
- **Interface plumbing correct**: `store` is `storage.DoltStorage`; `DoltStorage` now embeds `FastStatisticsStore`; `GetStatisticsNoBlocked` compiles cleanly.
- **be-4b63 fix correct**: `Blocked: 0` now renders plain text (not red via `ui.RenderFail`). Conditional at `status.go:118-127` is correct — red only when `*stats.BlockedIssues > 0`.
- **omitempty correct**: `blocked_count_skipped` absent from default JSON output; appears only when true.
- **Help text updated**: New flag in `--help`, examples and Use cases section updated per spec.
- **Pre-existing test failures**: Failures in `cmd/bd/doctor`, `internal/beads`, `internal/config` are pre-existing on main (verified). Not introduced by this PR.
- **Coverage gap acknowledged**: be-zkzw tracks integration tests for `--no-blocked` path — criterion (b) satisfied.
- **Security**: No new injection vectors, no new network calls, no secrets handling. No OWASP Top 10 concerns.

---

### FINDINGS

#### [BLOCKER] F1: JSON contradiction when `--assigned --no-blocked` combined
- **File/line**: `cmd/bd/status.go:96-99`
- **Severity**: Medium
- **Confidence**: High

When both `--assigned` and `--no-blocked` are passed:
1. `GetStatisticsNoBlocked` is called → `stats.BlockedIssues = nil`
2. `getAssignedStatistics` overrides stats → `stats.BlockedIssues = &blockedCount` (real value)
3. Output is built: `BlockedCountSkipped: noBlocked` = **true**

Result: JSON says `blocked_count_skipped: true` but `blocked_issues: 5` — contradictory. Any machine consumer checking `blocked_count_skipped` to guard dereferencing `blocked_issues` would misread this.

**Fix** (one line):
```go
// Before (status.go ~line 97)
BlockedCountSkipped: noBlocked,

// After
BlockedCountSkipped: stats.BlockedIssues == nil,
```
This makes the field reflect whether the skip actually happened in the result, not whether the flag was set.

---

#### [RECOMMENDATION] F2: `Ready to Work: 0` misleads when `--no-blocked` used
- **File/line**: `internal/storage/dolt/queries.go:115`, `internal/storage/embeddeddolt/statistics.go:49`
- **Severity**: Medium
- **Confidence**: High

Both `GetStatisticsNoBlocked` implementations return `ReadyIssues = 0` (zero value) because `ReadyIssues = OpenIssues - blockedCount` requires the blocked set. The designer's spec example shows `Ready to Work: 263` in the `--no-blocked` output. With the current implementation, users who run `bd stats --no-blocked` will see `Ready to Work: 0` which looks like there's no work — potentially alarming and incorrect.

Options:
- Also render `Ready to Work: (skipped)` in the human output when `noBlocked` is set (symmetric with Blocked)
- Or: document this clearly in flag help text ("Note: Ready count also shows 0 when --no-blocked is set")

This can be a follow-up bead rather than a blocker, but builder should decide before merge — the current silent '0' will confuse users.

---

### Summary

One blocker (F1): trivial one-line fix. One recommendation (F2): design decision on whether to show '(skipped)' for Ready count too. Routing back to builder for F1 fix. F2 is judgment call — builder can file follow-up bead or fix in same commit.

description:
## Source
Design: bd-f5zqs (bd perf Q4 — make bd stats blocked-count optional).
Full UX spec lives in the bd-f5zqs description field.

## What to build

### 1. Type change — internal/types/types.go
Change `BlockedIssues int` → `BlockedIssues *int` (nullable JSON):
```go
BlockedIssues *int `json:"blocked_issues"`   // nil when --no-blocked
```
After the change, grep every caller and add nil guards:
```bash
grep -rn "BlockedIssues" cmd/bd/ internal/
```
Expected sites: `cmd/bd/status.go` ~line 108 (human render path),
`getAssignedStatistics` (constructs Statistics directly — must switch to *int pointer),
any test assertions that compare `BlockedIssues` to a literal int.

### 2. StatusOutput struct — cmd/bd/status.go
Add `BlockedCountSkipped bool` with `omitempty`:
```go
type StatusOutput struct {
    Summary             *types.Statistics      `json:"summary"`
    BlockedCountSkipped bool                   `json:"blocked_count_skipped,omitempty"`
    RecentActivity      *RecentActivitySummary `json:"recent_activity,omitempty"`
}
```

### 3. CLI flag
Add `--no-blocked` to `statusCmd`/`statsCmd`. **No short alias** (performance escape
hatch, not a daily flag). Position in `--help`: after `--no-activity`, before `--json`.

### 4. Logic
When `--no-blocked` is set:
- Skip `computeBlockedIDs` entirely
- Set `stats.BlockedIssues = nil`
- Set `output.BlockedCountSkipped = true`

### 5. Human output
When `BlockedIssues == nil`, render:
```
  Blocked:         (skipped)
```
`(skipped)` uses `ui.MutedStyle`. Right-align to column 32 (same as numeric values).
**Do NOT omit the Blocked: line** — absence implies the command is broken.

### 6. Help text
Append to `statusCmd.Long` after the `--no-activity` example line:
```
  bd status --no-blocked             # Skip slow blocked-count scan (faster)
  bd stats --no-blocked --json       # JSON output without blocked count
```
Add to `Use cases:` section:
```
  - Fast CI status checks that don't need blocked-count accuracy
```

### 7. JSON shape
Default (no flag): `{"summary": {"blocked_issues": 42, ...}}`
With `--no-blocked`: `{"summary": {"blocked_issues": null, ...}, "blocked_count_skipped": true}`

## Acceptance criteria
- `bd stats --no-blocked` completes in <100ms on a 10k-bead corpus
- `bd stats` (default, no flag) behavior unchanged
- Human output shows `Blocked:         (skipped)` with muted style when flag is set
- JSON: `blocked_issues` is null and `blocked_count_skipped` is true when flag is set
- JSON: `blocked_count_skipped` is absent (omitempty) in default output
- All `BlockedIssues` callers nil-guarded; `go build ./...` clean
- Help text updated with new examples

## Code pointers
- `cmd/bd/status.go` — main entry, flag registration, output render (~line 108)
- `internal/types/types.go` — Statistics struct
- `internal/storage/issueops/statistics.go:ScanIssueCountsInTx` — cheap aggregate (untouched)
- `internal/storage/dolt/queries.go:computeBlockedIDs` — what we skip with the flag
- `internal/storage/issueops/blocked.go:ComputeBlockedIDsInTx` — same

title: mol-tdd-build
description:
TDD build cycle — polecat isolation + red/green per task.

Takes a `ready-to-build` bead, creates an isolated worktree and feature
branch, then enforces a strict red/green TDD loop before submitting the
branch for review. Self-terminates after submit.

## Contract

1. Caller slings with a bead labelled `ready-to-build` and `--on mol-tdd-build`.
2. Builder creates an isolated worktree and feature branch per bead.
3. RED: writes failing tests expressing the acceptance criteria; verifies failure.
4. GREEN: writes minimal implementation; verifies all tests pass.
5. Pushes branch, relabels bead `needs-review`, closes bead, exits via drain-ack.

## Hard Gates

- After RED commit: `$TEST_CMD` MUST FAIL. If it passes, the tests are wrong.
- After GREEN commit: `$TEST_CMD` MUST PASS. Never hand off red tests.

## Rejection-Aware Resume

If `metadata.rejection_reason` is set on the bead, a previous attempt was
rejected. Reuse the existing worktree and branch, rebase onto latest base,
and fix the rejection reason rather than starting over.

## Variables

| Variable | Source | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| test_cmd | caller | Test command (auto-detect if empty) |
| commit_scope | caller | Conventional commit type (default: "feat") |
| base_branch | caller | Branch to fork from (default: "main") |
close_reason: all steps complete

title: Capture pre-existing test failures on base branch
description:
Run the test suite on the clean base-branch state to record which tests
were already failing BEFORE this task started. Do NOT fix pre-existing
failures — they are the baseline. The RED step only adds new tests.

**1. Determine the test command:**
```bash
TEST_CMD=""
if [ -z "$TEST_CMD" ]; then
    if [ -f go.mod ]; then TEST_CMD="go test ./..."
    elif [ -f package.json ]; then TEST_CMD="npm test --silent"
    elif [ -f Cargo.toml ]; then TEST_CMD="cargo test"
    elif [ -f pyproject.toml ] || [ -f setup.py ]; then TEST_CMD="pytest -q"
    else
        bd update $ROOT_ID --notes "<existing notes>
preflight: no test runner detected — skip"
        exit 0
    fi
fi
echo "Test command: $TEST_CMD"
```

**2. Run and capture:**
```bash
if $TEST_CMD 2>&1 | tee /tmp/tdd-preflight.log; then
    PREFLIGHT="pass"
    FAILURES="0"
else
    PREFLIGHT="fail"
    FAILURES=$(grep -c 'FAIL\|FAILED\|Error\|error' /tmp/tdd-preflight.log || echo "unknown")
fi

bd update $ROOT_ID --notes "<existing notes>
preflight: $PREFLIGHT — $FAILURES pre-existing failures
test_cmd: $TEST_CMD"
```

**Exit criteria:** Baseline recorded in bead notes. Pre-existing failures
documented and will not be treated as regressions.

title: Write minimal implementation to make tests pass (GREEN)

Write the minimum production code needed to make the RED tests pass.
No gold-plating. No abstractions not required by the tests. If in doubt,
write less and let the tests tell you what's missing.

**1. Write the implementation:**

- Follow existing code patterns (check neighbouring files for style and naming)
- Do not introduce new dependencies without a note in the bead
- Do not modify files outside the scope implied by the acceptance criteria
- Reuse existing helpers — do not introduce new abstractions for one-time use

**2. Run and verify GREEN — HARD GATE:**
```bash
if $TEST_CMD 2>&1 | tee /tmp/tdd-green.log; then
    echo "GREEN — all tests pass."
else
    echo "HARD GATE FAILURE: tests still failing after implementation."
    tail -30 /tmp/tdd-green.log
    echo "Fix the implementation before proceeding. Do not hand off red tests."
    exit 1
fi
```

```bash
git add <implementation files>
git commit -m "feat: green — $BEAD_TITLE (refs $ROOT_ID)"
GREEN_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
bd update $ROOT_ID --notes "<existing notes>
tdd_green: committed $GREEN_SHA"
```
